ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM Progress and Resume Issue: Advance Overwriting in Moodle 4.5
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, We are experiencing a critical progress saving issue with our SCORM activities that is preventing students from completing them reliably. 1. The Critical Symptom: Advance Overwriting The core problem is that progress made in a previous session is overwritten by progress made in the latest session, making it impossible to complete the activity across multiple sittings. Here is a example of what happens: A student enters the activity and completes Exercises 1 and 2. The student exits and later re-enters. The course resumes perfectly at the last visited slide (e.g., the start of Exercise 3). They can also view an internal SCORM page showing the saved scores for Ex. 1 and 2. In this session, the student only completes Exercise 3. They exit. Upon the next entry, the student checks their internal progress index and sees that only Exercise 3 is marked as completed . Exercises 1 and 2 now appear as not completed (0% progress). If the student navigates to Exercises 1 or 2, they can still see the answers they previously selected (the visual data is there), but the SCORM is no longer counting those exercises toward the final score/completion percentage. The student must re-validate the exercises. The next time they enter, only the last batch of re-validated exercises will be counted. This substitution of previous progress with the latest progress makes the activity almost impossible to complete. This issue doesn't always happen after the first exit; sometimes it starts after the third or fourth time the student enters the activity. 2. Environment and Course Configuration We are using Moodle 4.5 . The SCORM packages are SCORM 1.2 , generated with the authoring tool TalentSoft . A. TalentSoft Publication Settings (SCORM 1.2) Category Setting Value Used SCORM/AICC Standard used SCORM 1.2 Adapt content to browser size Always adapt Validation score 0 Pedagogy Random activity order No Number of activities All Section validation "When all activities are validated" Maximum time (No time set) Score calculation "Only from completed activities" Limit score 0 to 100 No Clear results on each pass No Section coefficient equals sum of activity coefficients Yes Navigation Progress bar coefficient corresponds to total activity coefficients Yes B. Moodle Activity Settings (Moodle 4.5) Category Setting Value Used Attempt Management Number of attempts Unlimited Grading method Highest attempt Force new attempt No Lock after final attempt No Compatibility Settings Force completed No Auto-continue No Auto-save No Master score overrides status Yes

ResponsesInList.Title: Displaying SCORM Time Spent in Report View
ResponsesInList.Text: No it's not. It is a e-learning standard. Actually, the most popular one. Besides API, it has very large data model that is used to collect and transfer data such as time spent, score, lesson status, lesson location, etc.... The real reason why we don't see the scorm data in course reports very often is it's complexity. Each course can have multiple scorm activities , each scorm can have multiple attempts recorded for each user. Each attempt can be used for multiple days when user is accessing the same scorm activity multiple times within the same attempt. Each scorm can have multiple SCOs - something like lessons within scorm activitiy. Each SCO has it's own set of data recorded in the database , such as time spent, score, lesson status, etc... I also use custom reporting for this kind of things, but different plugin - more advanced and feature-rich Configurable Reports. I know that some people don't like that this plugin loads the complete recordset initially before you can apply any filters to narrow down the results, but I also have SQL solution for this and it doesn't need any plugin or Moodle code modification (no php or js coding needed).

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle always marking as complete
ResponsesInList.Text: Why would you use the grading method Learning objects if you have a quiz with a required score of 100. Grading method should be either Highest grade, lowest grade or sum grade not Learning Objects. Maximum grade should be 100 if that is the max. Within Storyline content the passing score is set there, along with what "words" we will define as success. It is either Pass or Complete. However, it is created and published in Storyline has to match your Completion conditions in Moodle. If it is Passed in Storyline it has to be Passed in Moodle. No other checkboxes in the Completion conditions needs to be selected - with the exception of Receive a grade.

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle always marking as complete
ResponsesInList.Text: The variable in the API between Scorm/Moodle is cmi.core.lesson_status. This variable can only have these values: “passed”, “completed”, “failed”, “incomplete”, “browsed”, “not attempted”. For example, as soon as a student opens a Scorm in Moodle, it becomes "browsed". The authoring software/app should then set the value of this variable and transfer (commit) the value to Moodle. I have played around with the Mastery score (and override) to little effect. Others may have a different experience.

ResponsesInList.Title: Automatic SCORM closing
ResponsesInList.Text: SCORM OPENING (less important) -- Settings to open in a new window would be "Appearance" panel, "Display package" setting set to "New Window" -- this 'should' launch it in a new window instead of in the existing window, however, you 'might' also have to have that setting set when authoring the scorm in the original software... Settings to have it bypass the "click Enter" button, try these: "Appearance" panel, "Student skip content structure page" set to "Always" and "Display attempt status set to "No" -- note, as a non-student role, you will still see this "Enter" button, so you need to log in as an actual student with password to experience the one-click access to the scorm.

ResponsesInList.Title: Can I use SCORM without grading?
ResponsesInList.Text: I like the way SCORM works as a slideshow and I am building multiple courses that will have tens of SCORM packages as self-learning topics, sometimes over a hundred per course. I want my students to be able to step through the slideshow, but I don't want any kind of grading. Maybe for some of them I might make the students click to say they have completed, but that's all. My gradebook is rapidly filling with content that I don't want to have there. Is it possible to use SCORM without it affecting the gradebook?

ResponsesInList.Title: Can I use SCORM without grading?
ResponsesInList.Text: Don't do it! The type of content it sounds like you are creating would be better created using H5P - it allows you to generate content packages like the ones you are looking for. Take a look at the various videos/docs on using H5P in Moodle. Hopefully you'll stop reading ... and go away and invest time learning about H5P.. but... if you're still there and are completely determined to go down the SCORM route.... what you're asking for is really just an IMS / External package - Moodle allows you to add IMS content packages as a resource in your course - and you can read more about that here: https://docs.moodle.org/en/IMS_content_package Keep in mind the IMSCP plugin is not all that widely used, hasn't had any improvements in a very very long time, and is a plugin that I would advocate that Moodle should consider removing in a future release.

ResponsesInList.Title: Can I use SCORM without grading?
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you! I'll be contact with our content creators and suggest we pivot to H5P The reason for SCORM is that they are familiar with it and there's some tool we have that they use to convert our (many thousands) of slides to SCORM.

ResponsesInList.Title: Can I use SCORM without grading?
ResponsesInList.Text: I second. Unless you want an interactive Scorm presentation, using it just as a slideshow "works" but there are so many settings on the Scorm authoring side that you need to take into account (ie. it needs to still track data/progress in some fashion so it can allow users to Resume where they've left if they need to exit it and return later), and if a user skips a few slides then Moodle may not mark it as complete and I spend too many moments of my day manually marking scorms as complete for users who do not go through all 100 of the slides, or who have trouble viewing it due to pop up blockers. Again, you can make it work, but it's not worth the effort for just non-interactive 'slides'. With H5P Course Presentation activity type, I simply export my PPTs as PNG slides, then I upload those as my H5P backgrounds. Takes work up front, but so-so-so much better in the long run than Scorm in my opinion.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM file isn't uploading any content to course (Moodle 4.5.1)
ResponsesInList.Text: Have you tried re-publishing your scorm object from Rise? Do other scorm objects upload ok? Any errors with the package would show in red at the upload panel. I would suggest checking your upload location for capacity even though it is a small file, or looking for any reason why it won't upload to your server . Some reasons are: • PHP upload settings are blocking completion - check the php.ini file for file size uploads. If you regularly upload larger than 14Mb anyway, then it won't be this causing the problem... • File system issues prevent finalizing the upload - check your moodledata folder has correct file ownership and permissions on your server, and that your web server can write to it. If you normally upload and there are no issues, it's probably not this either... • Moodle's file processing ( AJAX or cron tasks) is stuck - if you can get to the command line and are comfortable checking in there, try this... php admin/cli/scheduled_task.php --list | grep scorm It should reveal if any scheduled task relating to scorm is in progress... including if it is stuck. You can try manually running Cron to get it moving, and I'd also check you've got a relevant command in your crontab to check for stuck tasks. In the CLI, type crontab -e and if you can't see one, add this line to make moodle run cron every 5 minutes: */5 * * * * /usr/bin/php /path/to/moodle/admin/cli/cron.php >/dev/null 2>&1 Database issues prevent SCORM from saving - go to system admin, developer and turn on debugging, optionally get it to show on the page (easier if you're not familiar with servers) but be aware anyone else logging in will also see the alarming rows of warnings and errors that appear... once turned on, try uploading again, and check the warnings and errors for issues relating to scorm upload. It'll reveal more than you need, but just try to filter out the lines related to scorm. If you can use the CLI, and write the errors to moodle's error log, then you can read those lines in there instead, keeping your site clear of alarming warnings. In the CLI, type: tail -f /var/log/apache2/error.log # Assuming you're using Apache as your web server tail -f /path/to/moodledata/temp/logs/error.log # Assuming you've got Moodle error logging running. either of these will show you the tail end of your logs, and you'll see some lines there to help debug what's happening.

ResponsesInList.Title: Passed OR completed seems to have changed
ResponsesInList.Text: Been a while since I checked in on this one... Moodle 4.5+, running scorm completion and using 'Passed' as well as 'Completed' in the completion settings. Previous versions suggest this would work as 'OR', since the 'help' text reads that 'checking one or more statuses will require at least one to be met...' Now, it appears they are on 'AND' : The line I am looking at is "Activity is complete when the student does all of the following". This means if we upgrade from an older version to 4.5+, and the original settings are carried over, that no new users accessing the same scorm are going to complete without both those requirements being true (passed AND complete). In normal circumstances, this would be ok as to achieve completion in scorm 1.2 you'd normally visit all pages and pass any participating tests. However, 3rd party vendors may not always structure their Scorms to follow those rules. To fix it would seem to require the completion settings to be unlocked and edited - this is not a good option since the client is recording exact date and time of user completion as part of their compliance checks (corporate client), and unlocking will change the completion data for everyone. What would be the best way to resolve this?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Passed OR completed seems to have changed

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Passed OR completed seems to have changed
ResponsesInList.Text: It seems there are two parts to this issue. The original problem was flagged by a client when their scorm objects stopped scoring in Moodle 4.5+, but were working perfectly before that upgrade. Checking the scorm configuration page, the wording suggest 'all' conditions must be true, yet when opening the scorm object, the entry page confirms 'passed OR complete' is true. there is an obvious semantic conflict here, which I hope can be resolved. Changing the scorm completion settings is possible to do directly in the database and this will NOT change the previous completion data, it will only affect new users. Scorm status is defined as a '2', a '4' or a '6' in the mdl_scorm table, within the 'completionstatusrequired' field. 2= 'passed', 4='completed' and 6=both status checked. But that doesn't resolve the issue of scorm not scoring - huge thanks to Dan Marsden for pointing me in the right direction. Moodle Tracker has got https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-82601 and this contains the fix. Within the /mod/scorm directory on your server , the locallib.php file is incorrect on line 476, and needs a simple edit. $v->id = $track->valueid; needs to become $v->id = $tracktest->valueid; Once this is done, the scorms started recording scores again. It's in the tracker, it's made it to the core and I believe future updates will incorporate this. However, if (like me) you've recently upgraded to version 405 (4.5+) then check this file if your scorms stop scoring.

ResponsesInList.Text:
I've been working with Moodle and Articulate SCORM 1.2 packages for years for several clients, so I also encountered similar problems of SCORM occasionally fails to send data to Moodle.  Problem is in /mod/scorm/datamodels/scorm_12.js in LMSCommit function. Search for this line: result
= StoreData(cmi,false); Be careful because the same line appears twice in the same file - once in the LMSCommit function and once in LMSFinish function. You need to change the line in LMSCommit function only. Just change the second argument to true, so the same line after change would be: result = StoreData(cmi,true); Use this on your own risk, but this solved the problem for me. Before this, I had SCORM reporting problems with approx. 2-3 percent of the users. Since applying this patch few years ago, I have zero problems with SCORM reporting. ZERO my friend! I know this is not popular solution because you have to apply this after each Moodle upgrade, but it's better than nothing. Best regards, Zoran

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Interaction tracking SCORM 2004
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Pablo, Interactions are pretty similar in 1.2 and 2004 - the main difference is that 2004 allows the storage of the question text itself and 1.2 just records an "identifier" - but both report the students answer and if it was correct or not. That functionality should be in a working state for 2004 but I haven't tested it recently myself, although keep in mind that there is an "interactions" report in Moodle that didn't get adapted to support 2004 - there are some differences in the parameter names that are used between the 2 - for example 1.2 stores the reposonse in a "student_response" field, but 2004 uses the name "learner_response" and that report is only looking for the 1.2 value but you should be able to see the 2004 data by accessing the db direclty. When you talk about a user being able to re-open a previously completed scorm and continue where they left off - that's not actually something that we do anything with on the Moodle side. Moodle simply stores the data that the SCORM package asks it to, and then allows the SCORM pacakge to request that information back. Typically "progress" is stored in a field called "suspend_data" and on re-entry the SCORM package asks Moodle "give me the last suspend_data" record (but it can also ask for interaction data as well.) Then it's up to the SCORM's own Javascript to load that into the package presented to the learner. If you're just wanting to report on the interactions data for a 1.2 (or 2004 package) you should already be able to do that now, but you might need to adapt the existing reporting to report on all the 2004 data that will be stored in the db (If your SCORM package is actually saving interaction data - not all SCORM packages do this anyway.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Interactions Report Timeout
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Tommy! 😊 To tackle this, you can use the `userreporttracks` report available on Moodle’s GitHub . Here’s a step-by-step guide: Download or copy the code from this report, and set all values from lines 29 to 33 as needed for your specific case. This will help generate the report without relying on default configurations. Change the `$download` variable to `1` . This will ensure the report is generated for download.  Delete all `$PAGE->...` entries in the script since we don’t need the page’s HTML interface. The goal is to generate the report directly, bypassing the web interface. This is a crucial step! The `$table->finish_output()` method ends with an `exit()` , which stops the script and prevents capturing the content. Modify this part so the script can continue running. Use `ob_get_contents()` to capture the entire output of the report. This way, you can save it directly into a file within MoodleData, allowing you to access it later without depending on the interface’s response time. Eduardo Kraus Teacher and Programmer

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to Decode SCORM Progress Data for Analysis in Moodle 4.3?
ResponsesInList.Text: Unfortunately most scorm packages use the value "suspend_data" to store user progress. The SCORM authoring tool itself decides how that data is encoded and decoded(not Moodle) and there is no "standard" way it is encoded across different authoring tools. ResponsesInList.Title: How to Decode SCORM Progress Data for Analysis in Moodle 4.3?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Lukas! 😊 First, the SCORM data is stored in the `mdl_scorm_scoes_track` table, which keeps values in the `cmi.suspend_data` field. This is where interpreting student progress comes in. Since Articulate Rise360 generates this content, it’s likely that the data is encoded in a specific format, making it difficult to read directly. However, with some adjustments to the SCORM file, we can extract this information in a more accessible way. Unfortunately, Rise360 lacks advanced options that could provide more sophisticated SCORM configurations, so a bit of programming is necessary. First, unzip the SCORM ZIP file and open the `lms/scormdriver.js` file exported from Articulate. This file is responsible for the course’s communication with Moodle; every time a student interacts with the SCORM, `lms/scormdriver.js` records and organizes these data for Moodle. Inside `scormdriver.js` , look for the method `SetDataChunk(strData)` . This method handles sending progress (in this case, the `cmi.suspend_data` value) to Moodle, and this is where we can add the necessary logic. Eduardo Kraus Teacher and programmer

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ocurrió una excepción mientras se procesaban datos de privacidad
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hola, Eduardo Kremenchutzky! 😊 ¡Qué bueno que trajiste esta cuestión aquí! Vamos a resolverlo juntos. Este error ocurre porque Moodle está intentando eliminar datos relacionados con SCORM en la tabla `mdl_scorm_scoes_value` , y por algún motivo, hay una falla al acceder o manipular los datos. Aquí tienes algunos pasos detallados que puedes seguir para resolverlo: Verifica la tabla `mdl_scorm_scoes_value` : Primero, accede a la base de datos de tu Moodle y verifica si la tabla `mdl_scorm_scoes_value` existe y está funcionando correctamente. Si hay algún problema de corrupción en la tabla, puedes intentar un comando de reparación en MySQL . Usa el siguiente comando: 
```text
REPAIR TABLE mdl_scorm_scoes_value;
```
 Este comando verificará e intentará corregir posibles problemas en la estructura de la tabla. Verifica las columnas esenciales: También verifica si la tabla tiene las columnas necesarias, como `attemptid` y `scoid` . Esto es fundamental para que Moodle pueda gestionar correctamente los intentos y los datos de SCORM. Usa el siguiente comando para asegurarte de que las columnas están presentes: 
```text
DESCRIBE mdl_scorm_scoes_value;
```
 Si alguna de estas columnas está ausente, esto puede causar el error. Si no están, puede ser necesario recrearlas o restaurar una copia de seguridad anterior de la tabla. ¡Espero que estos pasos ayuden a resolver el problema en tu SCORM! Si necesitas algo más, ¡estamos aquí para ayudarte! 😄🚀 Eduardo Kraus Profesor y Programador

ResponsesInList.Title: How does SCROM starts automatically from the point where left off??
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Pranjal! 😄 When a student accesses a SCORM module and makes progress, the SCORM uses a field called `cmi.suspend_data` to store information about the session state, such as the completed percentage, the page they stopped on, or even responses to activities within the SCORM. This `cmi.suspend_data` is essentially a set of data that the SCORM records for each user's attempt. When the user returns to the module, Moodle and SCORM use this information to continue exactly where they left off, as you correctly noticed when seeing different progress percentages for different users. The format of `cmi.suspend_data` can vary depending on the implementation of the SCORM package you're using. It may contain various information, such as: Activity identifiers, Progress (for example, completed percentage), Student interaction data. If the SCORM was well implemented, it will automatically handle saving and retrieving this information to ensure that students can resume the content without losing progress. And yes, this is a common practice when developing SCORM packages, especially for long courses or those with many interactions. 📂 Since you're dealing with Flash, be cautious, as this technology has been discontinued and may cause inconsistencies. Using Ruffle is a good solution for running Flash content, but in the future, it might be worth considering a migration to more modern technologies like HTML5. I hope this helps clarify how SCORM works to ensure students can resume where they left off. We're always here to help with any questions you have in Moodle! 💪😁 Eduardo Kraus Teacher and Developer

As u mentioned cmi.suspend_data stores information about completed percentage, the page they stopped on etc. For my use case I need the completion percentage. Do u have any idea how can I fetch completion percentage from cmi.suspend_data?? I am using SCORM 1.2!!

ResponsesInList.Title: How does SCROM starts automatically from the point where left off??
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hello Pranjal Sagar! 😊 I'm glad to see you're making progress in understanding SCORM! I'm super happy to help you, and let's dive right in with lots of enthusiasm! For your case, since you're using SCORM 1.2 and mentioned the need to capture the completion percentage from `cmi.suspend_data` , indeed, this information needs to be processed directly within SCORM. You can do this by calculating the progress percentage based on the pages the learner has viewed in relation to the total number of pages in the content. One possible approach would be something like this: 
```text
let currentPage = getCurrentPage(); // Function to get the current SCORM page
let totalPages = getTotalPages(); // Function that returns the total number of pages
let completionPercentage = (currentPage / totalPages) * 100; // Calculate the percentage
```
 After calculating the value, you will need to send this data to SCORM and store it within `cmi.suspend_data` . This way, every time the learner leaves and returns to the content, they will continue from where they left off, and this percentage can be used to track their progress. Another super important point! 🔍 You can check if the data is being sent correctly with something like this: 
```text
scormSetValue("cmi.suspend_data", 
JSON
.stringify({
    progress: completionPercentage
}));
```
 This will ensure that SCORM stores the information in the right place and retrieves it when the learner returns. And, of course, don't forget to run tests to make sure everything is working as expected! 💪 We're here to help whenever you need! If you have any more questions or challenges, just let us know! 🚀 Eduardo Kraus Teacher and Programmer 👨‍🏫👨‍💻

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How does SCROM starts automatically from the point where left off??
ResponsesInList.Text: suspend_data is a custom "bucket" that scorm packages can use to store anything they want - it's usually used to store information about completion progress but there is no standard on the dataformat itself - it could be serialized/json_encoded/csv data or some other custom data type - Moodle just allows the scorm package to store stuff in that bucket and gives it back to the scorm package when the user re-opens the scorm (or the scorm asks the LMS for that data.) You will need to investigate the code inside your scorm package (which might be hard with it being flash) to find out how it uses/interprets that data so you try and write a script to interpret it yourself.

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle dispalying Storyline score as percentage instead of points
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, Tristan! 😄 What an interesting question you brought up, and I'm here to help you! On Monday, I made a modification to a SCORM package in Articulate Storyline to improve how navigation progress is sent to Moodle. This way, managers can see exactly where users are and their completion status. Super useful, right? In your case, what's happening is that Moodle is interpreting the percentage as points, which is why the calculation is incorrect. In the Grading section, adjust the "Highest Grade" field to 100 . This will make Moodle understand that it's working with a base of 100%, and it will display the score correctly as a percentage. Since Storyline sends 2/10, configuring it this way, if a student gets 2/10, Moodle will correctly calculate 20%, which equals the correct value of 2 points out of 10. This should fix the issue! If you need to adjust any other settings, such as synchronization behavior or grading methods, let me know, and we'll work it out together! 💪 Eduardo Kraus Professor and Programmer

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: scorm review mode never completes
ResponsesInList.Text: This sounds like your SCORM package is in fact flagging the lesson_status as "completed/passed or failed" so when the learner re-enters the same SCORM attempt it enters the scorm using "review mode" - this is part of the SCORM spec and it's actually up to your SCORM package's own code to decide if it should send data back to the LMS when in review mode (and it sounds like your SCORM package doesn't do this.) The easiest way around this is to disable "review mode" by adjusting the setting "Force new attempt" you can read more about that setting here: https://docs.moodle.org/404/en/SCORM_FAQ#Handling_of_Multiple_Attempts

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Video in SCORM module freezes
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle 3.8 has a number of known issues related to SCORM that have been resolved in newer Moodle versions - some of those relate to modern browser behavior and upgrading your site to a supported release is the only fix, but what you are describing there is possibly network or bandwidth related. are the videos contained within your SCORM package or hosted on an external site like youtube or vimeo? If the videos are stored within the SCORM package itself - have you run them through any video compression tools? - are they 5MB files or 500MB files? - if they are massive you should spend some time compressing them down to a smaller size to help. If large numbers of users are accessing your SCORM at the same time, the Moodle webserver itself might be struggling - if the users are at home on slow networks/wifi - it could be an issue at their end. In any case - there's not much more we can suggest here except to check the filesize or the videos in the scorm and "upgrade your moodle" - failing that, k someone with the ability to dig into your server performance to see what it's doing at the same time your users are reporting issues.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM player has determined...how to fix?
ResponsesInList.Text: I note you haven't answered the questions I asked? - where/how is your Moodle site hosted? I also note you mention that maybe it relates to older versions of Moodle... if you are using an old unsupported version of Moodle that could very well contribute to this and an upgrade to a stable release might help. The pop-up error that occurs is saying "I tried to connect to your Moodle site, but the site didn't respond in a timely manner" - this means that either your internet connection is not stable enough or the webserver hosting your moodle site is overloaded and not responding in a timely manner, you can disable the checks by modifying the core code (we don't provide a setting that lets you do this), it's hiding the real problem (your server or internet connection.) SCORM as a standard is inherently fragile - and some SCORM packages can overload basic hosting infrastructure quite easily - if the webserver cannot communicate with the users browser in a timely manner - the communication and tracking implemented within your SCORM package silently fails and then you can get intermittent help requests from learners complaining that they have completed a scorm, but it's not representing as complete within the Moodle site.

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle 4.3 SCORM database structure has now changed (and upgrade warning)
ResponsesInList.Text: As mentioned in the integration exposed post , MDL-46279 landed in the 4.3 branch this week which aims to improve performance for SCORM reporting and changes the structure of the SCORM database tables - if you have custom sql -based reports these will need updating when you upgrade to 4.3. If you have a large amount of SCORM tracking data (eg many millions of records in the scorm_scoes_track table) - the upgrade process that converts this data to the new structure may take some time so you will need to keep this in mind when planning your upgrades (and ideally test the upgrade before doing it in production to help estimate how much time it will take on your site.) Normalising the table structure like this should give us the opportunity to make further performance improvements to some areas of the reporting too - my main focus in this patch was the basic report page and making sure that everything still worked with the new table structure. If you notice any regressions in 4.3 related to the table changes (hopefully not) - please create a new tracker issue with the details - thanks!

ResponsesInList.Title: Regression in latest stables preventing some teachers from updating/creating scorm
ResponsesInList.Text: The security fix for MSA-24-0001 (Denial of service risk in file picker unzip functionality) which was included in 4.3.3, 4.2.6 and 4.1.9 now means that the "private files space" or userquota setting is now also used when a teacher tries to update a scorm package. Depending on what your debugging levels are set to, you may see errors like: " Exception - array_keys(): Argument #1 ($array) must be of type array, null given" Or entry to your updated SCORM package may just show an empty box instead of the SCORM package you are expecting. More information on this is here (and some of the related bugs) https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-81060 In the meantime, if you are affected by this bug, you may need to increase your private files limits for teachers so they can upload or update existing SCORM packages. Moodle's SCORM code basically only tries to unzip the package again if it sees the file is different from the one it already has - so if you have a teacher that has broken their SCORM activity due to this bug, you need to modify the scorm zip slightly (I added a text file called 0.txt to some packages I was fixing this week.) then get someone that doesn't have that userquota limit to upload the new scorm (or increase the userquota limit to get around it.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Issue saving progress with Rise 360's SCORM, Moodle and Firefox
ResponsesInList.Text: SCORM standard has limit on suspend data string length.  Moodle has special option to ignore that limit, because Articulate (and other tools) stores more suspend data than allowed by SCORM. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What would cause some completions/grades in a SCORM to record but not others?
ResponsesInList.Text: Captivate modules can be twitchy and sometimes don't do what you expect. I don't love Captivate. But that probably isn't the issue. You are correct--it could be internet connectivity. Another option is that the students opened the module and left it open with no activity for too long an your system timed them out. The scorm module will still be open and act normal, because it is loaded but it won't report back to Moodle because it not longer has a connection from being timed out.  It's like a phone call. If the call is disrupted on either end, the either person can continue talking but the sound doesn't get transmitted because the connection has been broken. Sometimes Captivate wants Exit Activity clicked when the student is done. There may be other reasons but that's what I generally see.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What would cause some completions/grades in a SCORM to record but not others?
ResponsesInList.Text:
We had similar issues with different SCORM authoring tools. The reason is that Moodle doesn't write SCORM tracking info into it's database until user exits the activity. What do you think happens if student doesn't exit the activity, for example if he/she just closes the laptop or leaves a PC on for hours when SCORM activity is still opened? The solution is small hack in SCORM plugin. I know it's not the popular solution because you have to apply it again after each Moodle upgrade, but it works like a charm. /mod/scorm/datamodels/scorm_12.js function that has to be changed is  LMSCommit (param) result
= StoreData(cmi,true); // second parametar has to be changed from false to true It is on line 416 in Moodle 3.11 - 4.1 This little patch forces Moodle to regularly store SCORM tracking info to the database each time SCORM content sends new data to Moodle. So if student doesn't exit SCORM activity properly, it doesn't matter because tracking info is stored in the Moodle database anyway. Regards, Zoran

SCORM modules are very flexible and they can be a lot of things--some are created from video and track seconds in the module for completion, some are slides and it would be a percentage of slides...but what if there were branches and they skip some slides? And there aren't any good ways to tell it. Captivate allows completion criteria of slides but even then, it only tells you which page of the package they are, not relativity.

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle 3.9 - SCORM wrongly counts time spent
ResponsesInList.Text: I have had this problem for some time. I have a very long training course which should last 10h 30m. Employees do it over several days, going in and out of training each day. SCORM has a built-in mechanism that does not allow the slides to scroll. Every slide in the presentation scrolls automatically. For some reason, in the report, the variable that counts the time spent in SCORM results in some employees having only a few seconds when others have several hours. What could be the reason for the bad time accrual in this SCORM?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 3.9 - SCORM wrongly counts time spent
ResponsesInList.Text: Measuring time is primary the job of a SCORM package itself, not of the LMS (like moodle). Within a session the SCORM package has to report spent time setting cmi.core.session_time (for instance running `API.LMSSetValue('cmi.core.session_time', '00:10:07')` if the user spent ten minutes and seven seconds) in SCORM 1.2. The LMS just stores the total of this reported times which can be accessed by the SCORM package reading 'cmi.core.total_time'. So the most obvious reason is that your specific SCORM package hardly ever communicates the spent time to moodle or its time measurement is implemented buggy.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Get Current Course of Scorm Activity
ResponsesInList.Text: I do not think it is possible to get the course's name or its id of the course a SCORM activity is part of: A SCORM package is meant to be a learning management system independent content so it also needs to run well in learning management systems that don't implement courses. Or even on learning management systems that are not connected to the world wide web. All communication should be done only using the SCORM API so there should not be a need to know the course. The data model of neither SCORM 1.2 nor SCORM 2004 implement elements for course id or course name. Why do you want to send xAPI data? If communication is done via xAPI it is not a SCORM 1.2 or SCORM 2004 package…

Is there a specific debugging level that can help me understanding what's going on, where to loo for? It seems the package doesn't pass its state to Moodle, the package is quite old, could it be a php/browser compatibility issue? Grazie Luca

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM package not saving progress
ResponsesInList.Text: I think, it is best to check first whether or not your SCORM package performs the required API calls needed to save the progress: First open the javascript console while using the package. If it displays errors this is likely to be the reason why certain activities of the package (i.e. handling changes and reporting them to moodle) stops. Although old javascript should work well on new browsers there is a chance your SCORM package uses non standard or prohibited stuff (like Flash or requests to other websites without handling these cross origin requests in a save manner). In this case you have no change without changing the SCORM package itself. If there is no error message log the SCORM API calls and view them: There are debugging capabilities implemented in moodle, see https://docs.moodle.org/403/en/SCORM_FAQ#Debugging . Or you can use a service like SCORM cloud, just upload your package, start it and view the logs afterwards. I do not think it could be a php compatibility issue since SCORM packages must not contain PHP scripts. All logic of the SCORM package has to be done at client side.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Completion Settings Both View and Status Complete
ResponsesInList.Text: That is generally what I recommend--only check completed and not view. Checking view is, yes, more work for the server but also more work for you users--they have to evaluate what the completion messages mean. And sometimes they may assume one green check means they are done when they are not. I know the messages seem clear but I have talked to many people who really don't evaluate the messages properly and get very frustrated.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Completion Settings Both View and Status Complete
ResponsesInList.Text: Does this work to remove "view" from the completion settings after having the completion settings locked and dozens of students already completing the SCORMs? From documentation, it appears it "should" work?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Completion Settings Both View and Status Complete
ResponsesInList.Text: There are two types of completion--Activity and course. If you change activity completion, it resets it for all students and should update course completion if someone wasn't getting credit but will not reset it. If you reset course completion, it will not impact activity completion at all.  What you are referring to resets activity completion.

ResponsesInList.Title: Grades Reports and Scorm
ResponsesInList.Text: I built a course with Articulate Storyline 360 My quizzes are part of the SCORM file I imported to Moodle My question is: Can I see their grades in Moodle while the quizzes are embedded in the SCORM file? If I can see the grades in Moodle while the quizzes are part of the SCORM file then how do I see them?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grades Reports and Scorm
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, with caveats. If you set it to report when creating the package. The activity will populate the grade book--make sure you choose the right grade option, Learning objects will report a 0 (incomplete) or a 1 (complete), for example. There is also a report tab if you click your scorm activity. If you click the attempt for the person you want to know about, you can find information about access, grade, complete/incomplete, etc. This does mean any information is by user, not aggregated. And it won't compare attempt 1 to attempt 2. I don't know how Rise reports but some scorm packages actually list all the questions, correct answer, how they answer, whether they got it correct, etc (nice, the only thing I think I like about Captivate) while others list the answers in string format in the details (not nice, one of few things I don't like about Lectora). You'll need to test it to find out what Rise does. If you want actual statistics about what questions were answered as a group properly, etc, don't use quizzes in scorm. Scorm will not provide that information. You're better off using Quiz if you want good metrics on how people score. You could, theoretically, set up something like a crystal report to pull data out using an ODBC driver connection to the Moodle database . That said, you need to know how to build said reports (not the easiest thing in the world) AND you have to know how all the stuff in the database connects. I've done this on the string format details and...is not fun. And even then it's pretty ugly. I'm sure it is possible to get data out the same way from packages that report stuff (like Captivate) but it would be a whole different pile of weird...And then you have to do manual assessment of data. That is a lot of work and very little reward. I don't recommend it. It was horrible the 2 times I did it (for the same thing!! Person A asked for a report. I told them it would not be pretty. They hated it, asked me to pitch the report. Then they left the project and Person B took over and could not take my word for it that it wasn't the data they wanted. I will not rant. I will not rant...).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re:  Storyline Completion options locking
ResponsesInList.Text: Regardless of whether they are Storyline or other activities , if you have activity completion set up and participants complete the activity then it is "locked" because Moodle assumes it wouldn't be fair to change the completion conditions once people have met the conditions and completed the activity. So this is expected. If you really need to change the conditions for completion you can unlock them - but is there a reason why you don't want them to be locked?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Large SCORM packages crash on Moodle 4.0.8
ResponsesInList.Text: If your upload limit is 8 gb, a 500+gb package won't go up because it is larger than the limit. The can't connect message usually means it is timing out, this suggests to me that your reported limit and package size are not accurate--otherwise, the message would be that the package exceeded the limits. When we see this problem, we upload the package directly on the server. I can't tell you how, I just know that's what happens. Another option (if it exceeds limits) is to do an FTP .

ResponsesInList.Title: Rise 360 navigation problem (some iOS devices)
ResponsesInList.Text:
We are currently experimenting with Rise 360 courses and publishing them on Moodle using SCORM packages. This works fine on most devices, but not on some of the older iOS devices and iOS devices with a smaller screen (e.g. iPhone SE 2022). This is most likely because Moodle displays the Rise 360 SCORM package inside an iframe. This generates two
scrollbars — an inner scrollbar for the Rise 360 content inside the
iframe, and an outer scrollbar for the Moodle interface ( https://community.articulate.com/discussions/rise-360/cannot-scroll-to-next-less-on-ios-mobile-in-moodle-lms ). We have been searching for a solution for this problem for quite a while now. We have been able to tweak the (HTML en CSS ) settings so far that this is not a problem for most devices. Yet some older iOS devices and devices with a smaller screen (e.g. the iPhone 2022) still have this problem. Has anyone else figured out a way to solve this problem on all devices?  And can they share there solution with us? p.s. we did find a work arround by letting the iPhone user use a two finger pinch movement to zoom in and out and simultaneously swipe the screen up, which made the button visible and usable. But this isn't as user friendy as we want our courses to be.

ResponsesInList.Text: Yes. That is correct.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Will Moodle Attempts Management Override SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Attempts in Moodle and attempts within the SCORM are different things. When you reach the end (reported complete) in Moodle, it opens up the ability to start a new attempt. So you could complete the module several times or only once, or whatever Moodle set. Most SCORM modules only have attempt settings for quiz/test elements. So the user takes the course, completes the test, and has the opportunity inside the single Moodle attempt (before closing it) to take the quiz/test again without starting a new 'attempt' in moodle... Example: I have an IT Security course. The SCORM activity in Moodle is set to unlimited attempts. The actual package has 20 questions. You have to get 80% to pass. Each question allows 3 attempts. I open the module and answer each question. If I do not take the option to retry the questions in the module and do not get 16 correct, Moodle will allow me to start a new attempt. But I don't have to take it. I could reenter the module (assuming it does not open as a review) and return to retry questions. Then Moodle will show one attempt, even though I've retried the questions. The reporting in the activity really depends on what product you use and how the product is used. I have coworkers who created modules in Captivate that allow retries. Because of how they created the modules, when you look at the individual reports, you might see each question three times because the user tried three times. This is hard to read but gets the job done. My courses built in Lectora will allow you to retry questions but Lectora coding writes over previous attempts (it probably does that because I tell it to). But Moodle will allow (if you set it) users to start new attempts and start over completely.

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle tracking problems cause - not recording to DB as Scorm cloud does
ResponsesInList.Text: I did some thorough testing and debugging trying to figure out why scorm tracking is not recorded for some users in Moodle 3.8.3.  I also compared  tracking of the same scorm 1.2 package made with Articulate Storyline 360 deployed in Scorm Cloud. What I found out is that Scorm Cloud, unlike Moodle, records scorm tracking data to it's database immediately after the content sends new data to the server . For example, when user goes from slide to slide, content sends new session time and completion status. Scorm Cloud records the data immediately to it's database but Moodle doesn't. Moodle, for some unknown reason, waits for user to exit the SCORM activity and then records the tracking data to the server. You can guess what happens if a user stays too long in a SCORM activity, especially if it is opened in a new windows (because the space for scorm content  displaying in the main Moodle window is to small and not optimized at all). Browser session can get to time out, user can run out of battery on laptop, he can switch off the PC, etc... In all those and similar cases, Moodle doesn't record at all tha scorm tracking data to it's database. Scorm Cloud does, because it records whenever the content sends anything. Is this Moodle behavior changed in newer Moodle releases? If not, what has to be changed in scorm activity mod to force Moodle to actually record tracking data on time like Scorm Cloud does?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Creating a new Activity type based on the SCORM Activity
ResponsesInList.Text: I had similar problem - couldn't upload SCORM packages because they were too big. I might have a simple solution for you: file system repository . By default, when you create SCORM activity, it actually takes more than twice of disk space actually needed. It's because you upload SCORM ZIP package and then Moodle unzips it. So you end up with zipped and unzipped version of the package taking the disk at the same time. When using file system repository, you upload SCORM ZIP to the file system repository by FTP protocol using some of the simple free FTP upload tools such as Filezilla. SCORM ZIP is outside of the course files and you can use reference to the SCORM ZIP instead of copying SCORM ZIP to the course. So, in actual course you only have unzipped version of the SCORM package. This could save you up to 50% (a little bit less actually, depending of the SCORM content) of the disk space for each SCORM activity. This is far more simple to setup than it sounds. Another, better, but more complicated solution is to setup separate content server . When you create SCORM files with Captivate, it includes content and metadata (imsmanifest. xml , xsd - xml schema definition files, etc...). You can actually simply modify the package to include metadata only and have content in another place (content server). Actually, you move content form SCORM ZIP to another dir and modify URL 's in imsmanifest.xml. Since you don't want unauthorized users to access the content, you can't just move it to another http dir, you need some kind of security. And, if it's on different domain than Moodle, than you need some kind of reverse proxy or similar solution that will solve the crossserver scripting security challenge. I hope I gave you some ideas. Have fun!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to change Display variable "to do" in scorm?
ResponsesInList.Text: You could change it through the language pack customisations. This will change it everywhere in the course, not just within SCORM activities . Site administration > Language > Language customisation. Open the language pack for editing, choose your language, then in the "Show strings of these components" selector select Course, and set the "Only strings containing" to 'to do' then press 'Show strings'. Here is what kind of headers you get if you try to access any resources related with my scorm ressources : HTTP/2 200 OK content-type: application/ xml content-length: 1174 date: Mon, 13 Jun 2022 08:17:14 GMT server: Apache last-modified: Fri, 10 Jun 2022 14:07:29 GMT etag: "496-5e118756cf58f" Am I missing something ? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External SCORM maninfest - "SecurityError: Permission denied to access property "API_1484_11" on cross-origin object"
ResponsesInList.Text: yep - SCORM uses Javascript to communicate, modern Browsers will block "cross- domain " javascript communication - that means you can't have your SCORM packages stored on one domain, and then linked to from within Moodle - it just doesn't work. The external manifest only works if you have a folder on your web server that hosts your moodle site where your scorm packages sit eg: danmarsden.com/moodle - (running your moodle site) danmarsden.com/scormfiles (with all your SCORM files.) If you want to retain control of your content and host it on a completely different domain/url to Moodle - you will need to use a different technology - LTI is quite widely used for this sort of thing. Alternatively if you like the idea of SCORM (and have some good solid existing knowledge on SCORM....) then one thing the Moodle SCORM player does support is a standard called AICC HACP - however... the resources around for implementing AICC HACP are very limited (don't ask me for help to do it...) and if you don't have that knowledge already... you'd be better upskilling on how to make your "serious game" LTI compliant.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM displaying in a new tab
ResponsesInList.Text: If pop-up blockers are the main issue - if you set the student skip content structure page setting to "no" - the pop-up window (in Moodle) is initiated on user action so pop-up blockers don't usually cause a problem. A few people have attempted to get it to load in a separate window by making changes to the code, keeping the SCORM api in the parent window, but cross-window communcation for SCORM is problematic and SCORM is fragile enough already so we end up with other intermittent issues that are really hard to diagnose - for this reason Moodle requires the SCORM api to be loaded in the same window as the SCORM package itself. Good luck!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to get AICC url after enabling?
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle allows you to add external content packages that use the AICC format inside your courses - typically these are provided by organisations that sell off-the-shelf content packages - eg health and safety/compliance courses, standalone training etc. Usually they will provide you with a mini-zip file to add into your Moodle site using the SCORM activity. The zip file basically contains an AICC config file which includes the full url to the external package. Moodle's Direct aicc URL feature just allows you to put in the url to the external provider's content package, rather than using the AICC zip file. I suspect... what you are asking for, is a way for your Moodle content to be linked to from the other LMS you mention... if that's the case, and the external LMS supports the LTI standard, then you probably want to use LTI to do this. If they don't support LTI, you should post more information here on what you're trying to do and someone may have other ideas for you to consider.

ResponsesInList.Title: Can we create a definitive troubleshooting guide together?
ResponsesInList.Text: Like many others, I'm struggling with completions not being recognised. I've trawled through lots of posts but even when success is achieved, it's hard to relate them into a consistent troubleshooting methodology. So, can we come up with a common set of things to test, or check each time we have a question. I think that would be good for users (like me ) but also be a great addition to Moodle docs and be a good place to refer to set a benchmark for enquiries here. Even better if it's then possible to map SCORM completion requirements to Moodle settings. I'm not an expert but I can kick off with some suggestions - some of these might be incorrect -  and, because I'm no expert, some questions. Suggested troubleshooting questions: Which of the following are required for your SCORM content to be classed as complete? 1. A grade 2. A minimum grade 3. Visit x number of pages 4. Visit x % of pages. What software was used to create the SCORM content? What data is passed to Moodle to indicate completion? What Moodle completion settings have you set? Do you have the definitive list of what the user must do to successfully complete the SCORM course? And if so, c an you make the SCORM "complete" in the SCORM package reports with a test Student user? Is a single user affected or multiple? If some users can achieve completion in the SCORM package and this is recognised in Moodle too: 1. Do the users have identical permissions? 2. Were the attempts you compared made at around the same time? 3. Have the Moodle completion settings been changed during the period in which the attempts were made? Is a Mastery score set? Are there multiple SCOs in the content? And some questions from me: Do the completion conditions in the code e.g. like here (ignore the issue with additions) get added to the database ? If so, would it be a big job to surface the values received in Moodle from the SCORM content in a plugin that indicates which completion settings need to be set?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can we create a definitive troubleshooting guide together?
ResponsesInList.Text: A few quick things I can add: 1) SCORM Debugging - https://docs.moodle.org/311/en/SCORM_FAQ#Debugging - Use it so you can see what your SCORM module is actually sending to Moodle. I think this actually covers your last question about showing values received in Moodle from the SCORM? 2) There are some basic troubleshooting steps here: https://docs.moodle.org/311/en/SCORM_FAQ#Basic_Troubleshooting 3) Test your SCORM module in SCORM Cloud or a service like it to check if the issue is with the SCORM module or the communication with Moodle 4) Are there potential network issues? Are learners getting network timeout alerts - see https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-66444

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can we create a definitive troubleshooting guide together?
ResponsesInList.Text: Regarding this question "4) Are there potential network issues? Are learners getting network timeout alerts - see https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-66444 I found out the hard way that Moodle issues a network connection popup warnings if the internet connection is unstable, however if the SCORM is set to launch in a new window, the users won't see the popup warning because it's in the window behind the SCORM window. So, add to the list: Is the SCORM set to launch in same window or new window? (Better to launch in same window if you want users to see the unstable internet popup warnings.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle not recording SCORM (2004) interactions
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle 3.11.3; SCORM 2004; Storyline 360 (latest). The situation can arise where Moodle does not log the interactions from the SCORM package. On real courses this can result in a learner passing the course but that not being recorded on the LMS. We have tracked instances where learners have provided evidence of passing the course (screenshot of success slide) but neither the final scores nor status was recorded in Moodle - 1st attempt score were and in some cases part of the 2nd attempt is recorded too. The issue seems to only occur if the assessment is not passed on 1st attempt. SCORM is setup to allow 2 attempts. I created a simple test quiz in Storyline 360, based on a real assessment but with fewer questions. I enabled API debugging. The API debug consistently shows all the interactions (answers) being recorded but Moodle interactions report (and user activity logs) don't. For example, failing the assessment twice, closing the module, refreshing the page and going back in from the start may result in only some or none of the answers being recorded in Moodle, despite the API debug activity logs showing them all. In this situation, the server access logs also confirm that there's no posting of the SCORM data but there are periodic calls (30 seconds) to POST /lib/ ajax /service.php?sesskey=[session]&info=core_session_touch HTTP/1.0. So something is still happening. Nothing obvious in the browser console. Anyone have any clues why this can happen and more importantly, what can be done to fix it? P.S. This seems to be similar to this but that topic is locked without a clear resolution: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=417245

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle not recording SCORM (2004) interactions
ResponsesInList.Text: According to this link https://docs.moodle.org/311/en/SCORM_FAQ#Supported_Versions SCORM 2004 is not supported in Moodle. Parts of the API have been implemented, but others such as Navigation and Sequencing have not. Development on native SCORM 2004 support in Moodle has stopped. If you require a fully certified SCORM 2004 Player in Moodle, Rustici Software have a Moodle plugin which connects to their commercial SCORM Cloud service turning Moodle into a fully compliant SCORM 2004 LMS.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle not recording SCORM (2004) interactions
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks. We only switched to 2004 recently to get the two status returns as course was looking for wrong completion status and we didn't want to lose the learner data. Turned out that replacing the SCORM lost the completion status anyhow so that had to be manually restored by recreating the results in the database . Anyhow switched back to 2.1 and see the same behaviour, indicating it's not a SCORM version issue. I also raised this on Articulate forum so rather than repeat latest status here, see this comment: https://community.articulate.com/discussions/articulate-storyline/issue-with-scorm-randomly-stopping-communicating-with-lms-moodle#reply-781915 Looks like something is going wrong between receiving an interaction and processing it. ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM Packages and Completion Activity
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi All We have an SCORM activity which needs to be updated, this is part of a set of SCORM packages used as part of course completion When we remove the old SCORM and replace will we lose any of the Activity completion? Cheers

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Packages and Completion Activity
ResponsesInList.Text: It depends on how you do it and what version you are on. I'm going to assume that you are not on a version earlier than 3.0 (I know some people are still on 2.X and some still on 1.9 YIKES!). If you are on really old versions of Moodle (pre 2.1?), the following may not be true. If you modify the package and update it in the activity (edit the activity; delete the package from the activity OR overwrite, if they have the same name; load the new one; save), new attempts will use the updates and prior completed attempts should be retained. Incomplete attempts might be problematic but you can work with that. If you delete the whole activity and create a new one, yes, all your completions will be lost and you might need to totally reset your settings. Another option is to create a new version of the course and put the new stuff there--just depends on how much change is present, use of course, blah blah blah. And then close the old one and run with the new.

ResponsesInList.Title: Ri: SCORM not showing completed in Course completion status
ResponsesInList.Text: more in depth: from the help in scorm settings->Activity completion: Require status -> "Checking one or more statuses will require a user to achieve at least one of the checked statuses in order to be marked complete in this SCORM activity, as well as any other Activity Completion requirements" please, note: "…at least one of the checked statuses in order to be marked complete". again: that is correct, speaking of SCORM objects. but in mod/scorm/classes/completion/custom_completion.php you can see: $requiredcompletionstatusid = $this->cm->customdata['customcompletionrules']['completionstatusrequired'] ?? 0; // Check at least one track meets the required completion status value(s). foreach ($tracks as $track) { if (array_key_exists($track->value, $statuses)) { $statusbits |= $statuses[$track->value]; } // All completion status requirements met. if ($statusbits == $requiredcompletionstatusid) { $status = COMPLETION_COMPLETE; break; } } as previously said, if you have checked both conditions "completed" and "passed", requiredcompletionstatusid equals to "6". but a student will never have both "completed" and "passed" tracks, therefore $statusbits will be 2 OR 4, never 6. consequently, $status will be never set to COMPLETION_COMPLETE and, well… i call it a bug. regards.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ri: SCORM not showing completed in Course completion status
ResponsesInList.Text: Does your Captivate have an actual score? If not, it cannot really say Passed. What do the reports show? What score is being pushed? If you have no quizzing elements, Learning Objects does a better job than other grades settings--it assigns a 1 (complete) or a 0 (not complete). If you do have quizzing elements in your package (not using Learning Objects), make sure what you expect to be passing matches what Captivate settings actually say--there are two areas in Captivate to pay attention to: First: You have to enable reporting. You have to tell Captivate you use Moodle. You are better off publishing in SCORM 1.2 as Moodle is not 2004 compliant. 2004 mods will run but may not behave as expected. And sometimes it does not report. You choose if you use slide views or a quiz. If you choose quiz but there are no questions, it will publish but may not actually mark completed/passed properly. If you choose both and there are no questions, it may not mark completed. If you choose 100% slide views and there are any slides the user might skip (including results pages or an end page with help stuff or something), it will not mark completed. And...do you include interaction data? This can help track. The default is generally 80%. If you have a quiz, you have to make sure your passing percentage is consistent with what you actually expect. Grade to pass in Moodle (if used) should recognize Captivate scoring, which is weird. Captivate tends to automatically assign 10 points per graded question. 28 questions=280 pt. Multi-answer questions do get partial credit. If the student does not get exactly 80%, they don't get passing, 79.96%, nope, did not pass, no rounding but in Moodle, the score might look like a pass. Captivate is stupid complicated. The more stuff you put in it, the more room you have for weird behavior.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to find SCORM conditions?
ResponsesInList.Text: If you edit the activity, and look at the Activity Completion section, you can see Moodle settings. If you go to reports for the module and look at interactions data for both someone who is complete and someone who is not, it can help figure out what is missing. In the module itself, finding specifics for a package you cannot access the source file for...that is not going to be easy. In some cases, maybe not possible. You might ask some more questions. Were they on a stable internet connection when they completed? If not, reporting may have not happened. If a SCORM loses connection to Moodle, it stops reporting and does not reestablish the connection--it has to be closed and reopened. Are they using a mobile device? SCORM modules may not report if a mobile device is used on a phone or tablet--but using Moodle Mobile app can help. What version of Moodle do you run? What browser are they using? All these questions can help identify what might be going on.

ResponsesInList.Title: When Should 'Force Completed' Be Used
ResponsesInList.Text: Using Moodle 3.10.  Trying to troubleshoot ongoing SCORM completion issues.  When should 'Force Completed' be used?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: When Should 'Force Completed' Be Used
ResponsesInList.Text: We haven't used this option much but from what I understand of it, it will mark a SCORM as complete as soon as an attempt is started, no matter what the learner did inside of it. Most of the issues we've ran into with SCORM completion tracking not showing up properly was due to the module not always reporting status properly to Moodle. We used the "Auto commit" option to help make sure the package communicates at least once every 60 seconds. From https://docs.moodle.org/310/en/SCORM_settings#Compatibility_settings: Force completed If this is enabled then the status of the current attempt is set to "complete". Note that this only applies to SCORM 1.2 packages and is useful if the SCORM package does not handle revisiting an attempt correctly, in review or browse mode, or otherwise incorrectly issues the completion status. Auto commit Some SCORM packages don't explicitly call Commit() regularly for whatever reason so progress is not stored in the database . This patch will Commit() the data from the SCORM package 60 seconds after the values are set, unless the package Commit()s sooner.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM - Multiple Attempts
ResponsesInList.Text: Are you talking about a second attempt inside the module or inside of Moodle? You can create a SCORM which allows a second attempt within the same moodle attempt AND you can tell Moodle to allow a second attempt. If the user has a second attempt in Moodle, it creates a second entry. The first attempt must be marked complete for a second attempt option to trigger (as it puts out a check box to start new) unless you force completion (I never do so, I'm guessing that's what force completion does--my modules are longer, I don't want to make my users insane, so I don't make them start over every time, they complete in their own time). If the second attempt is inside the module (failed the quiz, clicked a button to try again without closing the module, retook quiz, passed), it may overwrite the original score and activity tracking. Or it may not. It depends on the product and the settings. I think in Captivate, it generally retains all the activity, though, I'm sure there is a way to clear the score while in Lectora, you can wipe out the entire score and start over. It depends on the product and your particular settings.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Session time and total time from Articulate Storyline content
ResponsesInList.Text: I did a test today to compare how the same Articulate Storyline package functions in Scorm Cloud (cloud.scorm.com). I noticed that the Scorm Cloud updates total time each time the content sets session_time. In other words, unlike Moodle, it doesn't wait for LMSfinish() to update total time, so if LMSfinish is never called, Scorm Cloud would save total time anyway and Moodle would not. Does anyone have an idea how to force Moodle to update SCORM total time more often, for example each time a content calls LMSSetValue for cmi.core.session_time?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Session time and total time from Articulate Storyline content
ResponsesInList.Text: The Articulate content often sends cmi.core.session_time to the Moodle. That's some kind of temporary value because we don't know if the user finished his SCORM session or not. When SCORM session ends, Moodle reads the last cmi.core.session_time recieved from the SCORM in that session and adds that to the cmi.core.total_time in the database. Each SCORM package (and each SCO) has it's own cmi.core.total_time. The problem is that sometimes a user doesn't close the browser window or the content window and just closes the laptop. Laptop goes to sleep but html session doesn't end so Moodle doesn't recieve the info that the user finished the SCORM. When the user turns the laptop on again wakeing it from the sleep, html session is already gone and Moodle never gets the info that user's SCORM session ended so it never adds cmi.core.session_time to the cmi.core.total_time. The solution would be that the Moodle adds first cmi.core.session_time to cmi.core.total_time when SCORM sends the cmi.core.session_time for the first time in the session. Later, for each subsequent cmi.core.session_time recieved from the content, the Moodle would have to calculate the difference between this one and the previous cmi.core.session_time received in the same SCORM session and add that difference to the cmi.core.total_time. So, cmi.core.total_time would be updated correctly each time the content sends the new cmi.core.session_time. If the user doesn't close the content window or the browser window and the Moodle never receives the info that SCORM session ended, cmi.core.session_time is still recorded in the database using all cmi.core.session_time values received from the content during that SCORM session. I'm not sure if some kind of solution can be done from the content side also, but I doubt it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM - Best tool to import word & powerpoint
ResponsesInList.Text: It really depends on what you are trying to do. SCORM may not be what you want. or it may only be part of what you want. Most authoring tools won't import anything from word. Lectora does a pretty good job gathering PPT but does require some clean-up. I have heard Storyline/Articulate deals with PPT well, also. I would not encourage Captivate as the imports essentially create images (not accessible) and to edit or change, it is a serious pain. Moodle can host ppt and word files. The question is what you want to do with them. If you want to track use, Moodle will report whether the doc has been opened. It can't track if someone actually read it, obviously. But you could put data from word into a Book and then embed H5P questions to test for comprehension. Or use lessons the same way. If you are not already using an authoring software, you might try to figure out what you want to use the LMS for and what it can do before buying software. SCORM is kind of old tech, if you can avoid it, you might try. And this is coming from someone who uses/creates SCORM all the time.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM - Best tool to import word & powerpoint
ResponsesInList.Text: Like Melanie said, it depends on your end goal. Generally its better to save MS Office files in a format that is natively supported by browsers (e.g. PDFs, video, audio etc). Viewing Office files in Moodle requires downloading them and opening the appropriate application whereas PDFs, videos and audio files are displayed by the browser and require no additional applications. For Word files you can save them as PDFs to preserve all the formatting and fonts and tend to be much smaller For PowerPoint slides it depends: if there are no animations, narrations or embedded multimedia you can save them as PDF. if there are animations, narrations or embedded multimedia, you can can export them as video. I use iSpring Suite for creating SCORM packages as it is a plugin for PowerPoint and it supports virtually all the animations and features and is very easy to use. Just my 2 cents.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I noticed that Moodle takes a zipped SCORM package and breaks it into pieces when putting it into the moodledata folder. Why not maintain the original file structure? Also does Moodle inject and code or make any modification to any of the uploaded files?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Does Moodle modify the SCORM packages in any way?
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle doesn't inject or modify any of the SCORM files. SCORM packages have to be unzipped before being served to the browser. Moodle stores file path/structure information in the database rather than on the file system (for all files - not just SCORM) - If you have the same file/scorm in multiple courses it only stores one copy "on disk" - decreasing the amount of files stored on disk, but this design also enables Moodle to take advantage of cheaper cloud storage solutions like Amazons S3/Object storage - there should be a few similar posts in the forums if you search generically for where files are stored by Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Data tracking with scorm 1.2
ResponsesInList.Text: Videos are not, by default scorm, if you are actually talking about a video. You don't typically click on a video...so. If you're talking about a scorm that plays like a video but is actually a series of slides that auto-forward at certain places (which would not require a next button), when you build your scorm module, you could create an action sequence that counts the number click (onclick add '1' to variableA). But how you do this depends entirely on the authoring tool and navigational options you use. And how that data reports to Moodle also depends on the authoring tool. In general, a lot of scorm data reports in strings all in the same field, meaning you would probably have to mine it out (no fun) or find a way to auto mail data from some point in the scorm.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Data tracking with scorm 1.2
ResponsesInList.Text: In fact, I created an html scorm package. I have javascript which retrieves the interactions on the video. So I have several variables (the number of clicks on this video) to send to the LMS. What I don't know is how to save these variables in the LMS.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Data tracking with scorm 1.2
ResponsesInList.Text: You don't set the variables in the lms, you create the variables in the scorm package and when the events trigger, they report to the LMS. Getting variables in your package is usually the easy part. Reading the stored data is the complicated bit. It might be that you need on on exit variable that when the package closes, the number of clicks is updated. Make the variable names really obvious, easy to see. The data is stored by user in the activity. As seen below...there is a Reports tab that shows attempts by user. If you click on the attempt number, you can access more data per user. This is one example from a scorm built in Lectora--there are questions in the content but no formal quiz. If a quiz was present, each question, represented by a variable, would appear in the cmi.suspend.data area with the selected answer (it may be possible to change how this reports but I haven't really attempted it). You can see VarFedprotect=3 in the screen that is the name of the question (Fedprotect) and the answer given (3), preceded by Var to indicate it is reporting a variable. This is an example of Captivate results, which include all of the above data as well as any questions included, quiz or not. If you have several questions, this can go on for some time...the course this comes from has 15 questions, so there are 15 entries with the same pattern of data. And...if the question can be answered more than once, unless you have an action in the module to totally clear the data, it will display all attempts for each question.  This can be hard to follow. The cmi.suspend_data field is longer and less readable in Captivate modules. If you want to know where the data gets saved, you can go to the background moodle database and look for the many mdl_scorm...tables. What program you use to build the scorm and what you tell it to do (Lectora has very granular control, Captivate does not--I can't change what it reports, others are more or less depending on skill and program) will determine what the reports look like.
