So I still have to do an extra step of downloading the users from bulk user download, then filtering them in excel according to institution, then sorting them by userid to see what their highest and lowest userid numbers are. Then using the scorm report in excel, I can filter by userid as a number range from the lowest to the highest and that gives me the same result. It's only working because the users in each institution were all uploaded at the same time in sequence, so their userids are all in sequence. I'll have to be careful to make sure there are no breaks in that sequence (eg - if users were uploaded at different times with users from other institutions added between them). I'm just using a calculation to check that there are no gaps in the userid sequence: highest userid - lowest userid = number of userids. If it's not, then I have to do multiple filters in excel. Maybe if I run into that problem too many times or it's too much of a mess I could bulk reassign all the userids for that institution so they are in sequence. I hope this solution helps you or others: maybe your users of the same groups are also in userid sequence (or you could achieve this by bulk operation). Hopefully someone will figure out how to add a group or institution column one day and post the solution here. In the meantime, let me know if you want me to share the code changes that I made to add the userid column.

The agency examines the results to give us feedback on what should be improved, or what needs further training, or which topics are understood by employees. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Which user data is sent from Moodle through a SCORM activity?
ResponsesInList.Text: So...this response is really guesswork... I have not been in a similar situation but build scorm stuff and have for a long time in several types of software, so I have some ideas as to what is happening. I think it depends a lot on what type of authoring software is being used and how it is set up. If they are doing what I suspect they are, when a score is submitted, an email gets sent with data, most likely not anonymized. Then the data is collated for evaluation. Lectora creators have more granular control over, well, everything. I don't have a copy these days, so can't confirm but I think this control may extend to how/what results get sent. I doubt they are using Camtasia to do this. Captivate allows less granular control and is just send it or not, there may be ways to choose to anonymize but I don't see them. If the module is built in captivate and you run it in your moodle, you could pull the scores out ( sql report) yourself and evaluate because it actually breaks results down by question (which is most likely the base of any game). If it is built in Lectora, this is a bit trickier because the reporting comes through in a data string separated by semi-colons (there may be away to change this but I don't know it). I can't speak to any others (other than Camtasia reporting is pretty ugly). There are probably ways to select variables and put them in an email with no student data for most softwares at all but they are probably more work. I could probably do it in Captivate but thinking about it makes my eye twitch and gives me a bit of a headache (so I'm not going to). A shorter answer would be: Your best bet is probably to ask them what they do, what the data they get looks like. You could ask that the data be sent to you instead of them. You could ask that they do something to ensure data privacy.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: failure in documentation within moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Scorm is a particular piece of code which has specific rules governing completion, and much of this is done when the scorm object is created. It is entirely possible that you've got a scorm object which requires all pages to be viewed before completion is reported to Moodle, but you've also got it allowing users to skip pages in the navigation. In such a case a user will only complete if they view all pages, but could also achieve a score from the scorm object of 100% and still not be reported as complete, if they can skip ahead to the 'test' section in the scorm. When testing, try to skip pages, or fail to open some hot spots (or reveals... whatever you like to call them), and see if you get a score... AND a completed status. Try turning on the scorm debug mode in the site administration, and setting your username as the only person who sees it. When you then access a scorm object a new window will pop open - it's the scorm API showing you exactly what is written back to Moodle and what isn't. But to answer your other point, yes, it is entirely possible that a network glitch is happening. It is also possible for you to open the scorm object on the same page as the moodle course, or in a new window. It can make a difference as to which you choose... BUT, if your scorm object is created to ALSO open in a new window, you'll get two pop ups appearing. If your users don't like the 'clutter' on their page, and decide to close the one without the content, then all progress will NOT be reported to moodle - this is the scorm player window and must remain open. Try using moodle to not open in a new window and see if the scorm pops out in a new window anyway - if it does then the scorm has been authored to do so, and can only be changed by re-authoring the scorm.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adding New SCORM to Existing Course
ResponsesInList.Text: You could put 'new' students in a group and hide (using activity restrictions) old activities from anyone in that group and hide new activities from anyone not in that group. Then there's no confusion about what they should do. Do you have ways to mark the 'new' students complete? I've got a course where 30 or so students completed the original 5 modules and then we 'replaced' them from a curriculum perspective with 9 or 10 new ones. I placed the original 30 students in a group and placed view restrictions on the original modules (must be in that group). The new modules got view restrictions for anyone not in the group. The activity following these modules required all 5 modules be complete. I modified the restriction to be must complete original 5 OR new series. It takes some time and coordination but can help.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle SCORM to NHS's ESR
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle is a "SCORM Player" - so you can upload SCORM packages and get it to play the scorm files and record progress from your users. You need 2 things for this to work. 1) allow your users to authenticate to Moodle - and store in Moodle something specific for that user that is also in your ESR system (employee number/email address or something that ESR "understands" 2) Export completion or grade to your ESR system using one of the existing plugins. But - before then you'll need to install moodle... my experience with organisations in the public health sector is that you are often under-staffed/ IT resources stretched - so it's incredibly important to partner with someone else to provide your Moodle hosting and regular updates to the latest version - someone needs to be patching that site every 2 months (or more often) and scheduling in yearly or bi-yearly major upgrades. Recently modern web browsers (chrome / firefox etc) made a number of changes that "Broke SCORM" in Moodle and we updated Moodle to fix it, but a lot of organisations running their own site (installed by someone who has since left the organisation) and unable to upgrade to the recent supported release is quite high and you'll see a few of these people in the forums complaining about SCORM not working in their sites. I'd highly reccomend you find a local Moodle partner and ask them to help with setting up your Moodle site - they will also be able to help you connect Moodle to your ESR system so you can pull accross your user completions/grades.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM grade not recorded
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, We are facing the exact same problem but apparently only for iOS devices, so iPads and iPhones. From as far as I've tested using Browserstack, this has been happening since iOS Safari 10, and it's now already on 13... so this is not exactly new. Though most of the complaints I've found on this particular issue on other LMLs, some of them Moodle-based, seem to have started around February or March 2020, so I don't know why this discrepancy... Regardless, from previous Googling it seems like more and more people have been suffering from this but there is yet no fix on Moodle's side, but I did read somewhere that the Rustici engine (i.e. what powers the SCORM player on Moodle) already has an update for this and I can confirm it, since I tested our SCORM files over at SCORM Cloud and indeed the progress is properly recorded when leaving the SCORM player there. Someone somewhere suggested turning on the auto-commit setting, but this didn't work for us... I don't know if it just doesn't work or if something needs to be done/enabled on our SCORM files. Oh, speaking of which, our SCORM courses were built on both Captivate 8 and 2019 and for both the progress is never saved, so it's really not a SCORM issue, it should really be on the SCORM player itself somewhere... From debugging on the browser side, I've seen that, when exiting the SCORM player on Moodle, any other browser sends 3 requests to /mod/scorm/datamodel.php with data relative to the user's progress during that session, but this does NOT happen when on Safari for iOS. These requests are simply not made on iOS, which would explain why the user's progress is not saved. Something I've noticed that also only seems to happen on iOS is a bunch of requests to the same file but which apparently doesn't exist. Since I've only seen this happening on iOS, I'm assuming Safari is somehow incorrectly building the path of the file it's trying to get and ends up asking for a file that doesn't actually exist. I don't know if this is somehow related to the saving issue or not... I thought this would be something that was already solved in more recent versions of Moodle, but I checked the git logs over at https://github.com/moodle/moodle , both on the master branch and on the Moodle 3.8 branch, and found nothing regarding this 🙁. I even thought maybe I missed something, so I made a clean basic installation of Moodle 3.8 and uploaded one of our SCORM courses, but alas, the exact same result. To me this clearly means that is something that has not yet been addressed and I have sadly not yet seen it reported anywhere moodle-specific. At least not in these terms. I just made a quick search through the Moodle issue tracker and the results were disappointing... The closest I found was https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-66545 and it was tagged as minor priority issue back in August/September 2019. Does anyone know of a way to get the devs' attention to this issue? Or any other helpful resource to go to? If this doesn't get addressed I'll be forced to put up a notice saying that our courses are simply not available on iOS. Or at least that users can try them but that their progress will not be saved not will they be able to complete them...

Hello Everyone; I have found a fix for problems in Chrome (Just like ali niciejewski ) and Safari. I just tested it on Safari, using SCORM 1.2 and Captivate and it appears to work. (Although I only completed a short course as the test) It has to do with a browser setting that does not allow an exchange of information between the server and the browser. The new browser settings blocked this exchange of information  by default. The link is below. It has screen shots so it shows specifically what you need to do for both Chrome and Safari. https://sisupport.freshdesk.com/support/solutions/articles/43000577639-trouble-completing-course A bit more information for those who are interested. SCORM sends the data to the server by Javascript , its not a problem with SCORM its a problem with the new default settings of these two browsers disallowing this XHR API. Simply uncheck the box and it works. XMLHttpRequest ( XHR ) is an API in the
form of an object whose methods transfer data between a web browser and
a web server. The object is provided by the browser's JavaScript environment.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Grades
ResponsesInList.Text: So, first, SCORM 1.2 is recommended for Moodle. Moodle does not support 2004. It has been some time since I did anything with iSpring...but back when I did (there was a free version, not the full suite), sometimes reporting was spotty. Are you using the full suite? You might check their directions, I know they've got a users manual on line. If your system has a timeout, your users may be getting timed out before they are done and then the score isn't reported. That is a massive pain. I get that timeouts are important for security but they interfere with SCORM reporting. I'm not an articulate person but your screen print looks like it shows a required number of slides, not a required score. And your Moodle info does not seem to have any requirements set. It might not be sure what to mark. Make sure you know whether it shows passed/failed or completed/incomplete--this is important as what the module reports must match your requirements. yours is passed/failed, so you want to require passed...but make sure it says what it is actually looking for. That max score tells you that that is the maximum possible score, not that it is the requirement. I make it a point to test the modules with student accounts many times before I make courses live (that doesn't prevent weird glitches, but it does reduce them).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Updating SCORM - content refuses to load for existing incomplete / completed attempts
ResponsesInList.Text: I suspect the problem is that the updated package has a slightly different structure than the original. If the update is exactly the same (number of pages, number of questions, stuff like that) and only content has changed there shouldn't be a problem BUT if you add a page or question or something track-worthy, it does not compute. and the existing attempt cannot open because nothing lines up. If the person is going back in, maybe they should start a new attempt. The problem probably isn't Moodle, it is most likely your package. Take a look at the original zip folder and compare it to what the new one looks like. I'd bet the structure is different is some relevant way. SCORM is considered old and broke, extreme old age--even SCORM people would be happy to see it phased out entirely and replaced with something else (H5P is the new hotness but has some pretty major...defects is the wrong word...things missing, that make it not quite up to replacing SCORM (tracking, they're looking at it)...but the e-learning world is changing and SCORM may be a thing of the past soon. ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM: Continue where left off and record grades?
ResponsesInList.Text: Afternoon, all, hope you're all doing well and keeping safe. My team and I have a possible project coming soon, the short of it is that it's a small SCORM with some activities and quizzes in it. One of the requirements is that a participant can stop and resume at their convenience without having to start back from the beginning, essentially where they left off. We are using Articulate Storyline 3 for this which is giving us great results so far. Problem is, we've have an issue with how grades are recorded whenever a user resumes their attempt, namely, it does not record any newer grades. I've been lurking through these forums before posting and it seems that it's a matter of the SCORM activity going into review mode after resuming an attempt, instead of the usual mode. We've tried to disable it unsuccessfully. Grades are recorded correctly when the user completes the activity in one go but not in various sessions, it seems. Right now this is our biggest issue to overcome as the completion of the overall package, when done in one sitting, is working correctly. Any input is appreciated.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM: Continue where left off and record grades?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Marco I agree that the likely issue here is that Review Mode is being tripped. When the SCORM activity opens as a New Window you should see 'Review' displayed in the top left corner if this is occurring. Note Review Mode will trigger when the Completion Status reaches Completed regardless of whether Passed or Failed. I am assuming you are tracking based on a quiz result slide (and not number of slides viewed)? Assuming it is on a quiz slide, if: Publish as SCORM 2004 (preferably 4th edition). Set tracking to Passed/Failed. In Moodle set Mastery Score to No and Force Complete also set to No. Set Activity Completion to When Conditions are met, must view and passed. With these settings - resume state, success status and raw score should work for uses re-entering prior to reaching the result slide. If a user attempts the quiz and fails, and gets as far as the result slide - this will trigger review mode. This is because the Completion status is updated to Complete (when exit after having got beyond the start of timeline on the result slide), even though the Success Status is Failed. Once Review Mode is triggered Success Status and Score can not be updated. To reattempt users would need to check the 'Start a new attempt' check box on the Entry page. (Entry page will only show if launching in a new window and if entry page to checked under Appearance settings) If you included a Retry button on your Result slide - it's important to understand the retry results will only pass back if the course has not been completed i.e. previously existed. If this the scenario you are trying to avoid, consider publishing as SCORM 2004 (preferably 4th edition), Set tracking to Passed/Incomplete. (all other settings as above) Now if a user fails quiz and exits, it won't trigger Review Mode (because completion status will be Incomplete, and success status Failed). In this case a user will be able to resume the package and retry the quiz (you will need to include either the Retry button on the result slide or custom build triggers to reset the quiz try). If they then pass, their new results will be tracked in Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Chrome change affecting remotely hosted SCORM/AICC?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi folks, Some of our clients use services from vendors like OpenSesame that provide SCORM or AICC packages that point to remotely hosted content. In this arrangement, the bulk of the content is on the external vendors' servers, and Moodle just hosts a "light" SCORM or AICC package to report completion and interactions from the external site to the LMS. (This allows the content vendors to keep control of their content. They charge a subscription fee for continued access to the content.) We received a message from OpenSesame indicating that an impending change in Chrome will affect the functionality of these remotely hosted packages. The message is pasted in below; it gives the technical details and indicates that OpenSesame is taking steps to address the issue on their side. My question for the community here is whether there might be any changes needed in the SCORM/AICC module for those of us who want to support this remote-hosted content use case. I'm not requesting that Moodle make this change (if there is one), necessarily; I'm just curious as to whether there's anything that might be done on the LMS side. Thanks for your help. All the best, Andy Hicken Message from OpenSesame: The OpenSesame partner team wants to alert you of an important
browser update which may impact course tracking on LMS platforms. The upcoming
release of the Google Chrome browser (Release 78) scheduled for release on 22
October contains a significant change which may impact course tracking in the
OpenSesame player and LMS platforms. Because
of the potential impact on our mutual customers, we ask that you reply to
this email by 9 October and notify us what your team is doing to prepare for
this change . We plan to communicate to customers later this week and
anticipate questions in response to the Chrome release. Chrome 78 release on 22 October The
new Chrome release scheduled to come out on 22 October will disallow posts to
external URLs to happen when the browser is closing or navigating away. As a
result, courses which are authored to be marked complete on-exit or post data
to an external URL (most likely to be AICC in the browser or remote hosted
SCORM) may no longer register as complete. In addition, learners’ progression through courses might not be saved. After
this release, learning management systems, particularly those recording
completion on exit, may fail to receive completions under Chrome. More
information, including Google’s recommendations for a fix can be found here: https://developers.google.com/web/updates/2019/09/chrome-78-deps-rems . Please see the section “Disallow sync
XHR in page dismissal”. The quickest change is likely replacing your POST or
GET requests with a FETCH having the keepAlive=true set. You can test using
Chrome 78 by downloading it here: https://www.google.com/chrome/canary/ . OpenSesame
is patching our system in advance of the release. We appreciate your prompt
attention to this important matter. If you have any questions, please contact
your OpenSesame Partner Manager.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Passing custom variable to LMS.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Manisha, Instead of the JavaScript solution, I would use triggers to pass the required points or custom information into 'hidden' SL quiz slides. The 'hidden' quiz slides are simply SL graded quiz slides, however, instead of letting the user submit an answer, you set the answer to be submitted to a variable valuable on the timeline start. You can 'hide' what you are doing by simply: unticking the Submit button and replacing with a Next button; formatting other content over the quiz interaction; and/or setting the slide timeline to 0.1 sec and adding jump to next slide on timeline end. Make sure you link the 'hidden' quiz slides to the results slide so that the information gets passed by to your LMS. I have had good success using this solution with our Moodle LMS. Cheers Christine

ResponsesInList.Title: Issue with SCORM's hanging
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I am having more and more people come back to me with a particular problem and need to know if anybody has run into this before and what the potential fix is. We author our SCORM's using Articulate Studio 13 and host them using Moodle 3.8.  When a user returns to a module, a box will pop up asking them if they want to resume where they left off.  Some people can't get past their screen by clicking 'yes' or 'no'.  I have to go in and reset their attempt in as an admin. Another issue they have is at times, when they go back into a module, they just get the spinning wheel like the course material is loading.  Same as above, I have to go in and reset the attempt.  I also ask them to clear their browser cache which at times seems like it fixes the issue. Any thoughts on where to go with this?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Issue with SCORM's hanging
ResponsesInList.Text: I wonder if the suspend_data field is being truncated somewhere. SCORM 1.2 spec states suspend_data is quite small - We have a "SCORM standards mode" - go to admin > plugins > activities > SCORM and untick that box if you haven't already - that will allow Moodle to "violate" the spec and store pretty much whatever is sent from the package. If that's already unticked, or unticking doesn't help - your SCORM package JS might be truncating it too and causing it to be unreadable when the user re-enters. I'd take a look at the users that have this issue and check their suspend_data field to see how large it is. If they are all suspciously close to 4096 characters then it's probably being limited/truncated somewhere which is causing it to become corrupt. If that's not it... hopefully your post in the articulate forums shows something up!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Issue with SCORM's hanging
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey Dan, I've asked for some help at the Articulate forum but nothing yet. I had a look at the SCORM Standard Mode and the box was already unticked. Ages ago, on an older Moodle install (2.4), I remember having to increase the size of 'something' regarding SCORM data.  Is that what you were eluding to with you said about the 4096 characters? I wonder why clearing browser cache fixed the issue for some and not others but when I clear their attempt, they can get back in. Any thoughts? Many thanks! Dave

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Issue with SCORM's hanging
ResponsesInList.Text: yeah - that tickbox extends the 4096 char limit in Moodle - but some SCORM packages will still have their own code that truncates that before it hits Moodle. I have seen some packages store progress data in cookies which is why clearing the browser cache might help, but others will be storing it in the "suspend_data" field and something must be corrupting that somehow.

It will look like the module is complete to the user but it will not report the completion because the connection has been broken. Storyline/Articulate has a pretty good rep. I haven't used it but they have a great community. I use their community for ideas, even if I don't use their product. Rumor has it they are/can be responsive.  Some of their stuff actually works with powerpoint, looks cool. I think they are less expensive than Lectora, more expensive than Captivate (though Captivate is getting pricier). Everything I've heard is they are really easy to use. I've used other SCORM stuff, like iSpring(freeware) and eXe (now eXeLearning?--this was a long time ago, used to be in core...ish) and Camtasia. For SCORM, not especially impressed, but Camtasia has improved. Still not awesome, has some weird things, but functions. I'd only use Camtasia if you plan to do a lot of video based stuff and need reporting. If you don't need reporting, H5P does some really cool stuff with video and can interact with YouTube. If you use interactive video with YouTube, you lose the YouTube captioning, if that matters to you. Addressing what Dan was talking about...yeah, SCORM is old. They've been saying SCORM was dying for as long as I've been using it...unlike flash, it seems to still be running around and functional. There are some upsides to SCORM, but also downsides. If you are not interested in documenting results, H5P is terrific. It has so many cool features. But reporting is not good. SCORM reporting is decent, unless your user has an unstable internet connection OR times out, then it gets frustrating. H5P can't really do software assessment; other than just video demo, it wouldn't be great for tutorials. I think about trying to do something like that for a minute or two, my brain starts bleeding, I stop. But it does have some super cool branching options and, other than poor reporting and no software assessment, definitely worth it, if you don't need reporting. Reporting is why I use SCORM. Figure out what you really want/need. Choose your tool based on that. I'm keeping my eye on H5P because I really want to love it. They're talking about making the score interface better with Moodle...when that happens, I'll re-evaluate.

ResponsesInList.Title: Ri: Re: Ri: Re: Best solution for responsive SCORMs in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Melanie, very useful guidelines. We don't have use cases using special features (like software tutorials needs), for now. Text, images, some multiple choice test. And some navigation logic, maybe. We could implement them using standard editing moodle functions, but we potentially have a great number of "pages" to build and maintain. So, we are considering an external authoring tool for faster and easier editing. Reporting could be an issue, but is not a fundamental feature.  "Poor" reporting  could not be a problem, "totally absent", could.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ri: Re: Ri: Re: Best solution for responsive SCORMs in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: If you haven't started using a SCORM tool yet, the learning curve can be steep. If you have a multiple choice test, I would build that directly in Moodle vs. the SCORM content using the delivered, core Moodle reporting. Less headaches around. So, if I was going to use the Moodle quiz activity, I would just build the content in native Moodle activities . External authoring tool is not necessarily faster and easier to edit. Read down through this Forum's threads to get a full picture of other problems with SCORM.

ResponsesInList.Title: Ri: Re: Ri: Re: Ri: Re: Best solution for responsive SCORMs in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks. We will consider using pure Moodle solutions, too.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ri: Re: Ri: Re: Best solution for responsive SCORMs in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: I agree with Shirley. I would always prefer a Moodle quiz to anything built in SCORM. So much flexibility, excellent reporting. If the only reason to use SCORM is to get something pretty...go for H5P and use quiz for testing. As I mentioned, we use it for a lot of software tutorial stuff...but we're trying to find ways to get away from it...which is why I am aware of the ups and downs of H5P.  H5P lets you set backgrounds, switch between, add all sorts of stuff. Super functional.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Best solution for responsive SCORMs in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Andrea, ADAPT is a truly responsive authoring tool, based totally on HTML5. But regarding effort, I guess at the beginning it is not easy. There is the authoring tool you can install in your server , but the learning curve is steep. There are a bunch of ADAPT developers that can help, though.

ResponsesInList.Title: Ri: Re: Best solution for responsive SCORMs in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Beatriz

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ri: Re: Best solution for responsive SCORMs in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: ADAPT is a great tool, but I also want to note it's not going to help in dealing with some of the issues you may run into with SCORM, particularly in terms of mobile device intermittent connectivity. SCORM assumes an uninterrupted internet connection, so unless you are using the Moodle app to have offline data handling, you'll run into issues with intermittent wireless connectivity. Take a look at https://h5p.org/presentation if your requirements for the learning modules aren't complex in terms of variables and other things.

ResponsesInList.Title: Ri: Re: Ri: Re: Best solution for responsive SCORMs in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, thanks to this point. It seems another important aspect.

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle webservice API to update scorm settings
ResponsesInList.Text: AS per our requirements, we need to support multiple attempts.  I know we can set "Force new attempt" to true to achieve this. But this global setting will work only for SCORM contents which are uploaded after doing this setting. We need to perform bulk update for all prior existing SCORM contents. Question: 1) Is there any API to do this? 2) Also, I see these settings are maintained in Moodle DB. Is it safe to update the "forcenewattempt" column to achieve this? Will there be any side-effect of doing this DB operation? Thanks in advance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle webservice API to update scorm settings
ResponsesInList.Text: Force new attempt forces every attempt to be new is set to always, forces new attempts if a previous is finished (based on your reporting criteria) or not at all...just allows them to choose if complete...but that isn't what allows multiple attempts. The setting above that says number of attempts (options 1-6 and unlimited) and this is what allows multiple attempts. It is pretty clear you are looking at the database end--not sure where those options show up there--but they are available in the activity settings.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: reducing mdl_scorm_scoes_track size  without causing issues
ResponsesInList.Text: Ideally we'd need to get MDL-46279 addressed which would go a long way to helping manage this data, but in the meantime I tend to delete old interactions data from our larger sites - interactions data contains the questions/answers to the quizzes within an attempt, but not the final score. Here's a query I use: delete from mdl_scorm_scoes_track where element like 'cmi.interactions%' and timemodified < 1577836800 The timemodified part there is a unix timestamp - that one I've included is for January 1, 2020 12:00:00 AM - so it will only delete the interactions data for attempts older than that date. I find this site helps when trying to calculate a timestamp: https://www.epochconverter.com/ make sure you test it before you run it on your production site though!

ResponsesInList.Title: Best practice for updating / replacing SCORM packages without losing learner progress?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, We have a number of trainings that require some corrections and content updates. These courses were built in Storyline, and are susceptible to having their IDs changed when making changes. We don't want learners to restart these courses to get back to their current slide. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Best practice for updating / replacing SCORM packages without losing learner progress?
ResponsesInList.Text: Updating SCORM content to allow for students to retain progress depends if the IMSmanifest file has changed from the original publishing. If you overwrote the original file without changing the file name/structure it is possible that the imsmanifest file did not change and your student's progress will be retained. Moodle and/or a plugin does not change the imsmanifest file. Save a run of the student's current activities status for a single course. Backup the course within Moodle. Make the changes to the content, do not change the file name or structure. Changing the name, such as; Math 101 V1.0 to Math 101 V1.1 will be a problem. Replace the current content with the updated content. Run the activities status report. See if they match. If not, restore the original course.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Video Tracking SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: I didn't see the original post...but yes... If you have something that publishes to scorm, you can put the video in the software and publish it. For example, Camtasia. If you want a reported 'complete' type score, you have to have at least 1 question in the module (at the end: I'm done T/F). Camtasia is pretty inexpensive--$250 or $275 bundled  with SnagIt; $169 if you qualify for the educator discount. It is relatively easy to use and can be set up to be interactive video, if your video is very long (5 minutes of video, question, 5 minutes of video, question, etc. Newer versions remember where the user left off (which was an issue in older versions). and, it gives you some options for fiddling with the video (like zooming in to a specific place for emphasis, etc.  You can put a video in, break it into pieces, stick ppt (or manually generated) slides in between sections and have a hybrid. For what you get, it is worth it. If you care about accessibility and you have a captions file for the video (srt file type, there are free converters on line if your captions are vtt or some other caption type), you can import captions and have closed or burned in captions for accessibility when publishing.. And if you don't have a captions file but have a Zoom pro account, you can start a session, start recording (to the cloud, which is why it has to be a pro account) , play the video through and then Zoom will give you a transcript. I've found it is about 75-85% accurate, depending on the video. If the sound is really good, the speaker speaks very clearly, does not use a lot of acronyms or lingo (and not chipmunk fast), the accuracy increases.  My videos always have lingo and acronyms and techie terms, so it's possible accuracy is better than what I see for less techie populations. The transcript downloads as a vtt, which I convert to srt and then drop into Camtasia. You can correct the 15%-25% errors in line in Zoom before you download as well, or in Camtasia. And...if it sounds like I'm having a love affair with camtasia...eek! sorry.  You can do the same with Captivate and Lectora. Captivate is much more complicated to caption (so complicated and time consuming), I avoid it for this purpose if I can. Lectora makes it really easy, captions are easy... don't know how well either one does for interactive video, I suppose you could cut the video up with some sort of conversion software or video editing software (like media encoder or premiere pro--expensive!) and then do it with video chunks. But both those programs are more expensive than Camtasia. I find Camtasia does the job fairly well. Other authoring softwares may do similar stuff...that's just what I've used.  Not sure how CamStudio or Wink would or even could do it (free or cheap products ...are they even still a thing?); it has been a decade since I've looked at them...

ResponsesInList.Title: External manifest and cross-domain question
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there! I want to host my SCORM packages on an external server . But I have heard that cross- domain restrictions will prevent the SCORM being able to communicate with my LMS server. Question: Are moodle.mysite.com and files.mysite.com considered cross-domain? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External manifest and cross-domain question
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Justin, Are moodle.mysite.com and files.mysite.com considered cross-domain? Yes Or would my SCORM on files.XXXX be able to communicate correctly with my LMS on moodle.XXXX ? No, they must be hosted in the same origin which means, in the old days: For any browser but IE : same scheme/protocol, same hostname, same port For IE: same scheme/protocol, same hostname In the past, you were used to host the content in the same origin of the Moodle instance i.e run the content on the same "web server" under a virtual folder/alias or on another web server but exposed via a reverse proxy under the same origin above. This is how in the past they solved this issue unless using "complex" SCORM Proxy solutions. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External manifest and cross-domain question
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for the confirmation Matteo, unsuspected as much, but was hoping. I stumbled upon the CORS specification. Have you ever tried this or seen it work ? I had never heard about it so I have some doubts... https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-origin_resource_sharing

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External manifest and cross-domain question
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Justin, CORS allows, under policy settings, the JavaScript running into an origin to connect to another origin e.g. JavaScript in Moodle code to consume a RSS feed. SCORM Run Time Environment (RTE) requires the ability to search and consume the methods exposed by a JS object called API , exposed to the content by the LMS, here Moodle, in a parent window with respect to where the SCORM content is hosted. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Package Slide Navigation
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle does not control how you progress through the slides in a SCORM module. Progression is controlled by the program inside the SCORM package.  But even if a person clicks, "I have read this slide", how do you know that is the truth?  You could just make your "Next" button labelled, "I have read this slide."  Anyone using the program can still click through the slides. I suggest that what is really important is whether or not the person understands the content in the presentation. It does not matter whether or not they read each slide if they know what is trying to be taught.  The best way to test for learning is to have an assessment (test/quiz) built into the presentation, or as a post-test outside the presentation. If you insist on having the user indicate they have read all the slides, then you can add a Moodle label resource in your course that states, "By clicking the checkbox to the right, I affirm that I have read all the slides in the presentation." Then configure the label to be marked complete when the user click the checkbox. Floyd

ResponsesInList.Title: From Captivate to Articulate (?)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello all! We changed software from Captivate to Articulate so i recreated my captivate courses to articulate. It is better to: A) Create new courses B) Update the old courses with the new scorms (keeping the same identifiers)?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: From Captivate to Articulate (?)
ResponsesInList.Text: First - I would suggest you take a step back and look to see if you really need to keep creating SCORM packages at all - we typically advise our clients creating new content to completely avoid SCORM - it's an old standard that was never designed for use on mobile devices - authoring tools like captivate and articulate try their best, but the underlying SCORM standard is quite fragile and often hard to get it working exactly the way you want. Typically there's no way to convert from one SCORM authoring tool to another, and if you have to re-create content you are better to look at more modern methods for authoring your content. You could look at recreating the content directly inside Moodle using the Lesson or Quiz activites - or if you are looking for something similar to your SCORM authoring tools you should really be looking at creating your content in H5P instead of SCORM. There are a lot of posts about H5P vs SCORM in the forums here - a google search should show up some other reasons why you should avoid SCORM. Aside from that... you can't update your old captivate scorm packages using articulate - you will have to recreate them completely, manually copying over specific assets like vidoes/images as required. Good luck!

ResponsesInList.Title: Ri: Re: From Captivate to Articulate (?)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Dan, thank you for the advice! you will have to recreate them completely, manually copying over specific assets like vidoes/images as required. <-- This is what i am doing. I recreated all my courses from captivate to articulate, slide per slide. My question was if it is better to create a new course in moodle or replace the existing activities . Let's say that i have an English course with 4 modules created in Captivate. I recreate those modules in Articulate with all assets videos img ecc. Now it's better to: - replace the modules (replacing old captivate scorms with new articulate scorms keeping same identifiers so i keep the completition report) - create new course like "English V2", with new modules ecc.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ri: Re: From Captivate to Articulate (?)
ResponsesInList.Text: I would highly reccomend you at least try to convert one of those to H5P instead of Articulate to see how easy it is, and the benefits you get from the different authoring environment. I haven't seen anyone try to maintain identifiers when transferring from captivate to articulate before - even if you did, the tracking data is unlikely to match, and anything in suspend_data is likely to cause all sorts of conflicts and possible errors. Definitely better to create new packages and hide the old ones, but if you really want to maintain completion status you could delete all data from the scorm_sco_tracks for that package and then just replace the SCORM - you'll still have the old grades pushed to the gradebook and the activity completion status, but no tracking data. Users who have already completed the SCORM might get confused when they enter the SCORM though because there would be conflicting information - activity complete, but no attempt data disaplyed in the reports for that scorm etc.

ResponsesInList.Title: Ri: Re: Ri: Re: From Captivate to Articulate (?)
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you for the tips! We have H5P installed on our moodle and i tried it a few times, but we use articulate for many reasons: we have a lot of videos and images and we do some games that can't be done with h5p. Maybe we can use h5p for courses with less interactivity.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ri: Re: From Captivate to Articulate (?)
ResponsesInList.Text: I've been resisting posting this response...but here I am doing it anyway... I've seen several posts where you support H5P over SCORM and I understand some of the reasons (scorm is old, scorm is fragile, sometimes it is seriously weird...) but one of the biggest SCORM selling points is something H5P cannot do. And in the more than 3 years I've been watching it, I don't see any indication the H5P folks have any intention of making it do it....tracking. I use scorm because it tracks and looks nice (ish, if I build them that way). Don't get me wrong--SCORM Interaction reports are painful...but they are there, they tell me where someone is in the course, they tell me if/when someone has finished, if/when they pass, I can sort them by groups and easily look at single users. SCORM is a lot of work...but I can make a SCORM look good more simply than if I try to make a Lesson look the way I want (and still meet accessibility standards...of course I use Captivate and have suspicions that accessibility might still not be awesome but I can try). I love lesson, it is brilliant but has some weirdness in tracking as well. It will track but some of the sophistication in if-then-else conditions isn't there. It doesn't have the flexibility in visual presentation SCORM has. I have to do a ton of 'branding' on everything I design and that is...difficult (not impossible). I also build a lot of software tutorials and Lesson isn't great for that. About the only thing that is good for software tutorials is SCORM... Quiz is fantastic but isn't good for content distribution. It is good for testing knowledge. Wonderful tracking and stats. Love the tracking and stats. I agree--converting to H5P is easy. I don't love the WYIWIG editor or the lack of ability to fiddle with html code. But easy to build. Many options. Lots of flexibility. I could probably do software tutorials using screen prints as backgrounds in H5P but it would be more complicated if I want the participant to do the thing I'm teaching...But tracking in H5P is labyrinthine at best. There is no way to require viewers see all the slides (we have to have that)--it will let you click the last slide and VOILA! completion. The new branching is really cool--I love the examples they use for it, they aren't applicable for me, but I really enjoy the way they are built...but I'm not sold on the branch interface--I don't love the pop-up branch and I'd like a way to disappear branches or check them if they have already been completed (which I do a lot with Captivate, and formerly Lectora). But it doesn't track, so it can't really do that. And if you use interactive video, users have to manually click the star thing in the video skin and submit every time they answer a question or it won't remember or report that they did it. Sometimes it remembers where they left off...and sometimes it doesn't. If it decides the video is too long, it just stops. And crashes your site. I agree that long videos are not good for learning...but crashing my whole site to prove a point seems petty. Accessing (the minuscule) reports is complicated (accessing through the gradebook is just weird). I'm sure you've seen my much longer post about why I want to use H5P but cannot...I'll stop here before it becomes a soap box (it is too late?). So...the purpose of my post: For those of us who use SCORM because we need interactivity, visual pizazz AND solid reporting...what do you suggest? Because H5P can't (currently) do that.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: From Captivate to Articulate (?)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dan, I found what you wrote very interesting and important. If SCORM is such an old and problematic standard, and xAPI is new and preferred one, why its support in Moodle is so minimal? There is 7 years old issue tracker about implementing it ( MDL-35433 ), but still a plugin is needed and it seems that even then fully xAPI experience is not yet supported.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: From Captivate to Articulate (?)
ResponsesInList.Text: xAPI isn't really a replacement for SCORM - and yes it's "newer than scorm" but to call it "preferred" depends a lot on your use-case - xAPI becomes a lot more interesting when you have multiple sources of learning content that can all generate xAPI statements (eg not just an LMS, or a single content package hosted within your LMS) If you only have a single LMS and you want your reporting to sit within your LMS then you probably want to develop the content within the LMS or use something like H5P which reports the data back natively to the LMS. If you have multiple LMS systems, or multiple systems that support the export of Xapi logs/statements then it becomes a really nice way to aggregate data from multiple systems and provide high level reporting within your Learning Record Store. Most of the tools I've seen that allow you to generate xAPI packages also suffer from some of the same shortcomings you have with SCORM (costly expensive commercial tools the published "package" is not editable and you need to maintain the source code from your packages in a backup somewhere.) To be honest - I've seen a lot more clients investigating the use of tools like MS Power BI to aggregate data from multiple sources than using a learning record store because it allows them to report on data in any form - but over time as more systems support the use of xAPI statements this may change.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: From Captivate to Articulate (?)
ResponsesInList.Text: An amazing use of XAPI was presented at DevLEarn in Oct 2014. The Ann Arbor Hands-On-Museum's personalized the exhibits. The children received a wearable badge, as they visited each of the exhibits the LMS tracked, where they went in the museum, how much time they spent at each exhibit, did they revisit an exhibit. etc. It was truly an eye-opener. But to Dan's point, there isn't a lot of demand for that level of reporting in the business or academic world.

But I do know a little about SCORM weirdness having been doing SCORM stuff for 10 years... 10 years! And I've managed to learn nothing about that other technical stuff! Cause for celebration! That's not what you wanted to hear about...so here goes: Sometimes, when your system has a time out, if a user starts a SCORM and then stops and doesn't do anything (they walk away to use the facilities and get side tracked, etc) for the time out period and then resume, it will look like they complete but then they have to start where they left off when they walked away...because it timed them out and the scorm content doesn't warn you that you've timed out and it is no longer conversing with Moodle. Like a dropped phone call. Just talking (or sending data) doesn't restore communication line. That happens all the time for me. Sometimes, SCORM modules are not set up in such a way to report properly--either in Moodle or in whatever authoring tool you use. Camtasia publishes scorm modules. Before the newest (2019) version, it would not 'bookmark' and if you closed and came back, it would start back at the beginning. Very irritation. Captivate sometimes is weird. In the old days, about 5 percent of all my users had trouble completing. I don't see that as much now...def not 5% of the time anymore. I had 5000 users back then and that meant...argh! math!...250? users had a problem. Unacceptable. But generally errors of that type are user error these days (and by that I mean SCORM designer)... If you force completion, it might make them start over. I never use that setting. Teachers have to have a student role to get credit...if you add the role, it should remember the participation (unlike quiz, which saves Teacher stuff as preview unless specifically directed). You might check the completion criteria, sometimes the criteria between the activity module and the actual package aren't speaking the same language and then it gets weird...completions can happen but the circumstances have to be just right or there has to be a  blue moon... What authoring do you use?

It appears that some modules download just about all the content to the browser when it is launched and some do not because many of the modules will keep playing when there is no network connection and some will not. The reason we are interested in learning more about the causes of these errors is because even though some problems are reported to the Help Desk, we don't think they all are. All we can do about user error is to educate the users and hope that they will not do things like start an attempt, leave their computer for long periods of time and then return expecting to just continue where they left off. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to get alerts after 2 attempts of SCORM object (a quiz)??

The Moodle quiz activity does have a bit more flexibility here though - (and is a lot more reliable/stable than SCORM.) - the teacher can grant extra attempts at the quiz to specific users and let them go over the main limit set. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM 2004 API Search Algorithm special characters not showing up properly
ResponsesInList.Text: It isn't that it won't allow special characters. It will but the data is stored in a single text field and those weird bits indicate what should be there: %20 indicates a space, %3 indicates a question mark, etc. I'm guessing that is a UTF8 thing. All the reporting data IS STORED IN ONE FIELD.  I think that is a little crazy. But that is how it is. I know practically nothing about programming and cannot contribute a better idea, so I cannot criticize...maybe it just makes me crazy trying to read it (honestly, I stopped trying reading those a long time ago...and some of the headaches stopped). If you really want to read those horrible things, you could set up some sort of search/replace thing that automatically replaces %20 with a space and %3 with a ? and so on. I'd have to do it manually but I'm sure there is a way. I ran some Crystal Reports on this type of data several years ago and that was one of the things I told it to do. Worked really well (outside of the having to work in Crystal Reports...but if you like that sort of thing, just fine). Oh, and Moodle isn't really 2004 compliant. You might want to use 1.2. It works better. Not saying 2004 won't work, but some of the stuff you might expect to work one way might not. And most everything I've seen here implies Moodle isn't interested in jumping through the hoops necessary to be 2004 compliant (Dan, if you are reading this: this is not criticism, I agree, it isn't worth it).

ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM grades query
ResponsesInList.Text: I am using Moodle 3.4 I am trying to query for SCORM grades using the mdl_grade_grades but none of my scorm scores appear there. I tried searching thru all mdl_scorm* tables but none seem to be storing any grades. Am I missing something? Please help.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM grades query
ResponsesInList.Text: OOOHHH....the hard questions. First--in courses with scorm modules, do you see grades in the grade book for the scorms? If you scorms don't report an actual grade (other than 0...), it won't do you much good. Second--mdl_grade_grades will store your scores if there are scores to be stored---but connecting grade_grades to specific item in a query is a little more complex. Because that table gathers data from all the activity tables, you have to know the item number and id, the user id etc--so the grade_grades table isn't sorted by course as much as...well, item id's which are actually a little less obvious than you might think. If you can figure out which ones you want, you'll want the final grade field. But what you probably want is to connect through the tables to connect the item name and number and grade...which would be a lot of work.  I've done something like it using Crystal Reports and it is pretty horrible. Scorm grades are actually stored in mdl_scorm_scoes_track. But it also stores other tracking data (completed, suspend data, etc),  so you would be looking for the element cmi.score.raw (or maybe cmi.score.scaled). The problem with querying this sort of thing is setting up the table connections and being right about what connects where and what you actually want pulled out.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm Slide View Persantage Tracking
ResponsesInList.Text: It really does not work that way. You are asking the dashboard to make judgements about an activity. The dashboard displays the percentage of activities and resources in the course which are complete. If there are three activities and one is completed, it would display 30% but if one activity is 30% complete, it doesn't care--it is either yes-complete or no-not complete. Also, this calculation does not  take into account required for completion vs not required (completion tracking set vs not set). it is only based on all the items in the course.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM package upload date
ResponsesInList.Text:
It's stored in Moodle, when you go to edit settings on the SCORM package and click on the file, it shows for example: 
```text
Last modified 23 April 2019, 5:08 PM


Created 23 April 2019, 5:08 PM
```
 For system wide report, we use the ad-hoc database queries plugin for this: https://moodle.org/plugins/report_customsql and a query, which shows only visible courses, the course name , package name, link to it and time it was modified. 
```text
SELECT 
c.id AS "Course id#", c.shortname as "Course Code", CONCAT("%%WWWROOT%%/mod/scorm/view.php%%Q%%id=",m.id) AS "Link to Module", s.name AS "Module Name", s.reference as "Filename", from_unixtime(s.timemodified) as "Time Modified"
FROM prefix_scorm AS s
JOIN prefix_course_modules AS m ON (m.instance=s.id AND m.course=s.course)
JOIN prefix_course AS c ON (s.`course`=c.`id`)
WHERE 
c.visible='1'
ORDER BY s.reference
```

ResponsesInList.Text: I work in an establishment which currently uses Moodle 3.5. The following information was passed out to us: SCORM 1.3 incompatibility. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Version Update
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm not surprised you're confused - the statement you pasted above doesn't make any sense. Prior to its release, SCORM 2004 was called SCORM 1.3, but the name "SCORM 1.3" is no longer in official use. Moodle does not provide full support for the SCORM 2004 specification (it's a massive spec and it didn't really get a lot of use.) There's a good doc that explains the different SCORM versions here: https://scorm.com/scorm-explained/business-of-scorm/scorm-versions/ There are some newer specs around like Xapi and CMI 5 but none of those have been as widely adopted as SCORM 1.2/2004 - In terms of Moodle I see a lot more people moving to H5P than the newer versions of the SCORM spec. Can you give some more context on who provided this statement?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM content not responsive in small devices
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, we found this post searching about this issue and posible solution. As stated, there seems to be no official solution: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-46563 https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-62057 We managed to workaround this issue with a small jquery script for now . We add the following snippet just before the </body> tag in the layout file the SCORM player is using. For example "embedded.php" for the pop-up window. <script> function resizeme() { $('#scorm_layout').height($(window).height()); } $( document ).ready(function() { $( window ).resize(function() { setTimeout(resizeme, 1500); }); }); </script> It just set the height for #scorm_layout to whatever the window height is. It works with a timeout because Moodle seems to be doing the same on resize but always changing it to a fixed number. DISCLAIMER: this was tested on Moodle 3.5 with a modified Gourmet theme. I cannot state it works in every situation. Best!

When turned on SCORM packages are limited to 4096 characters. In my experience the average Rise package requires more than this to save progress information. Once you disable this setting SCORM packages are allowed to save around 50000 characters. This setting used to default to 'on' in earlier versions of Moodle but in more recent versions it seems to default to 'off'. This may help resolve your issue with progress seeming not to track beyond a certain point in the package. Even with that setting disabled I have still been receiving reports of Rise courses not correctly tracking results in Moodle. So... if anyone has any other knowledge about this I would appreciate it. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM not recording in Gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: A SCORM package has an XML file that tells the LMS (Moodle) what do to with it, including the completion status and what questions should be recorded and graded. In Articulate Storyline, for example, you need to add something called a "results slide". On the results slide, you select which questions will be used for scoring and completion, and this is all written to the XML file and this is what would populate the grade book. It sounds to me like your SCORM file hasn't been instructed to log nor score anything. A good way to test SCORM packages is to upload them to SCORM Cloud ( https://cloud.scorm.com ), and test from there. Thus eliminating Moodle as the potential problem. If no results are tracked on SCORM Cloud then it's safe to say that the SCORM Package itself needs adjusting/fixing. I hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: scorms & moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Altan, I do a lot of Articulate Storyline work. Here are some suggestions. Check your Storyline publishing settings:  Reporting and Tracking.   If you are tracking based on a course completion trigger, be certain that trigger is at the end of the course. If you are tracking based on a quiz score, be certain you have selected the correct Result slide. Check your reporting settings - passed/failed, complete/incomplete, etc. The next settings are in your Moodle SCORM activity. These settings can be a bit tricky.  See https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/SCORM_settings . If your SCORM module reports a numeric quiz score, then select Highest Grade for the Grading Method. If your SCORM module reports back something like passed/failed, then select Learning Objects for the Grading Method. Activity completion settings: Deselect 'Student must view this activity ..." Disable 'Require a minimum score' unless SCORM is reporting a score. Select both Require Status - Passed and Completed.  These settings are logically ORed together so you cah select both regardless of which SCORM reports back. Try the above settings and let me know if they work.  If not, I may need to look at your SCORM settings and perhaps you Articulate Storyline file.  You can also activate SCORM debugging in Moodle and watch what SCORM is sending back to Moodle.  See https://docs.moodle.org/37/en/SCORM_FAQ#Debugging ~Floyd

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: The Flash Apocalypse

H5P is a really solid alternative to people used to creating SCORM packages using an external tool and it provides a lot of similar functionality to commercial SCORM authoring tools. I'm not completely sure what you mean by "easy hacking of scores" though. I couldn't see any open issues in the h5p tracker related to this, but you should create one there to find out the detail.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: The Flash Apocalypse (our experiance)

ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM quiz results
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi.  We're considering implementing SCORM on our Moodle sites and as a result, we've done some practice runs. The SCORM package itself came out - the test student account was able to answer all the quiz questions and obtain a score, but that's as far as we got.  That is to say, we couldn't see the specific results - only a final score.  We couldn't see what the questions were or the answer the student chose.  Is there a way we can obtain this information? Thank you.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM quiz results
ResponsesInList.Text: Unfortunately this is likely to be a limitation of the SCORM authoring tool you are using. Many SCORM authoring tools produce simple packages that just report a completion status to the LMS - If reporting on question use is important then you probably shouldn't be using SCORM (even if you get the SCORM package reporting the interaction/quiz data, SCORM doesn't make this very easy) But - there are also some big warning signs there - it sounds like you're only just starting out developing your content (and don't already have a bunch of existing SCORM) - you really shouldn't be creating "new" SCORM content - SCORM is an old unreliable clunky standard that was never really designed for modern learning. Moodle provides a number of tools that allow you to develop the content directly within the LMS ( lesson /quiz and many other tools) - but if you are looking for a more modern SCORM style replacement then you should be looking at H5P ( https://h5p.org/ ) - H5P is open source, (doesn't require an expensive licence like most good SCORM authoring tools) and provides a really good integration with Moodle and much better reporting than is currently available in SCORM. Good luck!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM quiz results
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for letting me know about H5P.  We'll look into it. I started browsing the site and I'm already impressed with some of its features.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM quiz results
ResponsesInList.Text: Dan, Does H5P require coding experience like TinCan (xAPI)? Kind Regards, Shirley

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM quiz results
ResponsesInList.Text: No it doesn't - I'd also suggest that people starting from scratch (eg no prior scorm knowledge) will find it much easier to create H5P content packages than learning how to use a tool like Articulate or Captivate to create their content.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Issues with tracking & gradebook with SCORM 1.2 in Moodle 3.5.1
ResponsesInList.Text: Andrea, It is possible the problem is caused by the way some of the slides in that one module are configured. I have seen situations where a module was published to show 'completed' or 'passed' based on the number of slides viewed.  At least in Articulate Storyline, a slide is not considered 'viewed' until the slide timing bar times out.  In some slides the timing bar might be set for 10 or 15 seconds, when the content in the slide takes the viewer only 5 seconds to read.  The user clicks 'Next' before the timing bar reaches the end, and the slide is considered 'not viewed'.  This is just an example that demonstrates the complexities you can run into. If you are using a score for completion are you certain that the module was published with the correct passing score, or that completion by score was correctly published? Moodle has a SCORM debug tracing mode that might help you find the problem.  There is a checkbox titled, 'Activate API debug and tracing (set the capture mask with apidebugmask)' at the bottom of the SCORM configuration screen: Site administration > Plugins > Activity modules > SCORM package.  Select that checkbox and save the setting.  When you open a SCORM module, a separate window will open where you can see the communication between your SCORM module and Moodle. Also note you can have this feature activated for specific users so it does not show for everyone. In the textbox below the debug checkbox, you can enter a username for which debugging can be activated, example for user myusername, you would type in myusername:.*  the colon period asterisk sequence after the username is important. Floyd

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm not marked
ResponsesInList.Text: Daniel, There are many parts of a SCORM package that must be correctly coordinated for reporting to work correctly:  the many authoring tool (Articulate) publishing settings, and the many Moodle activity configuration settings. First Articulate, I believe you likely have these correct: Publish to LMS, SCORM 1.2 Publish to HTML 5, if you expect some users might have really old browsers, you could publish to HTML 5 with Flash fallback. Be certain your Tracking setting is correct (slides viewed,  quiz score or complete course trigger. Moodle (thanks for the screenshot), you might need to test some different settings: The first thing I noticed is that Attempts Grading is set to First Attempt.  Subsequent attempts will then not update the grade.  You might select Highest Attempt.  This might be the main cause of your problem. Check the Grading Method setting - Learning Objects will return the number of passed or completed objects, Highest Grade will return the highest score. In Compatibility Settings, set Mastery Score Overrides Status to Yes In Activity Completion, you might want to deselect Passed because you want a score. Moodle has a great SCORM debugging tool that will allow you to view the SCORM communication and see what is being sent to Moodle. In the admin menu block, select Site administration ... Plugins ... Activity modules ... SCORM package.  At the bottom of that page select, Activate API debug and tracing (set the capture mask with apidebugmask).  This will then print a log of the SCORM communication - the log output goes to a separate browser window. Let us know if any of this helps. Floyd

ResponsesInList.Title: Scorm files - HTML5 & Flash outputs
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Not sure if this is the appropriate forum, but I'm being told by the software suppliers of my scorm files, that in order to bypass flash output in my scorm files, I should edit the imsmanifest. xml file to point directly to "index_lms_html5.html" instead of "index_lms.html" Would anyone know how to do this please ? I've attached an example xml file where it refer to both idexes, perhaps someone would know where the change needs to be made and the code that needs to beinserted ( if any ? ) ?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm files - HTML5 & Flash outputs
ResponsesInList.Text: I would be very wary about directly editing the manifest.xml file. It is very easy to introduce errors.  If the SCORM package was published correctly (e.g. for both Flash and html 5), then there should be an index_lms.html file in the package that selects Flash or html 5 based on the browser capability. Your manifext.xml file already references index_lms.html in the resource section (bold is my emphasis): <resource identifier="__6QJLTuCcz8u_course_id_RES" type="webcontent" href=" index_lms.html " adlcp:scormtype="sco"> It is the index_lms.html file that determines whether Flash or html 5 is launched first.  Most content creation programs let you select html 5 with Flash fallback. That means html 5 will be launched unless the browser does not support html5. Then it launches Flash. There is a line in the index_lms.html file that specifies the order of html 5 and Flash: var settings = { runtimeOrder: [{"type":"html5","url":"index_lms_html5.html"},{"type":"flash","url":"index_lms_flash.html"}] }; If the runtimeOrder parameters are switched (i.e. {"type":"flash", ...} occurs first, then flash will be launched first.  In that case I suggest ensuring the the parameters are as shown above (html 5 type is first). But, be aware that directly editing any of these files may result in breaking the code and the way in which the SCORM package plays. I take no responsibility for what might happen if you follow my suggestions - they are not foolproof and may cause errors.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm files - HTML5 & Flash outputs
ResponsesInList.Text: One further comment... It is likely your developer wanted you to change the manifest line <resource identifier="__6QJLTuCcz8u_course_id_RES" type="webcontent" href=" index_lms.html " adlcp:scormtype="sco"> to <resource identifier="__6QJLTuCcz8u_course_id_RES" type="webcontent" href=" index_lms_html5.html " adlcp:scormtype="sco"> That would directly launch the index_lms_html5.html file, but then it bypasses the index_lms.html file that does all the browser capability checking and error messaging.  You really want index_lms.html to run and handle the correct launching.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Replacing SCORM Package without Losing Data
ResponsesInList.Text: Paula, You need to replace the SCORM module (the .zip file) in the exact same SCORM activity. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Replacing SCORM Package without Losing Data

However, if you created a totally new SCORM package or used a different authoring tool, then you will need to open the .zip file and edit some of the files; See the following forum posts: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=228272 https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=334760 https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=276324

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Redirecting to next lesson
ResponsesInList.Text: I currently use Captivate but I've done similar stuff with Lectora and could probably do it with Camtasia, if I felt inclined that way. So, I'll describe a process I used recently--my course was IT Security and Data Privacy.  My activities include a SCORM module, a quiz activity, a feedback activity and a certificate that generates when all the activities are done. My SCORM got the largest portion of my attention, since it required a bunch of development time but once it was done, I did not publish it. Instead, I created my quiz and feedback activities.  I didn't have to populate them right then, just create the place to put the questions.  I copied the link to the quiz.  I reopened my SCORM project (Captivate in this instance).  I added a shape to the last page and set it up to be used as a button. Because captivate is too complicated for its own good, I created an advanced action that does two things: One, close/exit this activity and two, go to a web address.  I set the web address to the quiz link I copied earlier  If I were using Lectora, I'd just add two actions to the button and be done with it.  In captivate, I went back to my shape/button.  On the on-success/exit action I set it to execute an advanced action and selected the advanced action I set up.  Then I published my project and dropped it into Moodle. In this particular instance, I made the quiz and feedback not visible but still accessible for students.  I don't love this, it was at the request of the course owner (or the owner's boss); I'd prefer to just leave them hidden until the conditions are reached, but there you go.  Once that's going, I went in and populated my quiz questions and my feedback questions.  Then I made my certificate pretty and made sure all my conditions/completion criteria were correct and...four months later, 450 people have completed the course.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to launch scorm course directly
ResponsesInList.Text: Barbara, You can place a link from the main course page to a SCORM resource in a course. The URL you need to do that you can get by copying link location of the SCORM activity from the Moodle course where it resides. Be aware, however, that permissions settings will impact the usefulness of your SCORM results. For example, users will have to be enrolled in the course to access the resource, just like any other Moodle resource. If you change the course to allow guest access, the log in as guest option, then you will not get user-specific SCORM tracking results. Another option would be to add the SCORM content to the front page of the Moodle site. Once again, users logged in as guest would not have results recorded from them in a meaningful way. You would just have 50 different accesses by Guest User. Unless you change your site security settings to require login for a view of the front page content. Best, A

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Variety of issues with "video" SCORMs
ResponsesInList.Text: I do notice your suspend data is over 255 characters, so if the "scorm standards mode" box is ticked under admin > plugins > activities > SCORM that might be causing a problem.. but in general SCORM is pretty rubbish for this sort of thing - quite often the users Moodle session might timeout before they get to the end of the activity as the SCORM does not always post stuff back to the LMS to keep the session open. With this sort of thing I'd highly reccomend you move to using the core Lesson module - or even something like H5P which will give you a much more reliable solution.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Variety of issues with "video" SCORMs
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Dan, this is helpful. Are there any consequences to disabling the suspend data limit? Regarding the Lesson Module, will that be able to track progress through videos? Our use case is to users resuming the video where they left off (or at least as close as possible - eg beginning of slide), and to track progress and completion for the video. Videos within SCORMs have done that fairly well to date, but recently IE seems to have started causing issues.
