ResponsesInList.Title: Re: cmi.core.score.raw is 0 even though all my answers are correct
ResponsesInList.Text: the score must be passed from your SCORM package - quite often some scorm packages only pass the score to the LMS on the final slide and if the student closes the window before viewing the final slide you won't get a score passed. You should enable the SCORM debugger in Moodle and take a close look at the logs to see when the raw score is sent and see if you can reproduce the same issue. Take a look here for more info: https://docs.moodle.org/en/SCORM_FAQ#Debugging

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: cmi.core.score.raw is 0 even though all my answers are correct
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Simon, I agree completely with Dan that you should try the SCORM debugging available in Moodle. Something else we do for all SCORM 1.2 packages are to run them through SCORM Cloud before pulling them into Moodle. We check all ways through the course, passing and failing to ensure the scores are both reported and reported accurately (e.g. percentages vs points) to the LMS. SCORM Cloud is free for this type of testing. This way you know if your SCORM package is working on its own or if it's a Moodle settings isssue. Also, what version of Moodle are you running? There were some updates to the SCORM module a few (or more) versions ago that fixed a few things too. Finally, what version of Storyline are you using and what settings? We had to choose very specific settings in both Storyline and Moodle to ensure things are reported correctly. Having your results slide before the last slide of your course works well too. Good luck!

If this is to quickly convert a large number of existing SCORM packages and you have the original captivate authoring files (not just the published SCORM package) then it might be worthwhile getting a new licence of Captivate and republishing the packages to get you up and running quickly. If you don't have the original authoring files and only have the published zip I don't think Captivate will let you do any conversion at all - you will need to recreate the content. Sure you can add nice fly-over effects, and make things spin around on the screen just like lots of teaching staff used to do with powerpoint, but often the effort that often goes into this doesn't improve the learners experience with the content. Moodle has a great built-in tool called the Lesson module that allows for similar functionality to SCORM packages that let you step through a content package and present quiz style questions, it provides much better reporting and better reliability than SCORM but doesn't have the same built-in animation creation/image creation/editing tools that a SCORM authoring tool would. If you want to have a "photoshop" style content development tool like articulate/captivate you might want to investigate some of the other online content development tools such as h5p and Adapt good luck!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Multiple SCORM Alert Messages
ResponsesInList.Text: We sometimes see clients on high-latency connections having the alert when they haven't lost their Internet connection. Users on public/heavily used wifi also can get the alert more often. Dan is right to put you on the track of optimization, but that JS AJAX request is to a single, very small file on the server, and it's not in moodledata... Might be worth investigating your network performance. And all of this is a roundabout way of saying: this is a feature, not a bug. It's meant to warn you when your data and progress through the SCORM activity might not be saved because the network connection—and hence the SCORM API—has been dropped. So that should be your first concern, the lost API and lost user data, not the annoyance of the alerts. If I were you, I'd turn on the debugging log and make dang sure that the API is still active when these alerts are happening.

From what I understand, the 4096 limit is just an SPM ( smallest permitted maximum) - as in any LMS that wishes to be SCORM 1.2 compliant must allot at least 4096 characters for suspended data - so raising this value should still be considered compliant, right? And to extend that question further, if we raise the suspended data limit would the Articulate Storyline player experience any issues while resuming a session? We're mainly concerned about student progression becoming "corrupted" if suspended data becomes too long - but I don't think I've ever seen this happen. Could that be an issue, or is it completely safe and acceptable to raise our suspended data limit? Thanks!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM 1.2 suspended data limit
ResponsesInList.Text: raising the limit in the LMS actually breaks compliance with the spec and causes the ADL 1.2 tests to fail.. but if you don't care about compliance (no-one does really) - there is a setting in admin > plugins > activities > SCORM called "SCORM 1.2 standards mode" - if you disable that setting it will increase the limits within Moodle for suspend_data (and other vars) Important to note that some SCORM authoring tools include code that truncates the data before it sends it to the LMS - so you may also need to modify your SCORM packages to support the bigger limits as well.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM course will open in window but will not load
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Joe, thanks for sharing ! Indeed, some of those characters have a special meaning and are able to break the expected behavior, http://www.faqs.org/rfcs/rfc1738.html : The character "#" is unsafe and should always be encoded because it is used in World Wide Web and in other systems to delimit a URL from a fragment/anchor identifier that might follow it. More info can be found here: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniform_Resource_Identifier#Syntax (RFCs are clear but require more than a read to be fully understood ). Even the SCORM specs tell about the need to use valid URI i.e. by enconding those "unsafe" characters. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Status Updating /Review Mode issues with AICC
ResponsesInList.Text: We are using Moodle 3.0.3. We are having issues with how the review mode works in Moodle. Our courses are all AICC to an external content server . We've tried everything on the Moodle completion settings as well as turn off Preview Mode in the SCORM settings, but I am guessing "review mode" and "preview mode" are 2 different things? Our courses are about 4 hours long and made up of multiple modules. Students will sometimes exit the course and continue it another day. Which is why the review mode is an issue. The next time the student enters the course, it is in review mode. We made changes to our courses so that only the last module will return a score and status, which reduced this issue, but it is still an issue if they want to retake the course if they failed it the first time. Can this review mode be turned OFF? Or can Moodle accept course status no matter what the mode is?  A sample course is attached.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Status Updating /Review Mode issues with AICC
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Luis, you should avoid to submit a "status" (or a "score" when using a mastery score ) 'till the supposed end (at least, when a quiz has been submitted); otherwise, the next time the user will enter into the course the tracking mode will be set to review . HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Status Updating /Review Mode issues with AICC
ResponsesInList.Text: What we did is have the course return a score only after ALL modules were COMPLETED. Completed does not necessarily mean PASSED. The issue is if they do not pass the course and want to retake it to improve their score. The status of the course remains incomplete if they retry due to the review mode. We do not want to change our courses to send a score only when all modules are passed. That would not be a good idea.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Status Updating /Review Mode issues with AICC
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Luis, unfortunately, completion and successfullness have been mixed by the specs, up to SCORM 2004 (1.3), where the two concepts have been properly separated. That being said, I didn't attend to your "simple test" yet: could you share the exact (and shortest ) sequence of steps to replicate your issue? Will try one of the next days, trying to understand the why and, potentially, a workaround. Theory: review mode will e.g. prevent mastery score to work but review mode is not activated if the "status" of the course is still incomplete at the time of the launch: that "course status" comes from a logical sum i.e. if at least one AU will have an incomplete status then review mode won't be activated. HTH, Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Status Updating /Review Mode issues with AICC
ResponsesInList.Text: The steps are: 1. launch the course 2. take the 1st module and pass it with at least a 70% 3. take the 2nd module and fail it. 4. exit the COURSE and/or moodle entirely. At this point Moodle marks the course as incomplete. 5. Go back into the course and retake the 2nd module and pass it. 6. exit the course. The course status remains unchanged as incomplete. Most LMSes do not work this way. We have used our courseware on all the major LMSes and normally, we pass the status and scores at the end of each module, which we cannot do with Moodle.

I want to know if this can be fixed with some type of code in the \mod\scorm\aicc.php file? And yes, we also know that we could simply update our Moodle to use SSL, but we want to know if mixed content can be allowed via the aicc.php file? Thanks for the help!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to Allow mixed content(http-https) with external AICC courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Luis, AFAIK no, you can't: Moodle uses absolute URLs so we cannot apply here the trick of removing the scheme i.e. using schemeless URLs to let the browser select the protocol of the resources according to the one of the page asking for them. Besides HACP requires aicc_url to be passed as absolute: if you want to try I'd start with schemeless URLs in the descriptor files i.e. the au file. You need to play with the browser settings of each computer or, use something like Let's Encrypt to easily run HTTPS in the test environment. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to Allow mixed content(http-https) with external AICC courses

ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM 1.2 vs SCORM 2004
ResponsesInList.Text: Everyone seems to use SCORM version 1.2 vs SCROM ver 2004 even though 2004 is newer and after 8 years, would assumd stable.  Am I missing something?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM 1.2 vs SCORM 2004
ResponsesInList.Text: Scorm 1.2 was a fairly simple implementation that didn't specify a lot of options for the content. It was a rather naive implementation in my opinion. Many people felt frustrated by the limitations of fields, or write only fields that should have been read/write, and poorly scoped statuses (e.g. completed/passed). However the simplicity made it fairly easy to support server side and to build hosts for, as there was a well built test suite that ensured standards between LMS hosts - so confidence when building content was high that it would work on a lot of platforms. Scorm 1.2 content will work on a lot of platforms these days and covers off the most basic needs of many - how much time the content took, and whether it is complete, and whether it is passed or failed. Scorm 1.3 / 2004 sought to address a number of limitations of 1.2's internal model by bring in other emerging standards such as content sequencing, more meaningful objective statuses and more comprehensive information about the objectives/interactions (such as what they are for - metadata - which was sorely missed in 1.2). Scorm 2004 is considerably more complicated internally and quite a bit more fiddly for LMS's to implement; many content authoring/packaging tools still don't explit the power of content metadata and sequencing - and so if there's not so much Scorm 2004 need out there LMS's aren't going to go to the trouble of supporting it as quickly. Bit of a catch 22 situation.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM 1.2 vs SCORM 2004
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Tim - that's one of our biggest problems - there are a lot of people with SCORM 2004 on their wish list or as a checkbox in an RFP - but no one who is using Moodle has been interested enough to help by providing funding or development to implement it. Also - the cost of implementing full SCORM 2004 support in Moodle is likely to be higher than the cost of using the commercial Rustici SCORM engine in Moodle so even if people want full SCORM 2004 support and have $$ it makes more sense to just implement the Rustici option as is stable/proven/known to work well. We will get there eventually - we had a succesful GSOC project last year that implemented a test harness that allows us to run the ADL tests in an automated fashion and the same student has been succesful in an application to continue to improve SCORM 2004 support in Moodle - we're making small steps to slowly implement better support. make sure you check out the FAQ: http://docs.moodle.org/22/en/SCORM_FAQ#Supported_Versions and my blog for any further info/updates: http://danmarsden.com/blog/category/scorm/

ResponsesInList.Title: Ang: Re: SCORM 1.2 vs SCORM 2004
ResponsesInList.Text: Now 4 years later. We have been using moodle for about a year now and have made many trainings with SCORM-packages. However, we have begun to make bigger elearning trainings and it seems that the SCORM 1.2 format cannot correctly track progress and show all slides correctly either. It seems SCORM 2004 is the answer to our issues, so we have inserted a copy of one of our courses in SCORM 2004 instead and it seems that it works just like we could have hoped. Seeing that SCORM 2004 is still not "supported" in moodle, how will this manifest it self in our training? I mean, it doesn't seem like anything is not working properly, so what are we missing? Or is it indeed possible that a SCORM 2004 can work just fine in mooodle? Thanks for your reply! //Christoffer, LLAB, actlearn.org

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ang: Re: SCORM 1.2 vs SCORM 2004
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Christoffer, Surprisingly, during my testing of courses produced using Storyline 360, I found that SCORM 2004 fixed a similar issue, which is that slides stopped resuming to the last visited slide due to a limited amount of suspend data in SCORM 1.2. SCORM 2004 has allowed the user at any point to leave and come back to the same spot. Also, it turns out that for essay style questions, I can see up to 5000 characters of the user's response which is fantastic because in SCORM 1.2, I had to modify the SCORM package and change a setting in Moodle to get it to work. Hopefully SCORM 2004 will continue to behave this way.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ang: Re: SCORM 1.2 vs SCORM 2004
ResponsesInList.Text: Turns out that I had still had issues seeing the entire text response using SCORM 2004, so I switched back to using SCORM 1.2 packages and realized that after disabling (unchecking) SCORM 1.2 standard mode under Plugins > Activities > SCORM, I no longer had resuming issues and I could see up to 5000 characters of the user's response. "Disabling this setting allows Moodle to store more data than the SCORM 1.2 specification allows. If your SCORM packages allow users to enter large amounts of text or if your package tries to store large amounts of data in the suspend_data field disable this."

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to pass additional parameters from SCORM to moodle?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hello Rasha, here is a brief overview of how you can do this, i'm writing this based on Captivate 10, but common JavaScript interface (discussed below) feature is available from Captivate 8 onwards. Captivate provides variables (system & user) that can be used for better representation of information, u can also create your own. example: 'cpQuizInfoStudentName' is a user variable and provides Student's name captured from LMS. Captivate 8 onwards provides a way to include JavaScript codes. It can be used in 2 ways: 1. Communication between Captivate variables and JS (get/set variable values). 2. use JS code to directly put in published html document. this opens up a lot of features to use like one can directly use LMSGetValue("cmi.core.student_name") to get name from LMS (select 'top' position to put your code in captivate by clicking down arrow besides 'Script_Window'  button) and use this script to set it properly i.e 'cmi.core.student_name' return 'lastname,firstname' and can be modified to 'firstname lastname' and then u can use point 1 information above. for more information refer to: https://helpx.adobe.com/captivate/using/common-js-interface.html Cheers
and happy Moodling!

ResponsesInList.Text: hello Abhishek, Thank you for your help, I would like to clarify the following: - I have understood that I can use javascript to get the variable values from SCORM and I am aware of this. - Moreover the LMSGetValue("cmi.core.student_name") would get the name from LMS However, I would like to know if there is a way in which I can report custom variables from SCORM into moodle. Can I configure moodle to read custom variables created in SCORM? Thanks again for your support. Regards, Rasha

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to pass additional parameters from SCORM to moodle?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rasha, LMSSetValue() is used to report data to LMS through supported variables, but i suppose u want to want to report variables which u have created on your own and not supported in LMS or SCORM, if this is the case then: it will not be reported to Moodle and will give error, also it would be like avoiding scorm specifications. however it can be done by adding variables at appropriate places as follows: Goto:   your_moodle_dir/mod/scorm/datamodels/scorm_12.js    and add variable u want to create in 'datamodel' variable. u may need to add more specification based on the context , i hope u understand the code there before making changes. Conclusion: to add other variables besides defined in SCORM specifications functionality is not provided or intended to provide. however, it can be done manually and involves risk to break code.

ResponsesInList.Title: event to find cmi.core.session_time in SCORM objects
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hello All, Working on Moodle version 2.7 Background: I need to track the amount of time spent by a user in every session as soon as the session ends. When I ran the SCORM debugger tool, I see that the cmi.core.session_time is being sent. 
```text
Wed, 05 Apr 2017 14:29:34 GMT: LMSInitialize("", "") => 101


Wed, 05 Apr 2017 14:29:34 GMT: LMSGetErrorString("101", "General exception") => 0


Wed, 05 Apr 2017 14:29:34 GMT: LMSSetValue("cmi.core.lesson_location", "2") => 0


Wed, 05 Apr 2017 14:29:42 GMT: LMSSetValue("cmi.core.session_time", "0000:00:56.41") => 0
```
 This time value, according to the docs - is added to cmi.core.total_time however, this is not being updated at the end of every session. for example: if a SCORM module has a bunch of slides and a test at the end, and a user closes the SCORM after a few slides without taking the test, his time spent value is NOT being recorded in the value: cmi.core.total_time (in the scorm_scoes_track table) but the value: cmi.core.session_time is being sent in the SCORM debugger tool. Question: is there a way we can write an event to capture the core.session_time value? where in the mod/scorm module is this value being saved or added to the cmi.core.total_time (so I can trigger the event there)? Any other ideas on capturing this value are welcome. thanks for any help in advance. I will be updating the status of the issue as I go along and try to figure this out.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: event to find cmi.core.session_time in SCORM objects
ResponsesInList.Text:
According to the specification when LMSFinish() is called at the end of the session, the value in the cmi.core.session_time element should be added to the value stored in the cmi.core.total_time  element, and the value in the cmi.core.session_time element should be reset. To get the value you can use a script in the LMSFinish() function and get the value of cmi.core.session_time before resetting.
Hope this will help.

ResponsesInList.Title: cmi.core.session_time and writing cmi.core.total_time
ResponsesInList.Text: I have evidence of the situation I'm about to describe in both moodle version 2.4.4 and 2.6.4 with various different scorm 1.2 packs produced in Storyline by a number of different developers. I have access to a moodle 2.7 and could try to replicate the problem there, but at this stage I'm just trying to understand in general terms why the situation might be occurring, so that my further testing might be better focused. Situation: The scorms function as expected and have been tested in the scorm cloud and also with moodle API debugging switched on. When looking at the 'Track Details' of some students interactions with a Scorm Pack cmi.core.total_time is displayed, whilst other students have no cmi.core.total_time recorded and others have times recorded as just a few seconds. cmi.core.total_time: I understand that cmi.core.total_time is calculated by moodle, using the cmi.core.session_time that is sent by the Scorm, which I have seen in the API log. The scorms I tested send the cmi.core.session_time soon after the Scorm starts to play, and then again, just before the Scorm closes. I know that if an activity is allowed to be attempted multiple times, then moodle will add the cmi.core.session_time of a 2nd attempt to that of the cmi.core.total_time already stored. But in my situation the Scorm activity can only be actioned one time. Why the 'Track Details' are as described in the Situation. (My Logic) Clearly, if no cmi.core.session_time has been sent by the Scorm, then that will result in moodle not being able to calculate the cmi.core.total_time, hence the record does not exist in the database . Clearly if only one cmi.core.session_time (note: it's sent twice in my example) is sent, then moodle will calculate cmi.core.total_time based on that (hence some of my total times are shown as a few seconds if the cmi.core.session_time is not sent at the end of the Scorm Trying to Replicate the Situation. I've tried using different browsers, and operating systems whilst logged on as a student to try and generate a 'Track Detail' that replicates the actual students  situation I'm describing. Only once did I achieve that, and that came as a result of a 'warning - unresponsive script error' which eventually forced the browser ( Firefox latest version) to close. The script referred to was pluginfile.php/1862/mod_scorm/content/3/lms/SCORMFunctions.js:828 When this happened because the browser closed unfortunately I was unable to capture the API log. Unfortunately there are many student records in the moodle with no cmi.core.total_time shown in their 'Track Detail'. So here's My Questions What might cause a Scorm not to send the cmi.core.session_time? Could this situation simply be down to my students losing internet connection? Or.. What might cause the moodle to fail to write the cmi.core.total_time into the database if the Scorm has sent the cmi.core.session_time? Many thanks in advance for any information you might add to help me come to a conclusion with my understanding on this. Cheers

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle interpreting multi-sco package as single object
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I am running Moodle 2.8.5. I recently uploaded the same multi-sco package to my Moodle (SCORM 1.2) and to another LMS (D2L). Each learning object  within the package is a separate activity of one or more screens, designed to report an individual score and limited to one attempt. (NB: I understand it may be possible to override the attempts via Moodle's own settings - and that is not the problem here). In D2L, each activity is individually assignable and reports an individual grade to the gradebook. In Moodle, while it is possible to navigate between individual activities , these do not appear to be assignable or gradeable as Moodle 'sees' the aggregation only, i.e. the whole package is treated as a single object. Obviously I have a number of options about how the grade is calculated, but it's not an overall grade I need. I need the activities to be available and gradeable individually. I've done a bit of investigation, on this forum and elsewhere, but haven't been able to find an answer to the question of why a multi-sco package is interpreted by Moodle as a single object. My guesses are that this is either about (1) the way in which the content is packaged (i.e. Moodle DOES have the capacity to report on individual SCOs); or (2) Moodle's lack of support for SCORM 2004. Can anyone advise? Best, Cath

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle interpreting multi-sco package as single object
ResponsesInList.Text: Interesting to hear D2L have done it that way (I haven't seen this in other SCORM players myself) - in Moodle a SCORM package is a stand-alone object and the reports within the SCORM package show the information returned about the package but we only push a single grade for that package to the gradebook. To do this differently would require a significant amount of development and I'm not sure that it would be worth the effort. The easiest way to achieve a similar outcome in Moodle would be to separate it out into multiple SCORM packages and then improve the behaviour of SCORM when a user exits a package to allow them to automatically open the next SCORM package or return to the course homepage. I'd do this by adding a setting to allow the teacher to decide what happens when the user exits a scorm package for example -  return to course homepage/ dashboard /another activity in the course. This could also help to resolve MDL-44905

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle interpreting multi-sco package as single object

Does Moodle treat SCORM and Common Cartridge differently with regards to access and grading of activities e.g. one package = one gradable object? Best wishes, Cath

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Lots of white space in SCORM player
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jamie, Try adding this custom css to your theme's settings. Often this is nothing to do with the theme you are using but to do with Divs being allocated by moodle. body#page-mod- scorm -player { padding-top: 0px;} #scormtop { display: none; } This will remove the scorm top which contains the activity name and course structure in player items. Hello everyone.  I’m
having a SCORM issue – completion status is not being captured by Moodle. I am not sure if Moodle is the problem or if the software I
use to create SCORM 1.2 lessons is the problem. 
I am using iSpring Presenter (latest version).  I am using 3.2 (Build: 20161205). When an activity is properly “completed”, I noticed in the

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM activity is not "completed" but others are...
ResponsesInList.Text: For the benefit of everyone, I fixed my own problem, but this may come up again for someone else... The issue was not with Moodle.  I am using iSpring Presenter to create SCORM objects.  The software works great but if you have PowerPoint content, make sure you do not leave hidden slides in the presentation as doing so will never allow a student to "view all slides" to trigger a SCORM completion message.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Vertical scrollbar added to my SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Alberto, a lot of this is done dynamically with YUI when the SCORM package is rendered, but I've had some success in hard-coding minimum heights for the SCORM frame with the following CSS settings: #page-mod-scorm-player #scormpage { width: 1050px; height: 630px; } #page-mod-scorm-player iframe , #page-mod-scorm-player div { max-width: 1050px; max-height: 630px; min-height: 605px; } Keep in mind this will affect ALL scorm packages displayed by Moodle and this will only hard code certain values. It won't scale to the height of the actual module. If you are using modules that are very tall and involve lots of scrolling, a simpler solution may be just to have them open up in a pop-up, rather than embedding them in the Moodle page.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Vertical scrollbar added to my SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Also see this related thread around responsive SCORM in Moodle: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=339315 The short answer is there is no good solution right now without requiring the user to click the scorm link and having it open in it's own new window.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Vertical scrollbar added to my SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Alberto, I had a chance to look at the Moodle 3.2 demo site and run some tests, and the CSS code I suggested definitely does not work properly in 3.2. We're on 3.1 right now, sorry, I should have specified the version number when giving the information. You may be able to make some progress by inspecting the divs and boxes used and playing around with it. In the little time I had, I determined that most of the limitation is from the following tree: <div id="scormpage"> <div id ="tocbox"> <div id="toctree"> <div class="yui3-g-r" id="scorm_layout" style="height: 680px;"> The scorm_layout height looks to be dynamically set based on the device. For example on a high enough resolution screen (mock iPad Pro using Google Chrome Developer tools) it was set to 1000+ pixels, while on iPad portait size, 768x1024 height, it was set to 750 px. But hard-coding it in CSS will just enforce one expected screen size and may break other things, so for 3.2 I would not recommend going that route unless you know you are only targeting one device with a screen height of noless than a certain height.

ResponsesInList.Title: External SCORM Manifest over SSL Problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi. I am currently running Moodle Build 2.3.1+ (Build: 20120719) on a Windows 2008 R2 Server with SQL 2008 R2 backend database . Moodle is running under IIS 7.5 with PHP Version 5.3.13. We Run all servers under SSL to ensure maximum security. There are no exceptions to this rule. All SSL certificates are valid and correctly installed. All the following scenarios regrding external manifests are using the same manifest in the same domain as the moodle server, so there are no browser based cross site javascript issues. I am having problems with the External SCORM Manifest functionality. Create a New SCORM Module. If I run the moodle installation over HTTP (no SSL), everything works fine, ie I can create a scorm activity, type=External SCORM Manifest & link it to the scorm imsmanifest. xml file eg http://server.domain/scormlibrary/sample/imsmanifest.xml . When launching the SCORM module, everthing works as you would expect... But unencrypted access breaks our security policy so... Create another new SCORM module ( This is important ). If I run the moodle installation over HTTPS (with SSL), exactly as above with the except this time I change the url of the manifest file to https://server.domain/scormlibrary/sample/imsmanifest.xml (because the server should be serving SSL), when launching the SCORM module, you just get a grey box. The SCORM content is not working but moodle is also not producing any errors. If, I leave the configuration as above in point 2, but this time modify the url of the manifest file to run over HTTP (unsecured), the content works, but you are mixing secure & unsecure content in the browser and you get various dialog boxes. If I then change the URL for the manifest back to HTTPS again, the whole system now works over SSL as desired. On initial inspection, it feels like when Moodle is running under SSL, it is unable to read the manifest file over HTTPS, but when you change it to HTTP, the server is then able to read and cache the file. Then, when you set it back to HTTPS, it is reading the cache... I dug in a bit further and noticed that when creating a SCORM activity, there seem to be entries missing from the 'mdl_scorm_scoes' table in SQL when trying to run a SSL only installation. If you run over HTTP or start as outlined in step 2 onwards, the data eventually gets created.... Can anyone help me out? Is this a bug or am I being silly??? I'm trying to get things ready for the return of teaching staff in 2 weeks time and the external SCORM manifest is a great solution the we want to roll out to all staff. I'm not thick & have tried looking at the source code, but PHP is not my forte as I am from a .NET background and I'm really struggling trying to understand how everything works in code. Thanks Andy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External SCORM Manifest over SSL Problem
ResponsesInList.Text: When using external manifest the server itself tries to get the manifest file via https using CURL - this means PHP/Curl must have the relevant CA certs installed so it can verify the SSL cert is valid - if you're using a self signed cert this may not be possible. quick test to see if this is the issue - in mod/scorm/datamodels/scormlib.php change this: $xmltext = download_file_content($manifest); to this: $xmltext = download_file_content($manifest, null, null, false, 300, 20, true); just make sure you don't edit the file using notepad or wordpad... please... just don't.... if you don't have a text editor already try installing Notepad++ you could either leave that hack in place on your server or install the CA certs on your server and make sure PHP/Curl uses them.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External SCORM Manifest over SSL Problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dan. Thank you ever so much. That has worked. I'm not overly happy about leaving the patch in place although I will have to if I can't get this resolved. Can you explain something to me. I am using a wildcard certificate issued by globalsign and its valid and stored in the windows certificate store. I was under the impression that PHP just inherits the underlying certificate store on the operating sysem. Is this not correct? Do I have to register the cert or CA specifically with PHP? IIS seems to be using the certificate OK and we use this certificate on other servers without any issues. Any advive would be appreciated... Thanks Andy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External SCORM Manifest over SSL Problem
ResponsesInList.Text: I've managed to get things working properly now without your patch Dan. I was looking through documentation and it seems that the CURL PHP extension does not have access to the Windows certificate store. Apparently you have to provide the CURL extension with a 'CA Bundle'. This definitely affects IIS running PHP and according to some articles I was reading, it also affects Apache running on Windows Server (although I cannot confirm this as I am an IIS user). To work around this: You need to be running minimum PHP 5.3.7 ( http://uk3.php.net/manual/en/curl.configuration.php ) Download a certificate bundle from somewhere and save to somewhere on the server that the webserver will be able to access. I saved mine into the Moodle installation directory but maybe the moodledata folder might eb a better location. I used the bundle provided at http://curl.haxx.se/docs/caextract.html Create a new entry in your php.ini file called curl.cainfo and set its value to the path of your downloaded certificate bundle. eg curl.cainfo = D:\iiswebsites\moodle\cacert.pem Create a reminder for yourself to update the certificate bundle on a semi-regular basis as this config will stop working if some of the CA certificates in the bundle expire or new CA certs are issues and you don't have them in the bundle. Perhaps this issue might be addressed in the longer term through a patch or maybe distributing cert bundles with builds of Moodle or something else, but I'm not sure what kind of priority it really has. Maybe it's just a configuration task. I don't think is affects Linux or UNIX , but its definitely an issue on Windows and any SSL download requests that use the CURL functionality are going to have issues in future. Anyway, thanks for you help with this. It was much appreciated Andy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External SCORM Manifest over SSL Problem
ResponsesInList.Text: great to hear you got it sorted! older versions of PHP shipped a CA bundle with Curl but newer versions haven't done this for a while. Moodle doesn't really ship with PHP extensions/configuration - it's really up to the server admin to install a web server/php and configure it properly - Moodle does have a couple of installer packages that include apache/php but anyone who uses ssl shouldn't be using these packages to do an install anyway. But - it could be a great addition to the install docs to add something about Curl/SSL - I've run into this before with the Turnitin plugin as it connects to an https api via curl too.

ResponsesInList.Title: Captivate SCORM close button

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Captivate SCORM close button
ResponsesInList.Text: That's how it works. The Cp close button calls an action that closes the window. It isn't aware of the difference between the SCORM player window, the frame that it might be in, or the main browser window for Moodle. So if you want to use the Cp close button, I suggest setting the Moodle scorm activity to open in a new window. Then the Cp button will close that window leaving the main Moodle window in place. There is a usability issue here though if users have popups blocked. They'll get an error about blocked popups. Then they'll have to edit their browser settings to allow popup overall, or specific sites. Guess who they'll contact for help if they don't know how to do that? I went in circles on this exact issue for a while and finally decided to not use the Cp close button. Now I have an "exit slide" that says you have completed [projectname] and may now exit the activity. I use a Cp variable to insert the [projectname] Maybe even put an arrow that points to Moodle "Exit activity" link.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Captivate SCORM close button
ResponsesInList.Text: FYI - if you don't use the setting "student skip content structure page" then the pop-up is launched on user-action so pop-up blockers shouldn't get in the way.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Captivate SCORM close button

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Captivate SCORM close button
ResponsesInList.Text: Captivate isn't great at closing windows. Tends to get the level wrong. Either too high (in this case) or can be too low. Sometimes in a separate window it just closes the frame not the window. Leaving a blank window open. I've found the most consistent solution is to do a separate window and as Dan says skip the course structure. Then set any close buttons in your captivate file to call close.htm which contains this script. You need to unzip copy in close.htm and rezip you scorm after publishing. <html xmlns=" http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml " xml :lang="en" lang="en"> <head> <script type="text/javascript" language="JavaScript"> window.parent.close(); </script> </body> </html>

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Articulate Storyline Resource issue
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Gabor, we recently encountered something similar. What we determined was that the Articulate file had changed hands between two different users, one who had the linked PDF files on their hard drive while working with the Articulate file (and who had created the links to the files on their hard drive); and a second user who did not have the PDF files on their hard drive. When the file was saved by the second user and then handed back to the first user. When the SCORM was re-published by the first user, the resource links did not function and produced a 404. So the links had been broken by the Storyline file being opened and re-saved by a user who did not have the PDF files present (upon inspection we realized that the PDF files were not included in the SCORM package at all). The solution was for the first user to re-link the resource links to the PDFs and then re-publish. That brought the PDFs along in the SCORM package. Hope that info helps you out! ~ Jennifer

ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM, Learning Object Grade and Completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I'm having a peculiar behaviour regarding a SCORM activity completion, and I don't understand if it's due to a misconfiguration, a wrong understanding of mine, or some kind of bug in Moodle (3.1). I have a SCORM package made of two SCOs. Both are setting the cmi.core.lesson_status, but not the cmi.core.score.raw (we are just interested in the completion). I want the SCORM package to be tracked as completed only once both SCOs are completed. In order to do so I read the SCORM FAQ: SCORM and the Gradebook , and ended up with this configuration: Grade => Grading Method set to Learning objects ; Activity completion => Completion tracking set to Show activity as complete when conditions are met; Activity completion => Require Grade set to Student must receive a grade to complete this activity ; Activity completion => Require minimum score set to 2 (the number of SCOs that I have), and unchecked Disable . The logic seems sound to me. Then, I completed the SCORM package with a user, and noticed the score is correctly set to 2: Even though the score was correct, the SCORM package was still marked as not completed: This seems related to this post . The only solution given was to rework the SCORM structure so as to make it only composed of one SCO, which is not a possible scenario in this case. Any idea about where the problem is here?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM, Learning Object Grade and Completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Update: by looking into the code, I think I've found a part of my answer: it was indeed a bad understanding of mine, surely not helped by the tooltips. The problem is that the score is simply the score reported by the SCORM package. Since no cmi.core.score.raw was ever given, the score was never set, and the condition never met. The grading mechanism is separated, and cannot be used in the completion logic. Can anyone confirm my findings? Does anyone see a workaround for the situation?

So to the point of the discussion, I've come across this admin setting "Enable SCORM 1.2 standard mode"... @Site administration > Plugins > Activity modules > learning module. Where it enabled by default (ticked), it states the following.. " Disabling this setting allows Moodle to store more data than the SCORM 1.2 specification allows. If your SCORM packages allow users to enter large amounts of text or if your package tries to store large amounts of data in the suspend_data field disable this." In the Moodle SCORM 2.7 documentation is expands with: " If this setting is disabled, then it will be possible to exceed the allowed amount of stored data for SCORM 1.2 packages. Many SCORM packages go over the 4096 characters limit and while SCORM 2004 allows a higher number of characters, it is not supported. This setting will mean users can allow their 1.2 packages to store more data." Am I correct in saying my Moodle 2.7 site, where I run only SCORM 1.2 packages, that it would be wise to untick the box and (therefore would disable it?)? This has been a controversial topic at my workplace, as a specialist of Moodle advised us to keep it ticked (enabled) as "It only applies to SCORM 2004". Many thanks, Alex

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Admin settings - "Enable SCORM 1.2 standard mode" definite meaning
ResponsesInList.Text: The SCORM 1.2 specification sets some limits on the amount of data that different variables can store. This means that when complying with the standards if a SCORM package tries to store more than the allowed amount of data the LMS must return an error. Good examples of this are "suspend_data" and student responses to quiz questions. These bits of data can often go over the limit that the SCORM 1.2 spec defines and this often occurs with packages developed by the major well-known authoring tools. The biggest issue when this occurs with "suspend_data" is that when a student returns to a previous attempt it can't resume where they left off last as the suspend_data is not complete. When this occurs with student responses, the data is not stored. Sometimes these errors can cause other failures within the SCORM package as they do not always have good error handling implemented within the packages. Many people publish their basic SCORM packages as SCORM 2004 to get around these limits because the SCORM 2004 standard has much higher data limits on the same variables, but Moodle doesn't provide full support for SCORM 2004 (particularly the sequencing and navigation component of SCORM 2004) By un-ticking this box Moodle won't return an error state when your SCORM package tries to store more data than the 1.2 spec allows, it will accept the data and allow your SCORM to function as you expected it to in the first place. This setting affects SCORM 1.2 packages and allows them to work as expected by the teacher - I tend to disable standards mode on all our clients sites, I think the only reason I would enable standards mode would be to allow us to run Moodle through the official ADL compliance tests. It's possible that in a future version of Moodle we might have it disabled by default. Hopefully that helps?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Admin settings - "Enable SCORM 1.2 standard mode" definite meaning
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dan I've just stumbled across this setting and it sounds extremely useful, particularly for people who feel the need to have very lengthy courses in Articulate/Storyline/Captivate as such modules can easily be made to exceed the standard 4096bytes of storage that the SCORM 1.2 spec allows. My question is: when this option is unchecked, what is the new upper limit on suspend_data storage? Is there any hidden setting for controlling what that is or is it simply the limit set on whatever field in the database the suspend_data is stored in?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Admin settings - "Enable SCORM 1.2 standard mode" definite meaning
ResponsesInList.Text: it extends the items restricted to 256 and 4096 by the SCORM 1.2 spec to 64000 (the highest value allowed in the SCORM 2004 spec) https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/master/mod/scorm/datamodels/scorm_12.php#L45 at some point we should probably make the default value for that set to "off" for new installs - the only reason I can think of for it to be turned on is if you are running the ADL SCORM compliance tests.

ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM Alerts
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello I'm running Moodle 2.7 and my students are complaining about constant SCORM alerts "The SCORM player has detected ..." Is there a quick and easy way to disable this function. Usually there is nothing they can do about their connection. This alert comes and goes constantly distracting them. Any tips would be very much appreciated. Tim

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Alerts
ResponsesInList.Text: Those alerts are there for a reason. If they have flakey internet conectivity then it is likely that the SCORM content might display in their browser but any progress/grade they achieve may not be saved/passed back to Moodle - even if the SCORM package displays a succesful score or completion. In previous versions of Moodle this failed silently in the background with no warning provided to the user. If you have users with flakey internet connectivity you should not use SCORM or you should advise your students to use a computer that has reliable internet connection when using SCORM packages.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Alerts
ResponsesInList.Text: I also have many suspicions about those alerts, and I tend to believe they report a lot of "false positive". While I was testing SCORM packages on iPad, they hapened to pop up continuously on the iPad, while I did not get anything on a workstation at the same time. This was in an office with a good connection and with a perfectly operating Wifi...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Alerts
ResponsesInList.Text: If your server performs badly it could also cause the reports - there's a 2 second timeout value associated with those requests - it uses javascript to check for the file '/lib/yui/build/moodle-core-checknet/assets/checknet.txt' - if it can't access that file it assumes that the network is unavailable. I can't see how that would give false positive reports - the fact you are seeing the errors suggests that network connectivity or server performance is an issue. If the network is definitely ok - you need to check the performance of your server - a 2 second delay when requesting a text file suggests that your server is not coping well. SCORM needs network connectivity - intermittent network issues or bad server performance can result in grades or completion tracking silently failing.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Alerts
ResponsesInList.Text: Just to follow up on this issue. At the moment these warnings are here to stay - the warnings occur as the communication between the SCORM package and Moodle are failing and this means that grades and tracking information from the user will be lost. I have not been able to reproduce this on my own iPad when connecting to my local machine or when connecting to an externally hosted site. I suspect the reason you are seeing this more frequently is due to one of the following: Wifi access is flaky Connection between your wireless network and your moodle server is flaky or slow and the iPad times out when trying to communicate. iPad specific bug related to network connections dropping and re-connecting. SCORM requires a reliable internet connection with the Moodle server to function correctly. We MUST warn users if tracking data is going to be lost - we are always getting reports like "my students tell me that they sat the SCORM but it didn't record the score - what happened?" - My preference would be to halt access to the SCORM completely when this warning occurs so if anything we may make it more difficult to continue accessing the SCORM rather than removing the warning. Of course - if someone manages to trace/diagnose this issue as being a bug with Moodle code and provides a patch to improve it I'm more than happy to take another look.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Alerts
ResponsesInList.Text: Dan, I can say with confidence this is not just a Moodle issue with SCORM sessions being lost.  We have had it reported by our clients using commercial LMS systems as well, and WiFi connections seem to be the worst.  The strange part is, that though the SCORM session is lost the learnercan continue through the course which means they still have a connection to the server.  This seems to point to an lower tolerance to connection problems in the SCORM players then a typical browser connection. However, this new feature in Moodle is keeping us from upgrading to the latest Moodle.  I know the intent behind the fix, though I don't exactly agree with the implementation.  I would much rather have had this reported to the SCORM SCO as an error and then let the SCO decide what to do with the error. Personally I would like to have the option of disabling this error checking/message as an administrator until a different fix can be identified and implemented. Until then, for those encountering the message frequently, take a look at your firewall logs to see if it is interpreting the communication as a threat (e.g. flood) and temporarily blocking the device.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Alerts
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ron, The problem with allowing the user to continue working on the package even though LMS communication has failed is that they expect to get credit for their interaction with the SCORM and get a grade reported in the LMS - If they don't need a grade then it shouldn't be published as a SCORM package. IMO it is absolutely imperative that we display big warnings when this occurs - the number of support calls I've seen with users reporting they did something with a SCORM package but it didn't report the grade at the end is hard enough when you have review/preview mode to contend with let alone dodgy wifi connections. You do raise an interesting point about the firewall interpreting the communication as a threat though - it would be interesting to hear if anyone finds this is an issue.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Alerts
ResponsesInList.Text: As mentioned previously - I understand the frustration people have with this error but it's here to stay at this stage. SCORM requires a reliable/stable internet connection, if the checknet script is failing it means that the javascript in browser cannot communicate with the server. This means that tracking data cannot be saved. If you don't require tracking data you should be using the IMS resource or another method for including your SCORM package on the site. It is possible we could improve this check but it's not going to be removed from core and I don't plan to add a feature to allow people to disable it in core. Of course you are welcome to modify the code on your own site. Paul - feel free to submit a patch to improve the way the check works - I'm happy to decrease the frequency of the alerts after the first initial alert but my personal thoughts were to completely block access to the SCORM package if an unreliable internet connection is found (although I won't enforce that in core)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Alerts
ResponsesInList.Text: Whilst I am not in favour of making changes to the core, if you wish to reduce the frequency of these notifications, rather than turning them off completely, you should be able to do this by editing the moodle-core-checknet.js file.  This is found in "moodle/lib/yui/build/moodle-core-checknet/moodle-core-checknet.js.  The default is to display the warning every ten second (10000 milliseconds). I would think a safe setting is 5 minutes.  The user will still be notified of the problem, but at least it will not popup so often.  Modify line 160 as follows: change "value: 10000" to "value: 300000".  You may increase this number to meet your needs.  Ideally this is better done using a local plugin rather than changing the core.  Otherwise your settings are overwritten when you update your installation. /** * The frequency (in milliseconds) that checks should be run. * A new check is not begun until the previous check has completed. * * @attribute frequency * @writeOnce * @type Number * @value 10000 */ frequency: { value: 300000 }, /**

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Alerts
ResponsesInList.Text: you can't override this using a plugin - we increased the values in 2.8.8, 2.9.2 and higher versions ( MDL-49647 ) to a 4 second timeout and a re-test every 10 seconds. If your server is regularly taking longer than 4 seconds to return a simple text file from the server this is a much bigger issue and IMO you should not be modifying the code and "ignoring" the issue. SCORM requires a fast/reliable internet connection and a fast/reliable server otherwise bad stuff happens... and it's a real pain to diagnose and track down! Of course that doesn't help you much if you're using the 2.7 branch which still uses the older values (2 second timeout, 5 second re-test) so you will need to modify the core code. here's the full patch applied to the 2.8 and 2.9 branches: 552281e46

ResponsesInList.Title: Completion tracking with Storyline Module
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a number of course modules that are produced in Articulate Storyline 2. They are output as web packages and not as SCORM because we had previously found that there were problems with SCORM tracking. There are no quizzes to track in these modules, but we want to make sure people complete them fully. We have made future activities dependent on people completing the previous ones. However we have discovered that as soon as someone clicks on the Storyline package to open it up, Moodle marks the activity as complete. They don't actually have to go through the whole module. They can just click on it and then immediately exit it and Moodle will mark it complete. I don't think we can re-make these modules as SCORM packages because we have many people that have already completed them and their certificates are dependent on those activities being completed as they were already done. Does anyone have any good ideas or solutions to make sure people complete this whole instructional module in Storyline and have Moodle only mark it complete it they have finished the whole thing?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Completion tracking with Storyline Module
ResponsesInList.Text: Phil's already given you some good advice here: https://community.articulate.com/discussions/articulate-storyline/moodle-completion-tracking-challenge in short - make sure you have all updates applied to your version of Articulate, and that you are running a recent supported version of Moodle. (not an old unsupported version that hasn't been upgraded in a long time) - then Just use SCORM.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Completion tracking with Storyline Module
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Dan: The challenge now is how to change this in mid-stream. We have 1000s of people that have already completed the non-SCORM modules and their completion certificates are all tied to completion of these activities. If I load up new SCORM modules and tie the completion certificate to them instead, we'll have some people caught in the middle that are halfway through the course with the old modules and we could create a mass headache for tracking completion of these two different versions of the activities. Any idea how to get around that part? This wouldn't be such a big deal if the enrollment numbers were smaller, but we'll eventually have about 26,000 people going through this course.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Completion tracking with Storyline Module
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Whitney, one way to handle this is you backup the course without user data, then restore the course with a new name and in that version you replace the modules to all use SCORM packages. Then start putting new enrollments into this new copy. When people finish the old one, you close it out/archive it, or simply leave it as the 'previous' version. In our organization we have a 'template' course we maintain that doesn't have any users in it that we make and test changes in. Once we are happy to have users going through that version of the course, we backup and restore it, and enroll users into it. When there's a new version or major changes need to be made, another version is spun off, and users are enrolled into that one instead.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Completion tracking with Storyline Module

Our big challenge is that we have continuously rolling enrollments and people self-enroll in the course, so getting them to move over to the new course and not in the old course could be confusing and challenging. We do have a sandbox version of the course that we use to test everything as you mentioned and perhaps we can find a smooth way to make this transition. Thanks for the ideas!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Notice popping up
ResponsesInList.Text: SCORM requires a reliable stable connection - the SCORM player makes regular checks to see if it can communicate with the Moodle server - when this communication fails (or is too slow) it will throw that error. It happens a lot on flakey wifi or with intermittent 3G access.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Notice popping up
ResponsesInList.Text: if you're using an old version of Moodle that hasn't been updated to the latest stable version of that release (I hope not) - in particular any version prior to 2.7.8 or 2.8.6 then we found this check was a little more aggressive than it needed to be and adjusted the values. If you are already using a Moodle version higher than those numbers it's not a problem with "Moodle" - it's a problem with your hosting/network or the users local connection. many areas of Moodle will function fine on unreliable or slow networks... unfortunately SCORM is not one of those.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Disabling/Hiding TOC
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Mark, "Is it possible to disable this feature from within the SCORM package?" Yes. The setting for this feature is located inside the SCORM package activity itself. Try this; Go to your SCORM package>Edit Settings>Appearance> Show more link (it's inside the Appearance setting)> Display course structure in player. Set this to " Disabled ." ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Replacing SCORM content
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there, I think I have a solution for you. First, make sure you've re-exported the SCORM package using the same SCORM ID numbers. I think these ID numbers should by default remain the same in pretty much any development tool -- I know they do in Captivate. In Moodle, click the Edit link to the right of the SCORM package's name on the course page. On the Edit settings page that appears, drag and drop the updated SCORM package onto the "Package file" window to replace the old SCORM package. As long as the SCORM IDs are the same you should retain the previous student data. HTH , Jon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 回應: Re: Replacing SCORM content
ResponsesInList.Text: 2) If they are different, can I just revise it through Notepad? To that the answer is partially yes, you need to check the cpm.js file, the manifest, and the corresponding tables. Hope that helps

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 回應: Re: Replacing SCORM content
ResponsesInList.Text: The easy answer to your question is to find out if the original "source" file used to create the published SCORM package was updated (as opposed to an entirely new replacement source file being created). If that was the case, it probably won't matter which development tool was used. I know that Captivate won't arbitrarily change the SCORM IDs as long as you reuse the original file.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 3.02+:  Student skip content structure page = Always is not working
ResponsesInList.Text: are you logged in as a "student" - it's called " student skip content structure page" because it only works for "students" - not teachers/admins. This is because the only way to get to the reports page is from the initial structure page with the "enter" button, so if it skipped for teachers/admins they would not be able to find the link to access the reports page. - or are you trying to hide the content structure that shows while the student is inside the scorm package?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 3.02+:  Student skip content structure page = Always is not working
ResponsesInList.Text: you are probably using the Single activity course format - the "always" option is not supported when you use that because the content structure page is also the course homepage, which users are returned to on completion of the SCORM and you would end up in a redirect loop. There is a request in MDL-44905 to improve it further so that it redirects to the site homepage instead. That request has also been in the tracker for quite a while and not very many people have voted on it or expressed interest in getting it done.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: improvisation of scorm files performance, reducing the loading time.
ResponsesInList.Text: It is my understanding that there are a couple factors in how long it take to load up a scorm.  Of course, some of it has to do with how the server stuff is set up and the amount of memory the computer opening it has but the biggest factor is the size of the scorm. I have scorms that are small (less than 10 MB) and some that are very large (more than 300 mb).  The large ones take a longer time to load than the small ones.  SCORMs with video and audio take longer to load.  There are things you can do in some authoring tools to minimize this (in Captivate you can select the amount of the project loads before view) but it all comes down to the size of your package and the capacity of your computer. You could try breaking big modules into smaller parts.

ResponsesInList.Title: Setting anchors inside SCORM files
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Guys, I am working on a Moodle project which offers SCORM content for students. We are adding a SCORM file for each chapter in a course. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Setting anchors inside SCORM files
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Saravanakumar, you can't with SCORM 1.2: a SCORM 1.2 Package containing more than a SCO must be navigated through the TOC since there are internal logics like SCORM 1.2 Prerequisites that are taking into account before giving the User the next route. SCORM 2004 is supposed to enrich such logics by giving you the possibility to interact with the navigation (read: sequencing ) but Moodle officially supports SCORM 1.2 even though some of the SCORM 2004 features have been already implemented - unfortunately for you, full sequencing compliance is pending and it will be no more completed . It's up to you whether to decide for not giving that possibility to your users or to check for the level of the SCORM 2004 support in Moodle to explore the implemented features or to find some hacks strictly related with the code of a particular Moodle version i.e. sticking with that w/o upgrading it - e.g. Moodle 2.6 is supposed to heavily change the SCORM TOC code. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Setting anchors inside SCORM files
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Saravanakumar, if you're in need to create hyperlink-ed contents, in a inter-SCO way of thinking, I think you should use e.g. Book instead of SCORM: SCOs, the items composing a SCORM Package (PIF), are supposed to be self-contained for both instructional and technical POVs - the 'R' in SCORM means Reusable! - so on providing inter-SCO hyperlinks you're coupling SCOs when they are supposed to be loosely coupled. That's the reason why you find nothing in SCORM 1.2 and just a simple prev/next in SCORM 1.3 (2004 n-th edition). Regarding with your upgrade issues I'm not able to give you any advice but that 2.4 => 2.5 is quite documented in files called upgrade.txt , each of them contained in the folder of a block, module, theme, etc etc: you should identify the tables you're directly accessing to, identify the Moodle components those tables are belonging to and track back the changes required by each component: many of them, on average, should impact less on database structures. Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: mod_scorm_mod_form typo fix
mod_scorm_mod_form::data_preprocessing() called twice
ResponsesInList.Text:
Moodle version:  3.0.2 I should make this
suggestion as a Moodle Tracker issue. 
But, new user signup there is currently disabled.  So, I mention in here before I forget. The mod_scorm_mod_form
class ( vide moodle\mod\scorm\mod_form.php ) derives from the moodleform_mod
class ( vide moodle\course\moodleform_mod.php ).  mod_scorm_mod_form overrides the set_data()
function, and does the following. Make some changes to the given $defaultvalues. Call data_preprocessing(), which is an override of the parent's
data_preprocessing() but does not call the parent function. Call parent::set_data(). However, in the parent
moodleform_mod::set_data(), data_preprocessing() is also called. This results in
mod_scorm_mod_form::data_preprocessing() being called twice.   I think that this is unnecessary, and I
suggest the following changes. Do not call data_preprocessing() in mod_scorm_mod_form::set_data(). The rest of what mod_scorm_mod_form::set_data() does is make
changes to the given $defaultvalues. 
Thus, it could be moved to mod_scorm_mod_form::data_preprocessing. That leaves mod_scorm_mod_form::set_data() with nothing to do.  Thus, it can be eliminated. Another result of the
current code is that the parent moodleform_mod::data_preprocessing() is never
called.  There could be a good reason why
it should not be called when editing a SCORM activity.  But if not, then I additionally suggest the following
changes. In mod_scorm_mod_form::data_preprocessing(), call
parent::data_preprocessing(), likely at the beginning of the function.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: RLO - creating a reusable SCORM activity / object
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Matt, Great question... However, in terms of 'preferred of easier' it's hard to cull a straightforward answer because of the variety of ways to structure reusable courses using SCORM with Moodle.  However, much depends on the authoring tool you use to create the courses; the critical difference being how each communicates SCORM parameters.  I will note that your creating 'small SCORM courses' is vitally important and a great first step in terms of managing and tracking SCOs between courses. Further, keep in mind that: SCORM 2004 is not supported in Moodle. Parts of the API have been implemented, but others such as Navigation and Sequencing have not. https://docs.moodle.org/30/en/SCORM_FAQ#Supported_Versions The path to an answer is likely to be more curvy than straight. I'm sure other comments will make it less so! Peace

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Increasing CHECKNET SCORM alerts
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm surprised to see so much effort put into this... upgrading your site would increase the timeout values (and we haven't had the same number of false-positives with the higher values) - If you have upgraded and are still getting these pop-up warnings you should really focus on what is causing the problem at your server (rather than hiding the problem by increasing the values.) SCORM requires a stable/reliable internet connection. If your server doesn't provide this you should fix it or find another hosting solution. If your users need offline-access to SCORM packages or in areas where internet connectivity is not good you should look at using the Moodle mobile app which provides offline support for SCORM. Whenever you change Moodle code files you should perform appropriate testing to ensure it works as expected - yes you should clear the cache. Yes you should implement some form of backup procedure.. If these things are difficult you should probably not be changing the code.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Increasing CHECKNET SCORM alerts
ResponsesInList.Text: If you are only changing the files related to checknet timings the changed files are probably the only ones you really need to backup but you should really be running some form of regular off-site backup of your database and moodledata.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Increasing CHECKNET SCORM alerts
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Vaishak, purging the cache only effects the caching part of the moodledata directory, which is meant to be disposable anyways. When I was doing this, I can confirm all I did was update the files as you mention in part 1, and purge the cache via the Moodle admin interface. In terms of restoring from this, you would only need to restore the changed files you mention in part 1, and re-purge the cache. Seperately as Dan said, you should be backing up moodledata regularly, 3,2,1 backup methodology recommended. Veeam has a good post about this, you don't need to be using their software to do it though: https://www.veeam.com/blog/how-to-follow-the-3-2-1-backup-rule-with-veeam-backup-replication.html We rsync to a secondary server daily, and then do a tape backup of that periodically. So we have 3 locations (tape backup, backup server and live), two media (server hdd and tape) and one copy stored offsite (tape).

ResponsesInList.Title: Scorm: Reporting Attempts
ResponsesInList.Text: Is there any reason why in reports, SCORM will only show 1 attempt irrespective of how many you attempted. So if you completed 3 times, it still only shows 1 attempt. Is this rectified in SCORM settings in Moodle, or is it based on the package that designed the SCORM ie Articulate. It would be good to see results from all attempts, or certainly the top 3.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm: Reporting Attempts
ResponsesInList.Text: SCORM is designed to allow multiple re-entries into the same single attempt. It is up to your SCORM package to define when an attempt is finished. Then the SCORM spec states that we need to let the user re-enter the old attempt in "review mode" or allow them to create a new attempt. More info here: https://docs.moodle.org/en/SCORM_FAQ#Handling_of_Multiple_Attempts

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm: Reporting Attempts
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you so much for this Dan. Also the very prompt reply!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm: Reporting Attempts
ResponsesInList.Text: Dan and I have had a long discussion about this in another thread (and we agreed to disagree!). It is to do with what moodle counts as an attempt. Moodle counts each opening of the scorm object as an attempt. Where as captivate (and other authoring tools I believe) count each run through of of the module as an attempt. For a fuller (and duller) description of this with examples please see https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=206692&parent=1294716

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM not updating gradebook on some records
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi William, you should try to create a test environment in which you are able to replicate your issues and then you should describe those replication steps and share some of your packages. Indeed, unless an issue can be replicated, it will be difficult for any developer to work on it; you should share your Moodle version too. Based on what I've read in this forum and via PMs since years, there are some situations for some packages in which the quiz provides 0 as score and a status which are not what expected from a learning POV and usually people think at an LMS issue before a Content or a User's context issue. The fact that you've Completed and Incomplete with 0 means that you don't have a mastery score, as you've already told; otherwise, that status must be changed by the LMS according with the threshold, mostly as failed , ONLY IF the content will nicely close the tracking session via a specific API call, LMSFinish() . " 0 + Not attempted " could be an issue with the content or the way the user is used to close the browser i.e. maybe after having closed the connection to the network. If I was you, I'd start collecting data from the affected users e.g. network connection, browser, OS, browser add-ins, firewall, any other software/device configuration which could affect browsing a site via HTTP to search for some common situations to be replicated on my PC. Then, you can watch what the content tells to the LMS from the "replicated user context" by activating the SCORM debugging in Moodle, https://docs.moodle.org/28/en/SCORM_FAQ#Debugging: see https://docs.moodle.org/28/en/SCORM_FAQ#Debugging . This will tell you if the Content is missing something when talking - or telling much more than expected - to the LMS or the LMS has a bug since it misses to process a statement from the Content. For Community ref.: the OP has raised an issue into the Tracker, MDL-48767 . HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Link to specific slides within a SCORM activity
ResponsesInList.Text: Perhaps I will be corrected but as far as I can see that wouldn't be possible due to the way scorm works. When you access a scorm module moodle checks if there is any resume data for that user and goes back to their last point in the content. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM and GoDaddy hosting
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ryan, It sounds like you may have two different problems. The "warning: slash argumentsis disabled..." has to do with the fact that your results are being saved in a database (probably called mySQL ) that has a syntax (language) that can break (or cause other malicious things to happen) unless information is passed to it in a certain form . PHP has certain commands to pass this information to my SQL and has various ways to give it the information it needs (such as commands like "mysql_real_escape_strings", etc.) depending on the  version of PHP. However a 404 error (or server redirect error) is not one typically caused by a database error in sending/recieving information. These are usually caused by server issues  and are sent by what are known as "header files" or as a result of writing data into what is called a session (ie: something like a security breach that triggers a re-direct). I would see if the folks at GoDaddy support can pull your server  errors logs and start there. My thoughts anyway. Hope that helped. Wade

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM and GoDaddy hosting
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Wade - that's not correct. Slash arguments is a Moodle setting that relates to how files are loaded in the url - it has nothing to do with how things are saved in the db. SCORM forces the use of slash arguments as it doesn't work correctly without it - so it displays a warning in Moodle when it is disabled. Godaddy hosts by default don't support the use of slash arguments which is why the 404 error is given. - we even have a (very popular) FAQ item specifically about godaddy hosts: http://docs.moodle.org/en/SCORM_FAQ#SCORM_doesn.27t_work_on_Godaddy_Host a php.ini or php5.ini file must be created and located in the correct place on your site with the detail provided in that FAQ to allow godaddy hosts to support Slash arguments. If this doesn't work - it's likely you have the file in the wrong place, named incorrectly or the content of the file is incorrect.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Microsoft SCORM Package works with Firefox, but not with Internet Explorer
ResponsesInList.Text:
Not sure if you have resolved this but we have experienced several problems with SCORM 1.2 packages that were created by a tool and use Flash.  They seem to run fine in IE 7 & 8, but have problems with IE 9+. What we found as a work-around for these types of courses is to modify the them to add a meta tag at the beginning of the header section to set IE compatibility.  In our case, we have all SCORM course set to open in a new window so we were able to only apply it to the popup style in the theme.  The line of code we used is: 
```text
<meta http-equiv="X-UA-Compatible" content="IE=8" />
```
 If you need to force IE 7 compatibility, just change the IE=9 to IE=7.  The drawback to using this work-around is that we have found that it will break some themes.   For us, that meant we always launch SCORM courses in a new window and modify the theme to have a specific style for pop-up.  If a theme does not have a specific popup style, we copy one of the existing ones and modify it only and then change the config.php to use it. To find out which file in your theme to modify... In the theme folder, locate the theme you are using. Open config.php and locate the popup layout.  It will look something like: 
```text
'popup' => array(       


'file' => 'general.php',        


'regions' => array(),        


'options' => array('nofooter'=>true, 'noblocks'=>true, 'nonavbar'=>true),
```
 This example shows that it points to general.php Open the file (general.php) in a text editor Locate where it writes out <head> Add a line with the meta tag for IE compatibility. Save the file Hope that helps.

ResponsesInList.Text: Not sure if this is relevant, but we have noticed with SCORM modules that at least when embedded in the current page, what Moodle is doing is creating an iframe for the start page of the module. This will normally be an html page such as index.html. We have issues with the way Storytime modules play that are due to the html in that page.
