ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Emergency help needed with dreaded "unable to acquire LMS API" error!
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Ben, that is true but only if the settings in your php.ini file exceed the default IIS value ( 30000000 bytes i.e. about 28.6MB ). In that case you need to configure maxAllowedContentLength globally via http://support.microsoft.com/kb/942074 or locally by adding a Web.config file like the one below: 
```text
<system.webServer>


    <security>


        <requestFiltering>


            <requestLimits 
maxAllowedContentLength
="
524288000
"/>


        </requestFiltering>


    </security>
```
 HTH, Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Emergency help needed with dreaded "unable to acquire LMS API" error!
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Rick, just look at the display settings in the SCORM activity, https://docs.moodle.org/22/en/SCORM_settings#Display_settings , Display package - in current or new window . I've read about the popup setting straight from the logs inside the document you've attached in the post above: 
```text
34:Sat Mar 7 00:18:17 EST 2015 - In SCORM_ScanParentsForApi, win=
https://lms.preparis.com/mod/scorm/player.php?scoid=114&cm=93&
;
display=popup
```
 The strange thing is that you've several "errors" which cannot be related with a small change in the php.ini file like upload file size and even they started together even if not related... SCORM is affected by the so called Cross-Domain Issue which is due to the actual nature of the SCORM API being based on JavaScript : you can't host your content out of the domain hosting the SCORM API i.e. you need to host the files inside the LMS from which you access the content. That being said, again it is strange that you've falled into the cross-domain issue after changing the upload file size: what do you mean when you say that the Content is launched from domain A while the LMS is hosted in domain B? Do you mean that in your domain A you've links to the SCORM activities hosted in your domain B? That is legal and it should work: users will click on links pointing to domain B, another site. Do you mean that the raw files are hosted in domain A and you've published a skinny SCORM package in domain B using absolute URLs in the imsmanifest. xml file? In this case you'll fall in the Cross-Domain Issue and that is true regardless the upload size set in the php.ini file. I'm running out of ideas. HTH, Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Second attempt on a SCORM course in 2.8 goes to review mode
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm working with an organisation whose Moodle site is made entirely of SCORM courses, created in Articulate. Their clients have unlimited attempts on the courses, but when they go to replay for the second time the SCORM doesn't play and it shows Review Mode at the top left of the screen. They don't want to force new attempt either. Any ideas?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Second attempt on a SCORM course in 2.8 goes to review mode
ResponsesInList.Text: The SCORM 1.2 specification states that once a package has a lesson_status of: Completed, passed, failed Then the current attempt has finished. Re-entry to the SCORM package should allow either a new attempt to be generated or the existing previous attempt to be entered into review mode. If the SCORM content structure page is being displayed and the user enters the SCORM again they will see a checkbox under the enter button that allows them to enter and generate a new attempt. If this checkbox is not ticked it will enter in review mode. If you are using the student skip content structure page setting then your students will not see the enter button or the checkbox so to make sure a new attempt is generated you must enable "force new attempt" hopefully that helps to clarify.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Second attempt on a SCORM course in 2.8 goes to review mode

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What is the best  Scorm Package Size in Moodle 2.7?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hmm, maybe a good bet is to choose one of the HD "standards", especially the 720x480?. They are often referred to in terms of a p number like 720p etc.  Just found this blog here that systematizes some things, hopefully correctly http://forum.doom9.org/showthread.php?t=171390 I quote: "720 pixel width is just SD video ('old school' DVD resolution  ). 720x480, using the 'p' designation, it's 480p. SD = 480p (assuming progressive), 720x480 if using the full screen (aka, DVD) 'Full HD' = 1080p, 1920x1080 if using the full screen (aka, Blu-ray) (1920x[something smaller] if letterboxing is cropped off) 720p is an in-between resolution of HD (1280x720 if using the full screen, same as above). Frequently used for HD broadcast, but even those are now getting bumped up to 1080.... So a 1920x800, while technically isn't 1080 pixels high, is still considered '1080p' by most people, likewise for 720p and 480p. Though anything in the 720x480 range is usually just called SD." Among other "standards" there's the mentioned 800x600 and more: 640x480 800x600 Small HD - 854 x 480 Medium HD - 1024 x 576 Full HD - 1280 x 720 Not sure all of this is relevant, but may be useful. IF you want the scorm to be accessible on mobiles, maybe there is an option in your package to self adjust to the screen? This way if you use new window / pop-up window option especially, it should auto re-scale. iSpring Presenter can do this, for example. I'm not really an expert on these things. The above are some notes I've made also for myself

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle does not play videos embeded in SCORM course on iPad
ResponsesInList.Text: Here's a question to help with troubleshooting.. Have you tried it on an Android device? Does it work there? Have you tried uploading the SCORM to SCORM Cloud or to the http://demo.moodle.net/ site? That way you can isolate issues with your own network or scorm package from Moodle. The way Apple coded it, iPads and iPhones don't download entire movies, they ask for chunks of it at a time and stream them. http://blog.sallarp.com/why-your-video-refuse-to-play-on-ipad-iphone/ Make sure your server and the firewalls inbetween support byte-range requests, which will involve getting your IT team involved. Some more info around that: http://support.microsoft.com/kb/922330 You may experience this problem if a computer is behind a firewall or behind a proxy server. This problem occurs if one of the following conditions is true: The proxy server environment does not support the HTTP 1.1 range request feature. You are behind a SonicWALL firewall device, and the Enable HTTP Byte-Range request with Gateway AV setting is not enabled for the device.

ResponsesInList.Text: yes - Amy has a patch that I keep meaning to look at properly that could help prevent this from being an issue - see MDL-28261 for the details.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle timeout preventing SCORM completion?
ResponsesInList.Text:
We're getting reports that the session timeout preventing a SCORM package from being completed is still happening in Moodle 2.7 - it seems MDL-28261 doesn't fully solve the session timeout problem. One of our clients had this to say on the matter: "I've established that the primary cause of the failure in datamodel.php
and prereqs.php is the call to confirm_sesskey(), if you remove that so
the line becomes if(!empty($scoid)) { then the problem
goes away, so clearly the session key being passed as part of the
request is from the original session when the SCORM activity was
launched, but as they have now logged back in whilst in our course (due
to one of the course frames requesting a page/file from the server after
the timeout) the 10 character session key has changed (I thought it
wasn't supposed to?) and now no longer matches the original session key.
If the re-login picked up the original session key this wouldn't be a
problem. There is also another related issue here in that if due
to the browser caching the first request to the server post-timeout
happens to be datamodel.php then it redirects to the login page, because
of the requires_login(); line. However this is blatently a daft thing
to do on an AJAX call where the user will never see the resulting page. How
Moodle handles this is to simply throw a SCORM general exception error
message which actually isn't that useful because we don't know what
caused it. If it threw an explicit login exception we could react in the
course by requesting a page which the user would see (popup iframe or
something that would be redirected to login) and once logged in close
it, then retry the LMSCommit call to store the data."

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Expected behavior when user logs out without exiting activity?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Sorry for the necro post, but this is the google result for the problem and I've found a solution that works for us. In the theme's config.php file, adjust the incourse array from: 
```text
    'incourse' => array(


        'file' => 'general.php',


        'regions' => array('side-pre', 'side-post'),


        'defaultregion' => 'side-pre',


    ),
```
 to 
```text
    'incourse' => array(


        'file' => 'general.php',


        'options' => array('nologinlinks'=>true),


        'regions' => array('side-pre', 'side-post'),
```
 i.e. add the options array (or add nologinlinks to the existing array if you have one) This will remove the "(Log out)" link in the header and footer of the page while in a course, so the student can't log out without exiting the activity and hence don't generate the error where the javascript is attempting to write to a closed connection.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: scorm db tables
ResponsesInList.Text: whatgrade and updatefreq are both fields in the scorm table - most of the fields from the scorm table are from the scorm settings page when adding a scorm to your course and the names of the fields in the form match the names of the database fields. Each break point can be adjusted according to screen width. (Let's say that if you are not satisfied with 1024 as a screen width for desktop mode, you can adjust the  width to 1280 if you wish.) In context of responsive web design, Captivate 8 uses a parent-child relationship, meaning that it is recommended to start at the desktop level so that the tablet and mobile breakpoints would inherit the CSS . Once the desktop version is adequate, then you move on to designing in tablet mode and then to mobile mode. It's recommended that you use percentage based positioning for your media and text placement. Just to give you a heads up, some people might say that it takes less time to created a course. I think it is a misconception. There is a great deal of testing regardless whatever platform you are using. Adobe also integrated Edge Inspect so that you can view your course in different mobile devices (provided that Edge Inspect is installed.) Here is an Adobe Connect link: http://bit.ly/aelugm_carolina_06_19_14 I hope this is the answer you are looking for.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scrom Interaction  Report
ResponsesInList.Text: The first issue, I'm assuming you don't like the _ between each word.  I suspect that will pretty much always happen.  Basically, your responses have spaces between words but a lot of programs don't like spaces and the _ is inserted.  Most of the authoring software I've worked with inserts an _ when publishing images and pages and anything with names.  I don't think there is a way to stop it other than to stop using spaces. The second issue is easy to fix but has to happen in your package.  Each of the images you use as buttons can (and should) be renamed to represent what it is.  This can be as long or short as you like.  If the answer is apples, name the image "answer apples" or "apples".  You could even set it as A, B, C, and D.  If the answer is really long, distill it down to a couple key words. As for why you should rename them, it's an accessibility thing.  Even if you aren't required to design accessibly and don't make a habit of it, giving images relevant names is good practice.  When your SCORM displays a page with images, if the user mouses over the image for long enough, it will display an alt tag (unless you've specifically suppressed the tags) and that tag is the name of the image.  So, when users mouse over your image, they see Rectangle_4 in the tag.  Not relevant and potentially confusing (I've got a lot of staff who get confused at the weirdest things).  In my example above, the alt tag would read answer_apples.

ResponsesInList.Title: Identifiers to change with updated SCORM module
ResponsesInList.Text: The SCORM FAQ talks about matching "identifiers" when updating a SCORM module so as not to loose gradebook or other tracking data. " Ensure the item identifier is the same for the new SCORM resource." https://docs.moodle.org/26/en/SCORM_FAQ#SCORM_results_deleted_after_package_update My manifest has three different "identifiers" manifest identifier="_6KZEndHPrLR_course_id" <item identifier="_01_Introduction_SCO" isvisible="true" identifierref="__6KZEndHPrLR_course_id_RES"> resource identifier="__6KZEndHPrLR_course_id_RES" Does "item identifier" from the FAQ mean all three of these from my manifest? Thank you --Karl

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Identifiers to change with updated SCORM module
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Karl, here are the scopes of each identifier in the SCORM Manifest: manifest@identifier : it defines the identity of the package; item@identifier : it defines the identity of the item in the TOC of the package; item@identifierref : it is an internal ref used to resolve the item declared in the TOC and the HTML Asset/SCO associated with it: you can change it maintaining the "referential integrity". If you don't want Moodle to detect orphans SCO and to delete no more required tracking data, you should preserve: manifest@identifier : not required in Moodle but I strongly suggest to keep it equal for tracking the fact that you've updated the package to fix some content issues and not to change the overall training scopes of that package (the so called "Quick Fix" procedure); item@identifier : required in Moodle, to keep its tracking data still stored in the database . You can prove it by yourself by testing the package update process in a "sandbox", which should be always part of your "Update a SCORM package" procedure in a live Production environment: read an example for such a procedure in https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=228272#p994443 . Why? You could always miss to respect the constraints above and it is better to fix it in the "sandbox" before altering the real tracking data and Moodle, in the future, could have a regression/change in the above set of constraints. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Identifiers to change with updated SCORM module
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you.  Nice to know what all the "identifies" do. Would there be any harm to updating my "resource identifier"  ( item@identifierref) also? It might be easier for our authors to check that all the identifiers have the same value.   We use Articulate Storyline as our SCORM authoring tool. --Karl

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Identifiers to change with updated SCORM module
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Karl, you can change them too: no issues at all. It is not required since it is an internal ref to map each item of the TOC into a launch-able web item self-contained into the SCORM package. Create your own internal procedure, create a functional test for that procedure and let your authors to understand that procedure and follow the steps of your functional test EACH time they'll be in need to propose an update for a SCORM package. HTH, Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Handling Multiple SCORM Quiz Attempts
ResponsesInList.Text: We are using Moodle 2.7 and Storyline 2 for our SCORM authoring. What we want to achieve is the following: -- The student is presented a course that consists of two topics: 1) a SCORM-based quiz and 2) a certificate of completion. -- They can attempt the quiz no more than twice. -- If they pass it on one of their two attempts, the student can go to the next topic, which is the certificate of completion. -- If they fail both attempts, they do not get a certificate, and must instead take an entirely different course. We've tried to handle the limit of two attempts within the SCORM file by having the SCORM keep track of the number of failed attempts. If it is two, the SCORM does not allow the user to retry the quiz again. However, when the user exits the course after two failures and returns to it, they are dumped back into the course at the beginning of the quiz again. This isn't what we want. Instead, we'd like the user to be given a message about not being allowed to attempt the quiz again after failing twice. I'm beginning to wonder whether it would be better to handle the attempts within the SCORM or within Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Handling Multiple SCORM Quiz Attempts
ResponsesInList.Text: Don't really know storyline 2 but that all sounds like your scorm communication is not working at all or not set up correctly. Check settings at both ends (moodle and storyline) and make sure they match. Test by just moving on a couple of slides and then exiting and going back in. If it resumes from the same place then it is working. All possible as we do something similar (although with captivate). Scorm activity with only a set number of attempts in quiz. Passing that unlocks a certificate activity.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Handling Multiple SCORM Quiz Attempts
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Steve, as Sam mentions most of that should be possible. If you want to limit the number of attempts then you are better controlling this via Moodle (number of attempts allowed is an option in the SCORM settings). Resuming should work fine with Storyline (make ensure you have the resume where left off option on, which is my default). I've never been 100% sure that resuming part way through a quiz works (it's been hit and miss in previous versions of SL for me; maybe fixed in SL2, but it could be Moodle causing the issue too!). I prefer telling users to complete a quiz once they have started. Vispi.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Activity Incorrectly Marked as Complete
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Steve, according to the SCORM specification when the lesson_status in SCORM is set to "passed", "complete" or "failed" these are completed or finished attempts at the SCORM and allow the user to generate a new attempt rather than re-enter the previous attempt. You may need to modify how your SCORM package is authored so that it saves the value "incomplete" in the lesson_status instead of "failed" this might also be useful: https://docs.moodle.org/en/SCORM_FAQ#Handling_of_Multiple_Attempts

ResponsesInList.Text: Can I ask how you ensured LMSCommit is issued? I am having a sporadic problem with this within Moodle 2.1 - occasionally attempts are not recorded.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Attempts not being recorded.
ResponsesInList.Text: From the JavaScript that issues API calls to the LMS, you would add an API.LMSCommit(""). Place this call so it is not called by your content too often, right before you exit the course for example. LMSCommit() tells the LMS/Moodle to save any values you have sent ( lesson_location, suspenddata, etc. ). Apparently anything you send is temporary until the LMS is explicitly told to save it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Attempts not being recorded.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Leah, I found the solution while guessing my way around. My 'students' were actually in a role that did not have access to the save track permission . if you go to Site Administration -> Users -> Permissions -> Check System permissions Find a user that doesn't work and view their permissions, search for "savetrack" and you will probably see that they are not allowed to do it. At the top of the permissions page you will see a list of 'Roles' this user is in, you will need to edit one of these roles and change it's permissions to allow "savetrack" in Site Administration -> Users -> Permissions -> Define Roles Edit the role you want, just open the settings and find the "savetrack" permission and 'allow' and save. Hope it helps. craig

ResponsesInList.Title: Review Mode/Course Completion Problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Using Moodle 2.7 with SCORM 1.2 content developed using Articulate. We are having problems with students not being able to complete SCORM-based courses if they exit and return to the course.  Here's a simplified example of what we are seeing with a course with one SCORM activity which consists of a couple slides followed by a three question SCORM quiz.  The user must get all three questions right to pass the quiz. -- Student goes through the activity and does not pass the quiz. -- If they take the quiz again, without leaving the activity first, and answer all three questions correctly, everything works fine, and the activity is being marked as completed. -- If, instead of retaking the quiz, the the student exits from the course and then re-enters the course, they are shown as being in "Review Mode". -- Once in "Review Mode", even if they answer all the quiz questions correctly, the Moodle software never marks the activity as having been completed. In reviewing the student/course SCORM detail, it shows the following: cmi.core.exit    suspend cmi.core.lesson_status    failed My assumption is that being in "Review Mode" is the root cause of these problems. Based on some research, I've tried changing the "Grade to Pass" for the activity from 0 to 100, but this had no effect. Can anyone provide advice on how to disable "Review Mode" entirely, or to provide a way for the course to be properly marked as completed when a user re-enters the course as described above?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM & File Size Issue in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mark, Check the paths to the zip and unzip utility in your Moodle install. In the admin block for your install, go to Server > System Paths. The paths for zip and unzip respectively should be: /usr/bin/zip and /usr/bin/unzip. What happens, I believe, is that if you don't specify those, the server uses its own php script, and it can't handle the larger files. Best, A

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM - Change default Player to Flow Player
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Priyavadan, what documentation you're referring to in your feasibility study? SCORM module uses its own player to implement the SCORM specs while Flow Player is a multimedia player with no SCORM capabilities. Moodle uses Flow Player to automagically embed media in the text content created within Moodle e.g. Forum posts, Lessons, ..., when the Multimedia plugin is enabled . Supposing that you want to include Flow Player in your own SCORM content here is the relevant documentation: https://flowplayer.org/docs/setup.html . In the past (1.9), Moodle was able to activate its filter plugins' chain even in the SCORM content but it was mostly an hack before being production proof: SCORM contents are not simply plain HTML pages since ages. Starting from 2.0, this hacky feature has been wisely removed. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: passing scorm values to gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: HI Nishani, if you built a SCORM package you should be aware of the SCORM RTE specs too: there is an API which allows a SCORM content to communicate with an LMS some data about the current tracking experience of the user. So you need to have a read about: the CMI data model, about what actually is the data you can exchange with an LMS; the SCORM Run-Time API, about how the data above could be transferred back and forth; both depending on the version of SCORM which, I guess, could be 1.2 . Here is some food for thoughts: http://www.adlnet.gov/resources/SCORM-1-2-Specification?type=technical_documentation http://www.adlnet.gov/resources/scorm-user-guide-isd?type=technical_documentation http://www.adlnet.gov/resources/SCORM-Users-Guide-for-Programmers?type=technical_documentation http://pipwerks.com/laboratory/scorm/ https://github.com/pipwerks/scorm-api-wrapper Have a nice read&coding, Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: passing scorm values to gradebook

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Interpreting SCORM API Debugging logs help
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mathew, the difference is the missing of LMSInitialize() which is mandatory and must be the very first call before any other SCORM call during a (new) SCORM tracking session. What could be the reason for that? It depends on the way the Tracking Logics has been coded into the Content but also on the Network Connectivity: if the network is not stable, it could be not possible to complete the callback behind LMSInitialize() , on the server . Another issue is the Moodle Logged-In Session Timeout which prevents the SCORM callback to be executed on the server but again that call would be tracked in the API Logging , not the case above. The first improvement is to define a boolean which gives info about the SCORM tracking session being correctly opened after a successful call of LMSInitialize() ; otherwise, any other call will be prevented and the user should be informed that the current "learning" session has been started without any chance of being tracked or, better, some retrying logics should take place. The real fix depends on your Content. About the long time being "recorded": the counter is running client side, in the Content, i.e. without the need of any authentication, just keeping the Content opened in the browser. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM file doesn't update
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for your answer. I found an another solution : 1. Create a directory in /srv/moodledata/repository 2. Modify these directives in the php.ini configuration file (/etc/apache2  for opensuse) max_execution_time with a big value... (3000000000 for me) post_max_size and upload_max_size 3. Open my.cnf (/etc) and edit the line innodb_lock_wait_timeout and change the default value (me 5000000 secondes). Beware : A too big value, and the service MySQL doesn't restart. 4. Restart Apache and My SQL services. Now in Moodle. 1. Create a filesystem repository 2. Upload you scorm to this new repository 3 . Upload your BIG scorm into your courses from the filesystem repo. 4. And this is it...it's work See : Don't forget to bacward to original settings. Sources : http://www.manuelphp.com/php/ini.max-execution-time.php (in french) http://www.tonyspencer.com/2008/10/23/if-you-get-this-in-mysql-lock-wait-timeout-exceeded-try-restarting-transaction/ (in English)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM does not work propperly after moving to oher Server
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rolf, so you migrated your Moodle instance from a *nix server to a Windows server i.e. we're already sure that file name case is not an issue - Moodle has a case sensitive file system regardless the underline OS and since you were running the old instance in *nix you're for sure safe here. The SCORM API logging will never tell you anything about what's going wrong on the file delivery: it just tells you about the SCORM calls and if there are issues in talking with the LMS. You should provide more details about your environments, both the old one and the new one (OS, Web Server, Database server, PHP version and how it is managed by the Web Server, ...) and how the transfer has been done (DB dump, Files dump, Files restore, ...). There could be several reasons for your issue; among them: [ OK ] Slash arguments must be set for SCORM packages; Slash arguments must be correctly supported by your new environment: use the Health Center to check for it (http://hostname/path/to/moodle/admin/tool/health/); Files must be transferred in a binary safe mode: I guess that this could be the real good candidate for justifying your problems since it affects not the HTML/JS/ CSS files but the images, videos, .... Did you use FTP to move the files in the filedir folder? Note: the OP has filed an issue into the Tracker, MDL-47436 , too. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi people, I'm new to SCORM and need some advise from gurus to solve my problem. Is there a way to just retrieve the user first name only instead of firstname and lastname from LMS to flash? studentName = ExternalInterface.call("flLMSGetValue", "cmi.core.student_name"); The script works perfectly to retrieve full name but i've failed to modify it to retrieve firstname only.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM 1.2 - To Retrieve user firstname only (Flash)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Cain, We ended up just using the name as returned by the LMS because it does return the whole name. If you are really interested in trying to get just the first name you can try to parse the name to find the it but you will have to make some assumptions unless you know how the name is being returned from the LMS and what it may contain. The simplest logic would be to look for the first space or comma.  If a space, assume the name is formatted as "firstname surname".  If a comma, assume the name is formatted as "surname, firstname".  Then you can extract the portion you want. Of course, there can also be prefixes, suffixes and middle names/initials to contend with which will make the logic much more complex.  If you are interested in going this direction, Microsoft published an article on the logic, probably what they use in Outlook to accomplish this. http://support.microsoft.com/kb/168799

ResponsesInList.Text: The SCORM code in Moodle doesn't allow this easily. You can write single sign-on plugins and just redirect your existing users to a Moodle site with a custom theme and locked down systems so it only displays scorm. If you want to integrate a SCORM player directly within your LMS the best option is to use the Rustici SCORM Cloud - it's relatively easy to write an integration for external systems to connect to their cloud however it is a commercial option. I'm not aware of any good open-source SCORM players that operate in a pluggable fashion and allow easy integration with other systems.

ResponsesInList.Title: Scorm Issue
ResponsesInList.Text: OK, so I am relatively new to the Moodle world but not to e-learning scorm world. For my scorm packages I am using Articulate Storyline. I am migrating from Callidus Cloud to Moodle (for flexibility and unlimited user base). I am on the latest version of Moodle (2.7 I believe) My issue is with activity and course completion settings - I have dug through forums / web searches but having a difficult time finding specifics on my issue (I will admit I am used to the WISIWYG of my current LMS provider). So I have a series of modules (Scorm 1.2) that I have loaded into a course.  Each scorm module reports a score and is set to 50% as a passing score within the published scorm package.  The Activity the scorm package is loaded into within Moodle is set with an activity completion of the following: The next two modules have restricted access setup, the settings as follows: So, when I go through the module, get a passing score, the next course does not unlock.  Further, when I look in the course grade book, nothing is reported. Any help would be much appreciated.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm Issue
ResponsesInList.Text: So the simple answer is...  There is no simple answer. You need to look at how the results from the SCORM are published. This article is very helpful here. http://www.inquisiqr3.com/sharedResources/Documents/ICS%20Whitepaper%20SCORM%20Publish%20Settings%20in%20Articulate.pdf But looking at what your setup is, it is saying it must get score of 50, it must get a grade, it must be flagged as passed AND it must be flagged as complete, which unless the SCORM is set up exactly right, will generally not happen. The first decision is which should decide if the SCORM has completed successfully - the SCORM package, or MOODLE? We normally decide on the SCORM package, this way all our MOODLE settings are the same. We prefer to let the SCORM decide on passing, and use the "Pass/Fail" setting, and finally tell MOODLE to look for Require Status as passed. Hope this helps. Cheers Peter

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM and activity reports
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Marta, A quick explanation of SCORM.  A SCORM course consists of one or multiple SCOs.  A SCO is the smallest unit an LMS will track.  The main tracking capabilities of a SCORM SCO consists of: Status (Complete, in Progress, Pass, Fail, Not Started) Time (Length of time spent in SCO) Score ( a single score 1-100) There are some course defined fields that you can create custom reporting to display: Lesson location (typically used for bookmarking the return location) Suspend data (typically used for progress information, what was completed. There are also some additional fields for tracking individual question and objectives, status and score. Core Moodle SCORM reporting is not extremely advanced.  You can get details on an individual but for overall performance beyond status and score, you will need to create your own report. To get to the level of reporting you are looking for, each unit will need to become a SCO.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Need the SCORM to pass all grades
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle is designed to pass a course once, and it never expires. What we have done, is have the year after the course name. Each year, we create a new course, with the same content, and archive the old one. This way, they actually complete a new course each year. We even have a report which shows when someone is due to "Expire" due to the date they last completed it, and do a CSV enrol on the new course, which sends them an email stating they need to do the new course. A little ugly on the back end, however it works well for the students. Cheers Peter

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, most probably a simple question... I'm using Camtasia to create scorm packages. Within Camtasia, markers generate the right table of content. But how can I use the left tree (course structure), how to generate more entries? I only succeed to have one entry for each scorm package.. Best regards, Dieter

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Question to scorm navigation
ResponsesInList.Text: Dieter, The SCORM content structure consists of one or multiple SCO's.  In your case, Camtasia is creating a single SCO for your course.  This is why you are seeing just one entry in the table on the left. The idea behind the SCO was that they would be small shareable content objects that could be reused in multiple courses.  The SCORM content structure would control which SCO's were required for completion of a course.  This would be called a multi-sco course. If you do not plan on reusing or sharing any of the individual "modules" in the course created, there is not really a reason to break it into smaller pieces.  I would just disable the content structure.  The only advantage you might find is if you want to have multiple tests within your course, like a pre-test and a post-test.  Then you could break your course into multiple SCO's and each would report a score back to Moodle. Ron

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to change SCORM status in Moodle

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Updating (Captivate 8) SCORM Packages in Moodle 2.6
ResponsesInList.Text: Updating works fine if the item identifiers in the SCORM manifest file are the same as the previous package. SCORM packages define their structure in a file called "imsmanifest. xml " - this file tells Moodle what is contained within your SCORM package and how to launch it. Certain components in your SCORM are listed in that file with unique identifiers. If these identifiers are exactly the same then updating your SCORM pacakge will work fine. If the indentifiers have changed, Moodle will delete any tracking data associated with identifiers that no longer exist in the new package. If you have simply changed some text within the content of your SCORM then the identifiers would usually stay the same. Unfortunately the only way to check this is to open the old package and check the imsmanifest.xml file to see if it contains the same indentifiers as your new package imsmanifest.xml file - I'm not aware of any automated tool that checks this for you (but someone else in the community might have other ideas)

ResponsesInList.Title: Skillsoft, SCORM, AICC and Moodle 2.7
ResponsesInList.Text: This is mainly a documentation post to help anyone who is trying to use Skillsoft SCORM AICC packages with Moodle 2.7.    No replies are expected. After a long process of working through issues I found the following settings allowed the Skillsoft package to run: 1. Moodle SCORM Module in Site Administration: 'Enable external AICC HACP' needs to be enabled 2. Moodle HTTP Security in Site Administration:  'HTTP cookies' must be disabled. 3. The AICC content needs to be loaded into Moodle using the AICC metadata (e.g. a zip file package with a metadata file included), rather than just the URL method. 4. The content needs to be loaded in "current window” in Moodle - there is a bug in 2.7 with PopUp window mode. 5.    The course SCORM activity setting in Appearance  ...  (Show more?) ...  'Display course structure in player' must be set to Disabled. This is important.  You can make this a default setting in the SCORM section of Site Administration. 6. The Skillsoft Hosted Content Server (aka OLSA Content Server) needs to be setup to "break out” of Moodle IFrame (equivalent of using PopUp if it worked in moodle): a. olsa_launch_aicc_ro_in_new_window = 1 b. olsa_ro_launce_reuse_intermediate_window=0 Also see the followin g Tracker issues: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-46639 https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-46805

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How do the autoupdate settings work?
ResponsesInList.Text: as mentioned above, "I think its designed so you can update the original zip file without updating the module in moodle, but by overwriting the original file via some other method." so you upload a scorm.zip file to moodle, behind the scenes it extracts it, and stores it in moddata when autoupdate is triggered (on student load etc) it checks the md5 of the scorm.zip file and compares that to what the md5 is set to in the scorm table. if it's different - it triggers an "update" process to refresh the files in the unzipped directory... so - if you set it to autoupdate "every time it's used" it won't unzip the files "every time it's used" unless the md5 of the scorm.zip file is different to the md5 stored in the db. at least that is how I think it "should" work.....if it doesn't, then please file a bug report in the tracker. thanks! Dan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM - am I trying for the impossible?
ResponsesInList.Text: You could try using an SQL report (I Use configurable reports block) and pull student responses straight from the database. Unfortunately it is a little difficult to split specific question responses, however here is an example where it pulls all the responses into a table. (This is where a specific SCORM package ID is 67... SELECT u.username, u.firstname, u.lastname, sst.element, sst.value FROM prefix_scorm_scoes_track AS sst INNER JOIN prefix_user AS u ON u.id=sst.userid WHERE sst.scormID=67 AND sst.element LIKE "%student_response%" Cheers Peter

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM - am I trying for the impossible?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, SCORM does have the ability to store a fill-in type question where the answer can contain a few words.  Moodle supports SCORM 1.2, so if the answers can be less than 255 characters in length, then yes you can use the SCORM activity.  To make this work you will first need a tool that supports the cmi.interactions fields of SCORM and supports the saving of text input into the appropriate field. Moodle will report on the cmi.interactoins fields at the individual level, but if you want to run a more global report on all uses you will need to look into the Configurable Reports or Ad-hoc database reports and create your own SQL query to pull that data out. If you are looking at more than 255 characters for the answers, SCORM 2004 does allow larger answers to be stored in the cmi.interactions, however, Moodle has limited support for SCORM 2004.  If your tool outputs to SCORM 2004 you can try it and see if it will work. To guarantee support for more than 255 characters you have two choices, use the built in Moodle Quiz capabilities or look at the Tin Can API at http://tincanapi.com/ and tools that support it.  However, Moodle does not yet have support fore this API as part of it's core so you will need to install the plug-in and create an account on SCORM.com to store the data and report against it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM - am I trying for the impossible?
ResponsesInList.Text: btw - we added a feature for Moodle 2.7 that allows SCORM 1.2 packages to store a larger amount of data if the SCORM package allows it. more info in MDL-41476 But... this only works if your SCORM package is configured to send more data - many SCORM authoring tools will export packages that prevent data from being sent to the LMS that goes over the limits.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM - am I trying for the impossible?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Paddy, Moodle will store any valid SCORM data that your SCORM package sends, including the learners response. Note though that this may be capped by number of characters. See https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=216092 . Also note that SCORM is now a very old standard and the people behind SCORM have published a new tracking standard known as Tin Can or Experience API. Andrew

ResponsesInList.Text: Assuming that you've checked that you've uploaded ALL the necessary files (yeah, we all do it from time to time!) and that all the files are at the same web address, i.e. no cross domain security issues, I think it could be this... If you're getting just a blank screen it could be an on INIT issue where the stage dimensions are initially width 0, height 0. You can get round this by adding a stage resize handler like: stage.addEventListener(Event.RESIZE, resizeHandler); private function resizeHandler(event:Event):void { // organize the stuff on the stage here i.e. myDisplayObject.x = stage.stageWidth * 0.5; myDisplayObject.y = stage.stageHeight * 0.5; myDisplayObject.width = stage.stageWidth * 0.25; // etc... } Other problems could be the embed method you're using. SWFObject is a great embed method and they offer great support: http://code.google.com/p/swfobject/ I hope this helps! Matt P.S. For ActionScript related questions, I think you'll find actionscript.org forums much more helpful and responsive: http://www.actionscript.org/forums/forumdisplay.php3?f=75 I contribute there from time to time

ResponsesInList.Title: Crowdfunding: create your own SCORM objects with LiveCode for HTML5
ResponsesInList.Text: A generation ago, before the Internet, thousands of teachers and students all over the world created their own software using Apple's HyperCard programming software. LiveCode (formerly known as MetaCard and then Runtime Revolution) has kept the HyperCard project alive since then. LiveCode allows creation of software using a "stack of cards" metaphor and an English-like programming language. Last year LiveCode became open source, making it free for non-profit educational institutions. Until now, LiveCode has created desktop and mobile apps, but an app still needed to be installed to use it. Now, LiveCode is crowd fundraising to extend to creating HTML5 apps, which will run natively within a browser. What this means for Moodle users: using LiveCode, teachers could create their own rich media to embed within Labels or Pages in Moodle. Even more exciting, teachers could create SCORM objects to embed in Moodle, allowing rich interactive learning experiences like games, simulations, graphical quizzes, etc., and pass the results back to Moodle as a completion record or even a grade. This data could be displayed in the gradebook or used by other activities in Moodle to set availability criteria, grant certificates and badges. LiveCode is free, but the HTML5 extension needs funding. If you are interested in being able to create your own SCORM content with an easy to use, open source tool, please consider contributing to the funding campaign. There are 7 days left to pledge. For more information, see: http://livecode.com/livecode-to-html5/ Thanks! Elizabeth Dalton Granite State College (I have no financial relationship with LiveCode -- I just want to use it to create SCOs!)

ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM Package Type - Downloaded Package Does Not Update
ResponsesInList.Text: Greetings All, Moodle version 2.6.1+ Cron .php script has been run; CLI cron has also been executed via command line Courseware packaged as SCORM 2004, 2nd Ed. using Captivate 6 I hope whoever reads this can follow along, as versioning can be quite confusing.  I recently moved all of my SCORM files to use Downloaded Package Type in an effort to accommodate multiple courses delivering the same courseware file -- for example: Email_Etiquette.zip can be used in: On-boarding / New Hire class Refresher training Department-specific courses Future courses that are not currently offered, but will The goal was to update/maintain/support multiple courses referencing the same courseware file every single time there was a change.  The thought was that we could simply replace/override the file being referenced via the URL / "File Repository" to ensure the most current version is being accessed. Note: When referring to the URL as a "File Repository" I am NOT talking about any of the Moodle repositories.  Instead, we have designated a file repository outside of Moodle (a mounted drive on the same server ) that can be accessed within Moodle to store all of our production files. Here is an example of how our current site setup works: Students would go to the following site to access the Moodle: http://trainingsite.com Administrators would use the following URL to upload /manage new content in Moodle : http://trainingsite.com:8080/Courseware/filename.zip Moodle Site: Sample Repository: This works great when we setup a new SCORM object: The packaged file is placed in the designated courseware repository We then access (upload/ download ) the same file via Moodle Launch the courseware successfully The ISSUE occurs when: A change is made to the existing courseware via Captivate ( e.g., the title is changed, a page is deleted, a misspelled word is corrected, an image is replaced, the embedded exam is updated, etc. -- the file is UPDATED ) Could be the same day, may be a few months later The Moodle Cron.php scripts are executed The Captivate file is then saved and repackaged ( SCORM 2004, 2nd Ed. ) The previous courseware file within the courseware repository is overridden/replaced with the repackaged ZIP/PIF file Again the Cron.php scripts are executed It appears that the cached version is still there.  It is not a local setting, as I have cleared both my browsers' ( used Mozilla FireFox , Google Chrome, Opera, Safari, and IE to no avail ) and computer's cache ( browser options, flushdns, etc. ).  I have also Purged all caches in Moodle. I have also tried: Logging into Moodle as a different user On a new computer that has never accessed the courseware Launched the "updated" course Still see the old version appears I have also extracted the files directly from the repository and ran the courseware outside of Moodle (locally) to verify that the updated files reflect the correct package that Moodle should be extracting ( Auto-update frequency - Every time it's used ). As a work around ( defeating the purpose of going to the Downloaded Package type method ), I achieved success: Duplicating the modified ZIP file within the repository and renaming it (e.g., changed from filename.zip to filename2.zip) Updating the URL path under Downloaded Type The correct version did load after relaunching this specific course instance.  However, this was the ONLY course that updated, and would have to repeat the same action for the other course instances that used this SCORM package. If I changed something and repackaged the new filename2.zip, the issue persisted -- the unmodified version still appeared.  As a caveat, I did notice that if I renamed the file BACK to filename.zip, the newly updated/correct version displayed once again. HELP!!!  I have a number of courses that fall under the same boat with more to come, and this will be a nightmare to maintain if this bug does not get resolved. FYI , I am not an expert in PHP, and do my best to decode some of the logic -- I'm more of an AS3/HTML/HTML5 type of guy....not a programmer by any stretch of the imagination!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Package Type - Downloaded Package Does Not Update
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Edgar, thanks for the very detailed info! Unfortunately the described behavior is by design since the URL determines the version of the package and cleaning up the cache doesn't work 'cause of the package has not been actually updated. You should tell your users to append kind of versioning schema to the URL as an HTTP GET parameter: it will not hurt the download but it will fix the lacking of version information. Just start with appending ?v1 the very first time i.e. http://trainingsite.com:8080/Courseware/filename.zip ?v1 and then keep on incrementing it ( ?v2 , ?v3 , ..., ?vNNN ) when you want to force the deployment of the presumably updated package. The current behavior could be improved in order to automatically check if the file has been changed but this means that every time a user will launch a SCORM activity the package will be downloaded by Moodle to check if the package content is the same of the one already deployed: that means a great overhead (bandwidth, time, CPU). It will make sense to downloaded it no more than daily via cron - code can be easily changed -, but you'll miss the ability to update it as soon as the URL will be changed to promote a new version of the package. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Package Type - Downloaded Package Does Not Update
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you very much for your response Matteo, Unfortunately, I do not see the value in using the Downloaded Type if Moodle does not check to see if the SCORM packages are actually the most current version (e.g., by date stamp). As I mentioned in my post, versioning by changing the filename is very inefficient -- as this would have to be changed for every single course a module/courseware package is used.  Tracking this information is rather cumbersome, but apparently will have to be the direction I must take - reverting back to Uploaded SCORM Type. I absolutely agree with your point about the system checking everytime a user launches a SCORM Package, but I believe a better method would be to check everytime the cron script is run - checking the date created/modified parameters from the "SCORM Package repository" / URL, comparing it with the unpackaged versions inside of Moodle, and overwriting the oldest files with the "newest version".  I am still not sure what purpose the Downloaded package type serves or benefits administrators and users alike, if you still have to update/touch every instance a SCORM package is used [updating the filename parameter]. Warm Regards, Edgar Garcia

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Package Type - Downloaded Package Does Not Update
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Edgar, the purpose of that mechanism is to serve static content outside Moodle, relaxing the security Moodle puts while serving these files when installed locally to the application - users must be enrolled to see each piece of content, regardless someone will bookmark URLs of such bits for sharing them. BTW , I take your point and try to create a use case maybe to propose an implementation, in the future, as an alternate option. To avoid downloading the file in order to check the content - the real check that costs in terms of time and bandwidth - it is required to trust the data, when available, given by the server hosting the package about things like Last-Modified and to reduce the time and bandwidth required for this check the server must support HTTP HEAD or HTTP 206 Partial Content (the so called Range Request ) the hard part of the tech requirements. If the server doesn't support e.g. HTTP HEAD - yours? - what should be the expected behavior? Disabling the update or to downloading the entire package? My tech POV tells disabling the update . But... regardless the use case I'm trying to create and the potential technical limitations above, have you already tried the first option described in http://danmarsden.com/blog/2013/09/24/managing-scorm-content-in-moodle-2-6/ ? That should solve your need at the extra price of changing the current setup of your already created activities but you can start playing with it with the new ones - given that you accept to download the remote content to check for any update i.e. not trusting any HTTP Header provided but the file content being just downloaded and not introducing constraints about the HTTP HEAD support. HTH, Matteo

ResponsesInList.Text: I think it's the same problem pointed in this page: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-44548

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Package Type - Downloaded Package Does Not Update
ResponsesInList.Text: I think the problem is the "contenthash" of the files: The FileStorage gets the old file's content (and extracts it) because the new contenthash is still the same. So, it needs to be synced! In my case, I'm using the filesystem repository (in Moodle 2.7) to storage the scorm packages. To solve this problem, I make some changes in two php files: repository/filesystem/lib.php because the function "sync_reference()" was syncing just image files; mod/scorm/locallib.php before "$packagefile->import_external_file_contents();" need to call "$packagefile->sync_external_file();" and remove the conditions like "$scorm->scormtype != SCORM_TYPE_LOCAL" to call scorm_parse($scorm, false); It works for me. The file's changes can be download for now from: https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/6407866/moodle-scorm-sync-changes.zip

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, We are getting an error from Moodle (v2.6+ Build 20140110) when completing an HACP (HTTP-based AICC Communication Protocol) activity. The response reads: "error=1\r\nerror_text=Not Initialized\r\n". This issue seems to occur when the user takes multiple attempts to complete the activity. Moodle generates a new session_id for each attempt and we send PutParam messages to the aicc_url using the _most recent_ session_id we receive from the LMS. Any thoughts on what could be causing this issue? We can reproduce this reliably with the following steps: 1. Launch an activity as a student 2. Make some progress on the activity and close the window 3. Return to activity in Moodle an observe number of attempts is 1 and score is 0% 4. Launch the activity as a student 5. Complete the activity and close the window 6. Actual: Return to activity in Moodle and observe number of attempts is 1 and score is 0%. Expected: Return to activity in Moodle and observe number of attempts is 2 and score is 100%. After step #2 our web app sends a PutParam message containing Lesson_Status=Incomplete and Score=0 and Moodle responds with a success message. After step #5 our web app sends a PutParam message containing Lesson_Status=Completed and Score=100 and Moodle responds with the error mentioned above.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Not Initialized Error When Completing an Activity Using HACP
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Wes, does your content make a GetParam before performing any PutParam ? Indeed it is required to make at least a GetParam , before anything else, to initialize the tracking session. Some other commercial LMSs do not require it but the AICC spec tells about this requirement e.g. in cmi001v4.pdf , §6.3. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Text: ok - firstly we don't fully support SCORM 2004 packages so if you can publish to SCORM 1.2 you should. next it sounds like the modules you are referring to are completely separate SCORM packages - auto-continue is a setting used to control how a single SCORM package that contains Multiple scos operates - it doesn't have anything to do with Moodle's activity completion settings. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Possible to get SCORM Question text from moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: The SCORM 1.2 Spec doesn't allow for the question text to be passed to the LMS - it only passes the "ID" of the question as specified in your SCORM authoring tool - Many SCORM authoring tools allow you to customise the ID to make it easier to understand the reports. The SCORM 2004 spec includes a "description" field that some Authoring tools pass the question text into however Moodle doesn't officially support SCORM 2004 so the reports won't work quite right if you use SCORM 2004 and some authoring tools don't pass the question text there anyway.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: scorm html5 and mobile
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello. I gave Captivate a good try. At first I was really impressed, but after a while I gave it up. The main reason is that I´m looking for a single tool in which we can create activities both for web and mobile. And the activities range from simple instructional courses to more sophisticated gamified activities. And Adobe has several tools for these different jobs, so to get the job done we would need several tools, including some not so friendly ones (such as Adoge Gaming). And adobe Is still a bit attached to flash… Both Articulate and Captivate claim to export in HTML5, but in my experience both these outputs are much inferior to their corresponding flash outputs in both programs. Unfortunately they are more appropriate for desktops and notebooks. To create good html5 with Adobe you would need to combine tools like Dreamweaver, Adobe Edge Animate and Adobe Reflow. And the whole idea of ‘rapid development’ just gets lost… I want to create both mobile friendly activities and mobile apps. That is: activities to be run on the user´s browser (such as a Scorm package in an LMS or as a regular webpage) AND activities that can be converted to specific Android and IOS apps with PhoneGap. I found that the best way to test for the quality of the HTML5 output is to publish the output to a web server and access it with an Android device, using the native browser (WebKit). Than you can have a glance of the true mobile experience of the learners. And both with Articulate and Captivate this test was a big failure. And this exactly what the app would be like if created with PhoneGap. I still haven´t found the perfect tool for the job. Lectora has a few great advantages: it´s HTML at its core: there´s no Flash output (unless you include flash objects in the project). And it´s a much more powerful tool with many built in functions that require a lot of work in the other platforms (like a timer, recurring actions, a table of content, progress bars, etc). But it has some major drawbacks (the output is always fixed sized with absolute positioning, so it doesn´t have any responsive capabilities. Also the animations and transitions are really lame, although I´ve heard that the newer versions show improvement in this area). There´s really no reason why an html output wouldn’t work on Scorm in mobile devices. And for us this limitation was a deal breaker, so we ditched Articulate. If you already work with the Adobe suite and you have an adobe creative cloud subscription, it might be a way to go. But if you´re looking for a single tool for desktop and mobile development, Captivate will frustrate you. Good luck and let us know what works out for you. Cheers

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Edit grade not carrying through to report
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Vispi, A SCORM SCO is treated as an activity and not a course.  Therefore, it's data is stored independently of the course data.  The course Grader Report displays calculated scores from the activities and when you edit a grade you are only changing data for the course not an activity. To edit the score of a SCORM SCO, you would need to access the database directly.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm vs. "Lesson"
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm going to start with the third question first.  I'm not sure what you mean by making validation questions...you want to make sure their profile field matches a particular thing before they can access the activity?  If that's it, all the modules allow you to add access restrictions based on User Fields.  If that's not what you mean...well, I'm at a loss. Using SCORM activities requires authoring software (some of which is quite expensive) or mad developer skills to develop the content.  Sometimes both.  SCORMs are developed outside of Moodle and then uploaded. Lesson just requires skill, focus and practice.  Lessons are built inside of Moodle (you might write them up in word or something, but building question/answer/navigation is in Moodle). Your second question is yes.  You can build SCORM that require time in them be a specific amount.  You can set pages to only continue after a certain length of time, you can create variables that count time and compare it to something else, but that goes back to authoring software and mad skills.  I could do it (and have done in some ways) in a SCORM now...but five years ago I probably couldn't have...not because my software couldn't, but because I didn't have the knowledge or skill yet.  Of course, setting a time limit in Lesson is much simpler. It all comes down to what you want, how you want it to look and behave and what resources and skills you have.

ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM & Database Interaction (V2.4)
ResponsesInList.Text: We just launched a new course and required all employees to take it by June 30th. Before this, we really have had no system problems. We have had a hard time keeping the system up and responding due to the number of users hitting the system and the course at the same time. Are there special requirements when a SCORM course is used, like needing more disk space, CPU, etc? We have had to add 3G memory to the web server , add 30G to the web server,  double the size of the MySQL DB to 60G, and add 3 more CPUs. Now I am concerned about the number of contiguous users. Is there special sizing needed for SCORM courses? Is there somewhere here that discusses optimal sizing strategies for Moodle setups?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM & Database Interaction (V2.4)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Constance, it totally depends on the number of SCORM tracking elements involved and generally in the learning strategy implemented by the SCORM content i.e. the number of SCORM calls used to flush the SCORM tracking data into the LMS. You should attend to the course and look to the API logging to see how the SCORM content talks with the LMS (here, Moodle 2.4 ): I guess it will perform a significant number of LMSCommit() calls, which is the SCORM 1.2 command to flush the SCORM tracking data into the Database and it will make usage of interactions . Ideally, for performance reasons, the SCORM content should just perform an LMSFinish() call, accepting the risk to loose some data if the connection drops before that call. There is a generic golden rule in Moodle which tells 1 GB of RAM for ten users doing the same thing in the front-end but you need to check where the bottleneck was in your system: it could be also the database not able to serve the amount of "writing" required in the short time by your SCORM content, which creates some sort of queuing the front-end calls e.g. a domino effect. If your SCORM content is made by several files and some of them are also medium sized, you could get some benefits too in using X-Sendfile ( http://docs.moodle.org/27/en/Performance_recommendations#X-Sendfile , available from 2.3 , MDL-26028 ), to drop the load in the front-end while serving those static files. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Check and A: Visualization
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi guys, i have one question, what´s the meaning for the A and X? I attached the pics. https://moodle.org/pluginfile.php/137/mod_forum/post/1138102/Bi%20learning%20modulos.jpg https://moodle.org/pluginfile.php/137/mod_forum/post/1138102/Bi%20learning%20modulos%20error.jpg

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Check and A: Visualization
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Francisco, each of them represents the SCORM 1.2 status for each item (properly, SCO) of the package: "check" or "V" means completed or passed , "X" failed while "A" stands for Asset which should not contain any SCORM tracking data according with SCORM specs (Please, note that sometimes the imsmanifest. xml file declares an item as Asset while it is a SCO). HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Invoke LMSCommit manually

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Issue NetworkError: 407
ResponsesInList.Text:
Actually, there is one workaround but it depends on which version of Moodle you're running and it is not really a permanent solution. From Moodle 2.6 you an do the following: Open theme/yui_combo.php and find the 'rollup' section. Inside it there's an array of $yuimodules. At the end of the array, add the following two entries: 
```text
'dd-proxy',
'resize-proxy',
```
 The issue here is then caching. For people visiting your site for the first time, this will just work. For people who are coming back they will need to manually purge their browser cache. This is because we aggressively cache the JavaScript from the site using the YUI version number as an identifier. Hope this helps, Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Survey Results with SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ron, You stated, "I just can see if a student took it, but can't find a way to see what they voted for." The interactions report within in your SCORM module should tell you about each survey question. Captivate treats survey questions as quiz questions. The difference being that there is no grade for survey questions. So, you can see the results in the SCORM package>reports> interactions tab to see how each person answered each question. The interaction report will yield a user response and a right answer . The right answer is simply the radio button you selected in the Captivate survey BUT, presumably,  since there is no right answer on a survey you can just ignore the info. Then download the data  and use  a spreadsheet to sort and filter your responses. As a nod to the other comments, there are more suitable tools inside Moodle for generating surveys. There are also other web tools that are equally suitable for this task. But Captivate will work as well. it's  more time consuming on the formatting side but it offers many more customization options. Peace

ResponsesInList.Title: When will Moodle become FULLY SCORM and/or Tin Canconformant?
ResponsesInList.Text: (I'm sorry if this question has already been asked but I looked and couldn't find the answer.) I know there are various SCORM add-ons available for Moodle. But is it safe to assume that at some point soon Moodle will fully conform to SCORM standards?  I understand that Tin Can may supercede SCORM in some way so maybe my question is a bit off base. Bottom line: I need all learning content to be stored as XML so it is parsable into a database at a very granular level. Moodle would need to be extremely XML friendly for me to use it. Thx.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: When will Moodle become FULLY SCORM and/or Tin Canconformant?
ResponsesInList.Text: The only way to get a guaranteed time-frame for "Completion" would be for someone to fund the time for a senior Moodle Developer to do the work. We've had a small amount of funding that has allowed me to look at the patch for Tin can Jamie wrote in MDL-35433 and I've tidied it up a lot and renamed a few parts here: https://github.com/danmarsden/moodle/compare/moodle:master...master_MDL-35433 This still needs some further thought - I'm still on the fence about the best way to implement it in core. We have given up on SCORM 2004 (but still support SCORM 1.2 and AICC - see my blog /other posts in the forums about this) The SCORM module is maintained by volunteers like me - occasionally people pay for my time to fix something in SCORM that is annoying them (in my day job I work for the NZ Moodle Partner Catalyst IT) - and I spend a lot of time outside work as a volunteer improving SCORM support and have spent a lot of time looking at Tin Can. Moodle provides fully compliant support for SCORM 1.2 and AICC but not SCORM 2004 or Tin Can. Bottom line... if you need full SCORM or Tin Can compliant support from an LMS - Moodle doesn't currently provide it in core so you have the following options: * Pay for Rustici's commercial plugin (which supports SCORM and Tin Can better than Moodle core) and use it with your Moodle site. * Use your own Learning Record store (Learning Locker, Rustici, ADL have open source options and there are many other commercial options) Then use the 3rd party plugin for Moodle that allows you to play tin can content with the external LRS * Play with the alpha code I linked above. * Find a big chunk of funding to pay for someones time to further develop tin can for Moodle. * Use another LMS that supports SCORM or Tin Can better. Good luck!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: When will Moodle become FULLY SCORM and/or Tin Canconformant?
ResponsesInList.Text: I keep wondering if SCORM/Tin Can/Experience capabilities are not given priority at Moodle HQ and that's why development is relegated to volunteer-only status. Perhaps the pedagogy is not considered to be sufficiently " social constructionist " (a long-standing topic of discussion ). I assure you that these types of presentations are not only essential to corporate and government training programs but become ever more significant to colleges and schools as they switch to "flipped classroom" pedagogy .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: When will Moodle become FULLY SCORM and/or Tin Canconformant?
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle HQ provided funding that allowed us to become fully SCORM 1.2 compliant and personally I think we do a pretty good job of maintaining it as volunteers - we have a very low bug count in the tracker compared with other "HQ Supported" plugins but there's always room for improvement. Tin Can is a hard one though - there's a lot of buzz around but predominantly it is being used as a SCORM replacement and most tools that allow Tin Can content to be developed can also export as SCORM 1.2 (which Moodle supports) so the justification is not completely straight-forward. Most teachers are interested in completion, grade and question/answer reporting which SCORM 1.2 and Moodle do relatively well. There are many core projects that Moodle HQ focus on that directly affect a much larger group of the Moodle userbase like improved logging/reporting, Gradebook improvements, usability improvements. Personally I think this is a wise use of the limited funding and developer time available at Moodle HQ. Don't get me wrong - I do think Tin Can offers some interesting improvements to the SCORM spec which is why I've spent some time on it and why we've managed to get some pieces of funding to look at it (although not as much as I'd like) One of the areas that interests me a lot is the offline capabilities that Tin Can offers but this will only be useful to a smaller subset of Tin Can users.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: When will Moodle become FULLY SCORM and/or Tin Canconformant?
ResponsesInList.Text: Oh gosh, Dan! No disrespect intended. You and the other volunteers do wonderful work. I've been a Moodler since 2007 and have seen dramatic improvements. I'm grateful and my hat is off to you!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: When will Moodle become FULLY SCORM and/or Tin Canconformant?
ResponsesInList.Text: hah - no disrespect felt! - I just think Moodle HQ has pretty good priorities and the major core tasks they work on are more important in the greater scheme than focusing on things like SCORM (which is supported pretty well already) and Tin Can which is new and not used by many and is already similar to existing functionality that is available.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: When will Moodle become FULLY SCORM and/or Tin Canconformant?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dan, The SCORM support really is good in Moodle.  In the corporate environment we have come in contact with many LMS varieties over the years and they all have their quirks with how they implemented the SCORM specs and some big names we have had to debug their own players for them to help our clients get more reliable experiences.  Moodle support of SCORM is one of the best and I attribute that to the developers listening to the reports by the community and making fixes much more quickly. So a big thank you to all who have and still work on the SCORM interface for Moodle. I do disagree with you on one point about the Tin Can API.  Offline use will not be relegated to a smaller subset of Tin Can users for very long, it is a much bigger issue.  The demand for being able to take training on mobile devices is accelerating quickly.  Every client of ours is now asking if the SCORM courses we create for them will run on a mobile device and then the second question is, will it work offline. I know for Moodle it all comes down to funding, but I think the demand for the ability to take a course offline is only going to increase.  Though this would be a major change to Moodle core, think what it would be like to allow a student to download an activity to their device of choice and then disconnect so they are not using up their data plan or tied to WiFi connection.  It would give back the ability to take your assignment and go outside and sit under a tree to complete it. If Moodle were to offer this, it would be a major win in the market for all users.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: When will Moodle become FULLY SCORM and/or Tin Canconformant?
ResponsesInList.Text: Even if Moodle becomes the most SCORM compliant thing in the history of compliance, you will then need to be confident that any SCORM generating tool you use is entirely compliant. I am not.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: When will Moodle become FULLY SCORM and/or Tin Canconformant?
ResponsesInList.Text: yes I hear that pain... I feel that pain a lot while working on bugs in the tracker! I'm hoping that the Tin Can spec is better than the SCORM spec in this respect and we will find more consistant implementations that are easier to deal with.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: When will Moodle become FULLY SCORM and/or Tin Canconformant?
ResponsesInList.Text: The  feature I like the most from the Tin Can API compared with SCORM is the offline access possibilities and I'm sure there will be a demand/use for this feature but I still remain to be convinced how many people will actually use it. You might be interested to read this post related to providing offline access to Moodle Courses and sync of SCORM attempts back to a main site: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=260100 Obviously this method won't support mobile devices well but it is being used to deliver training in areas with no or limited internet connectivity on laptop/desktops. There is also work going on with the Moodle Mobile app that allows a lot of content to be stored offline on the device and it makes sense to add Tin Can support at some point to improve this further.

ResponsesInList.Title: Scorm quiz
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I noticed that some are talking about quizzes in SCORM package in moodle so I tried to add an XML moodle quiz to make a scorm package using reload editor but when i launch it in moodle i have the xml file and not the quiz where students can answer multiple choices questions. It is possible to do a quiz in scorm using reload editor or not?? And if not is it possible if i use another scorm packaging tool?? Thanks in advance

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm quiz
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, SCORM supports Quiz since its data model supports also tracking data related to quizzes BUT it's up to the tool used to create a SCO to implement the actual creation - read: bits an pieces for an HTML page - of a Quiz optionally using an XML file, e.g. based on IMS QTI or based on Moodle Quiz export, as the input for the "build". Reload is a tool able to create a package given that you've already created the SCOs and Assets: so if you add an XML as an item of the package you'll see that plain XML when you'll select that item in the SCORM package. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm quiz
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, You can use Reload to package content in line with SCORM's Content Aggregation Model, but you also need to ensure that the content meets the requirements of SCORM's Run Time Environment document. Also note that you can only package uo client side code such as JavaScript and Flash and not server side code such as php. This means that its not really possible to run a Moodle quiz as SCORM content. Why do you want to do this? There may be another way to achieve your goals. Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm quiz
ResponsesInList.Text: > This means that its not really possible to run a Moodle quiz as SCORM content. Why do you want to do this? Hi, I was just about to ask exactly this question: is there a way to SCORM a Moodle quiz? The reason for wanting to do this is that we currently use another assessment system which we need to replace. Moodle, including plug ins from the OU, provides a very good match for all the question types we currently use, the XML is in a readable format that we can probably create a transform for. the editor is already there so we would not have to create our own for developers to use. However, we do not want to be tied in to having to provide all our assessments via a moodle instance as some of our end clients are using BlackBoard so we would like the freedom of being able to package the assessments as SCORM to make them portable from one LMS to another (rather than implementing an LTI connection). Basically we want to use SCORM exactly as it was intended - to allow a SCO to be used in any compliant LMS. If it were possible to SCORM a Moodle assessment then Moodle would be the ideal solution for our needs. J

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm quiz
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Sarah, if that is your plan i.e. using both the Moodle interface and infrastructure, besides the plain XML, you could take a look at the IMS LTI Provider plug-in for Moodle while if you want to use the XML format of the Moodle Quiz you need to develop something (e.g. XSLT) that will translate that XML in a browser playable resource (e.g. HTML5+ CSS +JS), including the tracking logics. HTH, Matteo
