ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm Module developed !!!
ResponsesInList.Text: If your SCORM modules are getting so big that you're running out of diskspace, a possible hack is to make one copy of an un-packaged SCORM module in a directory somewhere and make all other versions of those files hard links to that one central copy. Seemingly, hard links /are/ supported in Windows - they're called "file junctions" in Windows-speak and are an underused feature of NTFS (only found out about this the other day whilest looking for something else, sounds handy). The above could be implemented by a server -based script, seperate from Moodle - something to check all Course file areas for SCORM module directories, any new SCORM modules could be copied to a central directory and hard links put in place, any duplicates could simply be replaced with hard links. This would make a good hack for those running low on disk space (i.e. if you've got a large SCORM module, perhapse with movie files in, that you want to use in several different Courses). "Duplicates" could (hopefully...) be identified by comparing file size, modified/created date and maybe checksum if you wanted to be really swish. I'm not sure what would happen if you implemented the above, ran the script over your server, then someone on a course updated a SCORM module, uploading new files. I've actually got a hunch that it might work quite well - the new upload would (?) replace hard-linked files with new files, you would end up using a mixture of old-and-new files... Possible idea: change the SCORM module a bit so that after it unpacks a Zip file into a directory it generates a signature for each file based on size, modified date and checksum. Then it checks each file against a central "asset" directory, hard-linking each duplicate it finds and adding any new files to that central directory. No need to worry about duplicate file names or new versions of files replacing old ones - simply give each new file a new name in that central directory and create hard-links to it. Have a periodic scan to see if there's any central files that aren't linked to from anywhere and delete them. Hmm, would that work?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm Module developed !!!
ResponsesInList.Text: So, after some more thoughts, here's the idea. After line 56 of the SCORM module's "validate.php" place code to implement the following psedo-code: // For each file in newly un-zipped directory (and subdirectories): //     Generate signature (modDay-modMonth-modYear-MD5). //     Check /moodledata/scorm/ for file. If not exists, copy file there (with filename DD-MM-YYYY-MD5SIG). //     Erase old file. {Platform independant} create new hard-link to central file. This creates a central "repository" for SCORM files, updated every time someone uploads a SCORM archive. It would need periodic scanning to remove orphan files (via cron.php). It would probably also be a good idea to scan for existing duplicate SCORM files and link them to this central directory, either via cron.php or some run-once script. This assumes that SCORM files are not edited "in place" by Moodle, that new/edited SCORM content always arrives via uploaded Zip file. Editing a SCORM file once uploaded to Moodle would result in all hard-linked files to that location being changed (probably confusing, although someone might find it useful). You would still have to upload and add the SCORM file to each course. Just thought - you could also add some lines /before/ line 56 in validate.php to make the uploaded SCORM Zip archive also be linked to a central location. This doesn't create a browsable, centralised reposatory of SCORM archives. All it does is reduce the amount of disk space used when (potentially large) files are uploaded to different courses multiple times. It doesn't help you upload, or even update, the same SCORM archive to multiple courses, either - uploading updated files (which will generate different signatures, of course) will simply create more entries in the central directory. -- David Hicks

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Last Seen Scorm Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: The actual SCORM data is kept in the mdl_scorm_scoes_track table, indexed by the userid, scormid (the course scorm id) and the scoid (the sco within the course), the attempt, and the scorm element id passed back from the course, containing the value passed.  Generally courses like captivate, articulate keep their status in the cmi.suspend_data element, and the last location accessed in the cmi.location element.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Last Seen Scorm Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Here's a snippet of SQL that might help get you there...  this one looks up all the suspend_data and location elements for all attempts on all SCOs in all SCORM-based courses taken by the admin user.  If the course in question has only one SCO (which is usually the case for courses that use an internal menu like Storyline or Captivate), then there will only be one SCO per course.  Of course you could retrieve other element values as well that indicate the exit/completion status, etc. of the SCOes. SELECT s.name, sst.attempt, sst.element, sst.value FROM mdl_scorm s JOIN mdl_scorm_scoes ss ON ss.scorm=s.id AND ss.scormtype='sco' JOIN mdl_scorm_scoes_track sst ON sst.userid=(SELECT id FROM mdl_user WHERE username='admin') AND sst.scormid=s.id AND sst.scoid=ss.id AND sst.element IN ('cmi.suspend_data','cmi.location') WHERE s.course IN (SELECT id FROM mdl_course);

For example, the SCORM package may show 10 slides, followed by a quiz, followed by 10 more slides, followed by a quiz, etc. We'd like to keep this same concept of multiple quizzes per chapter in Moodle, if possible. However, in some initial testing, we only get grade results from the last of the quizzes in each chapter. Is it possible for Moodle to track results from multiple quizzes in a single SCORM package? If not, what would be a recommended alternative? Break the SCORM packages out into multiple packages with one quiz per package? Use Moodle quizzes? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course Setup with Multiple SCORMs
ResponsesInList.Text: Single activity format is what it says...a course format for one activity.  Topics (or weekly, depending on what you want)  seems like the best bet for you course. Now, on to your SCORM question.  As with many SCORM questions, according to my Magic 8 Ball, the answer is unclear.  It depends on what product you uses, how it is set up and a variety of other questions.  Some products (like Lectora) allow you to create separate Assignable Units, each one has a quiz and scores itself separately but in one pot.  In this case, the way you set your Moodle activity settings (primarily the grade method should be Sum). Some products just report the last quiz but you might be able to set variables which add quiz 1 to quiz 2 and replace the aicc_score with the sum (I'm thinking of Captivate...definitely upper level user skills here.  I haven't tried this, though I'm sure it is possible.  It is definitely possible with Lectora). I've seen some packages that don't actually report a score, you continue if you "pass" but it doesn't otherwise care what your score is (in Moodle you set this type of module grading method to Learning Objects or you get a bunch of 0's...).  There are so many options for SCORM publishing (Articulate, Soft Chalk, iSpring, eXe, to name a few more), it's hard to give a definite answer.  They all have different levels of skill to use, different selling points and different quirks. The more you know about your publishing software and how it reports/decides what to report, the better off you are.   Your last question(s) is certainly an option, but if you already have 8 SCORMs, that might make for a monster course.  What I do when I have something like this is a) make sure I know what the package does and b) toy with it.  I try different settings to see what the results are for each one, both in the package and in Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course Setup with Multiple SCORMs
ResponsesInList.Text: I don't know if I'd call it a challenge, it's more of an adventure.  When you design the SCORM, you have to start with the end in mind.  If you don't have an expectation for what you want it to report, you don't get what you realize you want later.  I've heard good things about Articulate and I love their e-learning community.  I'm more of a Lectora girl, personally, but I'm not fond of their community area, but the Articulate community is super helpful and has all kinds of ideas and resources, so I lurk there, even if I don't use their products.  It's my understanding (which could be wrong) that some of the power-user type stuff I can do with Lectora reporting is more built in-background in Articulate, so I don't know how customizable it is. If you really want to be able to get item analysis for quiz questions, I agree with Rudy.  Quiz module outside of the SCORM package. Getting item analysis from SCORM is complicated and painful (and that was with reporting software pulling directly from the database in 1.9).  I use 2.5 now and SCORM works so much smoother, but getting data is even harder (I think) than it used to be.  It used to give a list of all recorded actions (variable changes, question answers (but not the question), comma delimited) but now the data is much less specific.  And even in the database it is hard to find specifics (maybe I haven't looked hard enough, I switched away from in-content quizzes just before our upgrade and haven't been sorry). Getting item analysis from the Quiz module is easy and simple.  The item analysis stuff give you so many options.  Very powerful and only getting better.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Interaction Report Showing zero
ResponsesInList.Text: So to complete my info: moodle version 2.2 is required and you are running 2.5.1 (Build: 20130708) OK unicode must be installed and enabled OK database mysql version 5.1.33 is required and you are running 5.1.66 OK php version 5.3.3 is required and you are running 5.3.18

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Interaction Report Showing zero
ResponsesInList.Text: Good work, Peter! So if you made this attempt with the same user account as before, then you should at the very least see that lesson_status is changed when you return to the first report table (what you took a screenshot of before). Not all interactions are shown in the table in your screenshot. But if you select the number (it's a link) in the Attempt column, and on the next screen, "Track Details," you'll get to a screen which displays (should display) all of the setValue elements set through the API (should match with the final values set in your API log). Have a look there and see if it's what you're looking for. I don't see any emergencies in your API log. We do often see issues where client authorware writes arbitrary data to cmi.core.suspend_data and, when it exceeds the SCORM 1.2 character limit, the API stops functioning normally. But that is not the case with your API log.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Interaction Report Showing zero
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Amy, '....if you select the number (it's a link) in the Attempt column, and on the next screen, "Track Details," you'll get to a screen which displays (should display) all of the setValue elements...' Yes, that is what I expected to see, but don't. Let me recap. I have the interaction report for the very same SCORM working in a version of moodle 2.3.1 In that version whenever a score is shown in the interaction report the very next column always shows the score/maxscore - then the interactions are listed - see below. In my moodle V2.5.2 I see the following so I click on the link '1' above to see what's copied below. Which is why I looked in the database to originally check that my SCORM data had been written to table mdl_scorm_scoes_track I know the id of my user and can see the record in the table, hence my question about how to test why my interaction report shows a score, but not the score/maxscore or the interactions. As my SCORM package would take someone at least 30mins to run through it to generate interactions in their own moodle I'm now going to download a SCORM that's been used elsewhere on the forums for testing purposes and run that through my moodle to see what I get. Perhaps with your greater experience, you could advise me of a better approach. Many thanks in advance. (note: I've now upgraded one of my moodles to version 2.5.3 and still get the same problem)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Interaction Report Showing zero
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm having this problem as well, in both the interactions report and the objectives report. I had someone test it on Moodle 2.5 and it worked for him, but in Moodle 2.6 that I'm running the database is adding the columns but not populating... I'd really like to get to the bottom of this!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Interaction Report Showing zero
ResponsesInList.Text: Some SCORM packages report interactions and objectives data but others don't - the report will only show information if a user has entered the SCORM and the SCORM has reported interactions/objectives data back to Moodle. Also important to note that the reports only currently support SCORM 1.2 packages (not SCORM 2004)

ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM Tracking Records orphaned
ResponsesInList.Text: This issue is perhaps akin to the situation where SCORM tracking records are removed when the manifest IDs don't match. However, we have taken care to make sure the identifiers don't change when uploading a new version of the course.  In this case, when uploading an updated SCORM zip, all of the records in scorm_scoes_track get orphaned.  I believe this happens because the SCO IDs get updated in the scorm_scoes table, but the scoid field in the scorm_scoes_track records doesn't get updated. This results in a bunch of records in scorm_scoes_track that reference a scoid that no longer exists, which causes problems for reporting. Has anyone else seen this behavior?  It doesn't seem to happen every time we do an update, which is perplexing, because I have tried debugging through the code to determine if there might be a bug, but have come up empty. Could it be related to a timeout?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Tracking Records orphaned
ResponsesInList.Text: I've had this a few times when at work - usually seems to be a time out issue for me. Either get an error or no response and need to cancel the upload . At times the file has uploaded anyway, but seems more to do the our work settings as usually goes fine when I try it from home.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Tracking Records orphaned
ResponsesInList.Text: I've  seen it happen when someone was using the SCORM and you update the SCORM package - this is particularly a problem if you are using Moodle 2.5 or earlier with the setting "update every time it's used" The main problem was that we relied on the order of the records too much - in 2.6 we added a new sortorder field to the table so now the ids of the scos in moodle don't change during an update.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Need help with SCORM thing

ResponsesInList.Title: Mime Issues with Microsoft IT Academy Courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello! We are experiencing MIME issues with all SCORM Modules for MIcrosoft IT Academy Courses. This problem is only present in IE 10 and 11, but not in Firefox etc. According to Microsoft, we need to add to mime types to our configuration: . xml application/xml .xml                      text/xml We have added these to our Apache config and the SCORM files run great outside of Moodle. But in Moodle the content breaks and does not load. I know that Moodle handles mime types in lib/filelib.php. There are currently the following entries: 'xml'  => array ('type'=>'application/xml', 'icon'=>'markup'), 'xsl'  => array ('type'=>'text/xml', 'icon'=>'markup'), How can I add text/xml to .xml in there? Adding a new line with it does not help. Moodle Version 2.6 Thanks!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mime Issues with Microsoft IT Academy Courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Michael, that's strange: you can't map two different MIME types for the same file extension, even in Apache. BTW , if you want to use text/xml instead of* application/xml in Moodle just properly replace the MIME type in filelib.php and: a. easy path: re-publish the SCORM package. This will update the MIME type info in the mdl_files table too; b. hard path: manually update the mdl_files table by replacing the MIME type for all files ending with .xml . When serving the file, Moodle reads the MIME type from the database and not from filelib.php so any change in filelib.php must be reflected in the database too, for those files already in the Moodle files pool. HTH , Matteo * text/xml should imply a simple ASCII character set, which is not really true being most of the time utf-8 .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm File Upload problem [V2.6.2]
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Hugh, it's quite difficult - not impossible* - to add all the required columns values by hand, it's better to update the package. If you don't change the identifier of the items in the manifest file, the tracking data will be preserved: parked during the unzipping and then restored. Deletion will happen for those items whose identifier is no more present in the "new" version of the package, to avoid orphan tracking data. You can test it by your own, by publishing the broken package in a new private course, attend to it to register some known tracking data and then updating that SCORM activity in the private course with the fixed package. Looking at what happened to your tracking data will give you the answer. Remember to hide/close the Activity/Course during the update to avoid your users to start a tracking session during your update ( MDL-40001 ). HTH , Matteo * You could first look at the mdl_files table to see if they are already recorded in the DB and then lookup/re-create the related physical file through its contenthash : details about the File API internals here, http://docs.moodle.org/dev/File_API_internals#File_storage_on_disk .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Errors in reports.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Sam, the very first step is to activate the API logging to record how the Content reacts in terms of tracking calls in the different scenarios, including to look at the manifest file to see if a Mastery Score has been set there. If the Content doesn't talk with Moodle, via the SCORM API, enough to track the relevant data, your reports will be blank in any LMS: the key point is to identify what the Content misses to tell about the User's experience and when . Then you can start looking at the JS code of your Content to address most of the problems, the why part of the game. You can't be sure that Network and Session issues will be 100% under your control so expect at least a 2-5% of "strange" tracking situations, if you can't control OS, Browser, Network and Bandwidth of your Users. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Text: HI, Has anyone encountered this? I have published a SCORM course using an authoring tool (Lectora), just a set of questions with multiple choices. (Users claim that they did get a passing score). SS 2: This is when "Track details" is clicked. Moodle mark the attempt as Passed. SCORM Publishing settings (Lectora): 1.) Has bookmarking. Users will be directed to the last question they were at when connection is lost or if exam windows is closed. 2.) Passing grade is set to 80 3,) Questions are not randomized 4.) ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Grade shows 0 on SCORM result.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dexter, your Content is not storing the score i.e. Moodle cannot elaborate grading based on the given score . You could activate the API logging to see when the Content sends the score to the LMS (here, Moodle) to try to understand when / why the score could not be transmitted. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Grade shows 0 on SCORM result.
ResponsesInList.Text: From your screen print, it looks like some attempts get grades but some don't.  I've been wrestling with a similar (but not exactly the same) issue which appears to be browser related.  Apparently security settings in IE11 don't play well with SCORM products.  I'd heard several months ago that it didn't play well with Lectora, but really, it is SCORM.  For my users, sometimes it doesn't store any data, which is a problem, but it isn't consistent.  Changing security settings (don't know which ones, IT is the one testing it) resolves the issue.  Is there a difference in the browser used between those getting credit and those not getting credit? Although...if you look at your suspend_data...the variables have been submitted and your test score is 0, so maybe the user did something to clear the score or something that is coded in overwrote the score?  I over-write scored in several of my titles for a variety of reasons (one replaces the grade with either 50 or 100...because the percentage isn't what we score). I've found with Lectora that their pre-generated "Cancel" button doesn't cancel, it basically submits and causes chaos.  I always remove them.  The "-" only shows up before the grade is submitted.  Once you have "completed" or "passed" a module, it displays the grade.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm Not Loading on some PC's
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Nikki, I have run into this issue with end-users as well.  It turns out that browser platforms are being difficult with the flashplayer plugin (especially the latest releases of safari), apparently in an attempt to force/pigeon-hole everyone into HTML5 without regard for the e-learning community.  The problem is that most authoring tools publish SWF outputs, and even when you wrap/publish for HTML5, any flash-based interactive widgets/content that you create/insert become sketchy.  (see this article: http://pipwerks.com/2013/03/13/flash-support-is-increasingly-a-minefield/ ) Anyhoot, I would suggest end-users experiencing this issue to have the latest flash player and java plugins installed on their computers, along with accessing Moodle using Mozilla or IE (as crazy as THAT sounds, though I have not tested with IE11).  Also personal popup blockers/firewalls may pose an issue, BUT I would suggest presenting these solutions as At-Your-Own-Risk if users are using their personal computing devices (for liability purposes).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM no cmi.interactions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey, indeed! I found the solution. When you publish a SCORM, there is a Configuration.js file in the folder of published quiz. ResponsesInList.Text: Lindsay: Client is getting mad... You're taking people's money to support Moodle using a low-ball.com ISP? Daniel: Neither you nor Lindsay may be doing anything wrong. It's quite likely the ISP you are both using (GoDaddy) is the problem. Image problem Lindsay reports may simply be that the GD library is not compiled into the web server (this can be checked in Moodle admin), or it may be related to something with permissions. In your case, make sure you unzip things on the server, not on your desktop first and then uploading. If you are on a Windows machine it will most likely change permissions on a folder in the process of unzipping. Check Moodle documentation closely to see what it needs (server), for the version of Moodle you are running. Then, if you're going to stay with GoDaddy ask them whether these requirements are installed on your server. Moodle is a complex web application and the requirements will change again when version 2.0 comes out. It is a good idea for the Moodle admin to know these things. Some of the Moodle partners offer Moodle admin training and there are a number of Moodle books available as well.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM tracking data deleted -   resolve with gradebook editing?
ResponsesInList.Text: HI Luke. I had this exact same problem when I wanted to update my scorm activity. What I had to do was create a stored procedure to automatically move all users to the last specific module that they had completed. For me it was relatively easy because my courses force users to achieve 100% (i.e., they cannot move past a question without getting it right) - if yours doesn't do this then it will be slightly more complex, but it's all acheivable, if you haven't yet deleted the tracking data (or have it backed up. In order to do it, I went through the course myself and stopped at the start of each module then saved all the completion data (from mdl_scorm_scoes_track). Then I created a stored proc which allows you to specify the userid, the module id and the Scorm and scoid's. When you call it, it selects the tracking data for the user for that module, deletes the old and then re-inserts it. For me, I didn't need to specify anything in the mdl_grade_grades table as Moodle will do it for you next time it saves, but you may need to do that too. I hope that helps. The short answer is, different modules (inc' updated) have different tracking data. Hugh.

ResponsesInList.Text: shouting (using upper case) isn't considered to be very polite. I almost ignored this thread because of it. SCORM issues can be very complex - many cannot be easily diagnosed without having a copy of the SCORM package. If you can't share it with us or create a new package that allows us to reproduce the issue then you are on your own unless someone else in the community with the same issue has a package they can share. In many cases I've found display issues can occur due to the way the package is authored. Just because it "worked" in 1.9.5 - doesn't mean it worked properly... one of the recent big changes to the way pop-up windows work/display in the latest release was due to an IE 7 bug - see here if you're really interested: http://danmarsden.com/blog/2011/07/13/ie7-and-xmlhttprequest/ That issue took over 20 hours to diagnose and propose a fix. I couldn't reproduce this bug on my local machine with the package provided - the client gave me ssh access to their webserver (and paid for most of my time) to diagnose, trace and fix the issue. The other option you have is to engage a Moodle Partner - you can privately share your package with them and they can try to diagnose the issue and suggest a fix. It's possible there are some outstanding bugs with the player in the latest 2.X release but we can't reproduce/test/fix these without receiving a (valid) SCORM package that displays this issue.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problem with SCORM frame size (do not window size) Moodle 2.1.1+ (Build: 20110907))
ResponsesInList.Text: I work with Bas, as he said we have the same problem. The older version for the scorm module plugin worked fine, the current version adds stuff in the pop-up window. I have a solution that works only for so far ive tested it (1 browser, 1 scormpackage, 1 theme), it didnt work completely when Bas tested it for another browser/theme, and also i do not know why/how it works. However, it might be a step further to a solution. 1) The new scorm module plugin uses a layout file from your theme. This is actually a nice feature; youre able to style the window as youd like. However, maybe youve put paddings and margins on the container divs thatll be placed around the scorm div. Solution for this: a) look in the theme folder (moodle/theme/*themename*), for the theme that is currently used b) look in config.php (moodle/theme/*themename*/config.php), see this text: 'popup' => array( 'file' => 'general.php', 'regions' => ar... c) change the text 'general.php' into '*mypopuplayoutname*.php' d) make a new file in the folder layout (moodle/theme/*themename*/layout), named *mypopuplayoutname*.php e) make sure to keep it as empty as possible. for reference, check the file general.php, copy it, use the name you want to use, and delete any wrapping div elements that you dont want to use 2) The new plugin scorm module resizes a little bit, which is why the body is shown underneath and besides the content. You want the content to be full screen. Solution for this: a) Go to the plugin scorm module folder and look in the file module.js (moodle/mod/scorm/module.js). b) On line 194 you see: newheight = YAHOO.util.Dom.getViewportHeight() *.82 Change the *.82 to + 10 c) On line 219 to 238 you see 3 times, in 3 different if/else parts, offsetWidth - 6. Remove the -6. *note:* i think the -10 and -6 px for the height/width you can see on line 219 to 238 have something to do with room for a scrollbar. 3) When youre on your moodle website, edit scorm settings: display course structure in player: set it to disabled. This will get rid of the space on the left. I hope somebody finds a solution! Kind regards, Jeroen

ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM activity completion question (bug?)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, We're using Moodle 2.5 and I need to understand why when I set the following: the SCORM activity Grade setting ->Grading Method to Learning objects and set the Activity completion->Show activity as complete when conditions are met.  I then unselect the Require minimum score Disable checkbox, and place a value of 3 in the input box. When I only complete two of the three SCOs (get 80% on QUIZ) then the whole SCORM activity is displayed as Completed ? Further details, the SCORM package is made up of: one SCO not score only completed or not a QUIZ which returns a cmi.core. lesson _status, and a cmi.core.score.raw and an EXAM which returns a cmi.core.lesson_status, and a cmi.core.score.raw. If I look in the Grades only a score of 2 is recorded, but I did specify that a score of 3 is required to complete.  Is it the cmi.core.score.raw that is interfering? Thanks for any assistance in resolving this. Regards, Robert.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM activity completion question (bug?)
ResponsesInList.Text: Yeah Robert, I´m too heaving a huge head ache with that, have searched thru the whole forum and nobody can answer me that. Have you know something new? Somebody have? My students can´t access the Quiz before they go thru all the Learning Object and this bug it´s stoping all our development in the platform. Moodle 2.6.1 here.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM activity completion question (bug?)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Andre, After digging around found that the solution was for us to break up our SCORM course into multiple packages where each package only contains one Scored SCO. Moodle is correctly implementing the SCORM 1.2 specifications which specifies that the SCORM Package activity completion status is determined by the SCORM Package itself. In order to make this work we would need to write a customized plugin to implement some Aggregate Rollup rules as implemented in SCORM 2004. The solution that we finally implemented was to split up the SCORM package in multiple SCORM packages, then use the Topic format and add SCORM activities in each, setting the restrictions on the previous activity (The first sections contains multiple activities that do not report a score and the Quiz that is scored).  See the attached screengrab. Hope this helps. Regards, Robert.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM activity completion question (bug?)
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you Robert for showing your workaround for this, that´s great, we here use captivate to create all scorm and after that we join them thru Multi SCO Packager that come´s along with Captivate 7. Your solution for us it´s the last one that I´m gonna try, goind to dig out something else because that´s make the usability tiring for the user, after the user finish the first scorm he got go back to the topics and select another one, from the way we´re using today he only choose the topic from the tocmenu above, as the image below shows. But thank you for your solution, I think I will make use in the future.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM activity completion question (bug?)
ResponsesInList.Text: Robert so I was looking for one solution that doesnt have to change the actual structure that we already have: • Multi SCO Package made by Adobe Captivate 7. My solution to this, so I can still have one Scorm Activity with many topics, as you can see from the image below. For that I dont set any Activity Completion status in the Scorm activity settings, so I set as "Do not indicate activity completion" , and the grading method as "Learning Objects" ok? . So below the Scorm Package the user have a lesson but before he have to reach 50% from the Scorm Package. And in the Lesson I set the Grade Condition to the " Course Total" at 50%, that´s it instead the Scorm Acvity only. Now the user is restricted to take the lesson only if him make that percentage of the Scorm Packager. Hope the images speak for themselves and it help any one that´s using the same approach as we here. Please rate me as Useful. See ya.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm never saves
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mignonne, I too experienced this issue a while back.  I found this article to be of great value in resolving this issue: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=119194 Basically you want to verify file size limitations and timeout values in the PHP.ini file meet your network requirements: upload_max_filesize post_max_size max_execution_time max_input_time Also check any server/network -side restrictions outside of Moodle that may be inhibiting you from uploading "larger" files.  I've attached the two files below, page 1 & pages 2-3 (note that given the size limitations of this site, the quality of the documents will be poor..... lol)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm never saves
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mignonne, Further to Edgars post, if you're on a hosted server, as your hosting company about updating the user.ini file, which is the user equivalent of the php.ini which in a lot of hosted environments can't be edited. Hugh.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm never saves
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, thanks for the clarification Hugh. My post was referring to managing your own Moodle server (rather than a hosted solution).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm never saves
ResponsesInList.Text: We have our own server, but the php.ini isn't the issue - I know that because if I just replace the Moodle install with 2.3 (instead of 2.5 or 2.6) it works fine.  So, it can't be the max upload size or any of those settings. Also, i did look at the link you suggested.  One thing that maybe has changed over time, I cannot see in "system->system paths" any reference to path for zip and unzip. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm never saves
ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry Mignonne, I should have specified further - try changing the php.ini values for: max_execution_time = 120 max_input_time = 120 ** Or try 240 if you still have issues. These were the two values that specifically fixed my issue, and according to the error message you posted (Maximum execution time of 60 seconds exceeded), I am fairly confident this should work for you as well.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm never saves
ResponsesInList.Text: Wow, that worked!  I can't quite say it makes sense - why did the old settings (60) work with 2.3?  Why did setting it to 0 (infinite time) not work?  Oh well, as long as it works, I guess I don't care.  I'm SOOOO happy this is solved, thank you so much!!!!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm never saves
ResponsesInList.Text: Your welcome Mignonne, all thanks to open-source collaboration is all !  I was in the same boat as you a few weeks back and thought it had to do with a size setting somewhere as well.  Obviously I was barking up the wrong tree, and was just as relieved as you when I got it to work.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm never saves
ResponsesInList.Text: The built-in Zip handling in PHP is supposed to be better so Moodle removed the ability to use binaries for zip - one of our team wrote a local plugin to allow the use of a binary as we've found the binaries perform a lot better than the built in PHP support - you can get the plugin here: https://moodle.org/plugins/view.php?plugin=local_externalzip ...or you could increase the timeout values as suggested above.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Module setting status not sent by package
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ian, I think I'm fine with the information you provided about Mastery Score: starting to review the code and recalling the past history. Indeed I need to recap in my mind the Moodle FAQ I've quoted - and wrongly reported in my previous post -, the SCORM Specification and some thoughts done in the past. Let's start with MDL-21305 when completed was removed from the conditional branch by... me. The SCORM 1.2 specs tell something slightly but significantly different from my previous post - apologies, I did a quick reply early in my morning - : see http://www.adlnet.gov/resources/SCORM-1-2-Specification?type=technical_documentation . There, in SCORM_1.2_RunTimeEnv.pdf : at page 3-25 , you'll find that the Mastery Score logics should be triggered when the lesson_status is equal to completed ... but only when the lesson_status is left to not_attempted by the SCO, when the LMS must move it to completed ; at page 3-43 the specs define the rule to overwrite the lesson_status when a valid score(.raw) has been provided by the SCO and the package contains a valid mastery score. That being said: Moodle has no bugs here; Docs trivial cleanup: FAQ must be reviewed in order to change the link to the conformance requirement specs, now dead (ADL changes their site "frequently"). @Dan, @Amy: shall we rewrite the FAQ to point to the RunTime Environment spec or to point just to a copy of the Conformance Requirements document, outside their site e.g. http://scorm12.com/SCORM1.2/SCORM_1.2_ConformanceReq.pdf - besides page number is 2-19 or the 39th, out of 155 -.  The 1.2 ADL Test Suite setup ( CTS1_2_7STSetup.exe , http://www.adlnet.org/resources/adl-conformance-test-suite-verion-1_2_7?type=software_downloads ) does not contain the Conformance Requirement specs. When we'll agree on what change, I'll do it; You need to remove the Mastery Score info from your package if you don't want your LMS - not Moodle but ANY LMS - to overwrite the SCO status when the SCO closes the communication - calling LMSFinish() -  leaving incomplete for the lesson_status value. If you look at the time when MDL-21305 and MDL-21306 have been implemented, your package worked as you'd expect in a Moodle version before 1.9.10 . Isn't it? HTH, Matteo

The documentation you refer to has the behavior for Pass/Fail when the status is sent to complete but Moodle is doing this when the status is incomplete. It has to be possible to suspend a package with a failing score and resume it. This was certainly available previously. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Module setting status not sent by package
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ian, interesting, could you provide the exact 2.4 version you were using? In my spare time I could try to replicate the fact that in 2.4 it worked in a different way from the current 2.5.2+: it's worth trying to do some more investigations to find out a possible regression. We need also the list of your SCORM settings to identify if a combination of those settings is the root reason for your issue e.g. providing the vertical output of the activity settings via your DB e.g. in MySQL : SELECT * FROM `mdl_scorm` WHERE `id`=<id_of_your_affected_SCORM_activity>\G; . About SCORM (not Moodle): the bug here is to provide a score , keeping the status incomplete : if you're writing a score , certainly you mean the session to be taken for credit . Isn't it? Besides the specs says a slightly different thing: an LMS should move from completed when it itself, the LMS, has moved to the completed status i.e. being the tracking session closed without setting, the content, a status i.e. being the SCO status equal to not_attempted ... which means, in other words, that the Mastery Score logics applies even when the LMS should move the status from not_attempted to completed . About Moodle SCORM code: it's quite easy to add the condition, I mentioned in my above post, back - though I'm interested in understanding the possible regression: as said above there was no changes in that SCORM logic since 1.9.10 - : look at https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/MOODLE_25_STABLE/mod/scorm/datamodels/scorm_12.js.php#L651 , there you'll find the conditions under which the Mastery Score logics should run, again, regardless possible regressions in other areas when you moved from 2.4 to 2.5. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Module setting status not sent by package

The LMS is responsible for setting the initial value to "not attempted". Additional Behavior Requirements: If a SCO sets the cmi.code.lessons_status then there is no problem. However, the SCORM does not force the SCO to set the cmi.core.lesson_status . There is some additional requirements that must be adhered to successfully handle these cases: Upon initial launch the LMS should set the cmi.core.lesson_status to "not attempted". Upon receiving the LMSFinish() call or the user navigates away, the LMS should set the cmi.core.lessons_status for the SCO to "completed". After setting the cmi.core.lesson_status to "completed", ... ResponsesInList.Title: Re: [V2.6] How to delete orphaned Scorm FIles
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Hugh, every time a file is deleted in Moodle, the Files API subsystem parks it into a trash folder - $CFG->trashdir . Defaults to: $CFG-> dataroot /trashdir - not accessible by human beans but the API itself. That trash folder is purged every four days , given that your Moodle cron has been correctly configured. FYI there are proposals to improve the control over the purge time range e.g. MDL-31645 , MDL-39083 . HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Grade of 50
ResponsesInList.Text: Grading in SCORM packages can be complex. If you are using the grading method "Learning objects" - it will be because you have multiple SCOS and the users have completed/accessed 50% of the objects required. If you are using " Highest grade , Average grade , or Sum grade " then the 50% mark will be coming from the way your SCORM has been created by the SCORM authoring tool - your SCORM package will be passing a 50% grade to Moodle somehow. more info is here: SCORM_FAQ#SCORM_and_the_Gradebook

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to determine completion of SCORM through database?
ResponsesInList.Text: Most of my remarks assume you are using lectora, since you reference "The Human Eye" zip file, which sounds an awful lot like the sample Lectora course they use to teach how to use the program.  What it really sounds like the issue is is that your particular SCORM isn't set to report properly.  So, if I'm wrong, ignore everything... The issue may be that the course isn't set to report completion (you can set the AICC_lesson_status to completed with variables which are case and spelling sensitive!).  If you don't it sometimes will reports passed/failed and sometimes complete/incomplete.  If you don't set it to completed, if you want more than one attempt, it won't let the user have a new attempt... As for facilitator access to completion, it should report to the gradebook and you should have a results tab (in the activity) which details users' attempt details.  If you click their attempt number, it should provide a track details link, which includes all variables (like quiz answers).   IF the Lectora module isn't set as an AICC/SCORM/Coursemill...Published title it might not report properly at all even if it looks like it should. If you really want to check details in the database, as you referenced, you have to know the sco id, the user id, and the scorm id and use the mdl_scorm_scoes_track table...but it only tells you the last page they viewed and a value.  Depending on how your scorm is set for reporting (completed?) it might show completed or a list of all variable or a variety of cmi data (which doesn't show up in human language).  This is an awfully complicated way to get data, when you can get it through the scorm itself... Hopefully this is helpful. I also use the Certificate module and don't put certificates in my projects...then I set the certificate with a dependancy on a grade for the SCORM and I can have a record of the certificate issue...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to determine completion of SCORM through database?
ResponsesInList.Text: The AICC_lesson_status is a SCORM setting.  It really depends on what SCORM authoring product you use.  I use Lectora primarily and have a bit of experience as well with Captivate.  In Lectora, I set the status using variables on the last page.  Captivate has some check box settings when you set up SCORM publishing which deal with the variable automatically but also allows you to create your own variables/modify variables.  I think iSpringFree auto-sets the variables (I never set them using that product and it modified the status, so it must do it by default).  Camtasia also does this automatically, as far as I know, as it doesn't really provide options to manually set, but I'm not as fluent with Camtasia.  Other products, of which there are many, I can't really talk about...having little or no experience. If the scorm is set for reporting based on your method, will it just show 'completed' or 'incompleted' and which table I will have to look upto to get these details? When a participant starts a SCORM module, a tracking report is started.  Click the activity, choose the Reports tab and click on the number of the attempt next to a specific name to get that particular report and an option to track details.  This shows the lesson location (last page viewed) and status, cmi.core.score.raw, and total time.  While it is possible to fiddle with the cmi.core.score.raw within your SCORM, it is quite difficult, in my experience (I don't recommend it).  If you want to see the specific moodle table where this stuff lives it is mdl_scorm_scoes_track.  But this stores all those variables, not just one and is very messy. As for what value score.raw gives...if your SCORM has a grade, this is it, in raw data.  As far as I know, this is what reports to the grade book.   If you have a required grade for the scorm, you can go to the grade book, edit categories and items and edit the specific SCORM to require a specific grade.  This is an "advanced" feature, so you have to click the See more bit to set a grade to pass.  This way, even if it set the status to completed, if they don't have the right grade, they don't get marked as completed for purposes on completion status and access to the next activity. And for help with code...I'm no help with code at all as I'm not actually a techie person.  I use course completion settings to track finish/not finish.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM bookmarks
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Alex, the bookmark functionality is achieved by using the SCORM (v1.2 here) cmi.core.lesson_location element of the CMI datamodel: any LMS supporting SCORM (v1.2 here), Moodle too, could provide this value to the content as well as the SCORM content could manage this value by means of the SCORM API. Usually the bookmark is set by the content when attending to something like a slideshow, updating that value on each new slide to let the user be asked if she/he wants to start where she/he left. You can find a list of tools in http://docs.moodle.org/26/en/Creating_SCORM_Content: unfortunately that nice tools screening doesn't clearly report the availability of the bookmark too, except for some tools. HTH , Matteo

However after some pretty extensive testing I have found a workaround...at least in v2.6...which is the version I have installed. if you compile the course in articulate storyline in Scorm 2004 format, version 4, rather than scorm 1.2 format, it works and you don't get the review mode problem on resume. i know that moodle are no longer supporting this format in favour of Scorm 1.2 but it may well act as a workaround for those of us it is affecting until the dev's have time to take a look at the problem. With this though, I've noted several issues. these are: 1. You have to delete the previous scorm attempts for those users who have not completed as its a different format. Actually I think moodle may even do this for you, so you might end up losing data if your course is already live like mine.....I've had to do a bit of messing around with the db to keep my completed users completed.... 2. iPad users. Oddly with this format, one fingered scrolling doesn't work ... But two fingered does. Weird! Just tell your users, because it means if you have navigation buttons at the bottom of your player they may not be able to see them. re point 1 it's just struck me that an easier way would be to make a new course and put those uncompleted users in there and leave the old one with the completed users intact! the good news is that in v2.6, the attempts management now works correctly with scorm packages so you can actually set users to just one attempt and it will track just one attempt with resume rather than incrementing it randomly. I hope that helps! Hugh.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Customise the "Track Details" SCORM Report
ResponsesInList.Text: FYI That user tracks page has changed a lot in 2.6 - it now shows tracks data in a single table  and allows export to excel etc(it doesn't show the interactions data separately on that page anymore) - ideally you should upgrade to 2.6 before you make any changes to the code as your changes will be difficult to port when you upgrade. To display interactions data you should be looking at the interactions reports but these reports have only been designed for SCORM 1.2 data as we don't support the use of SCORM 2004 in Moodle and development on SCORM 2004 features/improvements has stopped . If someone else does some work that meets Moodle coding guidelines to add better SCORM 2004 support to the interactions reports in Moodle 2.6 then I could review it for inclusion. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Customise the "Track Details" SCORM Report
ResponsesInList.Text: that report is designed to display all tracks from a user - if you want to only show certain ones then you should comment out line 134: $row[] = $element; Then in the block above make sure you set a $string value for every value you want to appear in the report. Unfortunately this change isn't something we'd be able to include in Moodle core as the report is supposed to show all values from the users own tracks - but you can easily maintain your own version of the report

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hiding SCORM block

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.5 issue with AICC HACP Communication Help
ResponsesInList.Text: Is your Moodle site accessible publicly? - AICC HACP requires your Moodle site to be public - it can't be hidden behind a firewall. so if you access your site internally using: http://mysite.com/ It must be possible for an external system not inside your network to access the url http://mysite.com/mod/scorm/aicc.php without requiring any further authentication

Otherwise you could give Fiddler a try: you've several options here. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 2.5 no completions showing of SCORM in IE
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Bill, According to your support case your organization was asked to review the site content before upgrade, to make sure there were no problems. Your organization approved the upgrade at that time. In the future you probably want to review your content in IE9, if you have users who cannot use other browsers. The SVG icon issue occurs because the browser is running in IE8 mode. IE8 does not support SVG icons, and Moodle does not appear to be designating fallbacks. Apparently IE9 in IE8 mode does not present the right cues to Moodle to serve the non-SVG image. Another user also turned it up here: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=223136 With regard to the content scaling issue, you may want to try some of the solutions proposed by Articulate: http://www.articulate.com/support/presenter-09/flash-movie-does-not-scale-properly-in-published-presentation Additionally, if you are able to designate ActionScript3 rather than ActionScript2 for your content authoring, that will result in a SWF that does not use fscommand() and therefore doesn't present the Flash bug which necessitates the meta tag that's causing your troubles: https://bugbase.adobe.com/index.cfm?event=bug&id=2928139 Regards,

ResponsesInList.Title: How can we update scorm file without vanishing grades or keep the grades?
ResponsesInList.Text: How can we update scorm file without vanishing grades or keep the grades? Please reply.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can we update scorm file without vanishing grades or keep the grades?
ResponsesInList.Text: If the new SCORM package uses the same sco identifiers and the imsmanifest. xml doesn't change then the grades shouldn't change. If the user has modified the indentifiers/added or removed scos from the package or is updating with a completely different package that doesn't match the original one it will delete any tracking data associated with the old sco indentifiers and the grade could possibly change. We do have an open feature request to notify a teacher when they upload a package that doesn't use the same identifiers as the previous package - ( MDL-24057 ) There have also been some unconfirmed reports of grade issues but no-one has provided enough information for us to reproduce this (see MDL-42474 for more info)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle SCORM error: Trying to get the non-object
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Phil, that sounds strange: there is no difference in publishing a valid SCORM/AICC package the very first time and updating it after some time, given that you'll use a valid package "quite similar" to the first version. Two the main expected issues after the update stage: If your updated package contains a different manifest ( imsmanifest. xml file) in terms of SCO identifiers you'll loose some tracking data during the update process; that's the reason why the packages must be "quite similar". This is not compatible with the described issue; If your updated package is not valid - e.g. being a compressed archive of the folder containing the course files - the update process will silently break your activity being updated. This could be your issue so I suggest to try to publish your updated package as a new activity to see if that package has issues. These are the known issues: if those above don't fit with your issue, in order to make some investigations we need some replications steps and probably two of your packages, the first version and a new version which breaks the activity after the update process. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCO code, Metadate file and Settings for manifest files
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Debbie, you should talk with them, especially if you selected them as your content provider ! Here are some short explanations: SCO code: it's the HTML/JS/ CSS magic mixture used to create a Learning Object for your SCORM package, such files are called SCO. It's quite strange that they are asking you the content already being created, should they provide the content to you or are they requested to package the SCOes you shouldd give them in order to let such SCOes be published as a SCORM package into your Moodle? Metadata file: it's potentially an external file included in the SCORM package describing the package itself according to LOM Specification. Useful to create a library/catalog, it will help you in classifying them. Moodle doesn't have advantages of them when searching the courses... yet, see GSOC 2013 and MDL-31989 ; Setting for the manifest files: usually, it means if you want some preconditions to block the navigation inter-SCOes (e.g. do not access the second unless the first will be completed/passed/failed) or to configure the so called Mastery Score threshold (to allow the LMS to set the SCO status based on the SCO score). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Conditional Activity w/SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dave, you didn't say which version of Moodle you were using. If you are using Moodle 1.9.x, you will need to install a 3rd party plugin called " Activity Locking " which will allow you to do that. If you are using Moodle 2.x, then Moodle has something similar build-in now called " Conditional activities ." Now that said, I found them to work differently. Somehow I had a Moodle site which I upgraded from 1.9 to 2.4. There is only one course on this Moodle site and the course has one SCORM package and a certificate (using certificate module). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Conditional Activity w/SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: You absolutely can!  And it is pretty easy.  Edit your Certificate (or other activity) settings.  Click open the Restrict Access section (last section if you don't use completion tracking, next to the last if you do).  You have several options...you can require a specific course grade before allowing access to the activity, or a grade on the specific SCORM.  The last field determines if you want them to see it or not before it is unlocked. If you use completion tracking and have turned it on in the SCORM, it is even easier, because you get extra options:  specific activity completion criteria.  It basically says, you can choose a status for the activity. Sorry the themes are so different, I switched between two different course sandboxes.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Question
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Annemarie, yes, network issues could be the culprit for your tracking issues: for the nature of a tracking session, e.g. if you don't close it ( LMSFinish / Terminate ), you could loose some information and triggering some events. That being said, network issues could happen not only for your provider's fault but, mostly, for the nature of the network connection of some of your end users, not stable enough to permit tracking information to be safely exchanged between the content and Moodle. Since your content provider has given you a reasonable explanation, you should ask him to find a solution like to re-transmit SCORM calls in case of network issues: it will cost some effort in coding such a SCORM calls queue manager but it will assure you that if there will be an issue, a re-transmit will be attempted... maybe as the last resort, a popup to the user telling about the inability to contact the Moodle server due to network issues: it will not solve your issues but it will give a clear feedback about what is going on. Another sensible area of issue is the cross-browser compatibility as well as the need of popups maybe being blocked by the end user: it depends on how your tracking logics have been coded in your SCORM content. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Storyline SCORM 1.2 SCOs Exit Course/LMSFinish Issue in Linux Moodle 2.4
ResponsesInList.Text: I am having an issue with Storyline SCORM 1.2 SCOs that were working fine in a Moodle 2.2 Windows implementation, but are now hitting a problem in a Moodle 2.4 installation on Linux. In doing some debugging work, I think I've identified where the issue is occurring and how it differs from the Windows installation. The issue occurs only when clicking the "Next" button in our course, where we have attached an "Exit Course" trigger. In the Storyline SCO debug window, a sequence of SCORM functions are called. The sequence looks like this: 1159: - In SCORM_Finish strExitType=SUSPEND, blnStatusWasSet=true 1160: - In SCORM_ClearErrorInfo 1161: - Setting Exit 1162: - In SCORM_TranslatgeExitTypeToSCORM strExitType-SUSPEND 1163: - Returning suspend 1164: - SCORM_CallLMSSetValue strElement=cmi.core.exit, strValue=suspend 1165: - In SCORM_GrabAPI 1166: - SCORM_GrabAPI, returning 1167: - Calling LMSSetValue 1168: - strResult=true 1169: - Returning true 1170: - Calling Commit 1171: - In SCORM_CallLMSCommit Now here is where the problem begins. In Windows Moodle 2.2, after calling LMSFinish, you see the following: strResult=true Returning True Returning True These lines are missing in Linux Moodle 2.2, which stem from the function SCORM_CallLMSFinish() defined in SCORMFunctions.js in the /lms folder in the published package. By looking at the API Debug window in Moodle, I see that LMSFinish is called, and then the API object shuts down. So the line "strResult = SCORM_objAPI.LMSFinish("");" from SCORM_CallLMSFinish() does not execute, since no API object exists. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Captivate 5.5 scorm not reporting completions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mia, I'm not a Captivate expert (never used!) but I can provide you some general hints when things seem to go crazy with SCORM: first, you need to be aware (probably you actually do it!) that everything - better, almost... bugs can always exist: If I recall an issue of yours, you're probably running a Moodle instance using Oracle as DB server : it could be that the issue is related to some problems with your data and the current SQL code - is managed by the content. In your case the content vendor is yourself with the help of Captivate which wraps your settings and resources with a proper set of HTML, JS, ... generally whatever required to play the SCORM content SCORM content is required to talk with the LMS (here, Moodle) using a common language and rules i.e. the Application Profile, through Javascript LMS (here, Moodle) needs to properly react according to the Application Profile Network availability can be an issue during the delivery of the content, preventing some of the Content<->LMS communication to be successfully processed: usually no content provider applies a good fallback strategy in case of errors during the communication with the LMS That being said, assuming that with "SCORM completions" you are talking about SCORM statuses and not Moodle completion (which "simply" adds an extra layer to the suggested testing process below) the best thing IMHO you can do is: [Optional but warmly suggested] create a clone of your production site (code and server deploy) to isolate your tests activate the Moodle debug feature: http://docs.moodle.org/23/en/Debugging#Debug_messages , DEVELOPER + Display debug messages activate the Moodle SCORM debug feature: http://docs.moodle.org/24/en/SCORM_FAQ#Debugging attend the two courses, good and bad, with the goal to replicate the issue for the bad carefully read the SCORM debug logs, http://docs.moodle.org/24/en/SCORM_FAQ#What_does_the_debugging_log_mean.3F . The wiki tells about the commands used to talk with the LMS via SCORM 1.2, being SCORM 1.3/2004 quite similar. The most relevant part are: start the communication ( LMSInitialize ), talks ( LMSGetValue / LMSSetValue ), sometimes commiting the talks during a long delivery ( LMSCommit ), close the communication ( LMSFinish ). Among these things the most important are setting score and status as well as closing the communication : closing the communication will allow Moodle to perform operations as per SCORM specs and evaluating its own features like compiling both gradebook and activty completion eventually share the logs here in this thread, using the Preformatted style and maybe just the relevant parts of them e.g. errors or missing commands having compared the delivery of the good and bad SCORM content once the SCORM issue has been identified, if it is not related to a bug in Moodle you need to play with Captivate to find the reason why it wrapped your content that way You can argue that (7) is the only relevant point but following the other steps will exclude issues in the Moodle instance as well as will improve your knowledge behind the wor(l)d "SCORM" . HTH , Matteo

The breakthrough that finally got me to the exact combination of settings was this link (no clue where I first read about it -- maybe on an Adobe forum): http://www.icslearninggroup.com/index.php/whitepapers-1/captivate-tips-and-tricks/ The most important thing I gleaned from that article was that just because Captivate makes a setting possible in its SCORM publishing settings does NOT mean that it's compliant and that the LMS will accept it. For me the problem was that I wanted to report just the number of slide views and have that be the completion criteria. It appeared possible in Captivate and perhaps that's accepted by some LMS' but that is not a SCORM-compliant feature and will not work alone as a completion criteria -- what I finally had to do is add a button to the last slide of my project that had a point attached to it, then I set all of the scoring and completion settings accordingly. I have been to a land of great pain / frustration and  back again over the last few days (and on a weekend too!!). In hopes of saving someone else the trouble I went through, attached are my final settings that worked in Captivate and Moodle for me. Oh -- I'm using Moodle 2.4 and Captivate 5.5. I will be installing the Captivate 6.x update this week so if I find anything else related to this with that version I will report back.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Captivate 5.5 scorm not reporting completions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mia, welcome back from your journey, really a good job! I think people using Captivate will have great benefits from your post. You could think at improving the docs in http://docs.moodle.org/24/en/Adobe_captivate by adding your use case too. Let me add some notes about your doubt regarding with identifiers , in the PDF: from specs perspective, identifiers should be unique within the same imsmanifest. xml file and often some of them could be involved in creating reports. Moodle doesn't care because it makes usage of the parent-child relationship between the elements in the Manifest but... I suggest you to adopt that constraint. Besides if you've more than 1 (!) Course it would be wise to extend the constraint to the whole Catalog, starting from the Course identifier, to get benefits from some cross-reporting too adopt human readable identifiers (being the human , here, who is charged to mantain the Catalog and/or to view Reports), if you have the opportunity to define them like in your screenshots i.e. for the Course identifier you could use an internal coding scheme - usually everyone creates it as a well defined Code in mantaining her/his own Catalog -, for the SCO identifier you could use just SCO_ n if you do not recycle some of those SCOs in other Courses otherwise you should adopt a good coding scheme at the LO level too, to mantain a LO-based Catalog (maybe skill-based) too. Please, note that it's a common practice not to use spaces (use _ or - instead) and to use just plain ASCII characters (English is AFAIK plain ASCII ) if you have a Course with more than a SCO you should adopt a different scheme to assign the title at both Course and LO level by using kind of a really short summary at the Course level and a topic-oriented sentence at the LO level HTH, Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM - WCAG 2.0 AA Compliant?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Kerry, SCORM 1.2 is an application profile i.e. a collection of standards and best practices focused in: creating self-contained objects, called SCO, able to talk with an LMS given a Data Model and an API aggregating, with sequencing too, SCOes in a collection, even with a hierarchy packaging them in one file called PIF That being said, SCORM requires ECMAScript to let the communication between SCO and LMS happen i.e., strictly speaking, it could be compliant with WCAG 2.0 Level AA but it totally depends on how the SCO is implemented in terms of code and how it will be accessed by the end user. HTH , Matteo

That debug message has been introduced with MDL-36641 : I suspect that the check gives a false positive because of HTTP HEAD is not correctly handled by the PENS URL. You could check it by temporarly disabling the "offending" check by adding one line of code as below (the green one) in mod/scorm/locallib.php : function scorm_check_url ($url) { return true; $curl = new curl; HTH, Matteo P.S.: found something but unrelated here, http://stackoverflow.com/questions/17591728/kenexa-lcms-8-2-content-to-moodle-lms-via-aicc-url .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error during: Moodle 2.5.2 AICC Direct URL
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Eric, no security issues at all: adding that line means that you're skipping the pre-check Moodle does to identify if that URL really exists, to avoid typos and unpredictable errors during the subsequent import which requires you to delete the activity and restart the import as well. HTTP HEAD is the appropriate way to do such a check because the server will return you all the HTTP Headers for that resource: there, you can find the answers (file exists, size, ...) without spending time to download the resource and trash it immediately, as it would occurs using HTTP GET when HTTP HEAD is not supported. That being said: you need to remember that if you'll update Moodle to a next version you'll be in the need of re-adding that line but... see below; I strongly suggest you to write to your Kenexa® LCMS vendor - refering this thread, too - asking for: [Bug] Change the HTTP Status and Reason Phrase returned when using HTTP HEAD against the PENS URL since the appropriate reply must be: HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed . Thanks to this issue we, you and me, were not able to quickly identify what was going on: indeed, HTTP 403 Forbidden means that, given your credentials, you're not authorize to access that resource, which is quite different from the situation described here; [Improvement - I think it's a bug] Provide support for HTTP HEAD calls too since it's a common practice before starting an import like that supported by PENS, to perform some checks including an HTTP HEAD hit to identify if the file really exists and what is the size of that file - on average it will potentially be a long transaction. HTH, Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM 1.2 Data Size Limitations?
ResponsesInList.Text: I am hip-deep in a major Moodle problem, and I can't seem to sort it out. We have been having trouble for weeks getting our SCORM packages to be able to score, resume, and complete properly, but after some focused research and testing, I felt like I finally understood all the settings in Moodle and Captivate and these issues seemed to be working.... ...Until we hit some of our longer quizzes, in which case the quiz would only remember some of the user's answers and would return them to a partially completed quiz. So, loooong story short, it looks like our Adobe Captivate quizzes pass too much data into SCORM's (version 1.2) cmi.suspend_data, which eventually results in a 405 error. Apparently, one of the limitations of SCORM 1.2 is that it can only hold about 4,000 characters, and we need more than that. We want our students to be able to review their quizzes, but this doesn't seem to be possible with this limitation. So, is anyone else having trouble with this limitation? I have done some searching and have found mention of it, but never found any helpful solutions. Here are the options that I've tried: SCORM 2004: I have tried working with this several times, but the results are flaky at best, and with the recent announcement that it is no longer even being worked on, I feel it's not worth pursuing. I find it frustrating that 1.2 is so outdated, 2004 is not supported, and Tin Can is still in process. It doesn't leave many options. (Please note I don't blame the developers who decided they didn't have the time to continue working on support for 2004. I'm just frustrated with my lack of options.) AICC: The Captivate SCORM packages won't even load in Moodle 2.5, so the error log can't even help me. I haven't been able to find much information about this format, so I don't know if it will even help if I can get it to work. Scorm Cloud: With the promise of SCORM 2004 support with Moodle, I installed the plugin, which is 2 years old and doesn't officially support Moodle 2.3 or higher. Several errors occur, though it didn't break significantly yet. It does seem to change the way the whole course works and looks, and I was really hoping to not have to learn yet another way to work with the courses, just to be able to record progress. I haven't eliminated it as an option, but I don't want to have to rework everything I have so far unless I really need to. Turning off "Resume Data" in Captivate. This works for the scoring and completing, but this kills a major function of the lessons—the ability to go back and see what you got wrong. So, long intro, quick questions: Has anyone else found a way around the suspend_data limitation with SCORM 1.2? Is there another option (Moodle add-on, extra settings) that I'm missing? I can't imagine that I'm the only one with this problem, but I haven't really seen any solutions. Am I missing something that will make one of the options above viable? Sorry for the long post, but I wanted to provide as much info as might be helpful. Thanks for your time and attention. Any help is welcome.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM 1.2 Data Size Limitations?
ResponsesInList.Text: SCORM Cloud works fine in 2.5 and higher (tested it myself last week) - you might need to get the code out of github instead of the Moodle plugins db though. SCORM 2004 should work ok if you only need the increase in cmi.suspend_data I've wondered if we should add a config setting to relax the cmi.suspend_data restrictions as it does come up a bit. You could do this yourself in code by finding this line in scorm_12.js.php CMIString4096 = '^[\\u0000-\\uffff]{0,4096}$'; and replacing it with something like: CMIString4096 = '^[\\u0000-\\uffff]{0,40960}$'; (added an extra 0 at the end of 40960) make sure you rebuild the cache/clear your local cache before checking to see if that works for you. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm no track in IE
ResponsesInList.Text: You also need to be aware that from IE9 onwards, 'onunload' events are not supported in unless the user specifically edits their group policy to allow them. The only way around this that I have found to support 'onunload' SCORMS in IE9+ is to make sure that the following is the first item in the 'head' section of the page's HTML: <meta http-equiv="X-UA-Compatible" content="IE=9" > The scorm module does attempt to do this via the $CFG-> additionalhtmlhead parameter in mod/scorm/player.php, but unfortunately, this does not work as the standard_head_html() function in lib/outputrenderers.php adds this as the last item in the header, rather than the first item (that it needs to be). Editing this function to put the $CFG->additionalhtmlhead at the top should work (or just asking people to use a proper web browser). It is also worth double-checking that the theme you are using calls 'standard_head_html()' as the very first item within the <head> section, as, from a quick glance, both the 'base' and 'bootstrapbase' themes (and probably all the rest) output the page title and favicon first (which again, due to the special way in which IE likes to make life difficult for web developers, will prevent the fix from working).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using SCORM modules (Lectora) with Multiple Assignable Units in 2.5
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Melanie: You will find eXe alive and kicking here: http://exelearning.net/?lang=en . It has many improvements and new features and it is being actively developed by many institutions and developers. I think your question is about SCORMs with more than one sco. In the particular language of SCORM, a sco is an instance of the SCORM data model, and therefore a grade. In eXe you can store them with the SCORM idevice. eXe creates a sco for each page and therefore, you can not pace more than one SCORM idevice in the same page. Moodle will not keep on developing SCORM2004 related features. It's a wise decision, because that version of the standard has very complex navigation specifications and you can place that kind of rules in Moodle. I would recommend you SCORM 12. If you publish a SCORM package in Moodle, you will find a configuration option named Grading method to define the behaviour of multiple grades inside the SCORM package: http://docs.moodle.org/22/en/SCORM_settings

ResponsesInList.Title: Closing a SCORM window with JavaScript
ResponsesInList.Text: It used to be that a SCORM activity could be closed with some variation of window.close() in the activity's HTML/ JavaScript host page, but this no longer works for me in the Moodle 2 SCORM environment.  This appears to be because the SCORM plug-in generates an HTML/JavaScript page based on YUI, and the html content of the SCO is no longer like the html included in the content package file. In any event, tightening browser security looks like breaking the windows.close() method as " there are certain security restrictions for using the close() method. The close method closes only windows opened by JavaScript using the open method." (from Javascript-Coder.com). This isn't yet entirely consistent across browsers, it seems, as I observe IE9 will close a window after asking for confirmation, but neither Firefox 6 or Google Chrome will respond to window.close() unless it is in a pop-up that was opened by JavaScript. After some experimentation based on the DOM of the html/JavaScript generated by the SCORM plug-in, I have found that the following will close a Moodle 2 SCORM pop-up when called by the SCO: <script Xlanguage="JavaScript" type="text/JavaScript"> function closeTheWindow() { var e = new Object(); e.preventDefault = false; content.close_window(e); } </script> However (a) this is a kluge with no guarantee of future-proofness, and (b) it contradicts the principle of transportability between SCORM LMSs. This post is made in the hope that you have a better solution for closing a Moodle 2 SCORM activity from within the activity's HTML/JavaScript host, that you're willing to share.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle upgrade from 2.4 to 2.5
ResponsesInList.Text: When you do an in-place upgrade (warning: good backups), the database and moodledata folder are adjusted to the new specifications (tables/fields/files/folders addd/dropped/adjusted). The upgrade should not affect any tables/fields that you added to the database yourself. A better way can be to clone your database and moodledata folder and use the copies to create the new version of Moodle. Moodle code is usually placed in a new folder parallel to the old code. You can then compare the php files that were edited by you and modify the new version accordingly. It is more work than using git -based merge, which is also possible to do, but safer since you can first evaluate the new functionality and decide how to transfer a given add-on feature.
