ResponsesInList.Title: Increasing the amount of data Moodle can store from a SCORM module
ResponsesInList.Text: I am creating a self-reflection course using Lectora, which will include rating knowledge of specific topics using likert scale questions, as well as open text reflections. As it will be used throughout an entire qualification, covering about 10 topics, I need the course to save the learner's reflections so they can open it up along the way, add information, amend information, etc. The problem I have is that it appears that the amount of data that the Lectora course can report back to Moodle to store is quite limited, and it tells me that Moodle can only store 255 characters per variable, which isn't enough if I want the learner to write a 3-5 paragraphs. Is there some way in Moodle to increase the amount of data that it can store per variable and for the whole SCORM course, so that the learner's reflections are retrieved each time the learner opens the self-reflection course? Also, is it just a setting in Moodle regarding the amount of data that can be stored per SCORM course, or is it also something within Lectora (linked to the SCORM standards applied when publishing the content to SCORM 1.2)? Thanks Jacki

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Increasing the amount of data Moodle can store from a SCORM module
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jacki, SCORM 1.2 is an application profile that defines, among the others, the Data Model for the tracking data and the Data Type for each element of this Data Model. The size of an element is based on the Data Type properties i.e. it is Lectora's responsibility to take care of such limitations and overcome them someway e.g. using a compression for the internal data representation. Here is another useful thread that gives you an idea of how hacking Moodle SCORM code - formally breaking the SCORM 1.2 compliance! - to overcome the "limitation" - imposed by the SCORM 1.2 specs, NOT by Moodle which "simply" implements it - of the CMIString Data Type: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=232736 . HTH , Matteo

Question: I have noticed that after a course has been created and a SCORM is added to the course, the SCORM package essentially doubles the size of the course. Is this correct? Example: Course A has a SCORM that is 897MB. It currently has no other activities or resources. No one is enrolled in the course. Once the course is created the course size becomes 1.79GB (rounded down). Steps: I upload the SCORM as a zipped file. I select the zipped file as the resource for the activity. I make my other settings; grade, display, etc. I save and display. Everything works. When I go back inside the file picker, I can see that two file folders are created, one is the zipped package file. When I click it I can see the file is 897MB. There is also a second file called Content Files. Opening that folder, I can see that It is all the materials in the SCORM, unzipped. I can cannot determine the size, because I would have to pick each file and tally. I can assume it is 897MB (roughly). I cannot see a way to delete the folder with the Content files, or I would test that. So, back to my question, is it correct that a SCORM will double the size of a course? Thank you for any advice. Steve

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM doubles course sizes
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Steve, yes, it is correct: by design, the PIF (the ZIP archive) is used to check the need for updating the raw content files the next time you'll update the activity settings e.g. adding a new PIF (an updated version) or changing another setting. If you want to overcome such a design you could publish your PIF using an external files repository configured in the same server hosting the Moodle instance where the package will be published: more details in http://danmarsden.com/blog/2012/11/01/managing-scorm-content-in-moodle-2/ , External Package type . What is the drawback of saving disk space using the method above? Less security since anyone could download part of your content (i.e. the raw files) even if they're not enrolled in the course containing the SCORM activity or, worst, not registered in your Moodle instance. HTH , Matteo

About #3: I know quite well SCORM 2004 since its very first draft - being involved in my past Company to talk to ADL people while we were implementing the 1.3 early draft support in 2003, providing some inputs to introduce UI best practices into the spec too. The same, with a smaller scope, happened starting from 2000 for 1.2, having attended to some ADL PlugFest too - and I have some ideas about the potential failures of SCORM 2004 adoption by both Vendors and Customers but what I mean here is: if you look at the current proposal for packaging you'll see that that we're missing the basics i.e. the support for prerequisites to make a basic but powerful conditional navigation between the items, here AUs. ResponsesInList.Text: I'm wondering if LMSs adopting CMI-5 will "stop" their XAPI implementation As far as I can tell, CMI-5 is a superset of XAPI. So you have to implement XAPI fully to have a CMI-5 implementation. From the PoV of the CMI-5 folks, they state that tehy are using XAPI and defining messages semantically to make it useful. I am not familiar with XAPI, so I don't know if there are interesting parts of XAPI that aren't "used" by CMI-5. If that is the case, the question is: is feature frotz of XAPI actually useful? If so, AUs will want to use it, and your LRS implementation will be incomplete without it. CMI-5 is IMHO THE candidate to replace both AICC and SCORM Agreed. Actually, it opens the door to a new model, where a vendor can offer complex AU functionality that requires their servers. For example, QuestionMark could give you AUs that are just a "shell", or a just client side code that performs additinoal processing on QM's servers, and then have QM's server call your XAPI callback URL. Even more interesting than QM, I imagine richer interactions -- webbased video editing, or something like queeky.com . So a service model is now possible. As long as your LMS is internet-accessible. why should we drop simplified prerequisites? I think they (reasonably) expect the LMS to control that, provide more sequencing and navigation support. My gut feeling is that SCORM 2004 navigation and sequencing stuff isn't widely loved nor implemented. Why? To control prerequisites usefully across vendors/suppliers of LOs, you need to also standardize the namespace. That's just never going to happen (I've been part of attempts to standardize the namespace across NZ govt, a notably congenial group, and it was nearly impossible -- anywhere else, forget about it). The course author should drive this, tag activities (quizzes, LOs) with appropriate achievement and prerequisite terms from his/her own preferred vocabulary (or the institution vocab). And navigation... the LMS wants to control that. Trying to reimplement that puts both the LO interop standard and the LOC content in a collision course with the LMS... so many ways this can go wrong... These are my opinions -- actually, I'll ask more about these topics here today.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can't find page to edit SCORM package and replace course file!
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Barry, Moodle 2.x has changed the way it manages the whole of the files used in the application in a way to be much consistent at the application - not at the human! - level and disk space saving. The drawback is that you can't change files directly into the file system of the server , like in Moodle 1.x, because only Moodle itself knows how to find them in the file system of server. If you're interested in the technical aspects, read more at: http://docs.moodle.org/dev/File_API http://docs.moodle.org/dev/File_API_internals That being said, Quick Fixes are part of real life (see also here ): such way of fixing should be done at the LMS level only when the LMS itself is able to keep an history of the changes i.e. when you've an LCMS. Otherwise, that's what I'm suggesting, it should be wiser to fix the SCORM package far from the LMS i.e. save the changes into a Source Code Management (SCM) system and create a new package with a different file name to track that it is different from the previous ones, potentially with references, in the file name, to your SCM to identify the set of files used to create it. DAVRoot is something I coded to understand the way Moodle 2.x works with files as well as to debug issues in the Moodle 2.x AICC/SCORM Module and.. it is also possible to use it to access the new Moodle Virtual File System even to apply Quick Fixes . HTH, Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: AICC export URL
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Michael, it depends on how the Package is structured on your web server : the Enable direct AICC URL is a nice opportunity if you want to share just one AU, out of a structure and Moodle will create, on-the-fly, the required descriptors to launch that AU as a local activity. If you want to share structured packages you should create a so called skinny package, where the pointer to each of your AUs will be replaced with absolute paths i.e. no more relative, pointing now to your web server and you'll redistribute that "special" package: the package will contain just the AICC descriptor files, that's the reason for being skinny . When Moodle will import it, tracking will be done by Moodle while files will be served from your web server: authorization will be out of this game and up to your overall deployment (e.g. based on client IP addresses). HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: results of quiz scorm
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, just to clarify further, do you mean the score in the quiz is not the same as the grade shown in the moodle gradebook? Check whether 'Normalize Score to XXX' is set in the quiz settings (in the iSpring program), and that Maximum Grade in the 'Grade Settings' of the moodle SCORM package is also set to XXX.  The two values should be the same (by default they would both be set to 100). Otherwise, if you mean the report at end of the quiz is not the same as the results shown in the moodle, as far as I know you can only get such a report sent to an email address you specify in the quiz settings (in the iSpring program), but there doesn't seem to be any option to directly send it to each individual quiz taker. There is, however, an option which allows you to ask the quiz taker to enter their email address, and then another option to use their address as the "From" email address when it gets sent to you or the address you specified. You could then set up a rule or filter in your email program to automatically forward (or auto-reply) the report to the quiz taker.  I haven't tried this myself, but I don't see why it shouldn't work. Boris.

ResponsesInList.Text: In addition , I've just found this issue ( as shown below) . To conclude , as my understanding it said that I can't track the information or activity if I use external Scorm since there are some problem about the communication. Is that true ? Do I misunderstand ? "External Package type External package type is disabled by default on new installations – it is not a great method of linking to packages as under certain circumstances your packages will not pass back any grade or tracking information to Moodle. If enabled and selected it provides a text field to paste a URL to a remote imsmanifest. xml (in an unzipped remote SCORM package) – this allows SCORM content to be hosted outside your Moodle site and the content is played from the external location and is not unpacked/copied into Moodle storage. This also means that if you update the SCORM package then the latest content will always be loaded (unless you update your core imsmanifest.xml file as this file is copied into Moodle) – be very careful updating your imsmanifest.xml file; if your SCO identifiers change then tracking information for any removed SCO identifiers for any previous user attempts will be cleared from the Moodle database . For the external package type to work – your SCORM content MUST be located under the same url as your Moodle site – If the base url is different from your Moodle url then built in web browser security will block cross- domain communication and no grades/tracking information will be passed back to Moodle. Adobe Flash and modern browsers (ever since IE 6) prevent cross-domain communication. If you really need your packages to sit outside Moodle on a different URL you should look at other options for hosting your content. To enable the External package type go to: Admin > Plugins > Activity modules > SCORM package tick the box for “Enable external package type” "

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can I use the external Scorm package from the different server ?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, external content work as expected but tracking, unless your Moodle instance and the external content run both under the "domain" of your Moodle instance e.g. if your Moodle instance is accessed via http://hostname/moodle and your external content is hosted in http://hostname/shared everything will be fine otherwise you'll miss the tracking features of SCORM. It's not a Moodle issue but a limit in the SCORM Specs called " SCORM Cross-Domain Issue ": other specs are not affected by this issue e.g. AICC or the emerging eXperience API. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Course marks itself complete as soon as it's opened
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi John, One thing you can do that will help you out a lot in getting what you need from the vendor is to enable scorm debugging and obtain an API log for a complete session for one of the SCORM packages in question. http://docs.moodle.org/23/en/SCORM_FAQ#Debugging http://docs.moodle.org/23/en/SCORM_FAQ#What_does_the_debugging_log_mean.3F One common issue with SCORM content is that data is seldom sent through the API. Ideally, upon launch, cmi.core.lesson_status is set to "incomplete," not "complete." Then some data (usually including cmi.core.lesson_location, and possibly updates to cmi.core.score.raw) is sent through the API every time the learner advances a traditional "page." Some SCORM packages send all reporting data at the very end of the activity. This may be the case for your problematic packages, based on your description. If you can easily hack the SCORM package, then a few things you may want to try to do is 1) update cmi.core.lesson_location every time the learner accesses a page 2) update cmi.core.score.raw (or cmi.core.lesson_status) on exit (using a onPageUnload() or other JavaScript event). This will be easier to do if the content is mostly HTML and JavaScript. It'll be a bit harder if it's HTML that loads a SWF. It really depends on the library being used, and whether or not you can easily hook into it. Best of luck!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Updating SCORM with new content
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Nathan, nothing IF you do not change the item identifiers, otherwise the removed identifiers will be deleted from the database , tracking data included (silently at the moment, details in MDL-24057 ), to avoid orphan data. Grades will be updated according with the tracking data belonging to the new SCORM package. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Updating SCORM with new content
ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry to butt in - but is there any reason why updating a SCORM package authored in Storyline with one authored in Captivate should clear the grades and progress? (given that the manifest IDs are the same?)? Having a lot of trouble with this one - any pointers gratefully appreciated Simon Humby

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Updating SCORM with new content
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Simon, following your question in https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=228991#p994441 here is my reply: you need to take care of the item identifiers and not (only) of the manifest identifier in order to prevent loosing the old tracking data, recorded before the update. To do that, you need to: build your course with Captivate; open both the manifests, the old one created with Storyline and the new one created with Captivate; copy the item identifiers from the old manifest to the new manifest, keeping the tracking data accordingly (first item of the old must match the first item of the new). Identifiers can be changed using a Text Editor - keeping care of not breaking the XML e.g. by removing double quotes - or, if you're running Windows, using an XML Editor like XML Notepad 2007 ; re-create the zip archive, containing the new manifest file with the restored identifiers Then you'll need to verify your work: publish the old package (Storyline) in a private course, closed to your users; attend to it to collect some tracking data; update the activity with the new package (Captivate) and, without attending at it, check the tracking reports to verify the expected tracking data from the previous run. HTH, Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM SCO Completed Navigation Status Problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, it's a LMS responsibility to decide when CMI data should be stored from the browser into the server , providing feedback to the user too, but the LMS must store CMI data when LMSCommit() and LMSFinish() are called by the content. Moodle, for a nice user experience, limits the communication with the server to what required by the SCORM RTE spec so try to call LMSCommit() after setting the completed status. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM Exit Activity v 2.33
ResponsesInList.Text: I've been scanning many of the posts here and don't see anything like my question... I'm currently running 1.9 but am working on an upgrade to 2.4/2.5 (if it is released in time) and have noticed differences I'm not sure represent proper behavior. In general, I find the SCORM functionality much improved in 2.33, which is the version I'm testing but there are a couple things that don't scan for me.  I'll start by describing 1.9 behavior and then describe what 2.33 does with the same scenario. In 1.9, I set all my modules to open in a new window.  I click the activity and get a the summary and an Enter button.  When you click the Enter button on a SCORM Activity, it changes the page to one when recommends turning off a pop-up blocker if a window doesn't open and includes an Exit Activity link AND opens the SCORM in a new window.  I added some custom text to the pop-up blocker page to provide extra stuff my users need, particularly if they have blockers on.  Users know to click Exit Activity or the course shortname in the breadcrumbs to get back to the course navigation page when they close the SCORM window. In 2.33, I also set all my modules to open in a new window.  When I click the activity, it provides the activity summary and a participation summary (like this: Number of attempts allowed: Unlimited; Number of attempts you have made: 0, Grading method: Highest attempt, Grade reported: None) with the Enter button.  I click Enter, the summary page doesn't change and the SCORM opens.  When I complete the SCORM and close, I'm still on the introductory SCORM screen but it still says I have no attempts, a score of 0, etc.  And (other than the course main page breadcrumb) there is no way to get back to course navigation.  If I refresh the page, it updates the information (still now way back to course nav). That's fine for me, I get what's going on.  Not so much for less computer skilled users. Some of my users really struggle to understand the breadcrumbs philosophy and need alternate navigation.  These same users will be confused and upset because they believe the module is not reporting (even though it is) and I envision chaos and craziness for months to come (I'm not sure how that's different from my current state but maybe just different chaos and crazy).  I could add information to address the discrepancy, but many users don't actually read the directions and that may be of limited value. Is there something I need to set to change the behavior?  Is it different in 2.4/2.5?  Ideas?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM and Moodle Issue - averaging the scores from multiple quizzes
ResponsesInList.Text: I would guess it is your scorm settings. I don't work with Articulate but I've used several other authoring softwares...basically, if you have two quizzes, unless you have changed the settings, it will average the two when the module concludes.  It probably has something to do with a variable like AICC_Score. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Displaying only the last interactions in Moodle?
ResponsesInList.Text: Without seeing a debugging report for 1 full session of the scorm activity, it's really hard to advise you about how to change things. That said, you may want to have a look at your attempts settings. It would seem as though every time the learner accesses the scorm activity a new attempt is logged. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Displaying only the last interactions in Moodle?
ResponsesInList.Text: So it looks like cmi.core.lesson_status is set to "completed" at least 3 times. Setting cmi.core.lesson_status to "completed" or "passed" is one of the ways the SCORM package tells Moodle to end the attempt. If you want only a single attempt, with only the final results the student wants displayed, avoid setting cmi.core.lesson_status to "completed" until the student has completed his or her final changes. Usually people do that by connecting the change in cmi.core.lesson_status to a button click. The student can load up the activity and exit several times, but cmi.core.lesson_status stays "incomplete" until the student selects the "Submit My Responses" button.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Wrong URL Used for SCORM datamodel.php
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Phil, how is your $CFG-> wwwroot configured? I'm supposing it is configured using the internal address ( moodle.test.health.local ) and there's no link translation, done by TMG, within the body/payload of the HTTP Response. That link is correctly hard-coded within mod/scorm/datamodels/scorm_*.js.php by means of DoRequest(myRequest,"<?php p($CFG->wwwroot) ?>/mod/scorm/datamodel.php ",... i.e. without translating the paths inside the body of each HTTP Response, you should configure your $CFG->wwwroot to point directly to the outside hostname ( theo.test.dhhs.tas.gov.au ), telling Moodle ( getremoteaddrconf : Home ► Site administration ► Server ► HTTP ) you're using a Reverse Proxy in front of your instance to let Moodle get the real client remote address, mainly for logging and black listing purposes. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Warning: Plan to remove "IMS Package type" setting from SCORM

The features it provided were mostly replaced by the Repository API in Moodle 2 This is a pre-warning to let you know we plan to remove this SCORM related setting from Moodle 2.6 - it doesn't work and just adds unecessary complexity to the code and UI - posting here to give people a couple of months to object before I remove it - you will need to give me a good reason to keep it as I'm 95% sure it doesn't do anything useful in the current state. See MDL-39239 for some more detail. MDL-28579 is a feature request to add some of the missing functionality that was possible using the old imsrepository to Moodle 2 - I'm hoping we might get this into 2.6 as well.

However, the SCORM is not triggering completion. I can’t think of any other reason for it not to trigger. Any ideas? Moodle 2.3.2

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM doesn't trigger completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi John, If you set up a quiz to be available according to a grade condition based on the score of a given SCORM activity, the quiz will become available only when students will reach that grade condition while attempting the SCORM. You may want to check the grade options set for your SCORM activity and when the package communicate to Moodle the score obtained by students. However, since you are using Storyline there are good chances that your package is composed by a single SCO. If this is the case and if you set up your package to communicate SCO complete/incomplete status, another option you could try is using the completion setting of the SCORM, then configure conditional access to quiz based on the SCORM SCO status: http://docs.moodle.org/23/en/SCORM_settings#Activity_completion_settings To configure conditional access to an activity based on completion status of another activity, make sure activity completion is enabled on your site and in the course as well: http://docs.moodle.org/23/en/Activity_completion

ResponsesInList.Title: Suspend Data Limit in Moodle SCORM Implementation
ResponsesInList.Text: We are currently using Moodle 1.9.9 and have used Lectora to create a SCORM-compliant course that captures a lot of student input.  During testing we after entering a lot of data we are encountering an LMSSetValue Error which appears to be related to the amount of data we are attempting to save in Moodle. According to a support engineer at Articulate: >  SCORM 1.2 is very limited in the amount of "suspend data" that it can send to the LMS (max. 4,000 bytes).  SCORM 2004 3rd edition currently supports about 64,000 characters of suspend data. I have read in Moodle Docs that not all aspects of SCORM 2004 are currently supported in Moodle. If we publish our course to the SCORM 2004 standard: 1. Will we have to upgrade to Moodle 2.0.x? 2. Even if we do, will this solve our maximum data limitation problem? Thanks for any help you can provide. Verne Morland ROI Learning Services Dayton, Ohio USA

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Suspend Data Limit in Moodle SCORM Implementation
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Verne - Moodle supports all of the SCORM 1.2 specifcation from 1.9 onwards, and the core 2004 specification (basically minus seq/nav).  The only way you are going to know whether it works for you (2004) is by being conservative around what features you use, and basically trying it out. Cheers, Piers Harding.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Suspend Data Limit in Moodle SCORM Implementation
ResponsesInList.Text: This is a follow-up and success report to the message that I posted last month about the 4,000 byte (character) suspend data limit in SCORM 1.2.  (For those not familiar with the SCORM spec, "suspend data" is the data that students can type into input fields in the course which will be preserved for them if they close the course and return to it later.) As I noted in my original message, we have a large course with a number of essay questions and we quickly found that we were exceeding the 4,000 byte limit that is specified in SCORM 1.2.  Through some research we determined that the spec for SCORM 2004 Third Edition expands the suspend data limit to 64,000 bytes, so my question was whether Moodle 1.9 and/or 2.0 supported this expanded limit. Piers Harding was quick to respond that he thought that Moodle would support 64,000 characters and he even provided a snippet of code that showed that value. I am pleased to report that after we republished our course from Lectora specifying SCORM 2004 and installed it in Moodle 1.9 the course is now accepting and preserving student data well in excess of the old 4,000 byte limit. Thanks, Piers, for your help on this issue and thanks to you, Dan, and the others who have and are working so hard to provide and support SCORM capabilities in Moodle.  Your efforts are appreciated. Regards, Verne Morland Managing Partner ROI Learning Services Kettering, Ohio, USA

ResponsesInList.Title: Ideas needed for improving the SCORM settings page
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear SCORM users, Coming soon in Moodle 2.5 are forms with collapsible sections . You can see them in action on the QA testing site . Consequently, many of the activity settings pages now need some reorganising in order to make the most of this new functionality. Here's my suggestion for improving the SCORM settings page (with section names in bold): General Name Description Display description on course page Content Package file Appearance Display package Width * Height * Options (Prevented by some browsers) * You'll notice I've moved the package file to it's own section named 'Content', making it consistent with the IMS content package and other resource type settings pages. Both 'General' and 'Content' sections would be open (not collapsed) by default. I also moved the available from/to settings to their own section named 'Availability' and changed the name 'Display Settings' to 'Appearance', also for reasons of consistency with other settings pages (see the setting pages review spreadsheet ). Finally, I gave 'Additional settings' a more descriptive name of 'Attempts', though I was wondering whether 'Attempts management' or something else would be better? If you have any comments, suggestions for further improvement, or ideas for other ways of reorganising the SCORM settings page, please let us know, so that MDL-38757 can be fixed in time for the release of Moodle 2.5.

ResponsesInList.Title: Assigning a Grade Category to a SCORM Activity
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a course which is broken up into modules.  The grades for each module consist of assignments and SCORM activities , which automatically report the grades for the quizzes embedded in them.  The assignments are categorized according to the module name so those grades will show up as being related.  How do I assign the SCORM activities to those same categories, so that when I look at the gradebook, those SCORM activity grades will appear under a given assigned category--as the assignment grades do?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assigning a Grade Category to a SCORM Activity
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Christopher, Although you can't set a grade category for a SCORM activity in the settings, as you can for assignments, you can do so within the gradebook by clicking the 'Categories and items' tab then 'Full view'. You can then select the SCORM activity and use the 'Move selected items to' dropdown menu to move it into the desired grade category.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Edit SCORM package new ID?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Michael, can you elaborate your question? You can publish the same Learning Package several times even into the same Course and for Moodle they will always be different things with the advantage, in 2.x, to be stored once to preserve disk space: tracking data will be coupled with the Activity instance regardless the Learning Package being the same. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: interaction between jquery quiz and Moodle scorm1.2
ResponsesInList.Text: Look at the same examples I referred you to before. The SCORM object uses a JavaScript wrapper to send data through the SCORM API. This is true whether the SCORM content is Flash-driven, JavaScript-driven, whatever. This resource (view the 1.2 version) will show you the data elements available to you via the SCORM API. The Pipwerks wrapper is a stable library with which to access that API. So you use your jQuery however you want to present content in the page, and when you want to save data, you just make a call using your wrapper of choice. http://scorm.com/scorm-explained/technical-scorm/run-time/run-time-reference/ To watch the API at work, you can turn on SCORM debugging in Moodle and watch the API log. I would recommend doing that with the Pipwerks samples.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Update a file in a scorm package
ResponsesInList.Text: This is possible by editing the SCORM Activity.  The exact steps depends on your version of Moodle. Open your course, then select the SCORM Activity to update. For Moodle 1.9, in the activity window you click "Update this SCORM/AICC" click the Choose or Upload a file button upload a new package or navigate to the folder that contains the individual file you want to replace For Moodle 2.x, under SCORM/AICC Administration click Edit Settings click the Choose a file button If you are uploading the entire package again, select the Upload a file button if you are just uploading an individual file, select the Server files button and navigate to the folder that contains the file you want to replace IMPORTANT: If you want to replace individual files and not update the zip file, you must have the Auto-update frequency set to "Never".  This function determines how often Moodle unzips the SCORM package to update the course. Hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM and short answer / essay question grading
ResponsesInList.Text: Greetings, This is not a specific technical problem, but a general inquiry as to how people are handling this issue.  We use several SCORM modules that contain both automatically graded (multiple choice) and manually graded (short answer / essay) questions.  The SCORM module automatically grades the MC questions and puts the recorded scores into the Moodle gradebook.  But we are trying to figure out how to best deal with the manual grading.  Using the Interactions report, we can see the student respones, but the horizontal summary format is inconvenient for teachers to scroll way out horizontally to read student responses.  It additionally, there is no way for teachers to record a grade from here, so they must do they seperately by editing the gradebook directly, and there isn't a good way to give student's feedback about their answers. How do other Moodle users handle this situation?  Are we crazy to have manually graded items in a SCORM module? The quiz module provies a nice interface for manually grading essay / short answer questions -- we are looking for a way to do something similiar with SCORM.  We appreciate any and all suggestions /help. Thanks!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM and short answer / essay question grading
ResponsesInList.Text: Are we crazy to have manually graded items in a SCORM module? Possibly. SCORM data elements aren't really designed to accommodate essay responses in the first place. Moodle has other tools for essay questions, and most people use those instead.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM and short answer / essay question grading
ResponsesInList.Text: Yea, I agree.  Problem is that we are just piloting moodle right now with this school.  So content is in Scorm to avoid being locked to one LMS.  But content standards require some open ended assessment in our area.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM and short answer / essay question grading
ResponsesInList.Text: Without being locked into a LMS, your options are rather limited.  If you are just looking for some keywords in the response, you could create some javascript to analyze the response against those keywords and provide a score back to the course.  If the responses are more subjective, then you will have to design an external means of grading the open ended questions and in the SCORM module setup a means of submitting those open ended questions.  The simplest form would be to submit the responses via email to an email account setup specifically for this purpose. Alternativley, if you have some control over the server you could create a server side page that accepts a submission from the SCORM course and stores it in a database for later review.  Of course then you will also need a means of someone retrieving the information, grading it and submitting the grade.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Aicc Interactions on Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Unfortuantely, the Moodle reporting for SCORM and AICC courses is not as rebust as SCORM Cloud.  The SCORM/AICC is located in the course description on the course page.  It looks something like "View reports for X attempts." Clicking on this gives you a list of all attempts for all participants. Locate the individual that you would like to view, then click on the attempt number, which gives you Status Time and Score. Click on the Track details and that gives you more detail. I don't have any courses that use cmi.intereactions so I do not know if that information will appear in the details, but it is worth a try. If that doesn't work, you can wait for the new report engine that is being worked on, or you can install the Ad-hoc database queries plug-in and create a query to extract the information you want.  This plug-in is at the global level so if you want to report on a particular course or individual, you have to create a query that will  filter the results for that course and/or individual. There is a list of contributed reports for the plug-in here that may be useful for writing your own query.

ResponsesInList.Text:
As far as I understand your scenario... You might want to use: 
```text
scorm.
set
(
"cmi.location"
,
 
"some string indicating the current stage your are in"
)
;

scorm.
set
(
"cmi.suspend_data"
,
 
"your custom suspend_data string"
)
;

scorm.
set
(
"cmi.score.raw"
,
 
score 
)
; // to indecate some Score to the student acivement on that stage

scorm.
save
(
)
;
```
 You can re-call and itterate over these sequance of commands to save accumulative data from your activity into Moodle's scorm engine/ database (idea came from original tip: http://pipwerks.com/2010/07/27/scorm-tip-dont-forget-to-commit/ )

ResponsesInList.Text: John, the only real difference between displaying content in a browser window and downloading it is how the browser handles it. While it is possible to make saving content more inconvenient, it can still be done. There is no effective means to prevent someone from saving web content. More generally, once something is in digital form, it can easily be copied. That's what computers do. btw , are you sure that all of your students have power point on their machines? what if they don't? It is probably worth saving the file in flash format to be sure they can see it. OpenOffice.org can do this for free.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Preventing Download of Powerpoint Presentation in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Not wishing to be negative but you  are going to struggle with this. Because to be honest, however he adds it, if students wanted to, they could take a screenshot of bits of it or make a screencast (video) of it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Yep, can't be done.
ResponsesInList.Text:
For the browser to display anything, it must be downloaded first. Generally the first thing the browser does with anything is save it to the drive, in the cache. The most you can do is suggest that the browser may not want to ask the user where to save the file. Any bright 12 year old will save whatever they want though.

All of the major online music retailers, Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, Napster, etc. spent MILLIONS of dollars trying to come up with music that could be played but not readily saved. ( DRM ). Every major seller has given up on that idea and just sells easily portable .mp3 files. They gave up after investing millions because they found there's just no way to make it work reasonably.

See also DVD. The movie studios spent millions trying to make it "impossible" to copy a DVD. On Google you can find a ripped copy of ay movie you want, often before the DVD is even officially released.

We spent about a year trying to develop a solution to this as well. The best you can technically do is mark the copies so if one gets out you can figure out who did it. Other than that, provide something of value aside from just the digital file - like interaction with the instructor.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: All SCROM course fail to load - FlashPlayer
ResponsesInList.Text: On our hosting platform this issue is most commonly associated with zlib compression. Classic presentation is that the base HTML file and SWF are loaded into the SCORM player, but the SWF is not able to load any audio or video assets, and therefore stalls. It sounds very similar to what you're describing. You can check your zlib compression settings as an admin by loading up the Server > phpinfo page. But zlib compression would need to be disabled by a server admin.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scroll bars with SCORM in current window
ResponsesInList.Text:
I also experienced scroll bars around the exercise frame in the scorm player. For me, the following solution worked: Adapt the following file: <moodle_root_dir>\ server \moodle\lib\yui\2.9.0\build\assets\skins\sam\skin.css look for: 
```text
.yui-layout-scroll div.yui-layout-bd{overflow:auto;}
```
 and change it in: 
```text
.yui-layout-scroll div.yui-layout-bd{overflow:visible;}
```
 Then refresh your local cache, and the scroll bars have disappeared.

ResponsesInList.Title: The Quiz Attempt feature
ResponsesInList.Text: Good afternoon. One of my responsibilities where I work is to facilitate the training program (Moodle-driven). When a student takes a quiz and makes below a certain grade, they have to retake it, but we don't want them to re-take it immediately because the goal is for them to re-study the material, and retain the information - versus just answering from short-term memory. So a 30-minute window is enforced. To accomplish this, we limit each quiz to 1 attempt and then increase it at the appropriate time. However, there are some problems with this process: 1. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Specific file in scorm package does not load..
ResponsesInList.Text: It's probably not Reload, but a localhost installation of Moodle, of the same version, that would be most helpful to your diagnostics. Set up a localhost install and see if the package plays fine on localhost. I don't understand how you can rename the file and still have the call from the parent SWF or HTML file work...? All things that aren't easily checked out without access to the content. Windows handles capitalization and spaces in file names differently that linux, so those are things to look at in the file names, both in the calling file and in the manifest. Many of the issues with file access from an active SCORM session are actually related to server settings, and not to the package at all. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM not loading
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jarred, Take a minute to congratulate yourself on having such a simple problem. You can set the Moodle SCORM activity to only allow a single attempt or set the number of (multiple) attempts allowed. But in order for there to be multiple attempts, rather than editing the settings of the existing attempt during SCO launch, the end-user does have to indicate that a new attempt is desired. That lets Moodle know to serve up a blank set of SCORM API data to the active SCO, so that, for example, rather than lesson_status of "completed," the SCO again gets a lesson_status of "not started". Another option is to configure your SCORM package so that users can still access the content even after lesson_status is set to completed. It really depends on what your goal is for your end-users.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM file is bigger than the maximum size!
ResponsesInList.Text: This situation is what I call "Pants". I've followed over a dozen links, recommendations and made as many attempts at configuration my php.ini and Moodle settings - sorry! File too big! I guess if our learners only want to read text on a page then that's acceptable, but perhaps they want a video or two?! Sorry, I'm of no help, but if anyone else would like to provide a real solution for this, or point to one of the many forum posts about this, then it would be welcome. In addition, an explanation of why we need to jump through all of these hoops would also be great, just out of curiosity ... you know... as a non Moodle core developer...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM file is bigger than the maximum size!
ResponsesInList.Text: What you need to understand is that these limits are there for a good reason. If anyone could upload arbitrarily big files to your server, then they could eaisly crash it just by throwing a lot of 10GB files are your Moodle. That would fille up the hard disc, and then the server would crash, so it would be an easy denail of service attack (DOS). (Or things might overload in other ways.) The Internet is a hostile place, therefore every bit of software in the stack has protections against this: The web server ( Apache or IIS ) has a limit for teh biggest POST request it will accept. So does PHP. and so does Moodle, since we need a more nuanced approach that depends on detailes that Moodle knows (e.g. students in this forum can only upload upto 100kb files, but teachers should be allowed to upload huge SCORMs to their course.) So, to allow large files through, you have to find all the things that implement an uploaded file / POST request size limit, and relax the limit. Alternatively, you could use one of the other mehtods for getting files in to Moodle, like the filesystem repository, or another repository plugin.

ResponsesInList.Title: Commit SCORM data, lazily, to avoid data loss
ResponsesInList.Text: I'd like to get your opinions about something.  We have some code we're using locally which may be of use to others. It seems to us it is good for data sent from a SCORM package, via SetValue(), to eventually be stored in the database so that student progress data isn't lost.  Preserving data is good, we think, even if the network connection is lost, the browser crashes, etc. a few minutes later. Some SCORM packages don't explicitly call Commit() regularly for whatever reason.  Moodle currently doesn't commit data itself unless the SCORM package explicitly calls Commit(), so data can be lost.  We wrote some code for local use which will Commit() the data 60 seconds afer the values are set, unless the package Commit()s sooner. As written, it's a lot like how most OSes write data to disk, to be efficient. It calls commit only if the client (SCO) hasn't already done so explicitly, and calls it only once per 60 seconds even if many values are pending, and doesn't call it at all if no values are pending. Would this be ueful to other people?  If so, I can re-arrange our new code in the form of a patch to scorm/datamodels/scorm_13.js.php.  The patch would basically consist of adding to SetValue(): setAutoCommit.timeout = window.setTimeout(API_1484_11.Commit,30000, ""); But canceling that if Commit() is called explicitly: window.clearTimeout(setAutoCommit.timeout); Let me know what you think about adding this to the master Moodle. Currently our does some magic subclassing to alter the functionallity of the stock code without modifying the files, so I'll reformat it as a patch only if it sound slike the patch would be committed.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Commit SCORM data, lazily, to avoid data loss
ResponsesInList.Text: sounds like a nice idea. I think if we were to accept it for inclusion in core we'd probably need an admin setting included that has it off by default to start with - also as it would be classed as an improvement it would only be approved to go into the master branch - feel free to create a bug and attach your patch and I'll take a look.

ResponsesInList.Title: Externalizing some media assets in a SCORM training.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, Using Moodle 2.3, Adobe Captivate 6, and Rackspace as my CDN. What I want to do: Take the audio files on each slide and the video files (.mp4) that make up some other slides and host them on my CDN so that the server I am hosting moodle on doesn't have to store those things. An Adobe rep told me in a livechat yesterday that it wasn't possible to have SCORM packages as a .zip that look externally for resources because that's simply not the nature of a SCORM package.  This seems to go somewhat against what the Captivate software allows you to do: Using the Import Video option to add a video to a slide by specifying a URL from which to stream. Has anyone had any experience using SCORM packages within Moodle while externalizing some of the media resources?  The audio and video files make up the bulk of the size for the .zip files, and I'm interested in seeing what I can do to utilize my CDN to help with that content.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Externalizing some media assets in a SCORM training.
ResponsesInList.Text: It's pretty common - as long as you're only hosting static elements from your SCORM package in a CDN it should be fine - where you run into trouble is if you try to host the whole package externally - that's when you run into web browser security restrictions with cross- domain communication. The core elements listed in your imsmanifest. xml should probably be within the SCORM package, but there's nothing stopping you from embedding CDN content inside those elements - hope that helps/makes sense.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM initializing but displaying blank screen
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Cherise, your content is "violating" some of the SCORM rules about the sequence for the API calls and syntax: you need to specify a CMI element when calling *Value() ; you need to open a new tracking session, using LMSInitialize() , within the next SCO, before talking with the API with *Value() . HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM 1.2 Student Reponse Capped at 250 Charaters
ResponsesInList.Text:
Which SCORM element are you using to store the student response? If you are using cmi.interactions.n.student_response, what is the response type?

The value column in the tracking table is longtext, so you shouldn't be encountering truncation issues there. Is the entire response being stored in the database ?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM 1.2 Student Reponse Capped at 250 Charaters
ResponsesInList.Text: I believe this is the element I am using to store the student responses, cmi.interactions_0.student_response. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM 1.2 Student Reponse Capped at 250 Charaters
ResponsesInList.Text: According to the SCORM 1.2 standard, the interaction type dictates the length of the response.  For example, if it is a True/False question, the response is a single character (0 or 1, T or F).  If the interaction type is "performance", the response in the LMS is limited to 255 characters, regardless of the settings in your publishing tool.  I suspect this is the limit you are experiencing.  The database is not limiting the length, but I think the SCORM API is.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM 1.2 Student Reponse Capped at 250 Charaters
ResponsesInList.Text: Robert is correct - the ADL SCORM 1.2 spec states that student_response is limited to 255 characters. SCORM 2004 doesn't have the same limitations - so if the length of the response is the only issue you have you could publish your package as a SCORM 2004 package and that might suit your needs. important to note that full SCORM 2004 support is not yet available in Moodle so you may run into other issues related to SCORM 2004 but many people with your issue have just used SCORM 2004 and found it worked as they wanted.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: High CPU usage when accessing SCORM courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Phillip, Moodle 2.x has introduced a revolutionary mechanism to store files into the so called Moodle dataroot ( $CFG->dataroot ). Shortly: files are now stored into the file system using hashes and the database is used to map these hashes - "the real files" - to the context used to represent these files e.g. "filename", "area", "context". That being said, every time you call pluginfile.php the code will connect to the database: you need to give more power to your database e.g. giving more RAM to the server and room (e.g. innodb_buffer_pool_size , investigating also innodb_flush_method=O_DIRECT ) to the Moodle database instance. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: High CPU usage when accessing SCORM courses
ResponsesInList.Text: I've heard of some PHP versions causing a perf issue - make sure you're not using an older buggy PHP version and running into a PHP perf bug - also make sure you're running a php accellerator like xcache/eaccellerator etc. Are you using activity completion in the course? - do you have a large number of activities in the course that is running slow? - if so this post might be useful: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=209142#p914177

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: AICC aicc_data error
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Sabina, to let Moodle play an external AU which has been coded to talk with an LMS via AICC HACP, you need to configure, in Moodle: Enable direct AICC url , to let Moodle wrap on-the-fly an AICC package containing the AU pointed by the given URL Enable external AICC HACP , to let the external content to talk with Moodle via AICC HACP That's in Moodle. To know how things work in AICC HACP regardless the specific LMS, you need to carefully read the AICC Publications , at least: CMI001 CMI012 To test your package in order to debug the tracking logics I warmly suggest you to publish the AICC package locally in Moodle first: this will give you the possibility to check those logics in a sandbox and you'll have the possibility to use tools such Fiddler to look at the HTTP POST plain text payloads - the CMI datamodel - exchanged between your content and the LMS (here, Moodle) to eventually debug the content itself. HTH, Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: AICC aicc_data error

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: AICC aicc_data error
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Henry, give Dan's advice a try. BTW you should also check with a sniffer (e.g. Fiddler ) what is the very first call from your content (the launched AU) to the LMS (HTTP POST to aicc_url as per Moodle definition). AICC says that the first call must be a GetParam command and these are the required parameters to be HTTP POSTed for this first command: command version , which Moodle do NOT consider as mandatory session_id aicc_data in the request is usually used for writing methods like PutParam . Keep care of any HTTP 404 coming from your http://hostname/moodle/mod/scorm/aicc.php: it will give you evidence that your content is not providing at least one of the required AICC HACP parameters and reading Moodle replies through Fiddler will give you a message about the reason for replying with 404. A HTTP 404 reply from Moodle could be the reason for your content not being able to parse&load the aicc_data value. Refs: AICC Publications , CMI001 . HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: How to prevent students download videos from a scorm created by Adobe Presenter.
ResponsesInList.Text: I am developping lecture in video. I would like to prevent learners from downloading video (by Internet Download Manager, or the like). What should I do?? Thank a lot for your help

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to prevent students download videos from a scorm created by Adobe Presenter.
ResponsesInList.Text:
For the browser to display anything, it must be downloaded first. Generally the first thing the browser does with anything is save it to the drive, in the cache. The most you can do is suggest that the browser may not want to ask the user where to save the file. Any bright 12 year old will save whatever they want, however.

All of the major online music retailers, Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, Napster, etc. spent MILLIONS of dollars trying to come up with music that could be played but not readily saved. ( DRM ). Every major seller has given up on that idea and just sells easily portable .mp3 files. They gave up after investing millions because they found there's just no way to make it work reasonably.

See also DVD. The movie studios spent millions trying to make it "impossible" to copy a DVD. On Google you can find a ripped copy of ay movie you want, often before the DVD is even officially released.

We spent about a year trying to develop a solution to this as well. The best you can technically do is mark the copies so if one gets out you can figure out who did it. Other than that, provide something of value aside from just the digital file - like interaction with the instructor.

PHP 5.4 will probably no longer magically create objects when they are first referred to, w/o those warnings in contrast to the current PHP 5.3 - and previous versions - kind behaviour: this is an issue for many PHP apps that will be addressed when 5.4 will be officially released. BTW , why not using PHP 5.3 which is the last stable branch (now: 5.3.10)? It will save your life! HTH, Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Video contained in scorm file stuttering
ResponsesInList.Text: Any multimedia packaged in the SCORM package is served via direct download to the client. FPS won't mean a thing if the file is large, it's being dumped via direct download into the browser and/or your end-user's Internet connection is anything less than optimal. If your multimedia is large, you may want to investigate a CDN. Captivate has widgets to add media hosted on a CDN to your SCORM content without adding it to your SCORM package.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM score and the grade book

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM score and the grade book
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jennifer, What you've got here doesn't include the return values from Moodle. I am seeing one error, but it's lesson_status, and not the interaction element you were posting about earlier. If your Moodle installation isn't providing a SCORM API interactions log with debugging on, then you are in a version of Moodle prior to SCORM 1.2 certification, and you should upgrade. -A

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM score and the grade book
ResponsesInList.Text: Right. I finally got the interaction ids working properly (that was a different thread http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=148635 ). It turns out that those errors had to do with the way Lectora names interaction.ids for test questions with more than one possible correct response. When I set it to grade the question as one question rather than grading each correct response individually, I didn't get the cmi.interactions.id errors. The error I am currently working on correcting is the "LMSSetValue Error: cmi.core. lesson _status to [complete] Incorrect data type" This started after I st the grading method to Highest, max score of 100, 1 attempt. I didn't get the error when I had the grading method set to Learning Object -- though whether that is what caused this new error to occur, I can't say. I am told by my Moodle administrator that our version of Moodle is SCORM 1.2 compliant. Is there a directory where I can have him look for the API interactions log? I don't have administrator access myself.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM score and the grade book
ResponsesInList.Text: cmi.core.lesson_status valid value is "completed" not "complete" so your passing an incorrect string/data type to the lms.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM score and the grade book
ResponsesInList.Text: The correct value for lesson_status is "completed", not "complete". cmi.core.lesson_status (state (passed, completed, failed, incomplete, browsed, not attempted), RW) Indicates whether the learner has completed and satisfied the requirements for the SCO http://www.scorm.com/scorm-explained/technical-scorm/run-time/run-time-reference/

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM score and the grade book
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you, that resolved my problem.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM score and the grade book
ResponsesInList.Text: Heh heh heh. Same problem here, thanks ethan/Amy.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM score and the grade book
ResponsesInList.Text: And it appears to be case-sensitive too. "Completed" gave us endless headaches with the "LMSSetValue Error: cmi.core.lesson_status to [complete] Incorrect data type" error message. As soon as we changed " C ompleted" to " c ompleted" the problem was resolved.

ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi David:

May be this option is good for you:

1) publish all the Scorm files outside moodledata but in the same server (otherwise tracking won't work)
2) unzip all the files
3) link the Scorm activity to the manifest

The Scorm activity will work as usual but you will be able to update individual files without changing the whole package.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Package Builder Tool
ResponsesInList.Text: Just to add to the list, Lectora, SoftChalk and iSpring.  I use Lectora and Captivate.  Lectora has a PowerPoint integrator which lifts all your powerpoint objects and places them into your Lectora module.  I actually like this better than the way Captivate does it, as Captivate basically turns it into one static image--so for accessibility , Lectora wins.  Captivate is a bit tricky on accessibility and is hard to find good info on.  Lectora is tricky to learn because it has so many features and options but is easy to build in accessibility once you know what you're doing.  Captivate is cheaper but SCORM reporting features are weird. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 1.9.18 yields error loading AICC package from HealthStream

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM activity w/ no scoring
ResponsesInList.Text: In Lectora, on the last or next to the last page, set an On Show action which modifies the variable AICC_Lesson_Status.  Set the variable contents to completed (no capitals).  This will change the the status to complete/incomplete.  If you have a "test" in the module, in the test properties, uncheck the grade the test box on results and uncheck include the test in the overall score. It sounds like you just want to track that they did it.  So set AICC_Score to 100 on the last page, that way, you know they did it if you see a 100 and they are happy they got 100! In the gradebook, there is a way to show a letter instead of a number (but not on the SCORM).  You'll have to do it for each activity, though.  In the Choose an action drop down (in my installation) there is an option called Categories & Items.  If you have tabs, it will be a tab above the actual gradebook.   Click the edit icon.  In this area you choose the grade display type.  Ususally it is set to Real.  Change it to Letter and only the letter grade displays.  There are other letter options:  Letter (percentage) which displays the letter grade and activity percentage in parenthases, and Letter (real) which displays the letter grade and the "real" score. This area also allows you to create categories for organizing your grade book.  If you don't actually want the participation to be part of the "grade", set a formula excluding the SCORM activity in the course total.  IF you've got a bunch, create a category and put all the no-grade activities in it and exclude the category grade in the course total formula.

ResponsesInList.Title: Show SCORM in a pop-up window without a frame in Moodle 2.2?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi All, We recently upgraded our servers to Moodle 2.2.1+, and now we're having an issue with how it displays SCORM objects. In the past, we would develop interactive software simulations in Adobe Captivate 5.5, deploy them as SCORM 1.2, and then use the SCORM module to serve and track them in Moodle. Since our users have a variety of screen resolutions on their desktops (including some at 1024x768), we learned to create the Captivate modules at 800x600 (plus a navigation bar at the bottom), then set the SCORM to open in a New Window with resizing allowed and minimal padding around the SWF. That way, our users can see the entire program on their screens without having to scroll. But now after the Moodle upgrade, every SCORM object appears in a frame, even if it is in a New Window, and our users can't see the whole Captivate program without scrolling back and forth. This is a big problem for us and our users, and I don't understand why such a big change was made to the module. I'm attaching a sample of what this looks like with one of our existing courses. My questions: Is there any way to launch a SCORM object in a New Window and not have it in a scrolling frame? Or is there any way to turn this feature off in the server settings or theme? Please let me know if anyone has any advice on this - any help would be greatly appreciated. Thanks very much, Eric Broach

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Show SCORM in a pop-up window without a frame in Moodle 2.2?
ResponsesInList.Text: Looks like you just need to turn the toc off - edit your scorm and find the setting "Display course structure in player" - set it to hidden or if using 2.3 you can set it to "disabled" which removes it completely. The change was done for a range of reasons which improve reliability and usability of the player - the old method had some annoying issues around pop-ups/background windows/reliability of cross-browser communication failing allowing the user to browse the scorm but no data reported back to Moodle, Major failures with IE7 etc etc - have a look in the forums or the tracker for more info.

ResponsesInList.Title: Using XMLHtmlRequest in SCORM
Re: Using XMLHtmlRequest in SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Luis I have limited experience in Moodle but from a JavaScript point of view, I would do two things to debug what's happening here. 1. Check that the "referencedPage" parameter does actually contain the correct URL to the page that you're trying to load. Maybe the URL parameter isn't getting passed into the page properly due to how Moodle can load pages via a file.php to check that a user is logged in to the site. 2. Use Firebug in Firefox to check what URL the XMLHttpRequest is actually trying to load and to see if the response is some kind of error or the page that you expected. Hope that helps, Andy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using XMLHtmlRequest in SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Andy, thanks a lot for answering. Well, the thing is that I actually used firebug to detect the problem exactly, but the URL is correct. The same exactly copy-pasted URL works externally, outside of the SCORM package. I think it shouldn't fail as it's a relative path, and file structure is the same both inside and outside the package. The problem is after calling send(). The returned response is null inside the SCORM, and correct outside.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using XMLHtmlRequest in SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: When the XHR object calls "send()", in the Net tab of Firebug can you see the request being made? Is the status "200 OK"? If you click the "plus" symbol beside the request for that URL, check to see what the response tab shows, can you see the raw HTML of the page that you were trying to load? Finally, and this is where my Moodle experience lacks, as the page is probably loaded via the "file.php" page that Moodle uses to restrict access of resources to authorised users, it's possible that Moodle is making some changes to the HTTP headers that are meaning that the XHR object isn't able to detect that the resource loaded successfully. Check that the resource shows the same HTTP headers in Firebug's "Headers" tab for when it's loaded via Moodle and without Moodle. FWIW, we do most of our coding using the PrototypeJS library which has onFailure and onException events when the Ajax loading fails for one reason or another. JQuery has similar events. We find that these are more reliable and have better cross-browser support than using a simple "if (window.XMLHttpRequest)" and using the XHR object directly. You could try a sample page within Moodle using PrototypeJS or JQuery temporarily to see if they have the same issues and if they return any better error messages. Hope that helps, Andy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New Window issue in IE8
ResponsesInList.Text: Simon gives a patch that fixes it in the Tracker issue which your IT guys can apply instead of upgrading if that's easier. The change in 2.3 for new windows was to prevent pop-up blockers from being a problem - the pop-up is now generated on a user action so most pop-up blockers will allow it to occur The old version of the pop-up would fail with pop-up blockers as it wasn't generated on a user action. ...problem is we didn't notice that it was a problem for IE 8 in compat mode and IE 7 (officially IE 7 isn't supported in 2.3 so it wasn't tested but this looks like an easy fix to apply) The change is generic for all SCORM so I'm not sure why you're seeing different behaviour on different SCORMS unless you're running into Browser caching issues or you have different display settings for the SCORMS. Once you've applied the patch or upgraded it should fix the issue for all your packages. Moodle 2.4 will have a change that makes the initial view page that shows the structure/users attempts (if set) redirect back to the course homepage after the pop-up has been generated - more details on the bug I mention in the comments on that bug.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm and Udutu
ResponsesInList.Text: I've just tidied up your post a little bit to remove some of the invalid formatting from your copy/paste. "Enable IMS package type" - definately make sure this is unticked. "Enable direct AICC url" - this is a very advanced setting that maybe .01% of people will use - make sure it's unticked. Disabling those settings will simplify the add SCORM page and they are usually disabled by default on a fresh install. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to launch course full screen
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Tammy, Couple of points: #1 - A browser window will always have scroll bars if you set the width and height properties to larger than the available space. Older laptops have smaller screen sizes than you have specified and with the number of browser addon bars, that take up yet more available space, the height of users' browsers' available space is unpredictable. #2 - Full-screen is not the same as full-browser: Full-screen launches a standalone Flash Player window and disables most of users' keyboards' keys (only escape works to exit full-screen mode) - useless if you want users to input text. Full-browser is when you set the width and height properties to 100% - the Flash Player window must be the only item displayed in the window for this to work, i.e. pure Flash embed and no other HTML on the page. This doesn't affect the dimensions of the embedded SWF file so if the window isn't big enough, some of the SWF file's stage will be cropped. I think that you possibly want to set the stage scale mode properties in the Flash embed code. If you set: <param name="scale" value="showall" /> or var params = {}; params.scale = "showall"; Depending on the embed method you're using, you'll get, more or less, the desired full-browser effect, i.e. the stage will automatically adjust its size to the available space. Javascript embed methods generally work more conistently with this. If you're Actionscript coding any part of your project(s), you can use "liquid layout" techniques that specifically adjust items on the stage according to the available space, much like an HTML + CSS web page does but you have more specific control over its behaviour. The AS event handler is stage.addEventListener(Event.RESIZE, resize); You can see some examples on my Moodle: http://moodle.matbury.com/course/view.php?id=17 - Try opening the Flash activities and resizing your browser window to see what happens. Since they're embedded on pages with Moodle navigation, only the width properties change. In full-browser mode, they adjust appropriately in all directions. Please don't hesitate to contact me if you have any further questions.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to launch course full screen
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Tammy, There are a few things that could be making your web pages larger. One is the default padding around the browser window (notice that text and images rarely go right up to the edges). You can eliminate this with CSS: <style type="text/css" media="screen"> html, body, #myFlashContent { height:100%; } body { margin:0; padding:0; overflow:hidden; } object { outline:none; } </style> You'll need to edit it appropriately for the embed code that you're using. Again, the screen resolution isn't the same as the space available inside the browser window. Firefox has some neat web developer tool plugins for measuring stuff like this. This'll help you find the optimum dimensions for your Flash files.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to launch course full screen
ResponsesInList.Text: also - your browser settings may be interfering here - modern browsers allow the user to set whether a JS popup can disable url/statusbar etc - if those browser settings are in place there's not much you can do. Also - please post full Moodle version information - especially when talking about SCORM - different Moodle versions have very different behaviors - 2.X has a revamped player and operates very differently from the 1.9 and lower versions

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to launch course full screen
ResponsesInList.Text: Our programmer got our screen to open full screen by modifying the player.js file.  Ours was for a SCORM file.  The player.js file is in the mod/scorm directory.  This is code we used: function scorm_openpopup(url,name,options,width,height) { windowobj = window.open(fullurl,name,'titlebar=no, scrollbar=no, fullscreen=yes'); //To force fullscreen mode on launch, the option variable was replaced with three parameters. if (!windowobj) { return; } if ((width==100) && (height==100)) { // Fullscreen windowobj.moveTo(0,0); } if (width<=100) { width = Math.round(screen.availWidth * width / 100); } if (height<=100) { height = Math.round(screen.availHeight * height / 100); } windowobj.resizeTo(width,height); windowobj.focus(); //An extra step to ensure the fullscreen activates return windowobj; }

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Updating an Object
ResponsesInList.Text: as long as you don't change the indentifiers in your imsmanifest. xml then simply uploading a new zip should work as expected. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Updating an Object
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Hal, scores are only deleted for tracks that no longer exist in the package. If you don't change the identifiers in imsmanifest.xml then nothing should get deleted. The SCORM does update the scoids against each sco when a new package is added to help prevent issues around browser caching etc but it shouldn't delete anything if the imsmanfest.xml file hasn't changed. If you change the identifiers in imsmanifest.xml you will orphan existing content in the scorm tables so it removes the orphaned data.

ResponsesInList.Title: Large Zipped SCORM Package Issue
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey there, I'm running Moodle 2.0 on a Linux machine and I'm having issues using really big SCORM zipfiles. Note that we upload these zipfiles outside of Moodle and that all works fine. It seems to work fine on a test 1GB SCORM zipfile, but we're on to a real course now, which is 4GB. With the 1GB zip, adding a new SCORM package and clicking the Package file Browse button works fine -- we see the 1GB zip, can select it, Moodle unzips it, and the course works perfectly. But with the 4GB file, clicking the Package file Browse button shows the 4GB zip, but not as zip. It's shown as a folder. Clicking the "folder" takes us into that "folder", but it's empty. i.e.: We can't select the 4GB zip file as a SCORM course. Is there some sort of upper file size limit setting I don't know about? Thanks. -=Cam

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Large Zipped SCORM Package Issue
ResponsesInList.Text: I've partially figured this out. PHP seems to have a 4GB limit on filesizes, so when PHP tries to do a filesize() it returns an error. And when it does a filetype() it also errors. /repository/filesystem/lib.php uses filetype() to determine whether the path point to a file or a directory, but because of the file size problem, filetype() seems to default to "dir" (odd default...). So I hardcoded lib.php to assume everything was a file. That worked as far as the file picker was concerned - although I could no longer navigate directories, >4GB files now registered as files so I could choose them as a SCORM package. But alas it didn't fix everything. Choosing a massive .zip returned an "Incorrect file pool content ." error. My hacky fix to allow me to choose the file was irrelevant because the same underlying 4GB limit of PHP probably messed it up somewhere down the line of unzipping the SCORM package and turning it into something Moodle can understand. Our solution is going to be making the course size smaller. Obviously not ideal -- I'd love if this could be fixed. -=Cam

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Large Zipped SCORM Package Issue
ResponsesInList.Text: well.. it's not really ideal to have a massive SCORM zip that big - it would be pretty nasty for users to download and heavy on your data usage! - ideally you should be thinking about optimising it anyway.... I presume some of the large data is static video files? - you could locate those files on a CDN or external site and link to them within your SCORM package to bring the filesize down too. But if you really have to work with files that big I'd suggest working with them in unzipped form in a directory on the same webroot as your Moodle install. Then when adding the SCORM to Moodle just use the url/path to the imsmanifest. xml file inside the unzipped dir.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Large Zipped SCORM Package Issue
ResponsesInList.Text: if you go to admin > plugins > activities > SCORM and enable the setting " allowtypeexternal" it will give you an extra option on the Add SCORM page to specify a url and you can point directly at the imsmanifest.xml file within an extracted zip. ResponsesInList.Text: My major issue with it is that it simply doesn't work on Opera. Yes, there are the problems with some XML methods in Opera (that's why it does not work). But we will implement workaround soon - work is in progress. ...the way it displays the index - rather than using SCORM (on the left in Moodle) it has a layer that appears... Not quite correct. You mean index of the currently open module - it is in fact displayed inside the module, and if you've made the course, that consists of single module, then it is the only structure you can see. The left Moodle index panel displays the course structure - not the module structure. Imagine, that you've made course consisting of single page in eXe - that is absolutely the same situation with CourseLab single module course. The eXe's page corresponds to CourseLab's module. The difference between eXe and CourseLab is that the eXe page is just page, and CourseLab module itself can be multi-page (and therefore can have internal structure). You may or may not use this feature (i.e. you can produce one-page modules in CourseLab too). This feature expands your abiliites - does not limit them. If you want to build complex index on the left side of Moodle window, then you can use multi-module course structure - then every course module (or folder) will appear on the left Moodle index. ...but I still prefer the ease of use, output, and cross-platform of exe-learning. Well, the tastes differ. Personally, I don't think that eXe is so easy-to-use Vyacheslav Shchinov CourseLab development Team www.courselab.com
