ResponsesInList.Text: As an afterthought, traces have been added for every relevant status and error event generated by URLLoader, and in VARIABLES mode the SCO trace record only adds that the file has been found (and then seems to die, or the connection is lost...) ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External URL query
ResponsesInList.Text: I think you just need to point to the zip and moodle takes it from there. You would only point to the manifest if you had unzipped it yourself "manually".

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External URL query
ResponsesInList.Text: the "Downloaded Package" option lets you set the url for the zip - the "External SCORM manifest" option allows you to select the imsmanifest. xml from an extracted SCORM  - this option(external manifest) will only work reliably if the URL uses the same base URL as your Moodle install - eg: www.yourmoodlesite.com/moodle and w www.yourmoodlesite.com/scorm1/imsmanifest.xml if your extracted SCORM is on a different url then the default Browser Security settings will cause Cross- domain Javascript communication to fail - Javascript communication in SCORM is required if you want it to return a grade or any other information from the users interaction with the SCORM package. But - if you use the Zip - (downloaded package)  it doesn't matter what url is used as Moodle will download a copy of the zip and extract it internally for use. hope that helps/makes sense!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can't find SCORM API
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, I have an idea, but not the solution . A year ago I had the same problem with Internet Explorer. The problem is that the content loads first, and in second place the API or to be precise the functions that allow the SCO to search for the API. So, the first time the SCO is launched, the API can't be found, as the content searches for the API before the API arrives, or before IE can find it. That's the reason a refresh makes things work, because the API and functions to find it are already loaded and the refresh makes the SCO search for API once again. At that time, when I was facing the problem I also had a warning of a JavaScript error, if debug is turned on in IE, you can track the issue, and you can realize that the functions are not available (a *.js files is not downloaded/loaded or available to IE - i don't know exactly what's going on), and that makes all things go bad. To be honest, I don't know why this happen, and I don't know how to solve it as it was a problem with Internet Explorer (at least for me). Now, with the latest versions of Moodle it doesn't happen (to me). Eduardo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can't find SCORM API
ResponsesInList.Text: I'll check on the "register_globals" is on or off.  However, that implies to me its complete success of the API loading (register_globals = on) or no success (register_globals = off) on the successful load and tracking Articulate driven SCORM content.  We are seeing it completly on a random  basis, hit or miss. As with the case of Dave saying IE fails to load Articulate Media and Kevin saying he's had success...sounds like what we noted. IE vs Firefox We examined the two browsers on 4 separate PCs.  Firefox would load the AP, Quizmaker, Captivate, etc SCORM properly.  On 30 attempts it did fail once for Articulate.  For IE, both IE6 and IE7 was about 20 success rate out of 30. What were seeing is its on the client-side... with different browsers, different PCs, etc. denotes whether the API is loaded before the Content.  Timing can become screwed up.  That's why were all seeing the "API cannot be found" as completely random. Solutions We're trying to get knee deep in code and look at options to ensure 100% success rate of the API loading for Articulate Presenter, Articulate Quizmaker, and Captivate (assuming those three Dave, Breeze would work).  We want to ensure the API is loaded first, followed by Content (not the cart before the horse)  Below are three conceptual solutions we're examing. Ensure API loads before Content - within PHP, we're looking for a unique identifier that says the API is loaded, then "say" proceed with content.  We're trying to find that red flag.  Pause the remainder of loading the page until the red flag has surfaced. Time Delay.  Having some type of counter in playscorm.php that says do nothing for 5 seconds, then continue loading content (to give the API time to load then be found).  Not as rigorous as Idea 1, because we are assuming 5 second delay should allow the API to load versus being notified it was, then proceeding w/ content Refresh - we noted a refresh of the playscorm.php worked each time.  You get the error of "API cannot be found", do a refresh and all is well  We're thinking of adding code playscorm.php that forces 1 refresh of the page.  The least rigorous, but I'll take a quick solution at the moment to get a "tighter" on later. Tracking Results In the event the SCORM module loads (AP, Quizmaker, Captivate or Breeze) and your smooth sailing with no message of "Cannot find API", be sure at attempt the following Dave. Articulate Presenter - given a presentation, let it complete. AP viewer says "Course Complete".  Do not leave the playscorm.php page.  Click the button that says "Exit from SCORM Course.  (we are showing that results are properly tracked when the user does a formal exit from the SCORM course). A bummer because you would have to tell users to ensure they properly exit for progress to be tracked. Slides - Given an 8 slide presentation, we have noted greater success of tracking given a 9th slide that concludes a presentation.  In AP, stating that user must view a miminum of 8 slides for example.  This is true if grading is complete/incomplete and based on a number of slides viewed. Quizmaker - Given a Quiz done with Articulate Quizmaker, it gives the user the chance to press "Finish" and even close the browser window.  This may be done and the user has not selected "Exit from SCORM Course" within Moodle (which has showed 100% capture of results if they do a formal "Exit from SCORM course" at the end of taking a quiz, etc. We considered embedding a quiz in a 2-slide presentation in Articulate Presenter (1 for the imported quiz, 1 for a conclusion slide just so the Quiz does not include the "Finish" button and users close the browser.  This means in Articulate Presenter, this SCORM module is pass/fail based on the embedded quiz, not the number of slides used. I'll keep folks in-the-loop on the efforts to ensure the API is loaded, before the Content is launched.  It appears to be completely random, based on the client and not the server, of which one loads first.   We're in the situation where we need 100% success rate.  1 event of "Can't find API" is not acceptable. Marc

ResponsesInList.Text: How I am convert my existing course content into SCORM compliant. Any one explain me what is steps to do this.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Convert my existing course into SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: you can't - Moodle courses don't export as SCORM The SCORM standard is really limited - it's only really designed for 2 things. Displaying static content. embedding quizzes within that content. Moodle does a whole lot more than this so there's no way we could write a SCORM excporter There are plans to write an IMS Exporter for Moodle which is similar in some areas to a SCORM package. If you have a Moodle quiz that you want to export into a SCORM object some of the tools on this page will import content exported from many of the quiz export formats: http://docs.moodle.org/20/en/Creating_SCORM_Content

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Convert my existing course into SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Ooooh! I find SCORM is a lot more useful that that - it would have to be to justify the effort!  For example, launching with different parameters, saving the restore point, text display and sound level preferences, bookmarking, current status of any number of things, and so on.  And there's no reason that content can't be as dynamic as the designer/developer team cares to create. That aside, I read the question differently, and suggest: Get hold of a copy of SCORM 1.2 documentation; in particular the runtime environment.  Its out there on the web. Decide whether you want to be able to launch a SCO with launch data as can be provided but the SCORM data model. Decide whether you want to save the data that can be saved, between sessions, with SCORM. Look at your courseware development tool and see whether it is capable of executing SCORM calls; if not, look around for a tool that can. Decide whether it's important that your SCORM courseware will run the same way in another SCORM environment (whether Moodle or in someone else's system). That's why SCORM is a standard. If you're happy with all that, decide whether there's a good business case for putting in the effort. HTH

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Articulate Rapid E-Learning Studio and SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Actually SCORM itself is not what makes courses slow and sluggish. SCORM in it's basic forum defines common data elements, LMS-Course communication, learning objecs and Packaging for Installation. More recently sequencing has been added so that a course can be created by linking many descreate parts (SCOs) together and defining how they are to be presented instead of having to create one large course. The focus being on reusability of individual pieces for many courses. Of course there is more to SCORM then this, but ot is the authoring tool and LMS implementation of SCORM that causes a SCORM based course to be slow and sluggish.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Articulate Rapid E-Learning Studio and SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi John, I'm afraid all the stuff we've created is hidden away behind various corporate firewalls, so I can't show it to you. But look on the Rapid Elearning Blog and in the Articulate forums and you'll see some excellent examples. There is a huge jump between Course Genie and Articulate. Course Genie is brilliant for turning Word docs into HTML with some added interactivity. With Articulate you start with a blank sheet of paper each time and have to think about exactly how you're going to put your message across, maybe including some animation and narration. What you don't do is put loads of words on the screen. It will not look good, and no-one will want to use it. Using Articulate is as easy as using Powerpoint. But to use it well is a different matter entirely (just like Powerpoint). You will need a strong eye for design, and a clear understanding of what is going to drive your students through the materials. Basically, if you need animation and narration then move to Articulate or something similar. If you're just delivering words and graphics, then go with CourseGenie or Exe ( www.exelearning.org ) - which has a very strong pedagogical focus. Cheers, Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Attempt continues when launching from content window

Access the scorm reports single attempt data and find out what's saved on the attempt for cmi.core.lesson_status. http://docs.moodle.org/20/en/Using_SCORM#SCORM_Reports_Screen Also, the screenshow you're showing is still an open scorm session. Simply selecting the SCO once more from the screen you're showing here is just loading it again within the same session, the same attempt.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error loading XML file from the repository

Hi Ian, having quickly taken a look at this thread, filename case issues excluded, the problem could sit into the Files API vs your package. Take a look at the mdl_files table, filearea = content , e.g.: 
```text
SELECT


    *


FROM


    `mdl_files`


WHERE


    `component` = 'mod_scorm'


    AND `filearea` = 'content'
```
 or share your content, maybe privately using an URL provided by PM; Moodle core send_file_not_found() , final responsible of your HTTP 404, can be triggered by several cases. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error loading XML file from the repository
ResponsesInList.Text: Problem solved: The Moodle 2 file system is case sensitive regardless of whether running in Windows or Linux. Windows doesn't care if FileA.swf is called as Filea.swf. An SQL SELECT search in the Moodle database will find the file reference, either way. But the Moodle 2 file system will not. Windows users, beware!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Creating flash animation for scorm?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Laura, From what you've described I think the most likely candidate for authoring animations like you've described is Swift 3D: http://www.erain.com/products/swift3d/ This will probably be the easiest to learn to use and the quickest to produce the animations you want. The animations can also be made dynamic and interactive and exportable for other IDEs. Other options are: Adobe Flash professional - http://www.adobe.com/products/flash.html This is the full-blown professional IDE and usually takes a fair amount of training, i.e. years, to use. Blender (open source = free) - http://www.blender.org/education-help/tutorials/animation/ This is mainly aimed at high-end video animation and I'm not sure if it publishes to Flash but it's an excellent tool for creating 3D objects, i.e. flasks, beakers, bunsen burners, etc., that you can export for use in other IDEs, e.g. Flash Professional and Swift 3D. FYI , There are also Flash applications that can read standard chemical compound files and create interactive 3D models of them. I've seen a few but I can't remember where. I put a really simple demo of an interactive 3D object on my blog a couple of years ago: http://blog.matbury.com/2008/11/13/papervision3d/ (Please note that Papervision3D has now been incorporated into Away3D). I hope this helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Creating flash animation for scorm?
ResponsesInList.Text: Swift3D supports exporting the 3d content to a Papervision 3D - so it's AS3 code and assets vs a vector pre-rendered framebased animation.  So it is usually smaller Blender has an export plugin that converts the models int AS3 classes so you can import and instantiate the model in actionscript code. http://code.google.com/p/blender-as-exporter/

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Creating flash animation for scorm?

BTW , it's generally a better idea to use a standard open format, in this case XML , so that any 3D models that you create can be imported by any software package that supports it. The industry standard for open format 3D model files is COLLADA, originally developed by Sony: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COLLADA The globe demo I linked to imports an external COLLADA file (.dae).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: overview of errorcodes in Scorm API Debugger available?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Sytske, There's a good scorm reference here: http://scorm.com/scorm-explained/technical-scorm/run-time/run-time-reference/ Be sure to select the "SCORM 1.2" option. But it looks like the particular value you're talking about is not specified on that reference. In which case I'd just print out the official docs: http://www.adlnet.gov/Technologies/scorm/SCORMSDocuments/Forms/AllItems.aspx?RootFolder=%2fTechnologies%2fscorm%2fSCORMSDocuments%2fPrevious%20Versions%2fSCORM%201.2%2fDocumentation%20Suite%20(SCORM%201.2)&FolderCTID=0x0120007F801FCD5325044C89D91240519482D7&View= {4D6DFFDE-3CFC-4DD9-A21A-4B687728824A} 405 means incorrect data type, but 307 chars is longer than the longest permitted string length in SCORM standard (255 chars). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: overview of errorcodes in Scorm API Debugger available?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Amy, Thanks for both the pointers, I've bookmarked them immediatly. I'm going to elaborate some on what I discovered. Probably 'old news' for most of you, but I found it quite educating. Maybe someone else can benefit. With these references (especially SCORM_1.2_RunTimeEnv.pdf at adlnet.gov) I was indeed able to figure out the following: the data type of cmi.interactions.N.correct_responses.N.pattern, and of cmi.interactions.N.student_response depends on the type of question (cmi.interactions.N.type) apparantly, when the question is a Choice-guestion, both these options can only contain 1 character "Each possible response is limited to a  single character". and: "If there are more than 26 possibilities, then a performance type response must be used" and the format for perfomance is "an alpha-numeric field limited to 255 characters" So indeed: the number of characters is too long. I think I will turn to Articulate to ask what can be done about that. On the other hand: what I see Articulate doing, is not putting a Letter or Number, but the whole choice option as is presented to the student. So if the anwer options are: "Coffee and a croissant", "Cereals and milk" and "I don't do breakfast, period", and i would choose the third one, Articulate apparantly sets cmi.interactions.N.student_response to "I_don_t_do_breakfast__period" What is nice about that, is that the track details in de Scorm Reports ( http://docs.moodle.org/20/en/SCORM_reports ) actually make more sense.Than if the correct responses would be recorded as "A" or "B" But the downside is, is that to benefit from this, you must make sure that the answers are never more than 255 characters. ResponsesInList.Title: Custom Scorm Player integration
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi guys, We developed a custom Scorm 1.2 player and I would like to ask you how can I upload it and make it work with the Scorm API without using the default Moodle scorm player. As I would like to use my own scorm player, I don't want to upload it as a Scorm package but If I upload it as a resource ( I have chosen: "Link to a file or a website") I can see my content and it works fine, but cannot connect to the Scorm API. Could you advise a solution please? Cheers, Zsolt

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Custom Scorm Player integration
ResponsesInList.Text: What exactly do you mean by "a custom SCORM 1.2 player"?  From the LMS point of view, the player IS the API in that it is responsible for launching and sequencing SCOs, communicating with them via the API, and storing the data in the LMS database .  What you are talking about sounds more like a shell that is running embedded content that you want to talk to the LMS like a SCO. In that case if you want to have it talk to Moodle via the SCORM API, you need to create a SCORM manifest for it, treating it as a single-SCO course (the SCO would launch your "player" shell), package (zip) it up along with the content it is "playing", and upload it like any other normal SCORM course package.  You tell Moodle voa the course configuration and the manifest information to not display/skip it's own SCO sequencing interface, since the package is a single SCO.  Usually such SCOs use the location and suspend_data SCORM fields to track status and suspend on exit until it considers itself/the attempt completed (possibly never).

ResponsesInList.Title: Tárgy: Re: Custom Scorm Player integration
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Stephen,

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Tárgy: Re: Custom Scorm Player integration
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Zsolt, I took a look at the example - you are not using a SCORM formatted manifest, but rather a custom XML sequencing format you are reading into a custom flash player shell to display an index and control/sequence flash content pieces.  I use a similar, albeit much more extensive, customizable shell designed from the ground up with a complete SCORM 1.2/2004 wrapper that I use in SCORM professionally for generating or converting embedded Flash courses.  To work with SCORM, a course has to be designed as encapsulated in a standard SCORM package/manifest, and communicates with the SCORM LMS on a SCO by SCO basis for status, etc.  Your package currently does not appear to do this - it is just communicating internally to read the XML sequence information and navigate your Flash content.  A SCORM LMS (such as the Moodle SCORM module) is designed to be in control when sequencing SCOs, whereas it seems that you want to be in control in your custom flash shell.  This can be accomplished in a number of ways - 1) design the course as a single SCO (i.e. currently this is the case), wrap it in a SCORM client player shell, and communicate completion/progress status of content pieces/ sections and other information using SCORM location, suspend_data, objectives and interactions rather than using individual SCO sequencing information (many courses/companies take this route to have a better user experience/take control of the content navigation), or... 2) more complicated - use an anchor-driven deep-linking method such as SWFAddress to deep link your flash SCOs to correspond to imsmanifest SCOs.  You would also have to work out a way of maintaining overall bookmarking information in that case, such as still using Global Shared Objectives to mark SCO status, may require some SCORM 2004 capabilities, and would also make use of the adl.nav interface to navigate between SCOs. I'm not too sure how well Moodle handles the latter, as the SCORM 2004 implementation is not complete by any means, although I've been generally successful with getting a lot of content to work, sometimes with tweaking to the Moodle SCORM player necessary.  Most of the professional stuff gets pushed to commercial LMSes with mature SCORM 2004 implementations such as Saba. Keep in mind that SCORM is designed to launch individual HTML SCOs, where each individual SCO element communicate with the LMS in a lifecycle through javascript . If you want to be compatible, you have to live within the standards/design rules or work your content to fit/play within these design rules.

ResponsesInList.Title: Tárgy: Re: Tárgy: Re: Custom Scorm Player integration
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Stephen, Thank you for your answer. That is not our project what I attached. It is very similar to ours but not the same. That was only a sample for a custom scorm player from another company I found on the net. I havent' decompiled it so I don't know the internal structure of it. Our custom scorm player loads and parses a valid imsmanifest and can play any Scorm 1.2 package (individual html pages as well). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Tárgy: Re: Tárgy: Re: Custom Scorm Player integration
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Zsolt, Ok, I thought you were pointing to your player.  I didn't decompile the example, just observed the interactions in debug browser logs.  The example was all flash with embedded flash scenes rather than html SCOs. It sounds like you are emulating an LMS, as you are reading an imsmanifest.xml - if you have a custom shell layout/format, why don't you just skin the existing moodle SCORM player?  The issue is that Moodle already parses the SCORM manifest, which is not a simple task to do properly and interpret the information contained there, populates the information to the database, and provides all the functionality your shell would be doing, other than perhaps the exact look and feel of your shell?  There is nothing preventing you from re-skinning the moodle SCORM shell as an alternate SCORM shell.  I've done this in the past to get a particular look and feel for a client. You really are not be talking to the SCORM API if you are reading the manifest and sequencing the content/manifest yourself, rather you are replacing the SCORM API (and other support processes and database-driven interface processes) in Moodle with your own version.  The moodle SCORM player does not interface with the server through an API, it reads and writes directly to the moodle database. Regards, Steve

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Tracking and Suspend Data
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dave, Not much data there. Usually Articulate is very chatty with suspend_data. The API may have been dropped. Also possible that LMSCommit() or LMSFinish() failing. If your end-user is clicking "Exit" and that triggers a command to call LMSFinish() and wait for a response, and it's not coming (due to API not being available). See if you can replicate his results with his browser, and with the debugging API turned on. Might tell you when communications are stopping. But sometimes a dropped API is hard to troubleshoot. We can always look over a debugging log here to check for any problems. http://docs.moodle.org/20/en/SCORM_FAQ#Debugging_in_2.0 http://docs.moodle.org/20/en/SCORM_FAQ#What_does_the_debugging_log_mean.3F Regards, Amy

So I have a flash based viewer which can load up individual videos from a batch of a couple of hundred files. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Managing video in SCORM packages
ResponsesInList.Text: Why is it that you need SCORM? Do you need to track data on who has watched these vids?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Managing video in SCORM packages
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Amy, Two reasons: 1. It's perceived to be a necessity by teachers I've talked to.  They expect any resources they get to be SCORM compatible, without any regard as to what that offers. 2. Installation - seems like the way to provide a flash-based resource for use on a VLE is to provide it as a SCORM package.  (Is there another way that I'm missing?) Incidentally, it's not just raw video files here, there's some interface and bits and pieces that the flash does - showing worksheets etc, so it's not just for the sake of showing a raw video.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Managing video in SCORM packages
ResponsesInList.Text: You didn't answer my second question: Do you need to track data on who has watched these vids? Sometimes laypeople who are not familiar with the SCORM spec request or advocate for it when it isn't necessary. I'm just trying to rule that out and save you some time if you don't need it. SCORM is only necessary if these teachers need to track detailed access data or present assessment questions or other interactivity for scoring in concert with your vids—none of which can be provided by a straight video format. If you don't need tracking/assessment there's no reason to package your content as SCORM, and you should educate said teachers accordingly. If that's the case, you can present video to learners with a simple object tag in an HTML resource or page view. Or, if the video assets will reside within the Moodle or a repo connected to Moodle, then Moodle has video filters and teachers can browse and select videos using the file picker even more easily than they could add a SCORM package to a course. Regards, Amy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Managing video in SCORM packages
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Amy - thanks again. I don't need to track data on who has watched the vids.  I also appreciate that it isn't necessary for the functionality I need, but it is necessary because teachers are expecting it.  It's one of those annoying things where a badge / label has become so expected that people will not use your product without it.  And that's the main trouble I'm facing.  While I could think of attempting to educate the people around me, I also realise that's not realistically going to happen and so I'm actually making two products - one that uses SCORM and works on a VLE and one that doesn't use SCORM (and nor does it use a VLE). These videos are not in a standard video format either so the player I've built (written in flash) has to be included.  Moodle's video filters will not recognise these videos - for the ease of explanation it's best to consider them a flash animation with a flash viewer. The stand-alone version of this product includes a large menu system and links to 4 GB of data / videos / flash animtations / flash based print-outs.  It's perceived by teachers that I must enable users to access this via SCORM packages as well - I guess that's so that teachers could set a single topic as a piece of homework - or spread out the topic to tie into their lesson plans. Now I'm wondering if i'm missing a trick, is there a way of distributing flash resources to a VLE in a non-scorm way?  (And a way that can cope with huge file sizes?)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Managing video in SCORM packages
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle has a swf filter. You can investigate the multimedia filters on your localhost install. There are many ways to include files and resources in Moodle in a non-SCORM way. You can add a file (including an HTML resource which embeds your SWF and/or performs JavaScript etc) or link to a file. You can provide teachers with object tag markup to embed your resource wherever they want in the course. You can investigate all of these options on your localhost install. Anything that works on the Web, with allowances for login and permissions, will work just fine in Moodle. Huge file size is handled the way it's handled everywhere else on the Web: by using a CDN to stream burdensome content.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: HACP / AICC GetParam returns login page
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, David is right about aicc_sid and Moodle PHP session relation. Looking at the code, confirm_sesskey() is used to validate the AICC HACP session_id provided by the content and if you look at the implementation of that function you could: try to access the PHP session cookie from your external content and submit it together with your HTTP POST payload: this is somewhat difficult since for security reasons you cannot access to cookies outside the domain of your Moodle; disable the session check globally using $CFG->ignoresesskey = true in your config.php file; disable the session check on a per user basis using $USER->ignoresesskey = true programmatically set by an hack based on a combination of user agent and Moodle AICC HACP page (HTTP POST on aicc.php ). See e.g. lib/setup.php for some examples. (b) and (c) will break your Moodle PHP session and this will break AICC HACP tracking too since the session is used for several other AICC HACP related information so you'll fix your first problem but you'll get many others not fixable issues. (a) is the right way but it strictly depends on where your external content sits and if you can carefully choose the domain of both Moodle and your external content repository. I guess you have very few chance to let external AICC HACP based contents run in Moodle but... I've no real experience on that so my post is just a quick analysis of the code with a bunch of ideas. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: HACP / AICC GetParam returns login page
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ben, you're right: reverse-proxy deployment gives a simple working solution for client side calls because of it helps the browser on keeping the same web session, as expected, during the user tracking experience by moving cookies back and forth. A server call (are you using kind of AICC proxy or injecting AICC tracking data?) requires more attention: you need a solution to keep the web session alive&available for each call under the scope of the user tracking experience (same of above); you also need to keep care that the web session will always be the one opened the first time by the user triggering the AICC experience on Moodle: the reason is that you need both authentication through a valid Moodle user profile (e.g. it could be re-created at each call) and a "fixed session" to let the AICC machine state, Moodle side, to happily run i.e. it requires the session to be unique along the whole user tracking experience. Client side calls automatically satisfy this requirement if (1) has been already satisfied. MDL-27306 will address, if and when available, both client and server side calls since it will mask the whole above under a Tracking Session Token which is charged to make the things run as expected, regardless the need of fixed web sessions. HTH, Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Writing data from entry fields in SCORM packages to Moodle database
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Group Members, For my employer i am doing research into the possibilities that Moodle offers to store data from SCORM activities . We use Moodle 2.0.1 and write interactive e-learning components with Lectora (published in SCORM 1.2). We face the following problem: In our SCORM packages we use input fields (entry fields) in which the learner answers to open questions. These questions and answers we want to transfer it to a Moodle page, so the learner will get an overview of work done and that later may reflect a digital logbook. So far I have not been able to find out how such a link should be realized. I am also looking for a good place within Moodle that could serve as a log, I myself have experimented with the "Journal" of Moodle but I can imagine that there are better applications. Do you have tips?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Writing data from entry fields in SCORM packages to Moodle database
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Bas, You might want to look at the SCORM 1.2 spec for the writable data elements you intend to use. Most data elements have some significant character length limits which make using a SCORM package as a journal prohibitive. I believe the longest is 200 chars. Moodle does not strictly enforce this, but it also claims no responsibility for characters 201+. Your second concern, drawing those answers out into a summative Moodle page, would take some work, probably a custom report or a customization to the SCORM mod. You would essentially be building custom functionality both to put this data into Moodle and to get it out.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle quiz to scorm
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Dr. S, Usually the point of using the Moodle question bank is that questions can be shared and mixed and matched across quizzes, or drawn in at random into a quiz from a large collection. Be aware that if you repackage the questions into SCORM you'll lose all of that. A SCORM content package is equivalent to a single quiz for a single assessment purpose, not a single quiz question, and not a general, all-purpose package that can be tailored to the context at hand by a layperson. It is possible to export quiz questions into various formats, and if I were you I'd probably go with the Moodle xml export format, then build a custom SCORM player to present the questions in that xml to the learner. *But* once again you'll run into how to tailor that question set to the learner. You're going to have to manipulate that XML file for each separate quiz you want to deliver with those questions. Are you sure it's not possible to import the question bank as such into the other LMSs? Even if it requires some custom coding, it will probably give you more flexibility in using the questions in different contexts, down the road. Might be worth investigating. Also, you might want to look at upgrading. We're now at Moodle 2.0.3+ and Moodle 1.9.12+. Regards, Amy

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle 2.0 Scorm error loading YouTube
ResponsesInList.Text: I've imported a scorm 1.2 package into a new moodle 2 set up but when it comes to viewing a YouTube video I get these results in 2 different browsers. Any ideas how I correct it without having the original source material to re-package the scorm pack? Internet Explorer 8 View Firefox 4 View of the same

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.0 Scorm error loading YouTube
ResponsesInList.Text:
Moodle 2.0 does not place the scorm content in an iframe, so it's not the markup of the SCORM player. Is the content in your SCORM package being loaded in an iframe? Also, do you have firebug installed on Firefox? Load the content with fb turned on and see what error that gives you. (You can also share the content here and one of us can take a look.) I find a clickjacking defense listed here which might elicit that error for IE : http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/cc288472(v=vs.85).aspx Clickjacking Defense: Some hackers try to trick users into clicking buttons that appear to perform safe or harmless functions, but instead perform unrelated tasks. Clickjackers embed malicious code or "redress" the user interface by using transparent frames that overlay specific UI elements with misleading text and images. To help prevent clickjacking, Web site owners can send an HTTP response header named X-Frame-Options with HTML pages to restrict how the page may be framed. `X-Frame-Options: Deny` If the X-Frame-Options value contains the token Deny, Internet Explorer 8 prevents the page from rendering if it is contained within a frame. If the value contains the token SameOrigin, Internet Explorer will not render the page if the top level-browsing- context differs from the origin of the page containing the directive. Blocked pages are replaced with a "This content cannot be displayed in a frame" error page. You can change or remove http headers from the HTML parent page in the SCORM package without recompiling any Flash inside it. That's what I'd try. Either remove the header, or change the iframe tag to an object tag, or both. Might also be cross- domain scripting issue when the vid is fetched. Can't tell you without having seen the content. Regards,
Amy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.0 Scorm error loading YouTube

But that would likely trigger a prompt for you to update your Adobe Flash security settings, not block the loading of the content entire. Check the root HTML file in the SCORM package for an iframe. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problem with lesson_status Scorm 1.2 MDL19
ResponsesInList.Text:
Here's what is in the scorm standard, on page 35 of 155 in SCORM_1.2_ConformanceReq.pdf, numbered page 2-19 (SCORM Version 1.2 Conformance Requirements Version 1.2). If the value for this element is not set to “incomplete” by the SCO, then the LMS shall re-evaluate and change the value based on the following: If there is no mastery score in the Manifest, and the SCO sets a score
(cmi.core.score.raw) and the lesson_status (cmi.core.lesson_status) then the
LMS shall not override the SCO determined status. If there is a mastery score in the Manifest, the LMS can change the status to
either passed or failed depending on the student's score (cmi.core.score.raw)
compared to the mastery score. If the student is taking the SCO for no-credit, (cmi.core.credit = “no-credit”)
there is no change to the lesson_status, with one exception. If the
lesson_mode (cmi.core.lesson_mode) is "browse", the lesson_status may
change to "browsed" even if the cmi.core.credit is set to no-credit. This should not be happening if lesson_status is set to incomplete, only if it's set to completed, passed, or failed... If you can verify that the behavior you're seeing isn't in accordance with what I've put above, then submit a bug report. If possible submit an api log from the scorm session, to demonstrate that lesson_status is indeed not being set to "completed" on LMSFinish(). Regards,
Amy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM compliant learning system
ResponsesInList.Text:
So let me get this straight: you're on Moodle.org asking for advice on building a homegrown LMS? Finding the most "appropriate forum" might not be your most pressing concern. Can we really help you answer that question? How feasible is this project? What kind of time frame for 2 developers who know next to nothing about SCORM usage and compliance? Anyone who attempts to answer this question without knowing your capabilities and the full feature set for the project is not going to give you anything valuable. Read the SCORM standard. Look at the models available for authoring SCORM content. You know what your team is capable of. There are cloud-based SCORM solutions out there; you might want to look at something like that. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM compliant learning system
ResponsesInList.Text: It's pretty unlikely that it will be cost-effective for you to develop a SCORM engine/player from scratch for your new LMS. Definately check out Rusticis SCORM Engine - you can integrate that with an existing LMS pretty easily - it's certified 1.2 and 2004 compliant. But if you're wanting to build a player from scratch with 2 people I'd attach a figure of at least 3 months for both people to get an engine that was compliant with SCORM 1.2 objects... double it and add a big buffer if you want it to be 2004 compliant as well. but... those 2 people would need to be awesome JS devs and really good at interpreting complex specs and good at working together on a single complex project. add some more time on top if you want fancy reports to come out at the end. but - those estimates are possibly a bit low. I'd estimate at least 1 year of developers time has gone into SCORM in Moodle - probably a lot more and we haven't even finished SCORM 2004 compliance. But... if you're hosting the LMS and not providing it for customers to "install" - then you could use some smoke and mirrors to "borrow" the SCORM player in Moodle(or another LMS with a SCORM player) and make it look like it's part of your own LMS - you write an SSO plugin for your system to seemlessly connect to Moodle and log a "user" in - then hide headers/footers in moodle from the user and when the user has finished you make a db call from your LMS to pull the data out of the Moodle db. Re-using code from existing projects with SCORM players may also drop the amount of work required back a bit. oh... did I mention you will also have to deal with buggy SCORM objects that don't actually follow the SCORM spec and that users expect will work?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Data - What I am looking at?
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm with Amy...SCORMs are like that.  The LMS has no control over what the module vomits out for "results."   I have collegues who use SumTotal and complain about all the data that is hard to use. I only have one module anyone cares about the data in and instead of doing anything with it in Moodle, I have a Crystal Report pull it out and clean it up a bit, separating individual variables and just looking at suspend data.  Transfer it to an excel spreadsheet, remove unneeded variables, edit the variable you want to see...very manual, time consuming.  Unfortunately, reports software doesn't clean it up much and, if anything in your answer has special characters, it translates them into their component referents (%20 for -, %28 for (, %29 for ), I'm sure there are others I haven't seen).  I've tell my facilitators that what I give them is what they get because I warn them in advance about the ugly data trail.  You could run reports with any reports software, like Jasper (I think that's the name of the open source reports software) or using ELIS (which uses Jasper), too. SCORM modules will report the result of any variable change...have 100 variables, it will show each one triggered, not necessarily in the order triggered, and that includes test questions.  So, the solution is to force each attempt as a separate data chunk. To do this, make sure there is no way for your students to go back and retake the test in the module (course completion page with no back and a pre-test page which has variables to turn off what ever button lets them into the test).  I use Lectora and set alternate text boxes on the page before the test which only shows if the test has been submitted that tells them they have to start a new attempt and if the alternate text shows, the next button disappears. This way, they can't accidently start the same attempt over, if they click the module and tell it they don't want to return to where they left off.  That would be one of the up-side to Lectora, lots of control.  Not sure it's possible in Captivate or eXe, the only other authoring software packages I've used, but I doubt it. In the Moodle SCORM activity, select the limit of how many times they are allowed to sit the exam.  Then make sure the "Student skip content structure page" is set to Never and "Course Structure Display (TOC)" is either on the left or in a drop down (I use on the left). This adds a step to the click to take the course process, it gives them the activity summary and a button that says "Enter".  They click enter and start their module.  If they haven't completed it and close (I don't know if this is allowed for your students), they can return to the last viewed page.  If they finish it, it reports their score.  Once their score is reported, the button remains but a check box shows up above it that says "Start a new attempt".  If they have exhausted their attempts, this disappears and they can only review previous results. Make sure to give directions in the Summary on starting new attempts (you might test it to see how it looks).  Then when you view the report, any student who has taken the test more than once will show multiple entries on the report and you can look at the data sheet for each individually, for what it's worth.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM not loading in IE; does load in Firefox
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Micky, We ran into a similar issue with IE7 and IE8 with Articulate. I used wireshark to watch the traffic and found that IE was telling the server that it could not handle any more data. It stayed like that for 5 minutes -- until the connection was released -- then finished loading fine. We have some theories as to why it was happening (httprequest opening too many connections?), but regardless we did find a workaround. I suggest letting the package sit for 5 minutes after it gets stuck. Use httpwatch or fiddler to see what happens, and turn on the scorm debugging. If it's the same issue, you'll see it getting stuck on different files each time, somewhat randomly, but consistantly restarting in 5 minutes. For us, it was the LMSCommit that always triggered the freeze. Here is a link to the thread: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=164445 I'd love to have additional testing for this fix. It works for us so far though!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Does a SCORM package unzip everytime it is run?
ResponsesInList.Text: Depends what your setting is for Auto-update frequency. If you have Auto-update frequency set to Never, then Moodle only unzips the package when you save the activity. It's more likely that your content is taking a long time to load because 25mb is a lot of data. Captivate in particular will stall playback until all content in the package is loaded. The end-user is left staring at an "Initializing LMS..." message until all content (including all video, audio, etc.) is loaded. Direct download is not the best way to present video/audio larger than 2mb. Regards, A

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to Store and show the socre of a flash?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jason, Here is some code I shared with another user on this forum using the pipwerks package. You can adapt to fit your needs. Matt's code does a good job too using the external interface if I recall. import fl.controls.Button; // assumes you are using the components imports import flash.events.MouseEvent; import pipwerks. SCORM ; // class file to track SCORM information var lessonStatus:String; // checks the status of lesson complete or not complete var lmsConnected:Boolean; // checks if LMS is available returns true is there is LMS available var success:Boolean; // Hold value to tell if LMS is active var scorm:SCORM = new SCORM(); test_btn.addEventListener(MouseEvent.CLICK, scormFinish) lmsConnected = scorm.connect(); // tries to connect to SCORM and returns true if it does if(lmsConnected) // if it is connected (true) { lessonStatus = scorm.get("cmi.core.lesson_status"); // gets the current status of the lesspm if(lessonStatus == "completed") // is the lesson is already complete { scorm.disconnect(); //Course has already been completed. // disconnect from the system } else { success = scorm.set("cmi.core.lesson_status", "incomplete"); // else set the lesson to incomplete //Must tell LMS course has not been completed yet. } } else { trace("Could not connect to LMS."); // returns a message if lmsConnected is false (not connected) } function scormFinish (event:MouseEvent): void // used to finish upon a mouse click { success = scorm.set("cmi.core.score.raw", "5") //raw score success = scorm.set("cmi.core.score.max", "10") // total score success = scorm.set("cmi.core.score.min", "0"); // min score success = scorm.set("cmi.core.lesson_status", "completed");// sets the project as having been compelted scorm.disconnect(); // disconnects from the system lmsConnected = false; // sets lmsConnected to false } The comments should help you work your way through it. Sticking to this naming convention should provide you with code hinting to help add your event listeners. The numbers 5 ,10 & 0 could be replaced with variables that would be impacted by the actions of the users. Hope this helps. Wade

When you write Actionscript code it feels like you're calling PHP functions and passing objects back and forth directly, it's that easy. Here's a few database driven learning applications that use it: http://matbury.com/moodle/course/view.php?id=9 (Login as a guest) I'm actually going to change them to XML driven ones because that's what most people are comfortable with. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 回應: How to Store and show the socre of a flash?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, @Leslie, Student IDs, names, groups, etc. are all handled on the server for security reasons. You can call the Users.php and Groups.php services at: http://code.google.com/p/swf-activity-module/source/browse/#svn/trunk/src/moodle/lib/amfphp/services to retrieve specific data about specific users, depending on the users' capabilities as set by Moodle, i.e. only teachers can get other users' data, students only have access to their own, etc. If you know Moodle's lib functions, you can create new services to access the messaging system and other functions so you can set up custom chat activities or send grades via email. Be sure to filter out any sensitive information before sending it client-side though! @Jason, AMFPHP is much simpler to implement than JSON + ExternalInterface and easier to learn. I'm sure you'll wonder how you ever managed without it! @Lawrence, if you want Flash to communicate with Moodle, then you need AMFPHP. The SWF Activity Module doesn't support JSON + ExternalInterface. Students can store their grades locally if you wish. Just use a local SharedObject and you can store almost anything you like, even mini database files, in users' browser caches. The grade book is the easiest to implement though, and Moodle's grade book is flexible enough to allow you to store grades and feedback that doesn't count towards students' final grades. I hope this helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: Does SCORM allow branching scenarios?
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm currently using Articulate to publish PowerPoint into flash/SCORM files. I have a large project that has some sophisticated requirements that are not possible with Articulate. I have a several-module course with between-module quizzes. Each quiz must be passed to advance to the next module. At the end of all of the modules there is a 20 question final assessment made up of questions from the different modules. A learner must earn at least 80 percent on the final assessment to complete the program. If a student scores 80 percent or better on the final assessment the course should be recognized as complete. If the student earns less than 80 percent, the student should be told how many were answered incorrectly and must be required to view the modules related to the questions that were missed. The modules in which the learner missed final assessment questions will be marked as incomplete and the student must fully complete these modules again before attempting another version of the final assessment. The student should only be required to re-take questions from the section in which they did not answer questions correctly. Learners do not need to be tested on the sections they have already completed successfully. The learner must retake the exam until a combined score of 80 percent is earned. For example, if the student answers 11 questions correctly and 9 incorrectly on the final assessment, he or she only needs to answer 5 of 9 questions correctly on the second version of the final assessment to demonstrate comprehension of the material. Learners will be allowed as many attempts as necessary to achieve an 80 percent score. Multiple versions of the final assessment will be used to pull new questions from the sections in which the student is answering questions incorrectly. Does SCORM permit this level of sophistication? If yes, do you know of any authoring tools that have these features? If SCORM is the limitation, rather than the authoring tool, can you recommend another route for me to solve this problem?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.0 SCORM Content Size Incorrect
ResponsesInList.Text: make sure you have the latest 2.0Stable code - a large range of fixes have been made since the initial 2.0 release. the settings to change the stage size in SCORM are only for the pop-up window - is that what you are trying to use? - if so, your browser is probably overriding those settings - modern browsers don't allow JS to control things like full window size, open in new window settings - they allow the user to specify how they want the windows to be controlled. If you're not using the new window setting and your scorm still isn't using the full window size with the latest 2.0Stable code, create a tracker issue and attach your package so we can reproduce it. ResponsesInList.Title: Round SCORM 1.2 cmi.core.score.raw output?
ResponsesInList.Text: (Moodle 1.9.11) I don't know if this has been answered before but I been searching for quite some time now. This question is more* aimed at the vet SCORM people out there but: Situation: I have these SCORM 1.2 exams.  When someone scores a 'nice' grade like 83, 95.75 etc. the package reports the score perfectly to Moodle and the Gradebook. When the grade is some monster long repeating decimal like...83.333333333333333336 it reports a 405 error on the score.raw line in the debugger and the score vanishes (learning objects 1 or 0 still works though but these are tests, we want to see scores). Question: How would one go about rounding to the nearest hundredths place in the SCORM package where it's reporting this grade?  The tool we use to create these packages is "Evolution" and as far as I can tell, I have torn it apart and there is no where to set these variables. Alternatively, how would I go about changing how many decimals Moodle captures? I can get up to five right now, but then again I dont want the grade book to be showing these long decimals... There is NO possible way I am the first to have this issue.* The attached file is the portion of the debugger where the situation I described is illustrated.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Round SCORM 1.2 cmi.core.score.raw output?
ResponsesInList.Text: I suppose we could add some code to tidy that up on the Moodle side - allowing longer decimal values to be passed back to Moodle - the 405 is supposed to be return for an invalid data type - but I suppose the spec could be interpreted to allow longer decimal values... but... IMO this should really be tidied up within your authoring tool - probably best that you try to contact the vendor that created/developed the evolution package you are using. - if you want us to accept those full decimal values in Moodle, create a Tracker issue for it and we might take a look at some point.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM tracking works in Moodle 1.9 but not 2.0
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Bill, see MDL-26880 . BTW , your SCO is calling Commit too many times, especially when there's nothing to commit . Please remember that every Commit call requires a remote call i.e. it slows the learner experience attending at your SCO: it could be wise to use a boolean to block such unuseful calls IF no successful SetValue has been performed since the last Commit . Besides the SCO needs to esplicitly Terminate the tracking session to let Total Time and other stuff to be evaluated on the LMS (Moodle here) side: a LO is a SCO ONLY when it is able to perform both Initialize AND Terminate calls, according with the specs. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Access to other lesson data
ResponsesInList.Text: Actually I find this is a very limiting interpretation and implemetation of SCORM objectives.  The SCORM runtime spec doesn't address the referencing of objectives by separate SCOs, but the AICC CMI Guidelines for Interoperability (which Moodle also supports)  does: 2.8 Objectives: Definition This element contains information on how the student has performed on objectives related to the AU.  The performance may be related to previous sessions in the AU, or to the student user's performance in other AUs (in the same course) related to the same objectives . These objectives... (etc) (my underlining and in AICC-speak, AU==SCO) The benefits of objectives being external to a SCO (even limited to within the same course) are clear; for example: A course certificate can reference the objectives associated with SCO elements in the course, to give an overall certificate of attainment. Prerequisites can be set up, requiring other SCOs (or specific objectives within those SCOs) to be completed before access. Separate pre-testing becomes a reality. To give a more concrete example, the knowledge of a specific safety procedure may be common to many activities covered in the course, and once competence has been demonstrated by the learner, any number of otherwise blocked activities could become accessible. The support of objectives in a SCORM (or AICC HACP) LMS is optional, so there can be no complaint about Moodle here, but maybe this thread can start a discussion leading to enhancement of Moodle's SCORM package.   As for my priority, the absence of external objectives would severely impact  the transfer my courseware to Moodle from another LMS (which does support SCO-external objectives).

ResponsesInList.Title: Bulk add of SCORM/AICC courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, Experts!  My apologies if this has been answered.  I could not find it in any FAQ. I have a collection of over 300 course (.zip) files.  I would like to advise our customer of a simple, unattended operation to load them. Does such a facility exist?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bulk add of SCORM/AICC courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi George, AFAIK it doesn't exist. It could be developed but it requires to strongly design the expected results, e.g.: one AICC/SCORM Activity => one Course; Course Fullname = Activity name => Package Title; Course shortname => Package Identifier; Lookup table to map (and optionally create, if missing) categories under which courses containing activities should be classified; Parameters for each AICC/SCORM activity e.g. popup window? ... Shortly: IMHO it's a matter of defining the scope/objectives and then of planning the efforts required to develop it. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Suspend Data Error
ResponsesInList.Text: Arnold, the 'rn' replacing your line breaks are carriage-return (ascii 13, typed as '\r') and linefeed (ascii 10, typed as '\n') characters that have lost their control character ('\') somewhere; ie '\r\n' is exported in suspend_data, and interpretted as the text characters 'rn' on  import. Where this is happening, and how to deal with it is something you need to look for.

ResponsesInList.Title: External Packages
ResponsesInList.Text: According to the Help "Downloaded package - Enables a package URL to be specified. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External Packages
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Silverio, it looks like (reading the 2.0 code) that the Moodle framework delegates these updates directly to the AICC/SCORM module, regardless how / where this external package has been defined: look at mod/scorm/lib.php::scorm_cron() code, there you'll find the logic, subjected to having a working Moodle cron, with which Moodle is supposed to update the package. The options ( mod/scorm/locallib.php ) are: /// Constants and settings for module scorm define('UPDATE_NEVER', '0'); define('UPDATE_ONCHANGE', '1'); define('UPDATE_EVERYDAY', '2'); define('UPDATE_EVERYTIME', '3'); where UPDATE_EVERYTIME is really aggressive, implemented in mod/scorm/locallib.php::scorm_view_display() and in mod/scorm/locallib.php::scorm_simple_play() . Whenever the update is triggered mod/scorm/locallib.php::scorm_parse() will be called and the behaviour about an external package is subjected to these conf params: . .. } else if ($scorm->scormtype === SCORM_TYPE_EXTERNAL and $cfg_scorm->allowtypeexternal) { ... } else if ($scorm->scormtype === SCORM_TYPE_IMSREPOSITORY and !empty($CFG->repositoryactivate) and $cfg_scorm->allowtypeimsrepository) { ... The first thing I can see here (need of some tests and more code review to judge my statements above) is that Moodle has decided to unbalance the two types of IMS packages, the SCORM one and the pure one, probably limiting the possibility to use a Repository Plug-in to handle just IMS Packages, being those ones friendly using a remote domain (== no SCORM cross domain issue here since an IMS package is not tracked at all). The second thing is that both 1.9 and 2.0 does not allow you to change the update frequency value (default to 0 = UPDATE_NEVER ), unless you directly edit the related value at mdl_scorm.updatefreq : you've just hit an hidden feature ;). Room for improvements here. The third thing is that it sounds like an external package here means the URL to an external imsmanifest. xml and not to all the ZIP archive. Shortly, it seems it should work with some limitations and hacks but never tested by myself. @Dan: am I wrong? HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: External Packages
ResponsesInList.Text: ERRATA CORRIGE 01 About my "second thing": Moodle gives you the possibility to visually change the updatefreq value by editing the activity i.e. no need to change it exclusively by editing the database . Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: loadSCO.php / myFindAPI() js error in Firefox
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a tricky one I think. Here's the situation: I have a website hosting an iframe containing Moodle (don't ask). When the website launches a course, it pushes the player.php page into that iframe, and the course is set to open in a popup. As expected, it pops up. It beings playing in all browsers except Firefox (latest: 3.6.13). I've traced it and FF encounters the following error: Permission denied for < http://ourmainsite.com > to get property Window.API from < http://ourmainsite.com >. It's hitting this in loadSCO.php in the javascript function myFindAPI(), which looks like so: function myFindAPI(win) { while ((win.API == null) && (win.parent != null) && (win.parent != win)) { myFindAPITries++; // Note: 7 is an arbitrary number, but should be more than sufficient if (myFindAPITries > 7) { return null; } win = win.parent; } return win.API; } I find it odd Firefox is throwing this error but no other browsers. It also seems odd that it thinks that our MAIN site is its parent window, where I'd assume that it should think the iframe is its parent window (seeing as it is). This may be a Firefox bug, but it's something that should probably be handled in loadSCO.php. The result of this is in the popup window it hits the javascript error and stops, so it just shows "Activity loading, please wait ..." and goes no further. I see the meta refresh on the page, but I assume it won't continue due to the js error. I tried just returning null right at the beginning of myFindAPI() (thereby skipping the entire function) and everything seems to work fine then. There's no longer a js error, the meta refresh kicks in and the content loads. I assume there would be downstream repercussions from doing this, though. I don't know much about how any of this works, but I assume it needs that API. Any thoughts? Thanks in advance. -=Cam function myFindAPI(win) { while ((win.API == null) && (win.parent != null) && (win.parent != win)) { myFindAPITries++; // Note: 7 is an arbitrary number, but should be more than sufficient if (myFindAPITries > 7) { return null; } win = win.parent; } return win.API; } function myFindAPI(win) { while ((win.API == null) && (win.parent != null) && (win.parent != win)) { myFindAPITries++; // Note: 7 is an arbitrary number, but should be more than sufficient if (myFindAPITries > 7) { return null; } win = win.parent; } return win.API; }

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I am testing some of our AICC content using the HACP protocol en found some problems. I upgraded to te latest 1.6.1+ release before testing. 1) I got a JS error in aicc.js.php in the datamodel initialization line 136: eval(element+' = datamodel["'+element+'"].defaultvalue;'); After removing the following two elements from the datamodel the error message was gone: line 74: 'cmi.evaluation.comments._count':{'defaultvalue':'0', 'mod':'r', 'writeerror':'402'}, line 75: 'cmi.evaluation.comments._children':{'defaultvalue':comments_children, 'mod':'r', 'writeerror':'402'}, 2)  The names in the name/value-pairs of the HACP request message (command, version, session_id, au_password, aicc_data) should be case-insensitive (page 171 of CMI001 Version 4.0). The required_param() and optional_param() functions used to retrieve the parameters (aicc.php lines 5:7) only check for lowercase names. 3) The aicc_data in de response of the "getparam" command should use "carriage return/linefeed" as end-of-line markers (also on page 171 of CMI001 Version 4.0). Moodle uses only "linefeed". 4) A 'completed' lesson is set to 'failed' if there is no masteryscore. "If a value is present for both Student Data.Mastery Score and Core.Score.Raw, the CMI must change the Core.Lesson Status to “passed” or “failed” accordingly for that AU. If the AU does not return a value for Core.Score.Raw, then the student is considered to have not performed the portion of the AU’s content that was the scored activity and the CMI does not modify Core.Lesson Status based on Student Data.Mastery Score." (page 63 of CMI001 Version 4.0) from aicc.php lines 248:252 replace: if ( !empty($sco->masteryscore) && !empty($score) && ($score >= $sco->masteryscore)) { $lessonstatus = 'passed'; } else { $lessonstatus = 'failed'; } with: if (!empty($sco->masteryscore) && !empty($score)){ if ($score >= $sco->masteryscore) { $lessonstatus = 'passed'; } else { $lessonstatus = 'failed'; } } Hope this helps, Albert.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: lesson completed - maybe a bug?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi, I work with Andrea and we may have found a solution to this problem, that implies commenting a few code lines in moodle. I will resume here the problem and the solution.
The question is: does our solution affect negatively other parts of the Moodle code? The problem As Andrea already said, we have inserted a SCORM learning object in our Moodle, and we expect to see in the reports each lesson as "completed" after viewing the 80% of it. What we actually see is: - viewing lesson for a few seconds (<80%) and stop: report says "incomplete" - viewing same lesson for another few seconds (<80%): "complete" - viewing same lesson for another few seconds (<80%): "incomplete" - viewing same lesson for another few seconds (<80%): "complete" - ... and so on: complete, incomplete, complete, incomplete... - until I reach 80% of the lesson, then the report always says "complete" Steps to reproduce You can find the course zip here: http://dl.dropbox.com/u/3198614/impress_scorm_con_asset_v2.0.zip The SCORM has been generated with Adobe Captivate 4, with this reporting options: - SCORM 1.2 - Report interactions and the score - Report Complete/Incomplete - Report Score to LMS as Percent - 80% or more of total score to pass Moodle SCORM configuration is shown in the Andrea's post screenshot. The proposed solution After doing some debugging with firebug and monitoring DB changes we noted that: - every time the player loads the lesson, it's set "completed" even before actually playing it the first time (loadSCO.php) - when the sco is being played, after each slide it sends the status information to the LMS - when the sco is stopped, it sends the completion information to the LMS, which in case of status "incomplete", overrides the "completed" set by moodle when the player is loaded - the problem is here: the completion status is being sent to the LMS only alternately I think the problem is on the Captivate side. Anyway, we have seen that commenting this lines in Moodle's moodle/mod/scorm/loadSCO.php solves the problem: (lines from 72 to 77) /* if ($sco->scormtype == 'asset') { $attempt = scorm_get_last_attempt($scorm->id,$USER->id); $element = ($scorm->version == 'scorm_13' || $scorm->version == 'SCORM_1.3') ? 'cmi.completion_status':'cmi.core.lesson_status'; $value = 'completed'; $result = scorm_insert_track($USER->id, $scorm->id, $sco->id, $attempt, $element, $value); } */ This way it works fine for us. Any comment on this? Is it dangerous to leave this lines commented? Thanks for any suggestion. Cheers, Federica.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: lesson completed - maybe a bug?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Federica, IMHO you should fix your package and not hack Moodle code 'cause of the bug here is in your package. A SCO i.e. a web unit able to interact with the platform using RTE calls, must be declared as sco and not as asset , being the default type. Looking at your package, the above statement means that e.g.: 
```text
<resource identifier="RES-379A3904953B88CE5A35E9D89CABEDF8" type="webcontent" href="I01%20Introduzione%20a%20Impress/I01%20Introduzione%20a%20Impress.htm">
```
 should be: 
```text
<resource identifier="RES-379A3904953B88CE5A35E9D89CABEDF8" type="webcontent" 
adlcp:scormType="sco"
 href="I01%20Introduzione%20a%20Impress/I01%20Introduzione%20a%20Impress.htm">
```
 If you look at your package you'll see you've multiple imsmanifest. xml , each one addressing a LO and those files are correct: it seems you've wrongly re-packaged those LOs in one course. Ciao, Matteo

ResponsesInList.Text: the only thing I can think of here is that the "response" being passed isn't a valid utf8 character. It looks like "D" in the screenshot which should theoretically work - is it possible that you have a non utf8 character there? also - the interaction type "choice" has this requirement in the spec: one or more single characters separated by a comma. Legal characters are “0” to “9” and “a” to “z”. If all the characters must be chosen to assume the feedback is correct, then the comma-separated list must be surrounded by curly brackets: { } note the spec defines lower case a-z not A-Z (although I'm pretty sure we aren't that strict in Moodle) so...if you're pasing "false" in a choice interaction type that might cause issues in other LMS as well - you may want to change to using "fill-in" instead.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: filesize limit on SCORM course
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Gilles If you are FTP'ing your SCORM course (SCO) you need first to take note of the id# of the course you want to use it in. The course id# is found at the end of the course url. This number corresponds to the folder# in the moodledata directory and is where the course's files are kept. (at this point I am presuming you are using 1.x.) Add your SCO to the directory that corresponds to you course id#. You can put it inside another folder if you want, but it is not required - I think this is where you confusion originates. Basically what you are doing is adding your SCO to the root folder of your course's files area. From inside your course now, create your SCORM activity. When you click on the browse button, you will see the root folder of your course's files area (the  numbered moodledata folder you have just uploaded your SCO to). Select the SCO that you have just uploaded. Once you have completed the activity, if you go back into the moodledata folder, you can see that moodle has added (if it wasn't there before) a moddata folder. Inside that is a scorm folder. If you drill down from here, you will eventually come to your SCO unpackaged somewhere within its very own folder. This is where you saw the "oddly numbered/named folders" is it not? Don't worry about these. Moodle automatically creates these each time you deploy a SCO. The more SCO's in your course, the more folders within the moddata/scorm folder. HTH - Carl

In Lectora, go into the title property, content tab and set the Type of Title to “AICC/SCORM/CourseMill (3x and above) Published Title.” This will put your content into a SCO or as Lectora calls it, an Assignable Unit. 2. Then publish the title with SCORM 1.2 support. Moodle’s SCORM 2004 is lacking. I think the key is you have to put your content into a SCO (aka, Assignable Unit). As a side note, if you are going to have the SCORM API enforce things like prerequisites between SCO units (Assignable Units), you have to publish for SCORM 1.2. SCORM 2004 did not work. Hope that helps

This is a very poor way to fix it for product, but great for me because it works :D Seems like the finalheight should be the configured height if it's set. Anyway, I hope this helps someone. - Joe

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Object Stage Dimension Error
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everybody: I had the problem of dimension in SCORM so I tried some of the possible solutions posted here. However no of them worked for me. Then I found a code into the theme EduMoodle that I tried into my own theme and others and it solved the problem. Just copy the following code into the file styles_layout of your theme ( In some themes such as in the aardvark theme , the name of the file stats with the theme name, for example: aardvark_layout instead of styles_layout) : /*** *** Modules: Scorm ***/ .structlist { list-style-type: none; white-space: nowrap; font-size: small; } .orgtitle { font-weight: bold; font-size: small; } #mod-scorm-player #scormpage { position: relative; width: 100%; height: 100%; } .mod-scorm .top { vertical-align: top; } .mod-scorm .scorm-left { text-align: left; } .mod-scorm .scorm-center { text-align: center; } .mod-scorm .scorm-right { text-align: right; height: 100%; } .mod-scorm .scoframe { width: 100%; height: 100%; frameborder: 0px; } #mod-scorm-player #tochead { text-align: center; top: 3px; height: 30px; } #mod-scorm-player .toc { width: 80%; margin-left: 20%; } #mod-scorm-player .no-toc { width: 100%; } #mod-scorm-player #scormobject { height: 400px; } #mod-scorm-player #scormtop { position: relative; width: 100%; height: 30px; } #mod-scorm-player #scormbrowse { position: absolute; left: 5px; top: 0px; } #mod-scorm-player #scormnav { position: absolute; right: 5px; top: 0px; text-align: center; top: 3px; width: 100%; } #mod-scorm-view .structurehead { text-align: center; } #mod-scorm-view .structurelist { list-style-type: none; white-space: nowrap; } #mod-scorm-player #scormbox { width: 74%; position: absolute; right: 0px; top: 0px; } #mod-scorm-player #tocbox { position: relative; left: 0px; width: 24%; font-size: 0.8em; } #mod-scorm-player #tochead { position: relative; text-align: center; top: 3px; height: 30px; } #toctree { position:relative; width:100%; overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: auto; } .structurelist { list-style-type: none; } #mod-scorm-player .structurelist { position: relative; list-style-type: none; width: 96%; margin-left:0; padding-left: 0; margin-right:0; padding-right: 0; padding-top: 0; padding-bottom: 0; margin-top:0; margin-bottom:0; } #mod-scorm-player .structurelist ul{ padding-left: 0.5em; margin-left: 0.5em; } #mod-scorm-view .structurelist { list-style-type: none; white-space: nowrap; } a#mod-scorm-log-toggle { font-size: 0.7em; font-weight: bold; } That's it. Hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Item tree is not played
ResponsesInList.Text: that Zip file is corrupt - it uses slashes in the filenames instead of valid directories. it will unzip fine on windows, but on linux machines it unzips with slashes in the filename - which confuses Moodle 2.0 file handling processes. Unzip the file on windows(which will work for some reason) - then re-zip on windows and upload the newly zipped file and it will probably work fine. Moodle 1.9 worked by "fluke" on linux machines due to theway the old file handling worked, but 2.0 requires your zip to use valid directories. here's another post with the same issue: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=158881 what did you use to generate the zip?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Activity and Gradebook Communication
ResponsesInList.Text: Just a bit of information here for those whom are interested in getting the Scorm 1.2 working with Moodle 1.9.x . If you are having problems with the gradebook not bringing over those SCORM scores then take a look at your mod/scorm/lib.php file in particular the function scorm_update_instance($scorm) which actually updates the 1.9.x gradebook via a call to function scorm_grade_item_update which actually then makes a call to the grade_update function located in moodle/lib/gradelib.php. The actual issue I have seen here is in mod/scorm/lib.php around line #494: /** * Update/create grade item for given scorm * * @param object $scorm object with extra cmidnumber * @param mixed optional array/object of grade(s); 'reset' means reset grades in gradebook * @return object grade_item */ function scorm_grade_item_update($scorm, $grades=NULL) { global $CFG; if (!function_exists('grade_update')) { //workaround for buggy PHP versions require_once($CFG->libdir.'/gradelib.php'); } $params = array('itemname'=>$scorm->name); // $params = array('itemname'=>$scorm->name, 'idnumber'=>$scorm->cmidnumber); The $params array can case issues with scorm when trying to include cmidnumber. Simply in 1.9.1+ I had to remove this to allow the function to complete without errors. The grade_update('mod/scorm', $scorm->course, 'mod', 'scorm', $scorm->id, 0, $grades, $params) function will then execute and write those grade entries in the grade_grades table. Make sure that your grade items settings are not locked as well. These can be accessed from within your course -> grades -> edit ->Categories and Items When setting up Scorm I like to use Categorie Aggregation "Simple Weighted Mean of Grades" with my scorm Grading Method set to Learning Objects.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Activity and Gradebook Communication
ResponsesInList.Text: I would like to point out that by the SCORM definition, the lesson_mode was designed to inform a SCO of how a student would like to interact with a SCO and not to control the LMS (Moodle). As of SCORM 1.2 the lesson_mode has 3 values: browse - The student wants to preview the materials, but not necessarily challenge the SCO for a grade normal - This indicates that the SCO should behave as designed for a student wanting to get credit for his learning review - The student has already seen the material at least once and been graded By these definitions it is up to the SCO to decide what to report to the LMS.  So if you do not want a score to be reported during review mode, then the SCO should check the lesson_mode and determine if the score should be sent or not. By removing the ability of launching a course when the maximum number of attempts is reached you effectively block a student from using the course as a reference once their attempts are exhausted. Ron
