ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Activity and Gradebook Communication
ResponsesInList.Text: Handling of preview mode is up to the content, not to Moodle. Most software-generated SCORM content doesn't deal with it intelligently. You might want to take a look at this post: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=150969#p660385 From Piers Harding: Preview mode is only a signal to the SCORM content developer for them to change hows the package behaves. If the content developer chooses to ignore this indicator, then there is nothing stopping them from utilising the full SCORM API, and generating any (legal) tracking data. However, the idea is that the content developers should take the hint, and operate the package in a browse only mode, until it is restarted.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Flash As SCORM Activity
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ihsan, AFAIK , you have two options; Option #1 - Go to the ADL website and look up the SCORM specifications and develop your Flash applications and other supporting files accordingly. Pipwerks also has some useful utilities for creating SCORM compliant packages. However, this usually takes months, sometimes years to learn to do effectively. Option #2 - Use an IDE package that publishes SCORM compliant packages. There are many to choose from, all with their pros and cons. I hope this helps! Matt

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Flash As SCORM Activity
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you for the reply, for option #2, is there any IDE package that you can recommend?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Flash As SCORM Activity
ResponsesInList.Text: I'd say it depends on what you want to do. Presumably, you want to use the SCORM module in Moodle so that you can create SCORM compliant quizzes and/or track learners' viewing activity. The most widely used IDEs are Adobe Captivate, Techsmith Camtasia, and Raptivity. They're all slightly different versions of screen recorders with bells and whistles added. There's also some open source (free) alternatives that are worth looking at, depending on your needs. Personally, I think that the types of quizzes that SCORM IDEs produce can be replicated and handled better with Moodle's Quiz module. There are 3rd party plugin question types that support drag and drop, hotspots and one that also deploys Flash. Moodle's Quiz module is also context sensitive and so the appearance with change along with theme and styling changes keeping everything consistent. The project I'm developing is also worth looking at, although it's just the framework for deploying Flash elearning apps, not the apps themselves: http://code.google.com/p/swf-activity-module/ I hope this helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Request SCORM Debug Interpretation Help
ResponsesInList.Text: The cause of this problem has been identified. The SCORM API returns a comma-separated string of group elements with a space after each comma, e.g.: LMSGetValue("cmi.core._children") - student_id, student_name, lesson_location, credit, lesson_status, entry, score, total_time, lesson_mode, exit, session_time This is nice for human readers, but not for computers.  If this string is stepped through to get data (as it should be, because if an LMS does not support an optional element, it won't be in the list), then the space will invalidate the element value as an arguement; e.g: LMSGetValue("cmi.core. student_name") returns a 201invalid argument error (note the space after 'cmi.core .').

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Request SCORM Debug Interpretation Help
ResponsesInList.Text: You're getting an invalid argument error, which makes sense given that you've got a space in every cmi.core element name that's throwing an error. "cmi.core. student_name" is not the same as "cmi.core.student_name"

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Request SCORM Debug Interpretation Help

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Captivate SCORM w/ embedded flv problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, seems I have been able to get an answer for my problem, and I wish to share it here. It seems the problem with embedding .flv files into SCORM objects requires: 1) The .flv files have been encoded correctly 2) The .flv files must have SCORM compliant names 3) The SCORM packager puts the appropriate names with the appropriate .flv files. In my case, the files were not encoded quite right (resulting in some crazy metadata ) and there were some hidden characters in the names of the files. SOLUTION: 1) Re-encode the files correctly 2) Make sure the names are SCORM compliant WORK-AROUND: A few of files were fine, other than the names. Renaming in Windows explorer did not work - the hidden characters remained. Opened a Windows "shell" and used DOS to rename the files, ensuring that they had a compliant name and the .flv extension. What do you know... the embedded .flv files now work in the SCORM package, and when tested with SCORM TEST TRACK ( http://www.scorm.com/scorm-solved/testtrack/ ) everything is fine. I hope nobody else looses any more hair over this problem.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: AICC course xmlHttp status 404
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Nitin, looking at your report the reason appears to be a missing HTTP GET/POST parameter, command : A required parameter (command) was missing Usually HTTP Status 404 is sent by Moodle to the caller through an internal function call, required_param() , in this case: 
```text
    $command
 = required_param
(
'command'
, PARAM_ALPHA
)
;


    
$sessionid
 = required_param
(
'session_id'
, PARAM_ALPHANUM
)
;


    
$aiccdata
 = optional_param
(
'aicc_data'
, 
''
, PARAM_RAW
)
;
```
 You coud try to add my patch to allow the creation of a debug log of the AICC HACP communication per course per user, MDL-21354 , to track the entire coomunication. That being said, maybe the issue is not at Moodle side but into your code, try to add: xmlhttp.setRequestHeader( "Content-Type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" ); to your code just before the send() call, to configure the correct content type being an HTTP POST call, see here for more details about a supposed running sample. ( Edited by Helen Foster to apply fix as suggested in MDLSITE-1121 - original submission Wednesday, 27 January 2010, 10:45 PM )

ResponsesInList.Text: It should also be noted that you can load content from a different server even with SCORM. People do it all the time. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Get when user has finished activity

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New window - Unable to find SCORM API
ResponsesInList.Text: If the pop-up isn't blocked and automatically opens then it should be able to communicate with the api fine - if the pop-up is blocked by a pop-up blocker and the "click here to open a new window" link is used top open the window then some Browsers block the JS communication. I've recently removed the "click here to open a new window" link from the latest 1.9stable release and replaced it with some text like this: "if a pop-up didn't appear, please enable pop-ups and reload the page" - it seems to have been more reliable that way. If that doesn't describe the behaviour you're seeing it would be interesting to hear more info on the web browser you are using.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New window - Unable to find SCORM API
ResponsesInList.Text: next step would be to check for any JS errors that occur when pop-up window is used - if your object (or Moodle) is throwing a JS error it will cause the API communication to fail - try using something that allows you to see the java console/errors in your browser like the web developer toolbar or Firebug . If you get a JS error from Moodle, post the details here so we can take a closer look.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM 1.2 lesson_location not being written
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Sean, from a SCORM perspective that value must go into the DB only when an LMCommit()/LMSFinish() is called and Moodle adopts that flow, i.e. local caching and then remote flushing triggered by those calls. Are you sure your content always performs at least the required LMSFinish() on "closing" the SCORM activities ? Usually SCORM content fires that command on the unload browser event and sometimes this event is not correctly managed. Another point of failure is setting the value of cmi.core.lesson_location: do you check the API for errors e.g. due to uncorrect data format (CMIString, SPM: 255)? HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Proven Authoring tools for Moodle SCORM player
ResponsesInList.Text: Budget considerations apply - many of the more professional SCORM authoring tools are designed for the enterprise training community and are priced accordingly. But budget aside, the authoring tool you choose will depend in part on the pedagogical approach you want to pursue. For example, is the main focus in what you are trying to achieve the learning experience, or the learning content? There are plenty of tools that do "information dump" and presentation level instruction in the form of text and slides with the occasional check on learning. Some fancier versions of that use information mapping, which is great as a way to structure content but maybe not so great as a way to structure a learning experience. If you want to create a rich learning experience, advanced tools like, for example, ToolBook, make it easy for the author to specify how the user will interact with varous kinds of objects. They will run circles around presentation or text-based tools when it comes to provide interactive learning where, for example, a user might be interacting with a multivariate simulation of a complex process. But they also require more thought in the instructional design, and often they have a correspondingly longer learning curve. From a technical perspective, you will want to look at whether the content generated by the tools you are trying passes the ADL certification test suite *without cheating*.  The better tools can export in SCORM 1.2 or SCORM 2004, and may actually guide you in the authoring process so that you don't attempt to use SCORM 2004 features that are not supported if your target delivery is SCORM 1.2. The better tools may also be aware of the limitations of popular but not quite conformant LMS implementations. For example, because SCORM compliant systems like Moodle don't include full conformance, and many Moodle users are still using older versions of the Moodle SCORM engine, some of the tools might also be aware of Moodle limitations. But in most cases you can't find out without asking. For sales people SCORM conformance is often just a checkmark on the spec sheet and they may or may not understand what it means. In your inquiries, ask if the content products of such a tool can be *certified* to be conformant, and with which version of SCORM. An authoring tool itself cannot be certified, because an authoring tool may have too many degrees of freedom and allow you to create content that exceeds the capabilities of SCORM. In the end the only thing that matters is that the content be interoperable, not the authoring tool. There is a useful list of SCORM authoring tools at in the ADL Marketplace at www.adlcommunity.net (specifically: http://adlcommunity.net/course/view.php?id=11 )

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm 1.2  "ScormApi2004.LMSCommit:Undefined".
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Stefaan,

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm 1.2  "ScormApi2004.LMSCommit:Undefined".
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Stefaan, during the PIF publishing stage Moodle identifies the SCORM version by reading the IMS manifest file ( mod\scorm\datamodels\scormlib.php:scorm_get_manifest() ) and, on launching the item, it exposes the right Run Time Environment [RTE] ( API or API_1484_11 ) according with that discovered version above: I guess that your authoring tool wrongly creates IMS manifest and/or API engine, ending with a mismatching "SCORM situation". FYI : the Activity module is called "SCORM/AICC" 'cause of it is able to "understand" the right tracking standard according just with the descriptors inside the tracked course package i.e. there's no configuration at Moodle side about tracking engine type i.e. the selection is course "packager" driven. HTH , Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM 1.2 and cmi.suspend_data size limit
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I created a course using CourseLab and published it as a SCORM 1.2 package. My course has numerous interactions (questions) whose interaction data is stored in cmi.suspend_data in the LMS. Due to the limitations that SCORM 1.2 has in terms of how much data can be stored in cmi.suspend_data, I have been trying to find ways to reduce the amount of data that is saved in cmi.suspend_data in the LMS. This will help address the issue of too much interaction data being stored in cmi.suspend_data in the LMS (which eventually results in error messages displaying). I have had some success at reducing the amount of interaction data stored in cmi.suspend_data by altering the code in the files (runtime. xml and lms.js) contained in my published SCORM 1.2 course. The only interaction data I need stored in cmi.suspend_data is the ID and LearnerResponse . So far, I have been able to prevent the following interaction data from being saved in cmi.suspend_data: Type, Weighting, Timestamp, Latency, and Result. There are two additional interaction data that I want to prevent saving to cmi.suspend_data, namely the Description and something that looks like: <rr><r p=\"0\"/></rr>. Does anyone know how this can be done? Thanks! -Dan p.s. Please be aware that I know that SCORM 2004 allows significantly more data to be stored in cmi.suspend_data, however, the LMS (Moodle) I am using currently does not fully support SCORM 2004, and I have already researched various alternative LMS options that claim to be SCORM 2004 compliant, only to find that in one way or another these LMS alternatives either fall short or are too expensive. Also, separating my course into smaller modules is not feasible and introduces other problems, since many of the interactions in the course are dependent upon one another. The solution I am seeking is eliminating specific interaction data (as described above) to cmi.suspend_data. Thanks! -Dan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM 1.2 and cmi.suspend_data size limit
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Daniel, So, think of the cmi.interactions object as an array. It can contain info for lots of different interactions. Each interaction inhabits one space in this zero-based array. So your student response for your first interaction would go into "cmi.interactions.0.student_response". Try that and see if you get an error in response. It looks from what you've pasted here like you're hard-coding the wrapper file, and that might not be the best idea... I'm not sure what CourseLab is publishing for you, but what you ideally want to do is call the wrapper function from your content and pass it values to the wrapper to save. From the JS you've pasted above, in the 2004 case there is a function for saving interactions data. Somewhere, during runtime of this package, there are interactions being saved to variables, and those variables are (I'll bet) being passed to the LMS by that SCORM_SaveInteractions() function. I would have a look at SCORM_SaveInteractions(). This will be 2004 code, and not 1.2, but, it will tell you where interactions values are stored by your SCORM package during runtime. And then you could, hypothetically, write a function to save those same variables to the LMS in a 1.2 case as well.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ynt: Re: Detailed Reports
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Aydin, It's easy to see the reports in action. Simply sign up for a free trail SCORM Cloud account, then invite a few people (or yourself) to take some training through the interface (up to 10 / month are included in the free trial). Once they've progressed through the training you should start to see the reporting data. It's available in a few places, but the easiest is to to to the History tab in the SCORM Cloud interface. Then you can click on "Goto Reportage for Full Report" near the top to get into the heavy duty reporting. From there you can drill down into any data you might want to see. Note that any widget on any of those pages can be embedded into another web page (the embed code is available by clicking on the arrow at the bottom right of each widget). You can also download the off-the-shelf Moodle mod we publish from scom.com/moodle. That mod has some reporting built in that displays in Moodle, but the full reporting is also available in the SCORM Cloud interface. The Moodle mod is open source, so you are free to customize it and add new reporting widgets as needed. Let us know if you have any more questions. Might be best to take the discussion offline so we don't pester the rest of the group with more detailed questions. You can email me directly at mike at scorm.com. Mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problem uploading a SCORM package
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Andrew, Do you have admin access? Can you check system paths, and make sure that path to unzip is set correctly, just to rule that out? The path might have been changed or something... http://docs.moodle.org/en/System_paths#Path_to_zip Articulate also sometimes fails to produce the manifest, or writes a manifest with some blank lines in it. Moodle does not like those blank lines. So make sure the imsmanifest. xml file is there and if so check for blank carriage returns. It's also worthwhile to create an account at http://scorm.com/ and load the package there. Just because a package works in one LMS doesn't mean it will work fine another. But the test environment on scorm.com is good at pointing out issues with the package, if there are any. Best of luck, Amy

ResponsesInList.Text: hi, i ve installed the exabis e-portfolio module into my moodle site for students, and they can add portfolio files, comments, categories, etc... my question is this... how can students package this eportfoolio up and take with them to either jobs, colleges, others, etc.. in other words i dont want them to have to access my moodle site to see their eportfolio.. thus if i export their eportfolio into scorm format... what then do i use to view/display this portfolio? thanks m

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM - eportfolio module question
ResponsesInList.Text: SCORM sounds like a strange format to export portfolios - the best format would be LEAP - (if exabis supports it) - LEAP is a standard for export of eportfolios and is supported by Mahara and several other ePortfolios. The other format used by a lot of eportfolios is the ability to export your portfolio as a standalone html set of pages - usually zipped up.

I need the results to reflect the captivate interaction IDs that I have set so I can know what questions the students get incorrect on any given test.  How can I filter the data or tell moodle to let this infor through from Captivate/SCORM. It is all set correctly in Captivate but does not come out in Moodle.  What can I do?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Reporting Help

I get the test graded properly but when I look at the details the Captivate IDs have been replaced with Moodle IDs so I can't tell what questions were answered correctly / incorrectly. The captivate is set to randomized answers and the test questions. Is this a SCORM manifest issue, a Captivate issue, or a Moodle issue?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Reporting Help
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Anthony, I believe that Moodle replaces '.' with '_' when it saves the interaction ids to the db. Is that what you're seeing? Or is it more substantial than that? If so, any chance you can get us a debugging report that shows the ids sent to the LMS, and then a screenshot of the resulting report with ids in Moodle? Thanks, A

ResponsesInList.Title: How to set comments_from_lms for a SCORM 1.2 course in moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, I'm developing a SCORM 1.2 course and I'd need comments from the teacher be shown together with the SCO content. To achieve that I thought I could use cmi.comments_from_lms, and it seems as Moodle SCORM implementation would support that. Main problem I have is I cannot find where I can set comments_from_lms value. It should be from outside the SCO, but from the LMS... but I'm lost. Any help out there? Thanks a lot! David

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to set comments_from_lms for a SCORM 1.2 course in moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi David, correct, it's LMS responsibility. AFAIK , being that element optional, there's no way to fill it using Moodle (1.9, 2.0): there's no mention in the whole code about setting this element even though it could be read if someone will write it down into the DB (never tested but I guess easy fixable, in case of errors...). IIRC the ADL Test Suite checks just the RO constraint: I fear this element may suffer from lacking of use cases. Indeed req #5.2 from SCORM_1.2_ConformanceReq.pdf tells: Initialize this element using the value entered into the LMS (if supported by the LMS). i.e. it gives room to avoid any implementation w/o failing LMS-RTE3 compliance. In my experience I never had the opportunity to see an LMS supporting the edition of this element. Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to set comments_from_lms for a SCORM 1.2 course in moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Matteo, actually I was surprised because Moodle claims to support this element (not in loud voice, indeed), and it seems it can be read; but the LMS doesn't allow to set this value. Being an optional element it seems to me more logical implementing no support at all for the element than supporting it while not allowing to set its value from the LMS. I cannot see the point of doing so, and that's the reason I thought I was missing something. Thanks anyway. David

ResponsesInList.Title: Here's the most concise way yet to install a scorm file.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Y'all Here's a super-simple, step-by-step way to install scorms: 1. Download (save to desktop) the zip of the scorm you want to try out. 2. Navigate to the course page. Turn editing on. Of course, you will have to have adminstrative priveleges to do so. 3. Go to add an activity . Under this menu, choose SCORM/AICC. The Scorm page will come up automatically, if you have Moodle 1.9 or better. If you don't, go to BD (Blue Domino) and install Moodle using their InstallCentral facility; that's, BD, Home, Scripting and Add ons, InstallCentral, More, Moodle in that order . 4. On the Adding a new SCORM/AICC page, type in a name for the scorm and a few words in summary. ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM, IIS 6, Slash Arguments, and ISAPI Rewrite
ResponsesInList.Text: Calling all Regular Expression experts! Apologies for this rather lengthy post, but if you can solve the following issue with some elegant regular expression code, you just might make a lot of current and future Moodle/ IIS /SCORM users very happy. Read on if you dare... First I'll lay out the background to this issue (apologies to those that already know it), then I'll explain what I think we need to provide as a solution to finally get SCORM packages working reliably on IIS. HISTORY: For years now, we have been seeing numerous posts in the SCORM forum (and other forums) from baffled Moodle users trying to get this wonderful LMS to work seamlessly with the IIS web server .  The complaints usually center around page not found (404) errors on combinations of files uploaded to Moodle that work perfectly anywhere else. Often those offering assistance comment that they have no issues playing the same content on their Moodle site running Apache server. Now we all know Moodle can work well on IIS, and it will play of almost any type. BUT , sadly it can tend to fail when you upload course files into your moodledata folder... IF ... those files require other linked files in order to play . So for example, if you have an HTM file in your course that needs a linked Javascript or SWF file to play course content,... THEN ...you will likely encounter issues with IIS....specifically page not found or 404 errors.  The files.php page digs out the requested HTM file, but then the browser goes looking for the other linked files in the same folder as files.php, not in the moodledata folder where the original HTM file resides! The issue is due to the way that some pages in Moodle pass information about the URL address of another page by tacking this information on the end of a URL. (E.g. mypage.php?nextpage=/folder1/subfolder1/otherpage.php) Though a common enough technique in web development, this can prove problematic, especially for IIS. SCORM packages seem to be most affected by this issue because they often involve a complex cascade of pages calling other pages, passing arguments in links to play the content and communicate with the SCORM API on the LMS, etc, etc. Their complexity is their downfall in this case. On Apache server, the issue often goes away as soon as you play with the Admin > Server > HTTP > Use Slash Arguments setting. But IIS 6 is unable to use slash arguments because Microsoft disabled this 'feature' as it was a well-known security hole exploited by hackers. (IIS 7 is rumoured to have options that allow it to operate safely again.) About ISAPI Rewrite: The workaround successfully used by some Moodle-IIS users in various forum posts to fix IIS has been to install a small application called ISAPI Rewrite that intercepts the call to URLs on IIS and dynamically rewrites them into a more palatable format. This app is well known to webserver admins and used to implement redirects and/or improve search engine friendliness of websites. Once ISAPI Rewrite is installed on your webserver, you just create a new Web Service Extension in IIS Manager, point it to the ISAPI_Rewrite.dll , make a copy of the httpd.ini file from the C:\Program Files\Helicon\ISAPI_Rewrite and copy it into your Moodle root directory (so that any code there only affects Moodle), and finally add a rewrite rule. The rewrite rule quoted in many Moodle forum posts as pulling off the fix is a line of code (a regular expression) that looks like this: RewriteRule (.*?\.php)(\/.+) $1\?file=$2 [N,I] This normally works and cures the slash arguments issue on IIS,...if your content only involves a single HTM file calling other files (e.g. an HTM linking out to images, javascript, or SWF files). Happy days...almost. However, it doesn't seem to work for most SCORM packages, and I believe the reason is that SCORMs involve much more complex interactions and argument passing between pages that this little rewrite rule doesn't allow for. Under SCORM, the rewrite rule can encounter not just one set of arguments but several. I'm currently using Moodle 1.82 on IIS 6.0 and ISAPI Rewrite with the rule shown above.   I can get any type of content to play,...except SCORM. Perusing IIS server logs I've found that the URL which is failing on my box looks like this: http://myMoodleServer/file.php?file=/2/Lesson_1/Lesson_1.swf?SCORM_API=0.2&SCORM_TYPE=0 Notice that there are not one but two question marks in this URL? I think this is why IIS is falling over and if we could tweak the rewrite rule to allow for this, we might just be able to get SCORMs (at least those created by Captivate) to play on IIS. We may even need multiple rules customised to a given SCORM implementation to get them working. Now since I don't know how to write regular expressions...is there anyone out there that can oblige?? If so, and we can put this issue to bed, we may have eliminated a major source of frustration for many Moodle users. Suggestions please...?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM, IIS 6, Slash Arguments, and ISAPI Rewrite
ResponsesInList.Text: Just to add more fuel to the fire. I've discovered that IIS, even with a rewrite rule cannot handle any extra arguments being added to the query string. Even a single ? on the end will break it. Apache has no such problems. See the graphic below. This is the same HTM and Javascript file set up in Moodle on Apache and Moodle on IIS (middle and lower). You can add anything you like on the end of the URL and Apache will still serve up the testpage.htm. On IIS it will only work if there are no additional arguments added.  SCORM packages would almost always do this. IIS only gives you one throw at adding arguments to a URL. Moodle's use of file.php to call files from moodledata folders by passing in the file URL as an argument would appear to be using that throw as far as IIS is concerned.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM, IIS 6, Slash Arguments, and ISAPI Rewrite
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi John, I think you misunderstand. The reference to file.php is not inside the SCORM. File.php is shown in the link because that's how Moodle fetch content out of moodledata course folders to serve up.  If you look at a typical web server trace of what happens when a SCORM is accessed in Moodle, you see a series of links like this, all beginning with file.php, followed by it's argument containing the path to each of the files inside the SCORM. SCORM packages have to be inside the moodledata folder for them to communicate with Moodle's SCORM API properly. You cannot have the SCORM located elsewhere on the webserver, or on another webserver, because the API communication breaks down and scores don't get passed. So the issue we're trying to solve here is not due to a problem in my SCORM package. The issue is due to the way that Moodle has implemented file.php,... specifically because it uses URL arguments to pass data about the pathway to a file (as shown in my example).  However, if that file also happens to have arguments on the end of it (such as ?SCORM_API=0.2&SCORM_TYPE=0 from my example) then IIS throws a fit. If there is even so much as one ? or / after the name of the file in the argument being passed by file.php, IIS cannot handle it. Apache just laughs and says: "No problem!" (Long live open source.) So, does anybody have ideas about how to get over this issue? I'm beginning to wonder if the only way to fix it is to refactor the files.php code to pass file path info via some other means.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM, IIS 6, Slash Arguments, and ISAPI Rewrite
ResponsesInList.Text: A little more info has come to light that should make this now ridiculously easy for anyone familiar with Regular Expressions (which sadly I am not). It turns out that the whole issue comes down to the question mark tacked onto the end of the filename of the file being called by files.php. If we can modify the rewrite rule to dynamically change this question mark to an ampersand, everything works! The files in the SCORM package are served up by IIS (via files.php), the content plays, and the SCORM score values are passed to the SCORM API. I've been able to verify this by manually changing where the character gets added in the original SCORM javascript code. So is there an easy way to change this regular expression... RewriteRule (.*?\.php)(\/.+) $1\?file=$2 [N,I] ...so that it turns the extra question mark found in some cases (such as SCORMs) into an ampersand instead? We just need to ensure it only does it under these specific conditions so that it doesn't break other pages unrelated to the use of file.php. Any takers?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM, IIS 6, Slash Arguments, and ISAPI Rewrite
ResponsesInList.Text: I think I may have found a solution to this now. Here is the code I have in my httpd.ini file inside the Moodle root folder: # Matches any URL with slashed arguments and adds ?file= before args RewriteRule (.*?file\.php)(\/.+) $1\?file=$2 [N,I] # Finds any cases of doubled up ? and changes the second one to & RewriteRule ((.*)([?]+)(.*))([?]+)(.*) $1&$6 [I] You must use the rules in the order shown. The first rule is a slightly modified version of the one previously used. It changes a slashed argument URL into one using ?files= so that IIS can accept it. I had to limit the scope to just the file.php file because it fouled up SCORM playback if you had already unzipped the package and were pointing directly at the imsmanifest. xml file. Don't know why, it just did. The second rule finds any cases of URLs that have two instances of ? characters and changes the second one to an ampersand (&). But it has to follow the first rule otherwise with slashed arguments on in Moodle it won't find any cases of doubled up ?s. With this now in place, I have IIS playing SCORMs in Moodle that wouldn't previously play...and...they are all reporting scores to the database . Yeehaa!! Anybody that can see an issue with this or knows of a better way to solve it is welcome to chime in. For example...There may be other pages in Moodle that use slashed arguments. If so, I'll probably need to add a version of the first rule to cover each one. I'm going back to bed now...bye.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm package not updating - not a browser cache issue
ResponsesInList.Text: I used to have the same problem and discovered it was caused by the way web browsers work. Web browsers cache or save copies of web pages...the first time you go to a page, it is not in the cache so you get a fresh download of the page. The next time you go to the page, the browser checks the cache, finds the web page there and shows it to you possibly with old, outdated information. Most of the time, this behaviour is no problem for general web surfing. But, with Moodle, you will keep seeing things you know should be changed each time you go back to a page like you have described. If you are using the latest Firefox go here and it will tell you how to fix it so it always downloads the page from the web site instead of the cache.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Articulate Attachments
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi John, Something to watch out for is that sometimes the code that triggers a " download " actually replaces the window in which the SCORM API resides. Just like when you select a link on one Web page, and are sent to a totally different Web page. The API is replaced by the attached file in the browser and the session is prematurely terminated. You can check for that by turning on debugging, and then accessing the SCORM content and the attachment. If the attachment replaces the SCORM session, then all API logs will stop in the debugging window after you access the attachment. http://docs.moodle.org/en/SCORM_FAQ#Debugging_in_1.9 If this does turn out to be an issue, it can be a tricky one to fix. Sometimes it's best to just move the "attachments" into the Moodle course as resources. Regards, Amy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grading problem in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Zy, Attempts handling depends a great deal on what your SCORM package is doing, what data it is sending to the LMS. We have documented the general rules for handling of multiple attempts here: http://docs.moodle.org/en/SCORM_FAQ#Handling_of_Multiple_Attempts There is also an option on Attempts Grading to count only the first attempt... but, as I said above, what is registered as an attempt will depend upon what your SCO is reporting to the LMS. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Student Prefs
ResponsesInList.Text: Ryan, there is no part of the spec that requires an LMS to track those values across various sco's at a global level for a student. The default value is either 0 or empty string depending on which one of the 4 your looking at. These values are not mandatory, so if the LMS supports it-it will usually be only for within the sco. It would probably only work for cmi initialization on first launch and then only within content built to the same spec. To avoid issues most LMS's (who have to think that lots of different content will run on their system) have never set up the bridge to global values from cmi.student_preferences, if they are supported.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Flash quizz (quizbuilder) SCORM-compliant : retrieve questions and response title
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Pascal, I agree with Amy, SCORM is a "standards" that software such as Quiz Builder and Captivate is designed to give specific types of data back to Moodle in a specific format. Thus it makes it easy for non-programmers to develop and implement all types of interactive software (eg: educational video games that track learning) within Moodle with relative ease. For your purpose of a simple quiz with results, the Moodle Quiz module may make the most sense. When I have needed data that was really custom (beyond what Moodle is designed for) I have usually built a custom Flash Application (or Form in PHP/ mySQL ), then POSTED the information with a URLVariable from Flash (eg: URLVar.POST) to PHP and used a PHP form to receive the info in a POST SuperGlobal Variable (eg: $var = $_POST['received data'] then build a query string to send this information to a database such as my SQL . I then tie this back to Moodle via the Webpage/File component. You could build such a form in Moodle with PHP but this would defeat the purpose of using a standard like SCORM. XML is Flashes native data type (based on E4X Syntax) and while flash can read XML files (via a URLRequest) it needs PHP to communicate to write files or communicate with a server . If you really would like to customize your application I will include some code that can help get you started in communicating between Flash and Moodles PHP/ Database . Just remember this is not SCORM and may not work on other SCORM systems. I will also post this in the Flash forum as it may be more appropriate there. Hope this helps. Wade Flash: import flash.events.*; // imported class libraries import flash.net.*; var req:URLRequest; // URLRequest variable var vars:URLVariables = new URLVariables(); // new URL Variable to hold url information var loader:URLLoader = new URLLoader(); // new URL Loader to load php file send_btn.addEventListener(MouseEvent.CLICK, sendData); function sendData (event:MouseEvent): void { req = new URLRequest("PHP_File_Name.php"); // request for the php file vars.student_name = student_name.text; // passess data to php vars.teachers_name = teachers_name.text; req.data = vars; // URL var is passed to url request req.method = URLRequestMethod.POST; //URL req set to POST data loader.load(req); // URLLoader loads the php file and posts } PHP: $student_name = mysql_prep($_POST['student_name']); $teachers_name = mysql_prep($_POST['teachers_name']); // These files are NOT based on object syntax such as 'this->obj' but you could use this approach //You would then use these variables to build a query string such as $result = mysql_query("INSERT INTO DBName (student_name, teachers_name)VALUES ('{$student_name}','{$teachers_name}',);", $DBconnection);

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: flash scorm quiz
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Spencer, There are two parts to this question using the Pipwerks package as Amy suggests. The first is building your quiz component in Flash using AS3.0 and keeping track of the information you want to pass to the grade book in a global variable. Then in your main .fla file use something like the following code to execute on a mouseEvent to send the results (I've attached comments): import pipwerks. SCORM ; // class file to track SCORM information at top of the .fla code var globalVariable: Number; // Used to hold the score your user attained and incremented ++ var lessonStatus:String; // checks the status of lesson complete or not complete var lmsConnected:Boolean; // checks if LMS is available returns true is there is LMS available var success:Boolean; // Hold value to tell if LMS is active var scorm:SCORM = new SCORM(); FINISH_btn.addEventListener(MouseEvent.CLICK, scormFinish) lmsConnected = scorm.connect(); // tries to connect to SCORM and returns true if it does if(lmsConnected) // if it is connected (true) { lessonStatus = scorm.get("cmi.core.lesson_status"); // gets the current status of the lesspm if(lessonStatus == "completed") // is the lesson is already complete { scorm.disconnect(); //Course has already been completed. Disconnect from the system } else { success = scorm.set("cmi.core.lesson_status", "incomplete"); // else set the lesson to incomplete //Must tell LMS course has not been completed yet. } } else { trace("Could not connect to LMS."); // returns a message if lmsConnected is false (not connected) } function scormFinish (event:MouseEvent): void // used to finish upon a mouse click { success = scorm.set("cmi.core.score.raw", globalVariable) //raw score success = scorm.set("cmi.core.score.max", "10") // total score success = scorm.set("cmi.core.score.min", "0"); // min score success = scorm.set("cmi.core.lesson_status", "completed");// sets the project as having been completed scorm.disconnect(); // disconnects from the system lmsConnected = false; // sets lmsConnected to false } You will also need to make some changes in the JavaScript Manifest and HTML files but how to do this is well documented in the Pipwerks directions on Phillip's web site. Hope that helps. Cheers, Wade

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: flash scorm quiz
ResponsesInList.Text: You'll want to look at the interactions in the cmi. Specifically cmi.interactions.n.type and cmi.interactions.n.student_response. There are predefined types in the scorm spec and those types decide what is allowed in student_response. So if type = "true-false" then the spec states student_response is a single character or numeral. Legal characters are 0,1,t and f. 0 corresponds to false. If a word is submitted then only the first character is significant. I've found that type = "performance" is the most flexible across clients as the student_response is a 255 character string.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM doesn't work on moodle 1.9.9+
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, You're problem might be solved by what I have written below; I also had trouble getting everything straight, but what appears below seems to have done the trick. How to upload or install Scorm objects (or zips, projects, whatever you want to call them). The scorm repository is full of good scorm zips. These contain all the files and directories needed to run the scorm, as well as a " front page " (front page for the computer, that is) called the imsmanifest. xml . Now, to install a scorm project, simply go to the scorm option on the drop-down menu called activities . You must be on the course front page, have administrative priviledges for the installation and have editing turned on to do so. Make a course called learning moodle, if you don't want to juggle what you're doing elsewhere. The page that comes up calls for an upload: After creating a folder with the name of the project that you want to use, upload the entire zip file of the scorm directory that you chose from the scorm repository pages. If you see anything except a small folder icon entitled "parent directory," you are uploading to the wrong place. You'll get the picture if you toggle back and forth between that and the other " database " folders a few times, and explore your database backup directories and folder trees. Now, when you have finished uploading and unzipping your scorm zip, go back to the same page, the installation page that appeared when you clicked on the scorm option under activities, and using the same window, the one labelled "package file," and which gives you a "choose or upload folder window/option," go back to the folder you just uploaded with a click of the choose file button, and select the file entitled "imsmanifest.xml." That is the same name that is used in every folder (the different folder names are what enable the computer to differentiate between the various imsmanifest.xml files). Now, if you have entered a complete sentence in the summary and a title of a word or more, when you go down the page and click on save and display there should appear on your screen the hyperlinked title of your scorm project. Voila, that's it! You will find the scorm project listed on your course page, as well. Thank you, Moodle community! Alex

Also, we were wondering if anyone is aware of a more up-to-date code for JavaScript connection to the SCORM API than the Easy SCO Adapter because it has not been updated in quite some time. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm imsmanifest.xml access under Moodle 2.0
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Larry, don't panic! the ability is still there, but disabled by default. It's disabled by default as the new file API in Moodle stores files according to the SHA1 hash of their content. This means each file with particular contents is stored once, irrespective of how many times it is included in different places, even if it is referred to by different names. So - if the reason you are keeping them in a "central" location is to decrease disk space then you don't need to do this anymore. But - there are several other reasons why you might want to do this so we've allowed people to enable the feature. Go to admin > plugins > Activity Modules > Scorm package and find the settings: * Enable external package * Enable downloaded package * Enable IMS package type once these are enabled you can select the type of file to use in a new SCORM here's an explanation of the different types * Uploaded package - Enables a SCORM package to be chosen via the file picker * External SCORM manifest - Enables an imsmanifest.xml URL to be specified. Note: If the URL has a different domain name than your site, then "Downloaded package" is a better option, since otherwise grades are not saved. * Downloaded package - Enables a package URL to be specified. The package will be unzipped and saved locally, and updated when the external SCORM package is updated. * Local IMS content repository - Enables a package to be selected from within an IMS repository';

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Display item status to user - multi part SCO
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dave, A couple of things you might look at here. One thing is that you might just need to rename some icons in your icon set. The other possibility is that your scos might be designated as assets in your manifest file. The asset icons are for assets only. They won't be used for resources in your scorm package that are packaged as scos. If the resource is given the attribute  adlcp:scormtype="asset" in the imsmanifest.xml, it will be treated as an asset by Moodle. If you want to track completion status, score, any more complex data, you should be using the sco type for those resources. If you want the icons associated with a sco, indicating lesson_status of "incomplete", "completed" and so forth, you need to use adlcp:scormtype="sco" instead. Look for resource nodes that look like this: <resource identifier="R_A3" type="webcontent" adlcp:scormtype="asset" href="assets/being_towed_alongside.jpg"> The resource node would need to begin like this: <resource identifier="R_A1" type="webcontent" adlcp:scormtype="sco" href="scos/sco01.htm"> I'm attaching ADL's sample manifest for multiple sco content.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 1 SCO link to multiple courses
ResponsesInList.Text: I found a solution to my problem. Don't know if it could help somebody else, but there is the way I've been able to use one SCORM activity in multiple courses. Thanks to the contributors of the post http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=114560 , where I understand that it could be possible to do it simply by integrating a local imsmanifest.xml file in each subcourses. pointing to the SCORM package extract in the parent course I extract my SCORM package in a parent course (name: Global meta-course, course ID: 90), a hide meta-course and put it in "Administration > Files > moddata > scorm > Test" I make a copy of the imsmanifest.xml file from this SCORM package and I change the links in the <ressources> section and add a relative path to each of the adress (see the annexe for an example) Then I create a new SCORM activity in my subcourse and import the changed imsmanifest.xml file as the "Package file". And that's it... I have my internal repository. And the Grades module of my subcourse keep tracking of the performance of my students. Hope that could be help somebody else! JF Note 1: The package have been create with Adobe Captivate 4

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 1 SCO link to multiple courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Another simpler solution that does not require changes to the imsmanifest file and the creation of metacourses is to place the expanded scorm package within the course 1 (site) files area (eg in a scorm parent folder) and point your scorm activity within each course to this imsmanifest file. eg http://yourmoodlesite.com/1/scorms/yourscormfolder/imsmanifest.xml The scorm package is not password protected but in most installations this is a moot point.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to get a SCORM from an external repository
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Bob, I didn't make that last post very clear did I! In the SCORM Settings page, in the box beside "choose or upload a file" you can type in a url such as http://mywebsite.com/scorm.zip or http://mywebsite.com/imsmanifest.xml if you select the imsmanifest. xml file you will have issues passing information back into moodle. If you select an externally hosted zip, Moodle will download and extract the zip locally and will work nicely. - it will also check the externally hosted version for updates based on the Auto-update frequency set in the SCORM settings page. The reason the imsmanifest.xml method causes issues, is that the files are not downloaded and stored locally by Moodle but loaded directly from the external site. for security Javascript does not allow cross- domain communication. eg a page on mywebsite.com cannot communicate with a page on mymoodlesite.com So your SCORM object hosted on mywebsite.com cannot pass information to the javascript SCORM API on mymoodlesite.com hope that explains it better!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to get a SCORM from an external repository
ResponsesInList.Text: I've posted about this a few times in the forums, but here's a quick summary. Moodle isn't the problem here, it's your Browsers default behaviour and the security imposed by the Javascript engine running in your browser. Javascript is set by default to prevent cross-domain communication... there's nothing I know of that we can do inside Moodle to get around this. If you point to an externally hosted zip instead of the full package, moodle will download it and install the package locally and will work fine.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to get a SCORM from an external repository
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, you could set your manifest to link to your launchable assets on a server you control. Configure separate courses per client then you can track the requests on your end to manage seats purchased etc with some server app programming. The issue with that is you need to deal with cross domain, any oddities that your clients lms's network has running (like a proxy server that blocks users from accessing the internet), new security in OS's/browsers, and any limitations the specific lms puts on that type of deployment. If you use flash it also has newer restrictions on cross domain communication. The SCORM spec supports the external launch but the LMS's, clients network security choices really make it hell to pull off. If you do it that way make sure you build in money to work out the issues or you'll end up losing cash on each client deployment. Business needs has really killed the viability of this solution on a scalable level across clients. Especially for smaller content houses who don't have big budgets. Xerceo Learn had a nice implementation a few years back but again that only good for that LMS. My company just includes a clause in our contracts to run surprise audits by our lawyers at anytime with stiff fines if they go beyond the seat license or repurpose our content.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to get a SCORM from an external repository
ResponsesInList.Text: "Well, you could set your manifest to link to your launchable assets on a server you control" The bottom line is that Javascript Cross domain communication won't work - you can't easily deal with the default browser security settings - it's not practical to educate your users to turn security settings in their browsers off and it's also not very wise. The only option would be for you to host the SCORM objects/players on your own site and then pass back a grade from your internal site to the external LMS This would require that you distribute a custom Moodle module for your clients to use which connects to your external SCORM player - it also means that you would no longer have the benefit of a SCORM package that can be installed in any LMS - unless you had some way to integrate your own player with several different LMS Another option would be to use Rustici's Commercial SCORM cloud - you would host all your SCORM objects in their cloud (they have a Moodle plugin that allows grades to be passed back) SCORM is a standard for Learning objects - and allows distribution of those objects to each organisation - if you want to hold on to your IP and not allow the copying/re-distribution of the objects then SCORM is probably the wrong thing to use. But - there's only so much you can do in this area - you're better to have a licensing agreement with your clients that deals with this rather than invest in ways to prevent copying - Just look at Microsoft and how much they spend on preventing the copying of IP/software and how quick the software is illegally copied/distributed.

ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM + Articulate, courses are always in suspended state
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi All, I have created a SCORM 1.2 complaint course using articulate and uploaded the same using SCORM/AICC module under course format. The problem is even i go through the all the slides of course up to end still it shows the state as ' Passed-Suspended ' and when i Enter the course again it opens it in suspended state. But ideally it should not be suspended as i have completed the course. Can anybody please help in this regard? Thanks, Garima

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM + Articulate, courses are always in suspended state
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Garima, According to SCORM documentation the SCO, course, is responsible for setting the exit state. According to Articulate support a SCO created in Articulate always sets the exit data to suspend even when it is passed or completed. This allows a user to return to the course without losing previous data. I don't agree with this decision by Articulate, but that is what is going on.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2.0  and SCORM 2004

ResponsesInList.Text: Wade is correct - SCORM 2004 isn't currently officially supported - for more information see: http://docs.moodle.org/en/SCORM_FAQ#Supported_Versions 1.9.3 is pretty old - you should be upgrading that site to the latest 1.9 stable - there's a patch that has gone in at some point which fixes the display of times for SCORM 2004 objects (submitted by someone else in the community) - I can't remember off the top of my head if this was backported into 1.9 stable or not. If tracking is working in the latest 1.9 stable for your object, but not in 2.0 it's likely a new bug - feel free to log a bug in the tracker with specific details (keeping in mind that we don't officially support 2004 yet so it will likely take a while before the bug is resolved)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Quick SCORM question...
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Nick, Both types of functionality you are looking for are dependent on the software you are using. SCORM is simply a standard that tell your software how to pass information to Moodle but the type of information that is passed depends on the software package you are using to generate the SCORM files. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Quick SCORM question...
ResponsesInList.Text: 1. Is it possible to get Moodle to tell the student their score at the end of the test? I am probably missing something obvious but cannot see how to do that. I know it works in the quiz activity but can't see it in the SCORM activity. -- If you are using SCORM 1.2 to communicate to Moodle then you will need to make sure that the courseware that is calculating the score for the quiz uses api.LMSSetValue('cmi.core.score.raw',the_score); to send the score (where "the_score" is a score between 0 and 100 converted to a string). 2. The SCORM files I have do not allow for a review of answers. -- SCORM is a data transmission standard only it does not provide functionality to your courseware. That being said "review of answers" has nothing to do with the SCORM part of the equation and everything to do with the programming logic in the actual courseware. Answer a question and click 'next' and that's it - your answer is commited. Can I change this or is it by design? -- This is the design logic for your particular course. If you are a programmer or are familiar enough with the tools that were used to create the course you can modify this logic to function however you like. Hope this help. Brian Caudill JCA Solutions http://www.jcasolutions.com The SCORM Authority

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Beyond Proxy?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Sarah, To display the Flash Object (.swf file) there should be no proxy (cross domain ) issues. Just "point your embed object code (HTML based) and it should display. I do this all the time to "beautify" my main Moodle index when my courses are password protected. However to return information from Flash to Moodle (in php/ sql by say calling Flashes External Interface Class or using a URLVariable.POST Method) then cross domain policies do apply. I believe the Pipwerks SCORM package sets cookies via JavaScript and then uses Moodles PHP to pull down the SCORM variables (I could be corrected on this as it has been a while since I have used it). I am not sure it was designed to work cross domain without modifications. ResponsesInList.Title: Handling of Multiple Attempts in 1.9.8
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi All, I've put together this list in attempt to describe how multiple attempts are handled in 1.9.8. I imagine that Dan M. and others who are familiar with the PHP will be able to tell me whether or not this is an accurate description of how multiple attempts are handled in 1.9.8. If y'all have time, could you let me know what I'm missing, or what's incorrect? Then I'll add the final draft to our documentation. To my knowledge, these are the behaviors that Moodle 1.9.8 has with regard to attempts: 1) The learner is not shown the option to start a new attempt until their first attempt is given a cmi.core.lesson_status of 'completed'. 2) The learner is thereafter shown a checkbox the 'Start a new attempt' when they access the scorm object via the content structure page. If the learner does not check that checkbox, they are re-entering the previous attempt, and when they leave, their original score will be overwritten. 3) When a second attempt, and subsequent attempts, receive a cmi.core.lesson_status of 'completed', they wil be considered when the gradebook score is calculated. I've also had customers ask about preview mode, and claim that cmi.core values are still being set when the scorm content is accessed in preview mode. Can anyone describe exactly what is happening in that case? When is preview mode triggered, if it is enabled, and what does it mean for the getting and setting of SCORM elements? Warm regards, Amy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Handling of Multiple Attempts in 1.9.8
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Amy - There are lot of possible outcomes in all the influencing conditions that go into the make up of attempts, completion and scoring. Firstly, the ability to have a new attempt is influenced by core.lesson_status = 'completed' or 'passed' - either of these on the previous will make available 'Start new attempt'. How they are considered for grading is heavily influenced by the grading scheme chosen - 'attempted', 'average', 'count last', 'highest' etc. Preview mode is only a signal to the SCORM content developer for them to change hows the package behaves. If the content developer chooses to ignore this indicator, then there is nothing stopping them from utilising the full SCORM API, and generating any (legal) tracking data. However, the idea is that the content developers should take the hint, and operate the package in a browse only mode, until it is restarted. Cheers, Piers Harding.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM module doesn't display - blank page
ResponsesInList.Text: Catalin, Remove the blank lines from the manifest. There should be no blank carriage returns. You would change the file paths inside the manifest file by changing the file paths inside the manifest file. http://www.google.com/search?q=file+paths&ie=utf-8&oe=utf-8&aq=t&rls=org.mozilla:en-US:official&client=firefox-a There are already paths there to every single file that the package needs to run correctly. You need to make sure all paths are correct. The manifest tells Moodle how to unpackage and present the content, and if there is 1 file path wrong in the manifest, then Moodle will not find that file and place it for use by the SCORM activity. This is why issues with the manifest often result in a file not found error. So check the file paths in the manifest to make sure they match up with the actual files and folders in the SCORM package. A

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM module doesn't display - blank page
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jose, The SCORM module in Moodle is compatible with Firefox /Chrome/Safari/Opera/IE (it even includes compatibility fixes for IE 6 - and I think it runs on IE 5.5 as well.) - Any Browser that has a recent/good javascript engine should support it fine. If your object only works in IE then it is probably related to the Authoring Tool you used to create your SCORM object - many Authoring tools include Browser specific code that won't run on other browsers - the most common of these is the use of ActiveX objects - see: http://support.mozilla.com/en-US/kb/Active%20X perhaps you could share what Authoring Tool you are using and others here may be able to comment on how you can modify it to work cross-platform.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Flash Scores and track details empty
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Sarah, looking at the red lines you'll find 404 and 201 SCORM errors. Whilst the internal course code seems to ask for the error through an LMSGetErrorString() call e.g. somewhere during the delivery there are alerts within the course or some sort of recovery strategies, the content cannot be defined SCORM compliant since it wrongly access some part of the SCORM datamodel and this could be the reason of the unpredictable results around your learning strategy/expected results. Another possibile reason is that the log highlights the missing of the call to LMSFinish() which closes the tracking session and let the platform definitely store the SCORM values into the platform. FYI : here you can find a quick but complete description of the SCORM datamodel (click on SCORM 1.2 tab). FYI: you should apply ADL SCORM test suite to check the full compliance, see here . HTH , Matteo

User report -track details Other Tracks Element Value cmi.core.lesson_location 3 cmi.suspend_data D1Enone$nP1Enone$nP1Enone$nP1Enone$nP Authoring tool: captivate 3 Moodle version: 1 .9.5 (Build: 20090515) In case someone needs captivate quiz preference. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM playback issue
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Aris, From what it sounds like you need to ensure that you click on the "Start New Attempt" check box at the bottom of the SCORM activity when making a second, third, etc. attempt from Captivate 3. I suspect the reason your having this problem (from the information you provided) is that navigation in Captivate 3 projects is based BOTH on "Flash Events" AND data provided by Moodle (and passed to the Captivate (Flash) Quiz. If you do not start a new attempt there can be old navigation passed to Captivate from a previous attempt YET "Flash Events" continue driving other parts of the quiz in different areas of navigation. From the details you are providing this is what I believe is happening. Sound in Captivate is controlled by what is called the "Sound Class" (amongst others) and is not connected to the SCORM code (for the purposes of navigation) which is used for question navigation. Clicking on "Start new attempt" in Moodle should flush old navigation data and sync. your files. Let me know how you make out. Cheers, Wade

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to integrate a SCORM player in my web page
ResponsesInList.Text: What happens with the grade that the SCORM object returns? - does it go anywhere? - or are these SCORM objects read only? - is this "view" really a preview of the object to allow people to decide if they want to install it in their site? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Tracking Flash Quiz Template Used in HTML Pages
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Guys, Here are some pointers to making your flash quiz work! Firstly you will need to save your source file as Flash MX 2004 format! (Select this from the drop down menu in the save as dialog box. Dont do Ctrl + s after this as it will save as Flash 8 format!!!) Then, I trust you have imported accross from a quiz template the 'GlobalQuizClass' and the 'Quiz Options Movie Clip' and the navigation (mc, frameNav. Give this an instance name of nav. Then select the {Interaction Type} Interaction movie clip the one which holds the actionscript for the learning interaction of you choice and in there make sure the interaction_id's are all different in your quiz. I named mine interaction_01 - interaction_## . Then click the options button at the bottom of the page and set an objective_ID for each learning interaction I named mine from 1 - ## (however many questions there were in my quiz! Then we go to publish! Publish your quiz with SCORM 1.2 tracking and Flash Player 7!! Right now we need to create an XMLmanifest, I used the ReloadEditor works a treat! This is what you need to do: 1. Create a new ADL SCORM 1.2 package and point it to somewhere you'll find it again! I used the folder with the learning interaction in it! 2. Right click on organisations and add a new organisation (you can name this something else if you wish) 3. Then Drag you .html file with your flash file embeded in to that organisation you've just made! Don't be suprised is you get a '>' you can change this! NOTE: It automatically adds to the Resource list the file that are require for the SCORM package! 4. If you want to set a pass grade then right click on the file you dragged to the organisation and click ADL editSCORM. In the masteryScore just enter the percent you wish your students to pass at! This can be left blank, but your students will pass even if they only get 10%! Package it up and upload it to moodle as a scorm and that should be it! Hope this helps! If you need any more help dont hesitate to ask! I will try and post one of my examples up, although they are just exceed the 100KB limit! Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Scoring in Moodle 1.9.8
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I wonder if anyone else has noticed this problem. Hopefully, you'll understand what I'm describing. Since upgrading from 1.9.6 to 1.9.8, the scores sent to the grade book of the same SCORM LOs with the same settings (grading method = average /100) have changed. Now any page that is viewed inside a learning object whether it has a score attached to it or not is calculated in the average that is recorded in the grade book. For example, when there is a SCORM item with three pages - one html and two SCORM quizzes - the page without a score is given a zero when the average score is calculated. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scoring in Moodle 1.9.8
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jim, If you have a multiple-sco scorm package, then the gradebook score is indeed going to be an average of all sco numeric scores. (Average is for attempts, not for the SCOs themselves. The SCOs will always be averaged into a single number before going into the gradebook.) You need to add score reporting to your third SCO that isn't reporting a score... This could be as simple as setting score.raw to 100 when the page is viewed. -A

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Sharing big SCORM packages among different course
ResponsesInList.Text: The approach is similar to the one suggested by Dan some post before. It works under *Nix systems but not sure about Windows. We will suppose you have 2 moodle installations http://instance1.mysite.org http://instance2.mysite.org Considering the Linux filesystem on a server, usally the instances are under /var/www/instance1 /var/www/instance2 the moodle installation require also a moodle-data directory for each instance /var/data/instance1-moodledata /var/data/instance2-moodledata Now the solution : - Put all the scorm content in /var/data/scorm-repo - Create a ims manifest for eache instance You have to modify the manifest to point to absolute path on your site like that: In the resources section <resource identifier="CALORES-AED9DF67-E423-6A3F-5444-300634C52C38" adlcp:scormtype="sco" href="http://instance1.mysite.org/scorm-repo/sco1.html" type="webcontent"> - Create a symbolic link for eache instance. marco@work>cd /var/www/instance1 marco@work>ln -s /var/data/scorm-repo scorm-repo marco@work>cd /var/www/instance2 marco@work>ln -s /var/data/scorm-repo scorm-repo and the same content will be accessible from http://instance1.mysite.org/scorm-repo http://instance2.mysite.org/scorm-repo Hope my explanation are clear, and obviously I'm open to suggestion ciao M

ResponsesInList.Title: Presenting supplementary course material - can I use SCORM?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all We have developed a range of online language courses for teaching English (and Spanish) as a Foreign Language. Up until now we have been packaging these courses in SCORM 1.2 format to allow us to use them on a range of different learning platforms, including Moodle. However, our latest product is a searchable database of activities which allows teachers to pick and choose which activities they would like to use with their students. Currently it is implemented as a web interface to allow searching of the database, and the results returned are links to web pages. These web pages can save time spent, scores obtained, etc, and, to re-use the exercises types that we have already developed, use the SCORM API to communicate this information to the database. This works okay as a standalone web application but now we would like to be able to also make this available to learning platforms like Moodle. My question is, what are the options for making this searchable database of activites accessible via Moodle? While the results returned from the search use the SCORM API for communication, I don't think that it can be a SCORM package as such because there is no "imsmanifest. xml " file which SCORM packages require. Am I missing something in the way SCORM works, would it be possible to somehow make this available as a SCORM package? If not, does anyone have any suggestions on the best way to approach this integration? Has anyone else done anything else similar? Many thanks, Andy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Presenting supplementary course material - can I use SCORM?
ResponsesInList.Text: HI Andy, SCORM uses Javascript for it's communication and cross- domain communication is blocked by default in users browsers. so if your web app is hosted externally on a different domain/url then Moodle won't be able to communicate via Javascript to obtain grades etc. You could write your own Moodle module that interfaced with your web app or if you're using Flash you should check out Matt's SWF Activity module.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Presenting supplementary course material - can I use SCORM?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi and thanks for the plug Dan. The SWF Activity Module is ideal for Flash <-> DB integration. As a proof of concept I created some Flash learning applications where the learning interaction data is driven entirely by Moodle database tables. Although, in this case it is actually better to use XML : http://matbury.com/moodle/course/view.php?id=9 The project site is here: http://code.google.com/p/swf-activity-module/ It uses AMF3 (similar to JSON but many times faster and lighter) to pass data directly between the server and Flash apps. No Javascript is involved and so there's no issues with getting a Javascript wrapper and ExternalInterface to co-operate, which can be a major headache. Using the NetConnection and Responder classes you can hook up directly to the AMFPHP gateway and pass Actionscript and PHP objects back and forth as if they were the same language. Cool huh? All you have to do is develop a Flash app. and a corresponding PHP service script to do whatever you want to do with Moodle. Here's the standard service library, which includes services to access the grade book, users and groups, via Moodle's lib API and all obeying Moodle's user capabilities settings: http://code.google.com/p/swf-activity-module/source/browse/#svn/trunk/src/moodle/lib/amfphp/services I hope this helps!

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, I'm new to Moodle and SCORM. I've set up a LAMP Moodle test server and testing SCORM content created with Scate Ignite Pro 4. Without going into too much detail, the SCORM content is mostly working but I have an issue when using a full SCORM 'course' with multiple quizzes (at least I think that's where the problem lies - packages that only contain one quiz don't seem to be affected by this error). The output from the SCORM API shows the following error: SCORM API Activity Log Fri, 26 Feb 2010 15:45:05 UTC: LMSSetValue("cmi.core.score.raw", "97.1428571428571") => 405 Fri, 26 Feb 2010 15:45:05 UTC: LMSGetErrorString("405", "Incorrect data type") => 0 The cmi.core.score.raw value is below 100 but still returns an error. I'm now thinking that the problem is either the non-integer value and the size of the value after the decimal point OR that the value is being delivered as an integer (which it's not) when Moodle expects a string. The Ignite package is specced to SCORM 1.2 / 2004. Any advice would be greatly appreciated. Thanks in advance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: cmi.core.score.raw 405 error
ResponsesInList.Text: The 1.2 spec accepts decimal points but does not offer a limit i length. My guess is keep it to keep it to 2 spaces. 2004 wants the value normalized between -1 to 1.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: cmi.core.score.raw 405 error
ResponsesInList.Text: That's peculiar, as the score is stored in the 'value' column, which is a Long Blob data type - it should take pretty much any value you put in it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: cmi.core.score.raw 405 error
ResponsesInList.Text: I can replicate with 97.1428571428571. But LMSSetValue returns "true" when I round to 2 decimals. -A

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: cmi.core.score.raw 405 error
ResponsesInList.Text: SCORM 1.2 specification tells that cmi.core.score.raw is a CMIDecimal datatype. CMIDecimal means a number that may have a decimal point. If not preceded by a minus sign, the number is presumed to be positive. Examples are "2","2.2" and “-2.2) . You can find a nice chart representing SCORM 1.2 datamodel e datatypes here . Ciao, Matteo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: cmi.core.score.raw 405 error
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Amy, You previously replied to a post I made in the aforementioned thread. You stated 'I can replicate with 97.1428571428571. But LMSSetValue returns "true" when I round to 2 decimals.' Can you please explain how you rounded the output to two decimals? My content-generation app outputs its own 'RequiredAPICalls.js' file which contains the following reference: ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////// // // Title: setClassScore(args) // // Description: This function is used to set a class complete score. // ///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////// function setClassScore(args){ LMSSetValue("cmi.core.score.raw",args); LMSCommit(); } Should I be able to edit this file to round the raw score to two decimal places before sending it back to Moodle? Your advice would be greatly appreciated. Thanks, David
