ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM in Moodle / Object Reuse in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: object re-use is not something that's well supported in Moodle 1.9 SCORM objects are also hard to "re-use" - you can point to an externally hosted zip or manifest file, however if the manifest/unzipped package is hosted on a different site the SCORM Javascript API will fail. Moodle 2.0 has a new repository api that would allow you to have an external "repository" of Scorm objects (only zip files if on a different domain ) and you could re-use this object in many different courses as necessary. Unfortunately Tags are not supported on modules in 1.9 either - the global search might work on description/title of the scorm, but I don't think it searches the content inside a SCORM object.\ hope that helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Auto-Continue between SCORM Activities doesn't work
ResponsesInList.Text: This is a subject I have posted on before and there are related postings, but I can find no solutions. In short, I cannot get one SCORM Activity to Auto-Continue to the next, although I note others seem to have the opposite problem.  If the following is long-winded, my apologies, but I am trying to provide any information which might be relevant. The following are our Environment settings: Moodle Version  1.9.4+ (Build: 20090415) Name Information Report        Status moodle   version 1.0 is required and you are running 1.9.4  OK unicode   must be installed and enabled     OK database postgres version 8.0 is required and you are running 8.3.9  OK php  version  4.3.0 is required and you are running 5.2.6.1.6   OK php_extension iconv should be installed and enabled for best results  OK php_extension mbstring should be installed and enabled for best results OK php_extension curl should be installed and enabled for best results  OK php_extension openssl should be installed and enabled for best results  OK php_extension tokenizer should be installed and enabled for best results OK php_extension xmlrpc should be installed and enabled for best results  OK php_extension ctype should be installed and enabled for best results  OK I have an imminent need to do this from "scratch". I also have a large (100Mb) SCORM running successfully in Moodle, as an Activity in a Topic; if the required score is obtained in the SCORM, the student can access a Certificate Activity in the same Topic, but I cannot get it to Auto-Continue, so the student must select the Certificate Activity once permitted - not good. I am looking to divide it into smaller SCORM Activities that will Auto-Continue from one to the next, as seamlessly as possible, in order to improve performance, response times etc. The original SCORM was created in Captivate 4. With this latter requirement in mind, I have subdivided the course into individual Captivate courses and published a SCORM from the Introduction course and from the final Quiz course, to test the principle. There is no scoring in the Intro, but scoring is retained in the Quiz. These have been uploaded to a new test course, as Activities within a single topic, but, until recently, just complete and then return to the Content page in Moodle. Suddenly, for no reason I can identify, the Intro now attempts to Auto-Continue to the Quiz, but fails because it specifies its own directory (moodle/file.php/7/moddata/scorm/14/PCP_PPS_Module9_QuizAndExit.htm), rather than the Quiz directory (moodle/file.php/7/moddata/scorm/15/PCP_PPS_Module9_QuizAndExit.htm), i.e. SCORM Activity 14, rather than 15. In an effort to eliminate a series of adjustments as the cause of this, I created a new course, with exactly the same settings, using exactly the same SCORM zip files, to observe what happens.  This does not attempt to Auto-Continue, but just returns to the Moodle Content page. The SCORM settings in Moodle are as follows: Grading method Highest grade Maximum grade 100 I can find no explanation of what the "Close Communication Method" (Help on Auto-Continue YES/NO) means anywhere in Moodle or Captivate documentation or forums, or really anywhere else. I have no idea what to do next and would appreciate any guidance anyone can offer.  I have no knowledge of PHP but can call on limited assistance if necessary. If any further information or sample files would help, please do ask. Thanks in advance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm Rapitivity /Elicitius Lesson
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jalpa, You've got a couple of different issues going here. Sequencing Within SCORM SCORM 2004 is not completely supported in Moodle at this stage. Parts of the API have been implemented, but others such as Navigation and Sequencing have not yet been implemented. - http://docs.moodle.org/en/SCORM_FAQ#What_version_of_SCORM_is_supported.3F Sequencing of Moodle Activities in the Moodle Course With 1.9+, and no modifications to core, you cannot control sequencing of activities. You can daisy-chain several lesson modules, but you cannot include other activity types in the chain. There is a hack to core called Conditional Activities, which will do what you want. But it is a hack to core, and will restrict your ability to upgrade. There is also the Certificate Module, which is not going to do exactly what you want, but will require completion of a set list of activities with a set score before the learner can download the certificate. So those are your options. Best, A

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM grading + gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Cristian, You've got a bunch of different issues here. This is the weird part.....one package update correctly the grades, the other one, just copy the grades gained the first time that the students went in to the Scorm package, they completed the SCORM, but still the grade is the same. * How many attempts are you allowing? Change it to 1 attempt. * Have you disabled Review Mode? If not, you should. Then SCORM is setting up to upgrade every time its used, also, if i check the report about SCORM, it is updated, but not the grade into teh gradebook The "Auto-update frequency" setting is for updating the SCORM package itself, not the information reported from the SCORM package. The settings are documented here: http://docs.moodle.org/en/Adding/editing_a_SCORM Additional Questions *How did you create these SCORM packages? Were they created with a particular authorware product, or written from scratch? *Were both created the same way? SCORM to Gradebook There are 2 different values that can get into the gradebook, and which one goes to the gradebook depends on the settings. cmi.score.raw --> If your scorm package sets this value through the API, and your SCORM activity grading method is set to Highest Grade, and the number for the maximum is the maximum that your SCORM will set, then this value will be reflected in the gradebook. cmi.core.lesson_status --> If your scorm package is set to Learning Object, and there is only 1 SCO in your SCORM package, then a lesson_status of "completed" or "passed" is reflected as a 100 in the gradebook. A lesson_status of "incomplete" or "failed" is reflected as a "0". You can tell which values your scorm object is reporting to the LMS by looking at the SCORM reports, or by running the package through debugging. http://docs.moodle.org/en/SCORM_reports http://docs.moodle.org/en/SCORM_FAQ#Debugging_a_SCORM_Module

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm works - but no CSS or images
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Seaghan, I'm assuming you added the package as the SCORM activity type. Have you looked inside the package to be sure that the image files are there? If they all were given the same file name, and were stored in the same dir, that would be somewhat problematic, and the problem would not be with Moodle, so rule that out. Take a look at the imsmanifest.xml file. Every single one of those image files should be listed with a correct path as a child for your SCO node. If they aren't listed there, then Moodle will not unpack those image files into /moddata/scorm/ with the rest of the content. The good news is that republishing the package, or manually adding the paths to the manifest, will solve this problem. Best of luck, A

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enabling SCORM activity time track report for Student access

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Flash Scorm and Questions
ResponsesInList.Text: If it's in a Moodle DB table, then you'll need to write a PHP query, and call the query from Flash. PHP can extract data from the tables, but a swf can't, for security reasons. Another thing you could do is keep the info in an xml file, or store it as a string of xml in a text file. But you need to be careful where you store that file, so it's not accessible on the Web. Don't keep it in public_html, and don't keep it in moodledata/1/. Even then, I don't think you can add nodes or delete nodes from an xml file with just Flash. You'd still need a PHP intermediary. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Flash Scorm and Questions
ResponsesInList.Text: You need to keep in mind what data the sco can read/write from the LMS via the SCORM standard vs what data is in the full moodle DB tables. SCORM does not deal with all data in an LMS DB. I'd use the interactions in the cmi object to store the individual questions. Then you can write a new report to pull that info. I think out of the box you can only see one students scorm data at time so the custom report would allow you to aggregate that data. As for getting custom user profile data in to the flash/sco you'll need to write a custom php process that your flash file can call as amy said.This is due to the SCORM standard not offering any place for that type of data in standard. Or I should say Moodle is not setup to do it as there is a value called cmi.launch_data that could be used to have moodle process the data you want and make it available on launch. You could look at writing a mod or hiring someone to do it for you. That value is supposed to be pulled from the imsmanifest.xml and would usually not be unique per launch but if your not planning to use the course on other LMS's and you control the moodle install you could bend the SCORM rules. This is not really any different than what Amy suggested Except that the bending of SCORm rules would happen on the LMS side vs having a sco call a LMS specific php DB query. Your sco would be more potable then as you could write an actionscript that looks to launch_data and if there is data use it and if not handle things differently.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Flash Scorm and Questions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Eric, This forum http://www.dynamicdrive.com/forums/showthread.php?t=14165 contains some examples. Keep in mind, though that there's no need to parse or read the XML using PHP. You can load and parse the XML just fine with Flash. What you need from PHP is *only* the write part. When you need to modify the XML file, you need to call a PHP query that will rewrite the XML in the way that you want. That's how I would do it, anyway. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Flash Scorm and Questions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Eric, If I can make another suggestion I would avoid fscommand() and instead use external interface class in Flash. This may also be part of the problem you are encountering. The fscommand is considered a rather old fashioned way to implement SCORM in Flash (under Actionscript 2.0) and is rather "sloppy" at that. While it should generally work under Windows XP & Vista it may not under other environments (eg: Mac & Linux, Windows 7??) and can return some rather unusual messages and data types. The External Interface class is considered current best practise. Eg: import flash.external.*; var EI_available:Boolean = ExternalInterface.available etc... You then usually develop "setter" and "getter" functions with the external interface class to access the commands within your class.

ResponsesInList.Title: IMS vs. SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everyone! I'd like to understand what are the differences between SCORM and IMS CP. As far as I can see SCORM uses IMS, but usually content can be exported (in eXe or other tools) as SCORM or IMS. It would mean SCORM is the same as IMS and have additional features? Thanks for help!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: IMS vs. SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mand, Here is my understanding of such things. IMS is simply a method of packaging content for web based learning management systems that uses Metadata to pass information to its resources. It was developed by the IMS Global group and was the original way to do things in LMS systems like Moodle. SCORM was an attempt (in the U.S. by the military I believe) to define a "standard" way of doing this so that packaged content would work on any LMS (or could be shared on any LMS) that followed the standard. SCORM adopted the work started by IMS Global and integrated it into the SCORM standard. Thus the reason the two look almost identical, althought "under the hood" this is not always the case. In terms of Moodle I do not believe IMS passes information to the grade book where as SCORM has a consistent and standard way of doing this (in theory ) so is used for that purpose (although I could stand to be corrected on this).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: IMS vs. SCORM

I don't believe it would function properly if you did (ie: Return results, etc.) Having said that I' have never tried this and could certainly be corrected on this point. The "Add an Activity Block" must have SCORM (or other compatible format) for the results to be returned correctly and recorded in the LMS & Grade Book. As of now Moodle has only been certified for SCORM 1.2 (unless this has recently changed). Perhaps one of the core developers in this forum here could provide some more insight here. Cheers, Wade

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Upload Max File Size
ResponsesInList.Text: We had the same problem, initially. You need to contact who ever is hosting your moodle site and have them change the file size limit for the server. A quick way to check this size is to go to "your_moodle_site/admin/phpinfo.php". Take note that your php.ini file is at the location shown in the "Loaded Configuration File" box. It's probably something like /etc/php5/apache2/php.ini or some variation of that based on your server installation. Scroll down to the Configuration section and near the bottom of that section is a variable called "max_upload_filesize". The value of that is your current limit. Also, go to "your_moodle_site/admin/settings.php?section=sitepolicies" and check that the drop-down menu for the maximum uploaded file size is set to the "Server Limit" or the largest file size you can choose. If your choices aren't large enough in that drop-down menu, then you have to open your php.ini file and change the values for the post_max_size AND upload_max_filesize AND the Apache setting, Limit RequestBody. Your server admin can make the changes to this file. If you're hosting your self you should be able to find the file pretty easily by going to the php info page listed at the top of this post. Hope that helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Captivate, Moodle, grading book issues...
ResponsesInList.Text: An attempt is when you execute LMSFinish and the exit value does not equal "suspend". That denotes to the lms that the user will not return. Your confusing sessions in an attempt of a sco with number of attempts of a sco. So as long as your sco's are configured to keep the sco attempt in suspend (until it decides the user is done) when a user leaves then on re-entry the cmi data will be pushed to the client.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cache issue: On Updating the scorm zip file, still plays the old one,
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Garima, I can see your problem: you can't ask users to go through complicated cache clearing tasks if you update a SCORM package that they've already downloaded once. This is true of Flash apps in general. There are suggested solutions of including "nocache" code and such on the web page in question but I haven't found one that works all the time in the most popular browser yet. The typical solution is to add a query string to the end of the file(s) in question. Something like: http://mymoodle.com/path/to/swf/app.swf?20090827164730 You can define the query string as anything you like; serial number, date and time, names of your favourite pop stars, etc. but the ? is necessary. You can also use it for updating any files like XML , JPEG, etc. However, while testing this may return an error in your Flash authoring IDE so it gets difficult and fiddly to keep changing it between testing on the IDE and on-line. Rest assured that once you've uploaded it with the query string it'll work as expected. I've built this function into the SWF Activity Module if you want to have a look at the code: http://code.google.com/p/moodle-swf/ AFAIK , SCORM won't let you automatically generate the query string you need (you need PHP from the back end to do that), so you'll have to update it manually each time you upload and test. Perhaps you could include some JavaScript to tag a random query string on each time it loads. The SCORM module really should have something like this built in. I don't have much experience of using SCORM in Moodle so perhaps one of the core developers can tell you if this is the case or not.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Garima, This is one of the most frustrating things about working with browsers as you have found. Can you provide the following information: What software are you using to create your SCORM course? How many files make up the course? How often do you have to update the course? How much control do you have of the computers that are being used to access the course? Ron

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cache issue: On Updating the scorm zip file, still plays the old one,
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Garima, "I tried to add extra query string after the URL, but it also didn't worked." Where did you add the query strings? As far as browsers are concerned every file can be cached so for each file that gets downloaded in a package, you have to add a query string to it. Even if you rename the SCORM zip file, it's still possible that the browser will use the previously cached files. It depends on how the SCORM module handles the unzipping process. Like I said, it's a pain to have to do this manually and it really should be taken care of by the SCORM module.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Showing "Complete" in Gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dave, Having the gradebook show the text "completed" might be tricky. There is the option of changing the grading method for the scorm objects to "Learning object." This records a 1 for a lesson_status of "completed" or "passed", and a 0 for "incomplete" or "failed". This translates into the Moodle gradebook as either a 100 or a 0. The lesson_status of "completed" is displayed in the SCORM reports, but it is 3 screens deep, and only shows 1 learner at a time. You may also want to run this past the gradebook wonks. I have never heard of being able to modify the gradebook result view in that way without custom code, but there might be a way. Best of luck, A

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Saving a button press / click in Flash as3 / SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text:
If you're using the pipwerks wrapper, it is very well documented, and you can look over the code and see what's being done by each function. What you need to do is call your wrapper's setValue function and set the correct parameter. In the pipwerks JS wrapper, this would be the 
```text
 



pipwerks.SCORM.data.set = function(parameter, value){}
```
 which checks for the SCORM version, then sends the data to the LMS in the correct format. So if you're using the pipwerks JS wrapper *and* the pipwerks AS library, then from your AS, you need to call: 
```text
 



myReturnVal = scorm.set("cmi.interactions.n.student_response", "respString");
```
 It's a good idea to check the return value for "true" before moving on in the user experience. You probably want to set cmi.interactions.n.type to the correct type of interaction before you set the value. You can also use cmi.interactions.n.result to denote whether the learner gave the correct or incorrect answer. Be sure to call the commit function when you finish setting your values. I've placed a very simple sample by Aaron Silvers in the repository. Note that this is a more primitive wrapper by ADL, that does not include error checking, so the pipwerks wrapper is better. But this will show you the basic concept. http://moodle.org/mod/data/view.php?d=50&rid=3554

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Saving a button press / click in Flash as3 / SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, As per your email question, this is really, really oversimplified but try this with the pipwerks wrapper: import fl.controls.Button; // assumumes you are using the components imports import flash.events.MouseEvent; import pipwerks.SCORM; // class file to track SCORM information var lessonStatus:String; // checks the status of lesson complete or not complete var lmsConnected:Boolean; // checks if LMS is available returns true is there is LMS available var success:Boolean; // Hold value to tell if LMS is active var scorm:SCORM = new SCORM(); test_btn.addEventListener(MouseEvent.CLICK, scormFinish) lmsConnected = scorm.connect(); // tries to connect to SCORM and returns true if it does if(lmsConnected) // if it is connected (true) { lessonStatus = scorm.get("cmi.core.lesson_status"); // gets the current status of the lesspm if(lessonStatus == "completed") // is the lesson is already complete { scorm.disconnect(); //Course has already been completed. // disconnect from the system } else { success = scorm.set("cmi.core.lesson_status", "incomplete"); // else set the lesson to incomplete //Must tell LMS course has not been completed yet. } } else { trace("Could not connect to LMS."); // returns a message if lmsConnected is false (not connected) } function scormFinish (event:MouseEvent): void // used to finish upon a mouse click { success = scorm.set("cmi.core.score.raw", "5") //raw score success = scorm.set("cmi.core.score.max", "10") // total score success = scorm.set("cmi.core.score.min", "0"); // min score success = scorm.set("cmi.core.lesson_status", "completed");// sets the project as having been compelted scorm.disconnect(); // disconnects from the system lmsConnected = false; // sets lmsConnected to false } The comments should help you work your way through it. This assumes you have created a button with the instance name of test_btn to save your work. Sticking to this naming convention should provide you with code hinting to help add your event listeners. The numbers 5 ,10 & 0 could be replaced with variables that would be impacted by the actions of the users in the true - false interaction. Let me know how you make out. Wade

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Saving a button press / click in Flash as3 / SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, The Pipwerks SCORM.as class is a really handy way to custom build SCORM enabled Flash learning applications which can reduce the size of SCORM packages, as compared to authorware packages, and therefore server costs (bandwidth and storage) significantly, i.e. a few KBs compared to 10s or 100s of MBs. Re. this line: import pipwerks.SCORM; This is incorrect. It should be com.pipwerks.SCORM; I had a look at the downloads on http://pipwerks.com/downloads/ and they haven't included the all important /com/ directory in their packages. As an experienced Flash developer, I can't stress how important this is. The standard convention for ActionScript class libraries is the developer's site URL . For example, if Moodle released an AS class library, the class path would be something like: org.moodle.MoodleClass, meaning that when you download the class package, you get something like /org/moodle/MoodleClass.as This is so that the class path is guaranteed to be unique, since it's based on a unique path on the web. There are currently hundreds of AS developers distributing open source class libraries at the moment (I recommend checking them out on http://code.google.com/hosting/search?q=label:actionscript&filter=0&start=20 ) and this is set to increase dramatically in the not too distant future. If developers don't follow this convention, it'll create a huge headache and loads of recompiling whenever a class path conflict occurs.

ResponsesInList.Title: An up-and-coming possible alternative to SCORM for Moodle...
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, I'm just promoting something that may be of interest to people who'd like to use Flash with Moodle. If you'd like to avoid the rather steep learning curve and problematic nature of SCORM, there'll soon be an alternative available for Moodle 1.9. SCORM uses Actionscript's ExternalInterface.call() function, a Javascript wrapper and JSON to send quiz results and user tracking data, which is pretty much one-way communication, to Moodle's SCORM API. There's a lot that can go wrong with this chain of events as this forum bears testimony to! The SWF Activity Module uses an entirely different protocol with is many times faster and lighter, easier to implement and provides powerful, efficient and reliable two-way communication directly between Flash and Moodle using Actionscript's NetConnection.call() function. There will be no need for XML manifests or ZIP packages, learning interactions can be edited and updated as you would any other web content, i.e. editing media files, Flash files and any lesson files in their directories in the course files directory. We spend our time in this forum mostly helping people to solve problems with their authoring software, and not with custom SCORM content. The challenge with supporting SCORM isn't that you can't make SCORM work in its current supported version (you can, and very well), but that customers don't want to pay for the kind of custom Flash programming required to produce quality Flash content, either as SCORM or using your SWF activity module. Instead, they go with Captivate, Articulate, or another such product, each of which has its own snafoos, and is not as easy to debug/modify as an FLA file. I also, personally, would rather get my customers off of Flash altogether. Flash gets a lot of lip service, because it's become a corporate buzzword, but Flash development, with a development team larger than 1, is restrictive and expensive. Powerful JavaScript libraries like jQuery, along with the impending arrival of HTML5, are way more exciting to me than another way of putting customer content into a proprietary format. Ideally, I would build interactions right into existing Moodle activity modules, taking full advantage of all the social constructivist tools available in the Moodle interface, and I would not have to use a proprietary language or file format to create those interactions. If there were a way for me to report data from *that* sort of interaction, now *that* would be awesome, and a boon for the whole community. My two cents, A

The same can be done with Flash, utilizing XML, say, but it's not nearly as flexible, and can't be modified via CSS . Most eLearning content does not utilize the technologies you list, Ethan. For simple interactivity, JavaScript and Moodle's multimedia plugins will suffice. It's better to build on Moodle than tie Moodle to (partially) proprietary solutions. At least, that's what I prefer to offer customers, content they won't need to either hire me back or buy expensive software to modify. A

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: An up-and-coming possible alternative to SCORM for Moodle...
ResponsesInList.Text: @Ethan Thanks for clarifying those points about Flash. @Amy, re. custom development, your assertions don't take a few factors into account: #1 There are a lot more Flash developers than there are SCORM specialists and there are even developer marketplaces, e.g. rentacoder.com, that allow clients to post their requirements and have coders, who have ratings from previous clients, bid for them. So for custom development, clients have a much wider selection to choose from. #2 There are a lot of open source Flash projects already out there that would be very useful to e-learning. Customising those would be very easy and very cheap. #3 If the SWF Activity Module catches on, then there'll be a strong motivation for communities to share resources and create common libraries and marketplaces for Flash applications that run on it. There's a strong case to support the idea that it's better for a talented developer to create a new application based on a good idea and develop it over a period of time with feedback from a wide range of users than for individual learning content providers to commission separate, private projects. I think this model has worked quite well for Moodle, Open Office, MySQL , Apache , Wordpress, Joomla, Actionscript, etc. so far. #4 Re: authorware, I'm currently investigating to possibility of adding a "widget" to Adobe Captivate so that learning interactions authored with Captivate can be deployed directly in Moodle and record user data with the SWF Activity Module (Captivate 4 no longer splits its recordings into multiple files). This may also be possible for other authorware packages. See: http://www.adobe.com/cfusion/exchange/index.cfm?s=5&from=1&o=desc&cat=288&l=-1&event=productHome&exc=22 Re. CSS, Flash provides support for external CSS files. Also, with flash.system.Capabilities, you can get very specific information about the computer hardware and OS that a Flash application is running on such as screen size, CPU type and power, memory size, etc. and adjust a learning interaction accordingly. You can also relay that data back to Moodle for valuable user statistics for future development, e.g. the optimal video CODECs and pixel dimensions to use, instead of trying to guess and then waiting for the messages from irate learners who's browsers are crashing from media overload. The Eurpean Union is backing an LMS with an entirely Flash based front end for foreign language learning ( http://babbel.com/ ), EFL/ESL publishing giant Pearson Longman is backing an LMS which is heavily dependent on Flash ( http://livemocha.com/ ), the largest university press in the world, Oxford, has gone the Flash route ( http://oup.com/elt/englishfile/ ), including their CD-ROMs and most other proprietary LMS's use Flash extensively. In particular, OUP has says this about SCORM on its marketing website: "Despite some international standards aimed to facilitate the sharing of content between VLEs, content is not recognised and organised in exactly the same way by each VLE. In order to provide content which requires as little tweaking as possible to get it into each VLE, OUP has packaged the files for some of the most popular versions of VLEs." - http://www.oup.com/uk/orc/learnvle/#Why I've just published a blog article about the developer preview: http://matbury.com/wordpress/2010/02/11/moodle-swf-activity-module-developer-preview/ Again, comments are welcome. Matt

(from CourseLab Support) If these FireFox/Image display problems are not an issue then be sure to install the latest browser plug-ins. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM and 3D!!!!
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, it really comes down to how you configured it. If in the manifest you defined a resource with an external href then technically your good. An LMS will read the manifest when the user clicks that particular sco/asset in the toc and call the url. If it's an asset then no communication will occur back to the lms via an api. If it's defined as a sco then your SL objects are expected to find and initialize via the api object that the LMS deploys to the dom of the browser. I've seen where some courses have a local html file that is defined in the manifest that has it's own code that calls external assets. Technically that goes against the spirit of SCORM as the goal is to have any assets needed for the course to be defined in the manifest so the course is portable between LMSs. When links are buried in the code it makes it difficult to say set up permissions for a new LMS to access content remotely. Again this is mostly spirit type stuff. An lms will not stop it unless say an IT dept has put a block on certain sites or a proxy is used to trottle access etc.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grades not showing
ResponsesInList.Text: Jun, Check your grade book settings. I use Articulate all the time and your settings are correct for the Scorm activity. Under the Scorm/AICC activities is there attempt being recorded. The values that will be displayed in the grade book should be either a 0 or 1 for complete and incomplete. I just posted a quiz to my dev site and with your settings and everything is reporting properly. I would double check your grade book setting and make sure that you are not using a scale. Articulate will not report back complete or incomplete to Moodle just a numeric value.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm showing as incomplete
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Amy, I've run the package with debugging, and the setValue function appears to have run properly: Wed, 25 Nov 2009 16:54:34 GMT: LMSSetValue("cmi.core.lesson_status", "completed") => 0 Wed, 25 Nov 2009 16:54:36 GMT: Commit("", "") => 0 The incomplete reports occur infrequently and seemingly randomly, which may explain why the setValue function ran correctly above. Approx 5% of users complete the scorm, only their grade still reflects an incomplete (0.0 as a Learning Object). The incomplete reports have also occurred over a few different scorm activities contained in the course - in other words, the issue is not limited to a specific scorm activity. The content was created with Adobe Presenter 7, published under scorm 1.2, and most users (including the ones experiencing the problem) are using Windows XP and Internet Explorer - I don't have the specific version. The scorm contains a flash generated certificate that has been working properly. In fact that is how we discovered the issue - users were providing certificates, but Moodle had no record of their completion. We have investigated and determined that the certificates are legitimate and not faked. Typical settings for the scorm are: Grading Method: Learning Objects Number of Attemps: Unlimited Attempts Grading: Highest Attempt Skip Student Content Structure: Always Disable preview mode: Yes Course Structure Display: Hidden One other piece of information that we have found valuable is that the only common thread between the affected users is within the flash certificate. The certificate is designed to pull the user's name and info from Moodle. In the event Moodle returns an invalid or null user name, the user is prompted to enter their name for the certificate. In all of the affected users so far, they have been prompted to type in their name. Guest access is disabled, so the users have to login to even have access to the course. With a few exceptions (we had self-registration available for a short time), all users accounts (>1500 of them) were uploaded and created manually. I currently do not have a way to get the scorm into the repository - the scorm is over 500kb and I don't have access to an FTP site or other site to link to. I'll find some way to provide access to anyone who wants it. I've attached the API Activity log. Thanks for all your help! -Coby

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm showing as incomplete
ResponsesInList.Text: Coby, sounds like you have intermittent connectivity. Do you run periodic commits and have some kind of alert if the api returns an error? You should have some notice in the runtime when communication to the api and the api to lms communication fail. That way users do not continue to work in a session that has some issue. I'd look at if the logs show any kind of high latency when these users took the course. Could be they are connected when the sco first loads but the connection drops in the middle and your not vetting if the commit is successful at the end (assuming no commits in the middle of the sco).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm showing as incomplete
ResponsesInList.Text: "What Ethan said." Something is happening that causes the API to be dropped, such that the SCO to no longer knows who the user is when the certificate is presented. I had another customer with a similar issue, basically, the API was not kept open because the SCORM object did not make frequent calls to the LMS. Ideally, there should be communication every time the use interacts with the SCORM object in some way, a click, a screen change, whatever. The customer added a JavaScript timer to the package's wrapper, that called doLMSCommit() at regular intervals. That fixed the problem. But when I look at your posted log, it looks like this is happening just fine. So we know that your SCORM object is capable of functioning properly, and that Moodle is receiving the data correctly in most cases. You probably also want to find out what the operating conditions are for the users having this problem. Are there any patterns, with regard to OS/browser/Flash player/network/physical location? You need to be able to replicate the issue yourself before you can really troubleshoot it and isolate the cause. You want the API Interactions log from when you are actually able to replicate the issue. But you may be, as Ethan said, headed for a discovery that the user's connection was dropped and the API lost. In that case, the user should get an error message, and not be allowed to continue, especially not for 20 minutes or an hour, and get a certificate. If that's happening, then you may want to try to add some JS to the SCORM object wrapper to force an LMSFinish() in the event that the API is lost. The user might be bewildered, but at least when they go back to the course, their progress to that point will have been saved, and there will be a record of the certificate they do earn. Best, A

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm showing as incomplete
ResponsesInList.Text: Heather, I'll say this. My biggest expenditure of debugging client problems ends up directly connected to latency issues on their network and/or the lms vendors network. Many LMS's in my view expect a high bandwidth connection at all times which does not happen. Many shrink wrap apps expect that too. IE : do they show an error when the api returns an error code because the lms never responded to the commit call? or do they expect it to work everytime. Etc. Might be worth getting IT involved to get a sense of load and latency i the elearning setup your running.

ResponsesInList.Title: Ang: Re: Scorm showing as incomplete
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there, I had allmost the same problems with grades not being registered in moodle, it would say incomplete and give a score of 0, even tho the user had completed the course and gotten a score of say 80.. The reason i found was because i had not given the SCORM lesson a unique identifier, and it was tracking from another lesson that was not active. When you publish a couse in articulate, you can access the Reporting and Tracking option. under there make sure the couse have unique values under the identifiers. Hope this solves your problems. regards Marcel Huss-Nielsen

ResponsesInList.Title: Ang: Invalid Course ID error
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rhonda, I will try and explain the cause and solution to your problem. The reason Moodle is giving you the error "invalid course id" can come from 2 sources. (both are Articulate related) 1.) when you publish a SCORM lesson from powerpoint using Articulate, you need to make sure under the "Reporting and tracking" option that the Identifier under "LMS Lesson SCORM Information" got a unique value, if you make 2 courses with same identifier values the LMS cant sort out the scores. 2.) When you edit or make a quiz using the Articulate Quizmaker Quiz tool you can define what action the system will take when a user finishes a course and presses the "finish" button. Setting this to "Goes to URL " and specifying an URL that is invalid/dead/non exsistant moodle will report an error - this can perhaps also mess up moodle's score tracking. I had the same problems as you did, and solved them doing the above. Let me know if you make it work.

ResponsesInList.Title: Return from SCORM to the main 'topic outline'
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I've got a question about using a SCORM package in Moodle and I wonder if someone could advise what the best solution would be. I've uploaded a SCORM package to Moodle. From the Topics Outline view (the main course view) I click on my SCORM package link. It takes me to a new Moodle screen where I can have a text description of the course and there is an "Enter" button at the bottom. Click the Enter button and the SCORM package opens in a completely new separate window. When you have finished the SCORM course or if you close the window, you are returned to Moodle. The Moodle screen you are returned to just has the name of the SCORM package to the left. The rest of the screen is blank. There are no obvious buttons to return you to the Topics Outline (the logical place you'd expect to be returned to). The only way to get back gracefully seems to be to click on the breadcrumbs. Realistically it is likely a user will either click the Back button on the browser or they will close the Moodle window thinking that the Topics Outline window will be behind it. Of course it isn't and they will have to restart Moodle - rather annoying! After starting the SCORM package, on returning from it to Moodle, how can the user be returned directly to the Topics Outline page? Any help would be appreciated as it's currently not very user friendly. Michael

ResponsesInList.Title: FLASH Alternatives to SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: After weeks of struggling to get FLASH to present our course module consistently across IE , Firefox and Safari we were ready to bring in outside help. We were fortunate enough to discover Jonathan Rand at Lamda Solutions.net They were familiar with our problem. Amazingly, they told us how to fix it for free. They also offered to do the work, should we not want to pursue things anymore. The solution was a dismantling of our course so that we could separate the FLASH module into a stand alone activity. We then wrote our test questions in Moodle's Quiz section and used the Certificate Component to finish things off. Ultimately, this may be a better solution for us because it gives it much more flexibility in the testing section. So, to the next pilgrim who discovers this idea via Google searches, "All hope abandon, ye who enter SCORM." Instead, break it apart.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: cmi.core.total_time not set in Flash-Scorm1.2-package
ResponsesInList.Text: Total_time is read only. You need to set session_time with your value and then the LMS will add that value to total_time for the next session of the same attempt. That process only occurs once an LMSFinish occurs since multiple session_time calls in te same session will over write themselves. So you need keep a time tracker for the whole session and at the end pass it up. LMSSetValue("cmi.core.session_time", "0000:00:11.0") => 0 LMSSetValue("cmi.core.session_time", "0000:00:11.0") => 0 will not get total_time to 22 seconds.

ResponsesInList.Title: Ang: Re: cmi.core.total_time not set in Flash-Scorm1.2-package
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ethan Thanx for the answer. I know total_time is read only, and I only use the getValue in my code. I have indeed a time tracker. I use it to set the session_time every time they finish a question - there is 25... - so as you say, I set the session_time multiple times in the same sesssion. Maybe I can't do that? Can I only set session_time once in a session? Ole

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ang: Re: cmi.core.total_time not set in Flash-Scorm1.2-package
ResponsesInList.Text: No , you can set it multiple times but the LMS will overwrite it each time within a session so you'll only have the last value sent stored. Then when you execute LMSFinish the lms is supposed to add that session time to total time (and zero out session time) so it's available to you on the next session. I've seen some lms's that don't do it until the next session initialize which is wrong. So from your trace you won't see total time change from 0 until AFTER you fire LMSFinish for the session and then launch the sco again. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm, Moodle and relative addressing in HTML docs
ResponsesInList.Text: It is my understanding that, while relative links work "pretty well" most of the time, they break during backup/restore, which is the reason we are warned against using them (e.g., see this discussion ). This seems to be a purely technical, rather than a fundamental problem, and it is surprising that the problem--which creates such an inconvenience for so many users--has not been fixed by now. By the way, Moodle knows its absolute address: $CFG-> wwwroot . I just think it gets amnesia during backup/restore But AFAIK , relative links should work fine within a SCORM package, exactly the same way that they work on the Web. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm, Moodle and relative addressing in HTML docs
ResponsesInList.Text: OK. If you are running Apache the Admin > Server > HTTP > Use Slash Arguments setting should probably be ticked. I have one Moodle box running on Windows 2003 with Apache 2.2 and that's how it's set up. Just out of interest. Let's try a little test. Set up a dummy course in each of your Moodle installations for testing. Create a folder in the course Files area for that course, then upload the attached jstest.zip file to the folder and unzip it there. This zip has a single HTM file and a single js file.  The HTM file calls the JS file as a linked file when it loads. Point a topic in your dummy course at the HTM file and try to play it. It should give you a web page that says Hello World!. It's actually a function inside the js file that writes the code into the HTM file. If the HTM file can find the JS file, everything works. If you don't see anything written to the page, or you get a Javascript error saying the "object was not found" (meaning the function couldn't be loaded because the browser couldn't find the js file) then try toggling slash arguments and trying again. In practice, on Apache, this file should work with slash arguments switched on. Does it work for you? If so, we'll move on to other stuff. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grades not always recording properly (SCORM with Captivate)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Tim, First, it's a very good idea for you to upgrade to 1.9.4+. The SCORM support is much better in the versions since 1.9.3. Second, it sounds like you might have a buggy SCORM package, and there's nothing that can be done in Moodle to address that. Third, if lesson_status is set to "failed," instead of "completed," or "passed," that is significant. The interactions data is not used by Moodle to report back the score. It depends on what your scorm settings are, and I can't speak for your version, but usually Moodle uses *either* score.max vs. score.raw to determine a percent score, or moodle uses lesson_status to give either a 0 or a 1 score (0 for not completed or failed, 1 for completed or passed). Best of luck, Amy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grades not always recording properly (SCORM with Captivate)
ResponsesInList.Text: I am familiar with the error you are talking about and it should be quite easy to fix. The reason Captivate usually returns this error has to do with how the quiz pool manager holds the questions and how the random question pool generator picks and assigns values to those questions. You can assign "points" to questions in three places 1.within the question generators 2. in the random question picker and 3. in Moodle itself.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: FLASH acting spooky in SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi John, While JavaScript is based on ECMA Script standards, Firefox and IE do implement it slightly differently. There could be a whole variety of reasons your system is hanging not necessarily based on your SWF Object. If you believe that it really is the SWF Object, a couple of questions: 1. What version of FLASH are you running ? Is this Actionscript 2 or 3 ? Do you have this information or are you using a file ? 2. How was the HTML file generated ? Was it done at the time the file was created or later ? Did it include SCORM support for the correct version (1.1, 1.2,etc.) and is Flash version checking enabled ? 3. By hanging are you talking about a "freeze" or sitting with a bank screen (often an unimplemented trap of some time). Have you tried this file on another LMS other than Moodle to make sure it is not Moodle specific. (eg: Test track ?) These factors are rather important to know as Adobe dropped and changed some key support pieces for SCORM after Flash 8. In addition, the implementation of calls to an external interface has changed between version 9 & 10 of Flash and this can cause some really "weird" erratic behavior. These things could also be a factors. If you do have the source code you may wish to take a look at the pipwerks site. This is one of the best at helping with the implementation of SCORM with Flash and there are files you can download (including a HTML Template that is better than the SCORM one generated by Flash). You could then do a clean re-compile with some tested code inserts. If you have a compiled sfw you may wish to look at the article Preparing your website to handle the Microsoft changes to Internet Explorer by Adobe at http://www.adobe.com/devnet/activecontent/articles/devletter.html . If you can give me more details on 1 -3 above I may have some more specific suggestions. W.Gemmell

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi John, I believe that the API is established by the SCORM object, not by Moodle. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM timing out on Flash
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi John, What you are trying to do can be accomplished in your Flash Code. What you need to do is: 1. Load your file first (with a URLRequest and Sound data structures) 2. Enable an event handler that listens for an Event.COMPLETE then... 3. Executes a function that initializes your LMS in this case Moodle after your resources have been loaded The order in which the code loads is quite significant as you MUST ensure your sound is loaded below (thus before) your Event.Complete. I am assuming you are using AS3.0 and Flash compiler is set to default (bottom up read of code)Your code should look something like this: var sound:Sound = new Sound(); sound.addEventListener(Event.COMPLETE, dataLoaded); sound.load (new URLRequest("myFile.mp3"); ..... function dataLoaded (loadevent:Event): void { lmsConnected = scorm.connect(); // connect to SCORM and returns true if it does .... } While this is way over simplified (eg: no channel classes for sound,etc.) the order of the load is important before initializing the LMS. If you are using multiple mp3 file you may need to take care of some memory management by removingChild elements from the Sound after it has played. You can also use a pre-loader with a byte count to accomplish the same thing. There is also some compatibilities issues with IE 8 and Moodle. You may wish to put IE in compatibility mode if you are using version 8. Hope that helps. W.Gemmell Open Source Educational Software Developer

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Help on using fscommand() fucntion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dodo The fscommand is considered a rather old fashioned way to implement SCORM in Flash (under Actionscript 2.0) and is rather "sloppy" at that. While it should generally work under Windows XP & Vista it may not under other environments (eg: Mac & Linux, Windows 7??) and can return some rather unusual messages. I suspect this is the root of your problem. When I implement my SCORM in Flash I use the External Interface class which is considered current best practise. eg: import flash.external.*; var EI_available:Boolean = ExternalInterface.available etc... You then usually develop "setter" and "getter" functions with the external interface class to access the commands within your class eg(as per your example): success = scorm.set("cmi.core.score.raw", num) //set raw score variable Not sure how much effort you want to put into this file but you may want to edit your code or tie into a 3rd party library to make some changes. For AS2.0 there is D.Marsden's code at the Flash and Math Website and for AS3.0 there is Philip Hutchison's code at pipwerks. Hutchison's code also included the API wrapper, imsmanifest file and html header file with modification instructions. Hope that helps. W. Gemmell Open Source Educational Software Developer

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Help picking a scorm tool.
ResponsesInList.Text: Ben, your link goes to a custom Flash SWF, probably created/sponsored by the text book company. You're not going to get anywhere close to that without an illustrator and ActionScript programmer on staff. If those people happen to be you, then the sky's the limit. I handle all of the SCORM support issues that come through for our partner, and the majority of the unsolvable issues, the ones where I have to say, "I'm sorry, the SCO just isn't doing what it should be doing and I can't help you without modifying it," are SumTotal and Lectora. Rule of thumb: Anything that only runs on 1 browser(ie. Explo[d]er)==bad. Articulate is ok to support, in my experience. As a developer, however, I have moved my team off of Articulate and onto Captivate. As Ethan writes, there is far more interactivity, true interactivity, available in Captivate, it will import PPT if that's the way you work, but it doesn't piggypack on MS Office as a requirement. That means it's $400 cheaper! And even without the cost of MS Office, it's half the price of Articulate! I don't know why Articulate is so popular, except that maybe it's seen as a silver bullet by corporate management types who think that you take a PPT and add voiceover and there you have a wonderful eLearning experience. The truth is that if it's a good PPT presentation, it will probably make an awful online course content base, because we intentionally leave details out of a PPT slide so that it serves only as a framework for the presenter. The interactivity templates in Articulate Engage are mostly useless, in my opinion, because they teach the learner nothing about the content. What the learner is actually learning is how to interact with the 5 or 6 stock interaction templates in Engage so as to move on to the next slide and get through the boring corporate training. Captivate, by comparison, provides interactivity that actually allows you to provide the leaner relevant feedback and enhance learning, with clickboxes, mouseovers, hidden prompts, screencasts, and so forth. If you want something truly original, however, Captivate isn't going to cut it either. You need to pay the experts, or become one. If you can get ahold of the Flash IDE, then it will be much easier to learn, and you'll be able to do much more without a lot of knowledge. You can also use the Flex SDK to compile ActionScript files, however, which means that you can compile AS2 and AS3 and use just a text editor. You're not going to get the assistance with debugging, and the nice illustration interface and timeline, however, so the learning curve will be steeper. I have also used OpenLaszlo some. We have a bunch of simple eLearning interaction templates that I've build in Laszlo. This is good for us because we don't have to pay huge costs to get all of our instructional designers set up with Laszlo. For simple drag-n-drops, mouseovers, clickboxes, and very simple animations, Laszlo will do the trick, and it's free. XML -based code, however, is really hard to work with when you're developing a large application with lots of conditional functionality. Or, maybe I'm just thick in the head. But when I'm working on large projects, especially projects that interact with external data sources, I find myself going back to Flash and AS3. Hope this helps, or at least gives you some things to look at. Good luck, A

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Time Limit for SCORM exercise
ResponsesInList.Text: well, are you saying that the developer added a adlcp:maxtimeallowed into the manifest which is then passed to the sco at runtime via cmi.student_data.max_time_allowed? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Time Limit for SCORM exercise
ResponsesInList.Text: This does seem to be what the developer is saying, Mat, but I've never heard of that being used in practice before. If I were the developer, I would want to handle the time limit inside of the sco. I might get values from the LMS to know previous time spent, things like that, but my calculations would be done by javascript or actionscript inside the sco, not by the LMS. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Time Limit for SCORM exercise
ResponsesInList.Text: cmi.student_data.max_time_allowed is not mandatory in the SCORM standard, nor is adlcp:maxtimeallowed. it's just an option and i was trying to get clarification on how they implemented the time limit. My guess is that they handled the timer internally to their sco scripting. Nothing wrong with that, i do it myself at times as many LMS's do not provide an lms level control for it (and the aforementioned optional status of those values). I'm thinking what they are telling you is probably that you need to set the server time session timeout to be higher than the test timeout or a student could be dumped unfairly by the server. Not all sco's fire commits etc at every step (ie: to keep network chatter down) so if it does not do that then if the test is long or the students take a long time that could happen. Then they would recieve an error as the sco's session id is no longer valid on the server so calls fail. "seems that there are too many errors being generated." Can you post examples of the errors so we can look at them. You actually get error values back that equal 0, it means that the call was successful. So seeing the debug info will help us help you.

ResponsesInList.Title: Embed images in scorm compliant package
ResponsesInList.Text: Should I embed images within my SCORM compliant package or should I have these images reside in some external folder on the internet? What are the advantages and disadvantages to the two approaches? Thanks for your insights

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Embed images in scorm compliant package
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Art, It depends on the size of your images, and how you're building your SCORM package. It also depends how you plan to roll out the SCORM content. I'd be likely to want to package everything, just for the sake of simplicity. If the external folder ever goes away, then the package referencing it might lose its functional integrity. That said, you want your images to be Web-ready, of appropriate size, etc. If you need to load a huge image file, for some reason, then there's a good reason to consider locating it elsewhere. Usually people are loading external files when they have a very large FLV that needs to be streamed from a streaming server , that sort of thing. But you'd have to have one hell of an image to cause a similar problem. ;) Best of luck, A

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unable to find API Adapter problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello again, Just to say I've now solved the problem. It seems that any resource which calls the API needs to be defined as "sco" not "asset" in the manifest (e.g. use the resource element attribute 'adlcp:scormtype="sco"'). Otherwise the API handlers are never loaded into the SCORM player, and any function call to use them will fail. I hope that's of use to someone - I know several other people on the forum have mentioned getting the same error. Geoff PS: this discussion applies to SCORM module version 2005102800 - the latest release at the time of writing.

Make sure you try 1.5.3+ before 1.6 if that is what you are doing. Also, depending on what compliancy you are publishing to, scorm 1.0
almost always works better (more compatible) than scorm 1.1, 1.2 and
2004. And also, if you are passing along variables you may find that the
variables are what is messing up your LMS, especially if you get errors
upon returning to a scorm resource and not on the initial load. You may wish to implement a navigation based feedback structure, rather
than a variable one. If you have something like "if box 2 is checked
then go to correct answer page" and "if box 3 is checked go to correct
feedback page, and then go to the question page again" this way you
create a navigation based loop that can force the correct answer, but
not involve variables (if you cant solve the variable issue) That may be helpful, or it may not!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm/Captivate
ResponsesInList.Text: Or, as I've found, the software will do exactly what you tell it to do, but your end-users won't always understand what the software is doing. Sometimes I work with companies that are using Articulate or other packaged elearning software to develop content internally. If they don't plan ahead regarding movie size, they can end up exporting swfs that are 800x600 pixels or larger. In such a case, they really have no alternative but to open the scorm package in a new window. But I usually recommend against it. Any time a new window opens (especially a new window that is so large), you risk losing your learner. You risk a pop-up blocker. You risk confusing the learner with the loss of the Moodle header and breadcrumbs. I usually recommend that scorm content be developed to fit within the left-side menu/right-side sco frame layout. Sometimes this means taking several Articulate scos and rewriting the manifest. xml to package them into a single scorm package. But the advantage is that the learner, who may have been hard-pressed to understand the Moodle navigation structure in the first place, is not suddenly pushed out of the Moodle interface into another new interface. It looks like Jason is doing a good job providing some instructions to the learner, telling him or her to close the window when the sco is finished. This seems like a good middle ground, if opening in a new window is unavoidable. There should probably also be documentation earlier in the course telling the learners to disable pop-up blockers, and how to do that in all possible browsers. You can also add new window indicators to your links and sco titles: Office Safety 1 [opens in new window]. (My $0.02),

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm/Captivate
ResponsesInList.Text: We encourage our clients to set their LMS to open a new window for the training courses we develop. We find that helps focus the learner on the content and navigation controls within the course. That way they don't think they can click on say a link in the breadcrumb and then return to the course. They would have to restart the SCORM course and return to where they left off. To address the closing of the window, we have an exit button that will actually close the window for the user. We find that is more intuitive then asking them to click the close button of the browser window, especially for non-computer savvy users. In Moodle, the disadvantage is that it does not detect when the window closes like other LMS applications so the user is returned to fairly blank Moodle page and then needs to navigate somewhere. It would be great if Moodle would detect the closure of the window and navigate to a course results screen or even back to the course.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Captivate to Moodle, no grades
ResponsesInList.Text: It took me a while to figure this one out too, but I finally got it going. Here is (in both technical and nontechnical terms) what the problem is. There are two versions of Actionscript (Flash Programming Language) in Captivate 4 Actionscript 2.0 (older non Object based code (non OOP)) and Actionscript 3.0 (new Object based code (class based OOP). While Actionscript 2.0 externalizes its code by default, Actionscript 3.0 does not. SCORM files use Javascript (or E4X Syntax based on ECMA Script) to record the data in learning management system or in this case Moodle. Make sure you externalize ALL Javascript files in the preferences to expose them to Moodle so it can incorporate them into its manifest file. This must be done before you zip the file and upload to the server . Problems in Actionscript 2.0 are settings based and by playing with the settings can be made to work correctly. Problems in Actionscript 3.0 are based on how you "compile" (or more to the point Captivate 4) or put together your Flash file (.swf). With the Javascript exposed it should work. There are a few other glitches with regards to using Quiz Widgets with AS3.0 but I am working on a patch in Flex and will post to the Captivate exchange when done. Hope that helps. Wade (Open Source Educational Flash Developer)

ResponsesInList.Title: Adobe Presenter Not Sending Correct Exit
ResponsesInList.Text: We just began using Adobe Presenter 7 to convert PowerPoint decks to SCORM modules.  In our initial testing, all the SCORM functions worked correctly - scores were being recorded in the gradebook as expected.  Now, after the purchase, the reporting doesn't work.  We're using Moodle 1.9.3 and have never had any issues with SCORM modules produced with Captivate.  After republishing with different reporting settings, I'm still not having any luck getting the scores to record. After testing the modules using Reload Player, I found that the Presenter files are sending Suspend for the Exit command.  I've searched through Moodle and Adobe forums, with no resolution yet.  I found a couple of things that I just knew would solve the issue, but they didn't work. Does anybody know how to resolve this, or how to force Presenter to send the correct exit command?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adobe Presenter Not Sending Correct Exit
ResponsesInList.Text: First, upgrade to Moodle 1.9.4 or greater, or test your scorm packages in a more contempoary Moodle version. Then you can use the debugging interface to see all communications with the API. Every version after 1.9.4 has much-improved scorm support. Here are some things you can check. With the debugger running, look for doLMSCommit() and doLMSFinish(). Lots of programs send suspend data, but also set lesson_status to completed/passed/incomplete, and the suspend status isn't a problem in that case. doLMSFinish() is the command that should be sent to tell Moodle to finish up, save all, and terminate connection with the sco. If doLMSFinish isn't being called, you can force it with a small hack to the scorm package. Use the standard ADL apiwrapper.js provided in the SCORM content samples from ADL (links in our SCORM FAQ). Place that into your SCORM package, import the js file into the HTML page embeddeing your swf, and add a function, called by an onunload in the tag. In that function, call doLMSCommit, and then doLMSFinish(). Another thing that many SCOs fail to do is to regularly call doLMSCommit(). That is what saves values to the LMS. It also keeps the connection with the browser window open. If that seems to be one of the issues, you can place a JavaScript timer in the HTML page to call that function every 30 seconds or so, to be sure that the connection isn't dropped during a long presentation in which no data is sent to the LMS.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adobe Presenter Not Sending Correct Exit
ResponsesInList.Text: The suspend value should not cause the score to not be stored. exit="Suspend" simply tells the lms that the user left the course with the intent to return and continue the attempt. So when launching later do not present a new attempt with an empty cmi object. Instead please launch a second "session" in the same attempt.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problems with multi -page SCORM Module
ResponsesInList.Text: Are you exporting to SCORM 1.2 in captivate? SCORM 2004 is not supported in moodle directly. So make sure that it's 1.2. Under 1.2 there is a value called lesson_status, the allowed values are not attempted, passed, failed, completed, incomplete. Obviously there is nuance between passed and completed - usually a sco that has a testing component in it should be setting to either passed or failed. Completed is useful for a sco that has no testing evaluation in it-a sco with a streaming video for example. Something to keep in mind is that when developing 1.2 scorm courses there are 3 shifting parts involved: the standard, what logic is produced by the authoring tool, and what logic the lms implemented and what it expects from the coursware logic. Sadly the standard has many optional values so nothing works across the board. So it's possible that Captivate is choosing to set the lesson status to complete rather than use passed/failed. Check the first link as ver 4 has an option to deal with that. And you can see SumTotal for example likes incomplete/completed. Perfect example of what i mean not supporting the spirit of the standard, instead forcing it to fit how their LMS runs. Something you just have to get used to. As for Captivate sometimes the choices you make on tracking/scoring during export can cause unexpected results in the cmi data. If your using Captivate 4 look at: http://blogs.adobe.com/captivate/2009/03/lms_reporting_enhancements_in.html http://help.adobe.com/en_US/Captivate/4.0/Using/WSc1b83f70210cd1015881ff7211c9893458a-8000.html

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Does Moodle allow Bookmarks in SCORM?
ResponsesInList.Text: The short answer to your question is yes. Moodle supports SCORM which has a data value called lesson_location that accepts a string value. So captivate should be populating that data set with info to maintain bookmark placement between user sessions. One thing to check is make sure your setting lesson_status before the user leaves. For example when you launch the course initially you want to change the value to "incomplete". If you never change that value and execute a LMSFinish then the lms is required to set the course status to completed. If that happens then when you login in again it will be a new attempt (unless you set the attempts to 1 in moodle) and the cmi object will be empty.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Communication between submodul
ResponsesInList.Text: It all depends on what is accessing. SCORM standard defines what type of data a sco can save to the lms, but also what can access it. So sco 1 can have a cmi.score.raw value of say 70. Say that's your pretest sco. The next sco launched is completely unaware of sco 1's data. It also can not access it. The idea in the standard is by not allowing sco's to access and rely on other sco's it improves the reusability of the sco in multiple aggregations. Obviously many developers do not care about reuse but the standard did so LMS's that implement the standard must follow it and not let sco's access other sco data. You could side step the lms and try to add some php code in the sco that hit's moodle DB ad finds the pretest sco data in there but that's basically sitestepping the standard entirely. I highly suggest looking at the SCORM spec to better understand what the rules are.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Reporting - What does this mean?
ResponsesInList.Text: Actually the SCORM course is in control of what data is written to these fields with some predefined values. However the predefined values are not clearly defined in all cases and are open to interpretation. For cmi.core.exit a course can write use one of the following; suspend, logout, timeout, and an empty string. In your example, I would venture to guess that suspend means the course was not completed, passed or failed. For cmi.core.lesson_status a course can use one of the following; passed, completed, failed, incomplete, browsed, or an empty string. For cmi.core.total_time a course sends the amount of time for each visit to the course and Moodle will add the times together and place them in this field. However, the course is responsible for determining the amount of time not Moodle. In the report provided, the student either visited the course once and had it open for 20 minutes and change, or visited the course several times for a total of 20 minutes and change. However, it does not mean the student was actively viewing the material during that time, only that the course was open. The defined format for the time is hours:minutes:seconds.hundredths of seconds For cmi.suspend_data a course can write anything it wants. I believe it can store up to 4KB of data. So any values you see in this field only have specific meaning to either the course creator or the application used to create the course. In your example, I would guess that the student viewed the first 19 slides and exited while on slide 3. The sc#= values probably relate to some type of status for each slide and it looks like there are 25 of them. The LCS=3 may mean Last Current Slide since the value matches the value of lastviewedslide. Of course, this is all just a guess on my part. If you are interested, you can view the entire SCORM specification by downloading the document from http://www.adlnet.gov/downloads/DownloadPage.aspx?ID=240 .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Captivate and Scorm Bookmarks
ResponsesInList.Text: According to Moodle 1.2 standards, it's called cmi.core.lesson_location. You can set it by making a call to the basic APIWrapper.js, or use your own custom API wrapper. You can store a location in this variable, but it's the sco's responsibility to retrieve the value and display the appropriate content when a user returns. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm and Captivate
ResponsesInList.Text: Is there anything actually preventing the use of bookmarks in SCORM objects? No. In fact, Captivate does bookmarking inside SCOs very well for normal content, as does Articulate. And if you code the SCORM object yourself, then you have even more control over bookmarking. The bookmarking supported by SCORM 2004 is between different SCOs; for those who don't understand the difference, that's a totally different application of the term, and it might be a good idea to read the ADL/SCORM documentation to get a better understanding of the kinds of bookmarking available. Unless you make it yourself, line by line, and take the time to read the ADL documentation and understand how SCORM works, it's not going to be perfect, even though you paid $700 or $1400 for the "rapid development", "magic bullet" product that exports it. SCORM 1.2 is very well supported in 1.9.5+, and the majority of the functionality hangups in SCORM authorware are just that: hangups in the authorware, not hangups in Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Julia, As the package is bigger than the maximum file size set up for Moodle, you need to increase that size. For that, you need to be the administrator of your Moodle site, or pass the administrator the following information: In the php.ini file, which is usually located in the /etc/php5/apache2 folder (this location may vary in your case), you need to increase the value of the variable: ; Maximum allowed size for uploaded files. upload_max_filesize = 2M to 10 MB or even more. If you are going to work with scorm packages, I recommend to set up a value of 80 Mb, for instance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Start a new attempt missing
ResponsesInList.Text: Only 3 things affect this checkbox displaying: - if the user has not already started an attempt (i.e. the attempt status is not incomplete) then the checkbox is not displayed. - if the number of attempts taken already by the user is greater than the max attempts setting then the checkbox is not displayed. - to set unlimited attempts, set max attempts to 0. I would check the max attempts setting for the scorm.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Large SCORM VLE Packs
ResponsesInList.Text: The best way is to upload them directly to the site via . ftp . Look carefully where the folder is on the server and then upload them outside of the Moodle upload tool. The problem I find with quite a few of these larger packs is that they are basically large collections of worksheets or other similar resources that have just been lumped together and labelled as SCORM-compliant. Quite often they turn out to just be a directory listing of all the resources. Of course there is also some great content that is actually organised into useful courses, but it is worth having a good look at what the VLE pack actually contains.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm session time

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm session time
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle takes the reported session_time and applies it (adds it to) cmi[.core].total_time, however it does not normally, I believe, store the session duration (which could be used along with the tracking time stamp to determine the approximate start and end times of the session).  This could be added easily enough by adding the session_time data element to the items getting stored by the datamodel.  If you wanted this field to show up in reports, you'd also have to make some changes there.

ResponsesInList.Title: Scorm Reporting
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I have uploaded a Scorm made with Articulate which has a final assessment on it where the tracking is done.  It is tracked as pass/fail.  Where do I find the information in Moodle who has taken the Scorm and whether they have passed or failed?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm Reporting
ResponsesInList.Text: Stuart, You can find this information located under the activities block -> Scorms/Aicc -> View reports and then view the attempt for each student. Remember Pass and Fail will be reported to the grade book as 1 - Pass and 0 - fail ( from Articulate), when the Scorm object is set for a Learning Object when you are reporting off the slides. You can also create a custom scale to show that data to the student, these changes can be made on the front page under Grades ->Scales _ add new scale. Here is the link to the information on creating new scales: http://docs.moodle.org/en/Scales If you are reporting off the quiz I would would just leave the score and then set the pass grade in the grade book to what ever you institution prefers.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Saba Publisher problem after completing the quiz
ResponsesInList.Text: cmi.interactions.n.text is not actually a valid SCORM data element through the SCORM 2004 3rd Edition Run-Time documentation, which is why Moodle returns an error. The only text field in cmi.interactions is cmi.interactions.n.description. Saba/Lectora apparently made this field up, and the Saba LMS supports use of this field designation. Moodle could be easily modified to support this custom field, but does not out of the box. I actually encountered this field when generating courses for Saba and someone was asking me to populate the interactions "like Lectora", and had to take a look at the code to see what they were doing...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Saba Publisher problem after completing the quiz
ResponsesInList.Text: good spotting Stephen! - not entirely sure if we'd like to implement non valid SCORM elements (especially as we haven't even finished the 2004 implementation in Moodle yet!) but feel free to create a bug in the tracker about this and we'll consider it at some point down the track!
