ResponsesInList.Title: Import Scorm-Quiz - reporting of answers
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello everybody, last week we stumbled across a problem and thought about solving it with moodle. No luck so far. The idea was to create a quiz using an authoring tool (not creating the quiz in moodle itself) and exporting it to a Scorm-file. Then import the quiz into moodle, let people take the test and evaluate every single participant's answers (at the moment the test is done on paper). Is there any way to do this? Thank you very much in advance for all inputs or suggestions! Susanne

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Import Scorm-Quiz - reporting of answers
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there Well -yes-there are lots of ways you can make quizzes and import as SCORM. There are some free packages and some very expensive packages to do this job. Have a look at the SCORM tools in the documentation here. But you have to ask yourself: why do you want to make the quiz outside of Moodle and import into Moodle as SCORM? You are making more steps for yourself than necessary and -this is the problem - not all SCORM packages will display the results of each individual person's quiz or give you as much detail as you could set simply by using Moodle's own quiz itself. Moodle's quiz is very powerful and worth learning. If you don't like Moodle's quiz, consider using Hot Potatoes which is an easier way to create quizzes offline that you upload and have detailed score results in Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Import Scorm-Quiz - reporting of answers
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mary, - and thank you for you quick answer. I realize that I didn't describe my problem properly. We already have an authoring tool in use - the new problem is the evaluation of single answers (not only "training done successfully"). Susanne

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Import Scorm-Quiz - reporting of answers
ResponsesInList.Text: Well yes;that could well be your problem -as I said - not all SCORM packages will give you the detailed individual responses that you want - and that you could get with, say, using the Moodle quiz. Is it essential you use this authoring tool?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Import Scorm-Quiz - reporting of answers
ResponsesInList.Text: I don't actually think *any* of the SCORM packages will provide individual feedback on answers via SCORM. Through my developments of Moodle supported SCORM activities I don't believe it is supported. If I'm wrong, please tell me as it is something I'd like to implement too. SCORM reports back a grade and the 'course completion' status. You can feedback a score or percentage - Student X got 45% and link this to a grade via the Gradebook. As Mary suggests - for specific answer feedback in the way you desire it would be better to use the Moodle quiz.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adding a new SCORM/AICC - Keeps popping up even after selecting manifest
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Christine, What may have been happening is that all files required for the course may not have been found. If you selected the update frequency to always update, Moodle will attempt to look for updated files each time the course is launched. If it can't find the files, and the user has editing capabilities then it will present the settings screen. The correct way of adding a SCORM course is by uploading a zip file that contains all the files of the course along with the imsmanifest file. You then "choose" the zip file and Moodle will unzip the contents and locate the imsmanifest file to determine how to run the course. Hope that helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Usable report
ResponsesInList.Text: I've been creating quizzes and surveys using Articulate and have tried publishing them as SCORM and AICC. There are several essay and short answer questions in all of them. The issue I'm having is generating a report that would be understandable to the teachers. I click on "Track Details" and I get a fairly incombrehensible list of answers. Ideally I would like to have something that would be akin to reading a completed quiz as if it were done on paper. Am I missing something here?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Usable report
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Bayne, Nope you are not missing anything. For what you are describing you would be better off using the Moodle activities that support quizzes and surveys. You will get much better reporting. The downside to SCORM is that only basic information is required to be supported and all the extended data is optional to support, so most applications that produce SCORM activities do not support the optional data. This is one of the issues with using a tool like Articulate and is the reason we wrote our own SCORM interface so that we can support all SCORM data. Moodle supports just about all, if not all, of the extended data which includes the ability to report on a per question basis. It is just a matter of using a tool to create SCORM activities that supports the extended data. I think essay and short answer questions are a supported data type by SCORM, but I am not positive and I do not know if Moodle supports those data types for SCORM. That is something I will have to look into.

ResponsesInList.Title: Unusual Loading Problem with SCORM 1.2 package
ResponsesInList.Text: OK, here's one that's...interesting. We've created a course in ProForm and published it as a SCORM 1.2 package. We're testing it in Moodle, running on a Windows machine with Apache 2.2, MySQL 5.0.45 and PHP 5.2.6. The course consists of a bunch of text pages, default (SWF) pages and some text and audio pages. The weird thing we're seeing is that while the course runs fine in Firefox 3.0.5, the text and audio pages fail to load completely in Internet Explorer 7 (for those unfamiliar with ProForm, a text and audio page is a page that has both text and audio resources associated with it, and it loads both resources when the student accesses the page in question). The audio will play, but the control bar for the audio doesn't show up, and the text never shows up. The display area just shows a Loading... clip with the tiniest bit of the left edge colored in. Since our target audience will be using IE , we really need to make sure everything works on that platform. If anyone else has seen such a problem or anything similar, please let me know. The course does run fine in IE in a stand alone context , it's only problematic when the course is run via Moodle. I just don't understand why there would be a difference with the browser performance, my expectation would be that since the course is ultimately a Flash movie (player.swf) that the issues should be consistent across browsers if Flash is running at all. I should mention that we saw a similar issue with image and audio pages and converted them to SWFS to get them to run ok, and we could do the same with the text and audio pages, but I'd like to understand the problem. ProForm is performing excellently, but clearly there is something about the SCORM package running in Moodle and trying to load files in some way that is giving fits to IE. If anyone has had any Moodle/ProForm experience it'd be great to hear about it. Thanks in advance for any help you can provide.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unusual Loading Problem with SCORM 1.2 package
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello David, I don't have experience with ProForm but the issue you described sounded similar to an issue I do have experience with. The SCORM 1.2 packages I've created using Flash sometimes had issues loading external content into the main .swf. An example would be loading a snippet of text or audio that would only partially load or fail to load altogether. The solution I came up with is to use the setTimeout() function to delay the loading of the content in order to make sure all is peachy with the main swf and scorm player before trying to load in additional content. This workaround has proven very effective for our end users. Not sure this is exactly what you are experiencing but thought it might help with your brainstorming process.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unusual Loading Problem with SCORM 1.2 package
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi David, We won't be able to help you very much unless you load the package to the repository so someone can check it out. We'll also want to know what version of Moodle you're running. http://docs.moodle.org/en/SCORM_FAQ#What.27s_the_best_way_to_ask_for_help_in_the_SCORM_Forum I've only got a bit of time, but my educated guess, the first thing I'd check, would be whether you've got any JavaScript onLoad-type of events being called to bring those swfs in. IE supports some nonstandard JS events. In fact, I believe that IE has its own special version of JS (since they are so very prescient and special), and if ProForm isn't using a browser sniffer in the loading code, some functions might not get called in the IE way. So, check the JS in the loading HTML page. I have fixed problems like this by adding or substituting the IE onevent call for the FF/standard onevent. Also check in admin settings that your filters are allowing .swf, .flv, etc. Best of luck, Amy

ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Clark and Amy, I appreciate the advice.  Reflecting on the situation last night I had come to the conclusion that it was probably a JavaScript-related issue, since that's really the only major component with large differences between IE and FF. I'm investigating now to see if I can track down the specific problem.  I'm modifying the JS code in the scorm_12.js.php file in Moodle, and I'll be modifying the functions in the player.html file produced by ProForm to try and isolate the specific instance of non-loading. I unfortunately can't upload the package, the IP isn't mine (and the thing is about 80 MB as well).  Thanks for the ideas, I'll post back here when I have a better sense of exactly what's happening.

ResponsesInList.Title: Can a SCORM module be kept on an external server?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can a SCORM module be kept on an external server?
ResponsesInList.Text: I doubt it. When you create the activity, you cannot CHOOSE the SCORM unless it is on your Moodle server. Having said that, I do know that the SCORM editor eXe will let you export a SCORM lesson as a web in a self contained folder that could be on another server/computer. Of course doing it that way you would loose grades if you have scorable questions in the SCORM lesson, because Moodle would not be communicating with it. That would be fine if the SCORM was just an instructional lesson.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can a SCORM module be kept on an external server?
ResponsesInList.Text: In theory I would assume you could keep your moodle data folder on a separate server. If this is true then you would in fact be able to store your SCORM modules on a separate server. However, you would still be bound to keeping your SCORM modules in one place.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can a SCORM module be kept on an external server?
ResponsesInList.Text: The Zip file can be hosted externally with no issues - just type the url into the box provided, however you should not link to an imsmanifest. xml file on a seperate server. as the SCORM JS communication will fail cross- domain . check out this post for more info: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=114560#p508505 or: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=122417

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can a SCORM module be kept on an external server?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jonas...I am not sure of all the nitty gritty programming ins and outs...but here where I work at Vancouver Island University...we do use an external server to publish our SCORM content....and then link it "externally" as SCORM Modules... We use a software platform called Adobe Contribute...which is a web-publishing collaborative software...this allows instructional designers, media designers, and content experts to author and create content on one central server... ...then directly from the Contribute server...we can update the SCORM package...and this process updates the imsmanifest and zip files as illustrated here - http://screencast.com/t/om4DhnBbE We then have the option to upload the zip directly to the course and link the imsmanifest file "internally" or we can link directly to the "external" imsmanifest file that is located on the Contribute server...the advantage of linking externally is that it allows "instructors" to make last minute changes to content and then it all appear in Moodle without the need to re-package/zip and then upload and re-link, etc... cheers frank

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can a SCORM module be kept on an external server?
ResponsesInList.Text: while it will initially look like it works directly linking to an imsmanifest file hosted externally (on a different domain than your moodle site) - Javascript security in most web browsers I've seen will block cross-domain communication - which means that the object will "play" but NO grades/any other information will be passed back to Moodle. Which really makes it pointless as a SCORM object - you might as well just use html/flash without bothering about the SCORM stuff. Hosting the zip externally works well, and if you look at the advanced settings on the page, you can configure how often Moodle "updates" the locally stored SCORM object based on the original zip location.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can a SCORM module be kept on an external server?
ResponsesInList.Text: If your SCORM package is Flash based, Flash Player will also throw an error if the .swf file is on another server without a crossdomain.xml policy file appropriately configured: http://kb2.adobe.com/cps/142/tn_14213.html

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: learning content as scorm package
ResponsesInList.Text: You should ask the company the following: Is your course compatible with AICC, SCORM 1.2 or SCORM 2004? If it is a SCORM course, has it been certified and by who? You want SCORM 1.2 conformance as it is the best supported in Moodle. Moodle does support the basics of SCORM 2004, but not all features yet. SCORM certification does not guaruntee that it will work with Moodle but there is a much better chance then if it isn't. Moodle does have limited support for AICC courses, but I would not recommend them as the AICC specifications were not very specific and how a vendor chose to implement the AICC specification makes it harder to be compatible with every variation.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unable to find an API Adapter error message
ResponsesInList.Text: Have you tested alternate browsers? An API error can result from javascript handling errors, and browsers are a likely source. Your operating environment might also impact on the way that javascript is handled, but my understanding about all that is murky. I imagine that if your module runs fine in Reload then the problem is not with the API itself - either at the Moodle or at the SCORM end. You should test a non-Lectora SCO anyway, to make sure SOMETHING works - but just because one SCO works doesn't mean another will. (Which makes you wonder what the point of having a standard is, but that's another story...)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unable to find an API Adapter error message
ResponsesInList.Text: The SCORM test suite is your friend. If the LMS passes the SCORM test suite and the SCO passes the SCORM test suite there is a 99% probability that they will work together. The problems come from people cutting corners or "tweaking" the implementation to fit some older, non-standard implementation. Some of the API search ideas implemented in some generic scripts found in various tools do not follow the standard API discovery algorithm.  I suggest that you try your SCO in the latest version of the test suite first. If that works, I suggest you try to run a "known good" SCORM package or build one with a "known good" SCO to check whether there is a runtime environment problem.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Lectora Scorm module and display size
ResponsesInList.Text: Sounds like your problem is the screen size of your package. We have the same issue--because many of our users have smaller screens than the developers, the developer sees the package present with no problem but users have to scroll around to see all of it and complain piteously. We've solved this two ways--none of the Lectora/Captivate modules are bigger than about 730 x 550 and they are set to open in a new window. Then your moodle settings should be slightly larger and also set to open in a new window. I was suspicious of the whole open in a new window thing at first but it works very nicely and actually improves the user's capabilities. But pop-up blockers MUST be turned off...Hope this helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM Activity Debugging in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: As we work through the backlog of issues for the SCORM module, one of the things that I wanted to add was the ability to debug the interaction between SCORM packages and Moodle. This is something that could help me work on SCORM 1.2, and 1.3 compliance making it easier to see what is going on with the test suites. Also (more importantly), when it comes to helping people in the Moodle community work through their problems with mod/scorm, it would give visibility of how their packages are working with Moodle - are they Commiting properly, did Moodle handle all the posted data elements etc. So what I have done, taking inspiration from existing SCORM debugging wrappers, is to insert a layer into the mod/scorm API that logs the SCORM API interactions to a popup window. At present (this will evolve over time) this is in STABLE 1.8, 1.9, and HEAD and is activated by setting the DEVELOPER debug level. This enables the logging system wide, so at present it is a developer tool only. With debugging enabled, when you launch an Activity, you will notice a new link just below the bread crumbs at the top - "API Logging is On/Off": This allows you to toggle the logging on and off. With the loggin enabled, when the first API call is intercepted, the popup is launched and the logging messages are progressively appended with date/time, the parameters passed and the return code + result:

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, I'd appreciate any help you can give me on this. I am using the latest weekly 1.9 build of Moodle, updated through CVS . I'm currently experiencing an issue with SCORM 1.2 packages generated using the latest version of Articulate Presenter '09 update 4. The packages have 10-15 slides and end with an embedded Quizmaker quiz on the final slide. Export is made using the completed/incomplete reporting with a passing score on the quiz at the end of the presentation being used as a determining factor of completion. The problem is this: Through quite a bit of debugging, it appears that when the SCORM is played straight through from start to finish without suspending and a passing score is obtained on the quiz, moodle receives a value of cmi.core.exit of "suspended" even though the course has been completed. The SCORM, through the built in debug log offered by Presenter, shows that a value of "" is attempting to be set, though this is not recorded by moodle. Instead, moodle records "suspended" as the value and shows that the SCORM is suspended to the learner. However, when I start the SCORM, exit the activity before reaching the final quiz, moodle records it as suspended as expected. I then restart the activity, complete the quiz, and this time cmi.core.exit is set correctly to a value of "" as expected.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: cmi.core.exit not being set correctly via Articulate Presenter SCORM package
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, I have created an issue in Moodle Tracker regarding this: http://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-19283 It appears that modifying lms/SCORMFunctions.js in SCORMs generated by Articulate Presenter and commenting out the following lines correct the issue: //we want to set the exit type to suspend immediately because some LMS's only store data if they get a suspend request //blnResult = blnResult && SCORM_CallLMSSetValue("cmi.core.exit", SCORM_TranslateExitTypeToSCORM(DEFAULT_EXIT_TYPE)); Best, Paul

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Want to put severl links to same SCORM in same course
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Marshal, If I am understanding you correctly, then there is a way you can do this. Go to your SCORM activity and copy the URL from the address bar. Go to the Lesson of the course you want to add it to. From the Add Resource list, choose Link to a file or web page Give a Title to your link and paste the URL of your SCORM activity in the URL box For Window, choose Same Window For Keep page navigation visible... choose No. Then Save it That should give you the results you want.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Joe, I know it's about a year-and-a-half since you posted this hack, but I just wanted to chime in and say thanks. Your fix for changing the value for the unzip column in the mdl_config table was a winner. For others: I know there are some who are still getting this error as late as last week. (I've been reading the forums all afternoon trying to find a fix for the same issue I'm having with an Articulate Presenter SCORM 1.2 zip on Moodle 1.9.4+). I finally got it resolved just now. The fix I found might actually be a combination of what Joe suggested above, along with adjusting limits referenced previously for php.ini. When all is said and done, what finally got me past the blank modedit.php page after uploading a sizeable SCORM zip are the following: 1. In php.ini, I modified: max_execution_time = 300 max_input_time = 600 memory_limit = 100M post_max_size = 100M memory_limit = 100M (These are arbitrary values. I was just following earlier suggestions to up the limits from current.) 2. Then, in the mysql db for moodle, I set the value suggested by Joe above for the unzip column in the mdl_config table. (Turns out, I actually didn't have a value in that column initially.) After setting the value to /usr/bin/unzip I'm now golden. Thanks all.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Making SCORM modules in Flash 8 for Dummies
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Derek, Hand writing a SCORM manifest is a bit of a pain and easy to mess up with typos. If you're using a web authoring tool that supports plugins, then search for a SCORM manifest plugin. I pulled up this one for Dreamweaver: http://www.e-learningconsulting.com/products/manifest-maker.html BTW , Adobe Flash Professional doesn't offer any support for SCORM beyond MX 2004. They've shifted the emphasis over to Captivate, Presenter and Connect where it belongs, and there's no mention of SCORM in Adobe AS 3.0 language reference. Also, I'd recommend looking for 3rd party classes and libraries to avoid the malicious script injection security issues involved with using FS Command in AS 2.0.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Making SCORM modules in Flash 8 for Dummies
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Derek, I wasn't referring to SQL injection attacks, Flash is client-side and SQL is server -side. Even if you're using Flash remoting , it's unwise to set up any client to server communication that passes SQL. The malicious script attacks that I mentioned are, as usual, from Javascript. The problem with AS 2.0 is that it allows FlashVars to be instantiated at runtime and is therefore vulnerable, especially if you're using FSCommand (old) or ExternalInterface (new) for communicating with Javascript on the web page, which is how SCORM passes data between the Flash application and the server. You can find out more about Flash Player security here: http://www.adobe.com/devnet/flashplayer/articles/secure_swf_apps.html

ResponsesInList.Title: Allowing access to Scorm material from one LMS to another
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Folks We are currently using moodle to host our e-learning courses. We've recently started to use SCORM files to deliver the content of the course. Some of our students are teachers who have access to there own schools LMS. They would like to be able to use our SCORM material on their site. I dont want to pass out our SCORM files so i was wondering if it was possible to create a SCORM that can be uplaoded to the remote LMS site at the teachers location but pulls the learning materials from our site. This would allow us to keep materials up to date in 1 location without the worry of mass re-distribution Thanks All

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Allowing access to Scorm material from one LMS to another
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there the main issue you will have to deal with is Javascript security - The SCORM API Javascript runs on the remote LMS, which is a problem as Javascript doesn't talk nicely accross different domains. - the SCORM objects on your server cannot communicate with the SCORM Javascript API on the Remote LMS server so if you didn't need any form of communication between the SCORM object and the Remote LMS you would be fine... but if you want to let the Remote LMS receive grades - then it won't work. The SCORM module allows you to specify a url as the location of the SCORM file - either the SCORM zip or directly linking to the imsmanifest. xml file. - linking directly to the imsmanifest.xml file on an external domain will cause Javascript security issues as mentioned above. you can still use an external url to a zip file, but moodle downloads that file and stores it unzipped locally for use - but this may not suit your requirements. We have been thinking about ways of using the Repository API in Moodle 2.0 to store an searchable external repository of SCORM objects - but this won't be any use for 1.9! hope that helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: dataFromFlash Javascript error
ResponsesInList.Text: The Flash is certainly making an externalInterface for FSCommand call to the JS function. You are right about that. That's why I suggested that you override it by calling the function on load from the HTML wrapper. SCORM is a sketchy standard, and our developers are doing the best they can with it. Right now Moodle will do very well recording lesson_status, session_time, and score_raw. You should be fine if you report a single grade from your sco and you don't depart from the 0-100 point scale. Obviously, you have no control over what's coming from Captivate, however. So I can't really be of much more help to you than that. You can always use the SCORM debugger to track what API functions the sco is calling, however. If you have Flash, you could also import the Captivate project file into Flash and view the function calls that way. And you can talk to Captivate support to find out how their scos behave, and what API functions they call at what time. I don't use Captivate to build eLearning. But many of our customers do. I am the one that tweaks their swf/html/js/ xml when their Captivate export isn't doing what they want. This happens much less often for Captivate than it does for Articulate, that's for sure. What I usually tell people is to use a Moodle technology to deliver the assessment, and use a technology like Captivate to build interactivity, and just embed it in a Moodle page. That way non-technical users don't have to struggle with SCORM. I myself prefer to stick with lesson_status and not mess with setting scores from a sco. Hopefully there's some information in here you can use, Rob. Good luck. A

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problem when attempting to read scorm_scoes_track
ResponsesInList.Text: Actually, I was just able to resolve this issue. As I've seen in the moodle issue tracker, some more people had the same problem as I. A 'hack' had to be implemented in the locallib.php file and in particular in the function scorm_reconstitute_array_element. I had to change the $element_name."_" to $element_name."." in the following lines: - echo ' '.$element_name.'_'.$current.'.'.$current_subelement.'._count = '.$count_sub.";\n"; - echo ' '.$element_name.'_'.$current.'.'.$current_subelement.'._count = '.$count_sub.";\n"; I guess this is part of the legacy from SCORM 1.2 which uses more underscore characters in the dataset. I hope this is useful for others as well.

ResponsesInList.Text: Have you tried debugging the SCORM API? http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=103921 You need to ensure that your SCOs are setting atleast a lesson_status, and .score.raw, and calling LMSCommit() to ensure that the values are passed up to the LMS (name mod/scorm in Moodle). ResponsesInList.Title: Scorm test score won't register in gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: I am a new user running Moodle 1.9.3+ . I have created a simple quiz in captivate and added it to my course. The problem is that no matter what settings I change, I can't seem to get Moodle to show the score in the gradebook (It shows the score as empty). When I navigate to the 'report' screen however, I can see the correct score along with the user data, etc. What I am I missing here? Why does the Quiz appear to pass the score to Moodle but not show up in the students gradebook??? Rick

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm test score won't register in gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rick, Just wondering if you can give a bit more information, namely: 1. Are you exporting in SCORM 1.2 or SCORM 2004 format? Moodle is 1.2 compliant at the moment so there *may* be issues if you are using 2004. 2. How are you structuring the settings within the SCORM activity? Are you using the 'highest grade' setting or 'learning objects'?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm test score won't register in gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mark: I have tried both SCORM 1.2 and SCORM 2004 formats with no luck. I have set the activity to both 'highest grade' setting and 'learning objects' and the problem still persists. I also tried creating a Scorm-compliant quiz in Quiz Creator with the same results. I think the Scorm interactivity is working correctly, as I do see the correct grades in the reports. It just seems to be my Moodle settings or the program is not working as expected. Rick

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm test score won't register in gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: How are you creating your SCORM lessons? I use Adobe Presenter 7. It is probably a simple setting you have to change. I would recommend the following: 1. Try loading your lessons on my website and see if they report to the gradebook and 2. Have me load my lessons on your website and see if they report to the gradebook If you are interested in having me troubleshoot your problem, send me an email at BradleyLBailey@hotmail.com with a username/password to your website with instructor access in a course that I can load a lesson . I will provide the same to you for my website in a return email.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm test score won't register in gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: OK, so it seems that you quiz "Quiz in New Window -Test to see if SCORM 1.2 reports to gradebook using Firefox browser (Test passed)" was the only one that passed a score to the gradebook. What is it about that test that is different from the other ones??

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm test score won't register in gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: My Adobe Presenter Quiz in SCORM 1.2 worked on your website. It reported the score properly. My Adobe Presenter Quiz in SCORM 2004 didn't work on your website. It gave me an error message that said "not enough choices: cmi.interactions.N0.correct_responses.N0.pattern". I also tried an Adobe Presenter Lesson in SCORM 1.2 on your website. It didn't have a quiz but reported slide view completion. I am not sure why it didn't report to your gradebook because the learning objectives were met and the SCORM score shows 1 out of 1 (i.e., complete).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm test score won't register in gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Have you tried the API debugging mechanism to see what is going on? http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=103921 Cheers, Piers Harding.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm test score won't register in gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: So - the thing that immediately sticks out in the second log is that you have a score.raw but the lesson_status is not either passed or completed, so it wont go through to the gradebook (you will get an activity report though). Cheers, Piers Harding.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm test score won't register in gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: So Piers, is that a Moodle configuration error or would that be the fault of the Quiz software? Rick

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm test score won't register in gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: For grades to be passed to the gradebook, the final state of the attempt must have a non-zero .score.raw and must have a lesson_status of "passed" or "completed". This is the way mod/scorm has been designed to work. The Quiz software needs to configure the SCORM package to meet these criteria, IF you want the grades to flow through to the gradebook irrespective of how the attempt has been performed. In Moodle 2.0, there has been a feature added to "force" completion of an attempt if either the .score.raw or the lesson_status is set correctly - this is to try and assist course administrators who may have old buggy packages. Cheers, Piers Harding.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm test score won't register in gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: We have actively used production training site with Moodle - Moodle 1.9.4+ (Build: 20090204) Ever since upgrading to 1.9 in september and all newer versions since, we have been experiencing the same issues with our SCORM packages which were performing just fine with all previous versions of Moodle we had used. (1.4 .and up.to 1.7.2 ) Our Captivate 3 generated SCORMS would not pass data to the Gradebook. After trail and error attempts we figured out that If we re-save (without any changes - see below) the coresponding Grade item in the Gradebook, all SCORM scores received by students until this update is made, are passed successfully, but will not be passed when the students are completing the SCORM. If we republish the SCORM package with an option to report all interactions (v/s page completion and overall score only) the grades are passed instantly when the students are completing the SCORM. That is good, but generates large amount of useless data - the trainers really don't want to have all interactions reported - just the overall scores and slide completion. Our Authorware generated SCORMS would not pass data to the Gradebook. If we re-save the coresponding item in the Gradebook - just as with Captivate, all SCORM scores received by students until this update is made, are passed successfully, but will not be passed when the students are completing the SCORM. Due to the fact that we have numerous Authorware and Captivate SCORMs we desparately need to figure out what is the solution. Any help will be greatly appreciated.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm test score won't register in gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Janette, I'm having similar problems. I believe it may relate to the function "scorm_insert_track()" in mod/scorm/locallib which seems to be the only time scorm_update_grades() is called - the function which adds the record to the gradebook. The code if (strstr($element, '.score.raw') || (($element == 'cmi.core.lesson_status' || $element == 'cmi.completion_status') && ($track->value == 'completed' || $track->value == 'passed'))) { $scorm = get_record('scorm', 'id', $scormid); $grademethod = $scorm->grademethod % 10; include_once('lib.php'); scorm_update_grades($scorm, $userid); } seems to refer only to element '.score.raw' I'm using 'core.score.raw' which although is recorded in scoes_tracking correctly is not added to the gradebook. I'll try some experiments with this changed to the other element and see if it adds to the gradebook correctly.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm test score won't register in gradebook
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi - strstr($element, '.score.raw') looks for the value .score.raw in the string, so it will pickup cmi.core.score.raw, or core.score.raw. I'm assuming that if you are passing core.score.raw you are using scorm2004? While I don't think that this particular issue is your problem, I do think that it is likely that there are other problems with the gradebook interface. If you can distill me down a repeatable example (package + config) for me, then I'll do some debugging. Cheers, Piers Harding.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Any update to AICC-HACP
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey Kevin I have just finished working with Piers to patch the AICC HACP interface in Moodle to fix some compliance issues around AICC "data" but the HACP interface for remote content has worked fine since 1.8.3 You need the latest MOODLE_19_WEEKLY or MOODLE_18_WEEKLY (specifically these minimum versions 1.8.8+ (Build: 20090304) and 1.9.4+ (Build: 20090304) ) to get the AICC data fixes. The issues you may be finding is that the AICC_URL which is sent to your content cannot be resolved by your content, or permission is denied due to cross domain . Let me give you a couple of  examples: I work for SkillSoft and we use a Java Applet to perform our HACP comms. If our externally hosted content (content.skillsoft.com) is launched from (lms.behindthefirewall.local) and uses an UNSIGNED Java Applet then it wont track, WHY? because Unsigned Java Applets are only allowed to create network connections to the server they are instantiated from. Hence why we use a SIGNED applet that is allowed to communicate to any server. A customer was using some Flash Based content, Flash is prevented from crossdomain posting unless a special file (crossdomain. xml ) is placed in the root of the LMS server. See here http://kb.adobe.com/selfservice/viewContent.do?externalId=tn_14213&sliceId=1 A customer has a "server based" course they hosted (customer.content.com) the LMS was not internet addressible and so the "content" could not connect to the LMS. I hope these help point you in the right direction. Regards Martin

ResponsesInList.Title: Get cmi.core.score.raw returns an empty string.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all before posting this as a bug in the tracker I would discuss about the returned value from a call to doLMSGetValue( "cmi.core.score.raw") in a SCORM 1.2 package. The logic behind SCORM module in Moodle manage multiple attempts on complex packages (made of more than 1 sco) when all the scos are completed. Therefore, if a student make multiple tries on the single sco in the same attempt we have to manage his/her improvements. Our SCORM logic treats incompleted, failed and passed status, and let the user to improve its own results by redoing the sco. I'm arriving to the point! If a student get a score equal to zero and complete the attempt, moodle do not register it and when in the next attempt the SCOtry to retrieve this data (doLMSGetValue( "cmi.core.score.raw") )it gets an empty string. The SCORM RunTime Environment allows the return of an empty string but only if there wasn't a previous attempt or the previous attempt didn't set it. (page 36 SCORM 1.2 RTE cmi.core.score.raw definition - "Usage")

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Queries
ResponsesInList.Text: I do not believe that email notifications are available for SCORM modules. The answer to number two depends on how you setup your course and SCORM modules. If you have a single course with multiple SCORM modules then you can do the following: Create Grade Categories. For example you can create two categories, one called Practice and one called Final Mastery. See: http://docs.moodle.org/en/Grade_categories Assign each SCORM Module to the appropriate grade category and assign an ID Number to any SCORM Module you want to include in the overall course grade. In your case that would be only Unit 9. Edit the Course Grade Calculations. See: http://docs.moodle.org/en/grade/edit/tree/calculation If you have the SORM modules set up as one SCORM course with multiple SCOs, then the scoring is determined by the SCORM modules themselves. In that case, you should contact the creator of them to make this type of change.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is session time-out a possibility? What do you recommend?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Gaius, Though this message may be late for you, but just wanted to add a note which might help someone in the future: If session timeout is causing problems, it can be changed by setting it through Administration -> Server -> Session Handling and change timeout. If you want to set it to a custom value, please edit the file admin/settings/server.php and look for sessiontimeout. Find the line and add a new value to the array, for eg: the following code (bold) is for ~1 year. $temp->add(new admin_setting_configselect('sessiontimeout', get_string('sessiontimeout', 'admin'), get_string('configsessiontimeout', 'admin'), 7200, array( 30000000 => get_string('numhours', '', 8760), 14400 \ => get_string('numhours', '', 4), Thanks

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle-Lectora Interaction
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Monica, A SCORM course is responsible for sending data to an LMS (Moodle) and the LMS is responsible for saving it and reporting what was set. SCORM defines several Lesson Status settings that a SCORM course can set. There are no restrictions on which status a SCORM course can use. That means a SCORM course can set the Lesson Status to Passed and not send any value for a score. Moodle will mark a student complete when the Lesson Status is set to either "completed" or "passed". Based on your description it sounds like your course is not sending the score to Moodle. You will need to check the Lectora settings and make sure you are sending the score before setting the status.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm and Apostrophes
ResponsesInList.Text: Just chasing this one up - no one have any thoughts about it? It would be good to get some ideas

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm and Apostrophes
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Danny, Since single quotes (apostrophes) are used in coding to enclose text as data, there would probably have to be significant change to Moodle to allow an apostrophe in a filename. So my recommendation, as unpleasant as it may be, is to rename the file. Though many special characters are allowed in filenames, we have found a variety of problems throughout the years with different applications so we set the standard of using only a dash or an underscore.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm and Apostrophes
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for the reply It does seem strange, though. These files are just plain URLs, after all, and I'm escaping out the apostrophes as %27s, so it's hard to see how Moodle ever needs to see the apostrophes at all. I'd say this is a bug, really, and certainly a departure from the SCORM standard.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm and Apostrophes
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Danny - check out this discussion here for a bit of a background on this: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=85786 I don't see how supporting UTF8 filenames is part of the SCORM standard, but if you have a reference you can point us to - that's fine! Moodle 2.0 has improved file handling quite significantly, and I believe we may be able to support utf8 filenames better.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm and Apostrophes
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, I think there's a fairly big gap between supporting apostrophes (which are comfortably within ASCII) and supporting UTF8. I'm not asking Moodle to recognise an Arabic filename (yet...) As for references, well, I hate trawling through specifications as much as the next person, but I do think it's implicit in the fact that filenames have to follow the URI standard. I'd have thought that implies that any valid URI should also be a valid file. Seriously, I'm not meaning to carp. As long as I know what the position is it's possible to work around it, it's just a bit frustrating and I do think it's something that ought to be clearly documented somewhere (maybe it is, but I didn't see it!) Thanks for your help Danny

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm and Apostrophes
ResponsesInList.Text: ok - so the jump from an apostrophe to UTF8 might have been a bit much, but the biggest issue with apostrophes is that they just aren't supported well at the file/OS level here's an older page for Unix file naming rules: http://www.december.com/unix/tutor/filenames.html Different versions of Windows/Mac OS deal with them differently too... - and if you try to open a pdf with an apostrophe in earlier versions of acrobat reader...well..... Sure - you can name a file with an apostrophe, but with a SCORM object? - SCORM objects are supposed to be portable right? - so should run on a range of OS/LMS - naming files with apostrophes certainly isn't going to improve their portability, and should be avoided if possible. You obviously feel passionate about apostrophe support to SCORM files, hopefully it may be improved in 2.0 with the new file api. You could also contact your local Moodle Partner and they may be able to develop a patch for 1.9 that improves apostrophe support. ...but my reccommendation would be to avoid apostrophes when naming SCORM object files, as their portability across a range of LMS/OS will be limited.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm and Apostrophes
ResponsesInList.Text: And that is why we adopted the file naming standards we have and only using lowercase alphas, numerics, underscores, and dashes. This ensures cross-OS, cross-browser, cross-application, cross-etc.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cant run Camtasia SCORM package
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, This problem I had but I managed to track it down to the TIDY filter. This filter tidies up HTML content for all uploaded files (including SCORM packages). The TIDY settings are configured so that after the TIDY is completed only content between the body tags is returned. This means that some SCORM packages which try to load scripts etc in the head fail because the commands to load the scripts are removed by TIDY. When I disabled TIDY my SCORM package loaded fine. I have logged a bug http://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-18081 but a temporary fix is to disable the TIDY filter. Jim

ResponsesInList.Title: DSpace and Fedora (was Re: Moodle and Fedora repository?)
ResponsesInList.Text: Iris I must confess that I had always seen fedora and dspace in the same category, i.e. they were both open source repository systems that can be adapted for a variety of purposes. Both implement Dublin Core and can cope with a wide variety of file formats with multiple "streams" or content items per entry. Our principal reason for looking at dspace rather than fedora was the availability of end user tools whereas fedora is primarily a collection of web services. I must admit I had missed that fedora could support IEEE LOM. Our project, Mediterranean Virtual University , is only just beginning to look at a digital library to complement the learning enviroment (ie Moodle) so we don't have any papers so far. The aim is to provide a central resource that can be referenced by individual Moodle courses providing mainly background material and readings, rather than packaged learning objects. In this context Dublin Core metadata is sufficient for our purposes (indeed there is a debate whether the way IEEE LOM is actually used in practice really adds much more than is already in the Dublin Core). However, the main thing is to manage the authentication so that access to materials can be restricted to the appropriate students. Incidentally, we are also looking at setting up a handle server to manage and maintain links to external web resources. Course developers will then be able to reference a handle rather than a URL for a particular website secure in the knowledge that the handle will be kept up to date and pointing to the right resource even if its URL changes. In this case there is not much integration required with Moodle.

His team has been working on Fez/Fedora/Moodle for a while, and the code can be seen at http://git.catalyst.net.nz/gitweb -- I just don't know where things are at the moment, and what the exact plans are. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle and Fedora repository?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Yes we are working on Fez + Fedora and will be working on getting the objects to Moodle. There won't be direct integration with Fez/Fedora with moodle, the channel will be via SRW (a web service for searching). Why SRW? CPIT wanted not to be tied with Fedora and this would mean that we can use DSPACE which has a SRW add on too. We also made a simple repository plugin for OSLOR, so we will be creating a SRW plugin in moodle. This will be a read only (one way) access, that means getting objects from the repository and not a 2 way. If you need 2 way access from moodle and fedora, you can probably just get the fez file in include/class.fedora.php. This is fedora's API-A (read) and API-M (write) web services. Fedora is not binded to any metadata type, as it treats metadata just another datastream. While Fez can be configured to a document type that can be represented by a XSD. Since IEEE LOM has an XSD it is possible to for Fez to accept IEEE LOM and store it on Fedora. The current limitation of Fez XSD is it can't process xsd:include yet. So you will have to put any xsd:include inline. We are currently using MODS XSD as it provides better mapping to the document type that we have. There are plans to add IEEE LOM, although this is part of a different project. Hope this helps. Feel free to ask any questions.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Size SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: FTP is designed to handle HUGE uploads over a network so will carry on with it until either the file finishes or there was another error. Moodle looks at your PHP timeout settings - unpacking a 100mb zip file might take longer than your max_execution_timeout setting on the server's PHP configuration allows. Ask your admin (or change it yourself) to increase this setting and see if that fixes it (you might have to set it to something ridiculously higher then wittle it down. HTH Dave

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Size SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle's internal Zip routines aren't great and often fail when dealing with larger files. The easiest solution to this is to specify an external zip binary in admin > system paths Petr has been working solidly on this for Moodle 2.0 and with the new zip stuff in PHP 5.2.8 - it's looking much better!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM/Authorware/etc.
ResponsesInList.Text: Laura, I feel your pain. I spent the last two years hoping for such a solution, and the bottom line is that the solution only exists by pouring over the documentation on the ADLnet.org site. Here's the nutshell, but if you do a project for the navy with only this information, you will run into trouble. The best I can do for you is point you to ADLs "SCORM 2004 Conformance Requirements" pdf file and offer my consulting services I lived on the ADL product downloads page while I was learning to develop for the SCORM. The gist: For a SCO to be SCORM 2004(versions 1.3 through 1.3.3) compliant, it must find the LMS API called "API_1484_11" (ADLnet.org has sample javascript for this that pretty-much-everyone uses), call the function "Initialize("")," and call the function "Terminate("")." A SCO that conforms to these minimum requirements doesn't actually communicate any data about the student to the LMS. It just starts communication and stops it. It sounds like you will want to go at least one step beyond this and utilize the "SetValue(cmi.score.raw,"variableThatHoldsYourScore")" somewhere in between Initialize() and Terminate() to record the results of the quiz. *this only applies to the minimum requirements of the SCO, it doesn't address conformance requirements of the Content Package, Manifest or Metadata . There may be tools out there that can help you build these items, but I haven't looked for any SCORM2004 metadata generators. You can get "ManifestMaker" from the learning section of the Dreamweaver Exchange on Macromedia.com , which creates minimal SCORM 1.2 manifest files and grabs the XSD control files from the web, then use the ADL XML Transformer and the XSLT documents to convert it to a SCORM 2004 manifest. Here are the XML tools from ADLnet.org: ADL XML Transformer v 1.1 SCORM1.2 - 2004 Metadata XSLT v 1.1 SCORM1.2 - 2004 Manifest XSLT v 1.1 There is a new L5 SCORM Producer MXP on the Dreamweaver Exchange, but it is only for Dreamweaver 8, and it doesn't say what version(s) of SCORM it packages for. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Preventing students from revisiting an (SCO) exam
ResponsesInList.Text: How Moodle works with the number of attempts is allowed is whether or not the student can start a new attempt. It does not block the launch of the SCORM course repeatedly. However, when the maximum number of attempts has been reached, subsequent launches of the course sets the launch method to "Review Mode" and sets the SCORM data element core.credit to "no-credit". It is the responsibility of the SCORM course to check this data element. So it may be how your quiz was created. Sometimes you can determine which tool was used to create the content, however, seledom can you make any edits without the orginal source files. We get this type of request from our clients all the time. Sometimes we are able to help them without the source files, other times we aren't. It really depends on what type of files the tool creates. Your best bet is to go back to the supplier of the course and give them your requirements. If you do not want the user to even be able to launch the course if the number of attempts has been met/exceeded, even for review, then an edit would have to be made to Moodle. This type of edit would impact all SCORM courses.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Preventing students from revisiting an (SCO) exam
ResponsesInList.Text: We have it now! This is not a problem of Moodle, but of the QuizMaker code: the last attempt is recorded, but it doesn't prevent the student from revisiting the test again and again. As we had to work with QuizMaker, the only solution has been to change that code: We have made use of the following parameters (found in APIConstants.js): var LESSON_STATUS_PASSED = 1; //the user completed the content with a score sufficient to pass var LESSON_STATUS_COMPLETED = 2; //the user completed the content var LESSON_STATUS_FAILED = 3; //the user completed the content but his/her score was not sufficient to pass So, we add some lines to In SCORMFunctions.js if(SCORM_GetStatus() == 1 || SCORM_GetStatus() == 2 || SCORM_GetStatus() == 3){ location.href = 'already_attempted.html'; } The page "already_attempted.html" should be added to the package. This goes here: if (SCORM_GetLessonMode() != MODE_REVIEW){ if (SCORM_IsContentInBrowseMode()){ WriteToDebug("Setting Status to Browsed"); blnResult = SCORM_CallLMSSetValue("cmi.core.lesson_status", SCORM_BROWSED); } else{ //only set the status to incomplete if it's not attempted yet if (SCORM_GetStatus() == LESSON_STATUS_NOT_ATTEMPTED){ WriteToDebug("Setting Status to Incomplete"); blnResult = SCORM_CallLMSSetValue("cmi.core.lesson_status", SCORM_INCOMPLETE); } } //we want to set the exit type to suspend immediately because some LMS's only store data if they get a suspend request blnResult = blnResult && SCORM_CallLMSSetValue("cmi.core.exit", SCORM_TranslateExitTypeToSCORM(DEFAULT_EXIT_TYPE)); } WriteToDebug("Calling InitializeExecuted with parameter-" + blnResult); InitializeExecuted(blnResult, ""); if(SCORM_GetStatus() == 1 || SCORM_GetStatus() == 2 || SCORM_GetStatus() == 3){ location.href = 'already_attempted.html'; } Find the file attached. Fernando

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error when uploading SCORM package
ResponsesInList.Text: There are two major points of concern here. The first is that you are using 1.9.2, which means that it is very likely that there are 3+ months worth of solid mod/scorm hacking that you don't have. Please upgrade at your earliest convenience. Secondly, the fact that you managed to upload a package without a manifest file, and it still worked, most likely means that you have some form of caching working (browser/web server ), that is distorting the outcome. Where ever there is JavaScript development going on, it is always important to rule out caching issues by clearing your browser cache (clear cache, close browser, start again ....). If after upgrade, these problems still persist, then get in touch with me, and I'll test your package (so long as you can provide me with repeatable steps etc.). Cheers, Piers Harding.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is SCORM worth it?
ResponsesInList.Text: I believe we're reaching a consensus view, no doubt the obvious one, but still worth setting out... 1. That the pressure to use a SCORM-compliant VLE, from government sources in the UK, but especially from US government departments, makes getting SCORM certification a very high priority; 2. That the spread of Moodle may be hampered by it not achieving SCORM certification, especially in those fields where SCORM compliance is considered mandatory (I would add that some fund-holders appear to be specifying SCORM-compliance even though they don't know what they're asking for!); 3. That the benefit of being able to create presentational material elsewhere and upload it efficiently as a SCORM module, makes generating content of this kind very easy, and cost-effective in a commercial environment; 4. That although the SCORM content itself may be simple and inherently presentational or instructional, once brought into Moodle other more interactive features can be run alongside this material - attempting to achieve the best of both worlds; 5. That for those creating courses entirely in Moodle, SCORM is something of a distraction; 6. That SCORM-only courses lack much of the interest and interaction available through Moodle, and the SCORM model may be limiting or even detrimental educationally. Not all the contributors have expressed their agreement with all of these conclusions, but it is clear that even those having no interest in using SCORM still believe that we have to get certification. I suppose MD would rightly ask: what about the money? The only thing missing I can see is that we have not got a definitive list of Moodle activities (or resources) that you couldn't have in a SCORM module. Any offers? Thanks again, John

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is SCORM worth it?
ResponsesInList.Text: Excellent summary! I suppose MD would rightly ask: what about the money? Or the quality patches. There are tons of things that are important, and SCORM is without a doubt one of them. Now, mod/scorm exists, and this can be tackled by people with a definitive interest in it, and the ability to devote time and effort. How to start...? A gallery of good quality SCORM objects that show a problem or bug in mod/scorm ... a slowly growing collection of patches that fix those problems Funding is only one of the aspects of getting those patches going. Perhaps it's the easiest way, but not the only way. Note! There is literally a ton of buggy SCORM content out there. A good chunk of complaints about mod/scorm have to do with SCORM packages that are horribly broken. (Why do I say this? At Catalyst we had a few clients ask us to "fix" mod/scorm so that it'd run their existing content correctly. What we found were bugs in the SCORM packages. Everytime. While good, it was actually frustrating in that I wanted to use the opportunity to fix mod/scorm issues for the wider community. Not to say that mod/scorm is free of bugs but... it's a jungle out there. Anyone going to SF Moot, take a moment to talk to Jonathan Newman about this.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is SCORM worth it?
ResponsesInList.Text: I don't know how I missed this interesting discussion while it was ramping up. I'd like to jump in here because I think that there is a temptation, in the Moodle community, to disparage content delivery which is not inherently based on social constructionism . I don't discount Moodle one bit for its adherence to social constructionism . I think it's great. But I can say decisively that it's not my bread and butter. The truth is that, in the world of corporate training, social constructionism is just not of value for many types of content. We can rail against that by dissing SCORM, but it isn't SCORM's fault: it's the nature of the global economic system. For example: if I need to teach a learner how to quickly determine whether a load is too heavy to lift with the lift truck he or she is driving, then a forum is not going to work all that well. Especially if my (corporate) client wants learners to move through the course independently, and get a certification without ever taking the time to establish the kinds of relationships necessary to social constructionism. A Flash activity, on the other hand, which allows the learner to drag different loads onto the forks, drag the forks up and down, and move the lift truck around--that's going to have a substantial impact on how my learner thinks about reading the little weight rating placard on the lift truck. Especially if the little model lift truck will noisily wreck when loaded with too much weight. Flash is the best tool, right now, for creating interactive "learning objects" of this type. SCORM is merely the standard that lets my client see whether the learner successfully completed this activity. I usually try to steer clients away from using authorware, because revising authorware products is so difficult, and SCORM import of authorware exports is never as predictable as SCORM import of what I can code myself. Sometimes people say that "SCORM content" is boring, but what they mean is that formulaic authorware content is boring. You can create content just as boring with a Moodle lesson module, if you're being a dink. In my opinion, authorware SCORM isn't really the point: it's the superb interactivity provided by a combination of custom Flash objects and SCORM. A

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is SCORM worth it?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, In short, the answer to the question "Is SCORM worth it?" (I'm assuming you mean having it working in Moodle), IMHO, the answer is a resounding yes. As Martin said, it's on the "absolutely necessary" category on a lot of people's tick lists. If anyone's done a search of these forums about SCORM they may well have found a number of posts by me slating it. I'll repeat, I don't like SCORM, neither as a teacher nor as a developer. As a teacher, which is the most important consideration in e-learning, it promotes the very worst of educational models, referred to by many as dump 'n' pump. It's exactly what's wrong with a lot of school and university education where they've tried to cut costs by increasing testing and decreasing teaching, in other words an unbalanced educational model. As an educator, I want to be able to customise the results I generated by e-learning interactions. A single % grade doesn't really tell you much about a student's abilities or why they're not performing as you'd like them to. I want to be able to look at a range of activity data and analyse what's wrong and be able to do something about it. If a student breaks a fork-lift truck because he didn't understand a part of the training but passed it anyway, I want to know how and why it happened so that I can make the teaching materials better. As a developer, SCORM hurts. It's so big and so complicated and so difficult to deal with, that you're at the mercy of a few specialist 'experts' who make a pretty penny from consultancy and development fees. If you just want to deploy a quiz, a test, a questionnaire, a survey, or whatever, then use one of Moodle's many great modules that do the job much better, with less hassle and not so steep a learning curve or expensive consultancy fees. BTW , you can effectively simulate 80% of the content of Cambridge ESOL (English for Speakers of Other Languages) exams with only the core Moodle modules. Also, SCORM is incredibly inefficient. You have to create self-contained 'packages' which may be great for selling food (although we seem to be having a bit of a problem with food packaging around the world at the moment) and consumer goods in shops, but doesn't really fit in with good IT practices. I don't know about you but I quite like the benefits offered by Object Oriented Programming, layering, sharing media resources and so on. We're having a pretty good go at getting rid of the need to create mountains of packaging waste (not to mention the environmental costs of manufacture and distribution) through ideas such as downloading MP3s. Are we bent on creating the electronic equivalent with SCORM? How much server space will we have to take up before we say enough is enough? The scary thing is, although Moodle is great and it's getting more and more popular and it's one of the few LMSs with a successful learning model, it's encouraging people towards using SCORM by not providing an effective alternative for deploying Flash. Flash is the de-facto e-learning platform and at the moment, the only way to deploy Flash e-learning interactions in Moodle and store students results is to use the unfinished 3rd party plug-in Flash Activity Module that Jamie Pratt developed for the University of Barcelona some years ago. It's incompatible with any Flash e-learning interactions later than Flash MX 2004 (that's Flash 6 and we're currently on Flash 9 and Flash 10 is soon to be released). I won't go into the many reasons why Flash 9 and later versions are ideal for e-learning here. It's true, there are a number of way of deploying Flash in Moodle but none of them, except the FAM, can store student activity data. We really need a heads-up on this one guys or people are going to continue to create unsatisfactory e-learning interactions in Flash using SCORM and continuing the dump 'n' pump learning model. Let's set the bar higher and make Moodle extra special. Another multiple-choice test, anyone?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is SCORM worth it?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello all, this thread continues to provide incredible information and insight! I think that Amy so succinctly stated that “in the world of corporate training, social constructionism is just not of value for many types of content”. I wish I could have put it that way in my earlier post talking about the role SCORM plays in the corporate environment. I posted a while ago my thoughts on this and indicated the big problem we have is that there is a difference between training and education. After looking up several definitions for training you can find “activity leading to skilled behavior”, “To make proficient with specialized instruction and practice”, “…organized attempt to assist learning through instruction, observation, or practice…” and so on. The recurring theme in the definitions is Activity/Practice. I have always explained to clients and students that training as the practical application of learned skills through exercises (repetition). This is what the corporate world is after. We must be able to create good looking, engaging activity -based content. I am somewhat conflicted here because I not only consult in the corporate environment but I also teach at a local College. When I teach Intro to Safety Risk Management, for example, we look at the history of the industry, the industrial revolution, etc. It is important to understand where we have been and how we got where we are. However, I have to change my approach when “teaching” students how to fill out an injury/illness log. I simply need to ensure they know how to fill out the form correctly. So a blended approach works well. The same holds true for new employee orientations. Companies simply want to communicate a set of requirements, policies and/or procedures an employee must follow and check that they understand them (quiz). They are not interested in educating the worker on the history and evolution of the corporate environment, employment law, etc. and get their thoughts on the subject and share them with other new hires. However, the same company offering management training to up-and-comers might want to adopt this approach. That is where having a corporate LMS is beneficial. Content is what we need to separate from the SCORM conversation. Through my own research and discovery on this topic I have found that something else Amy stated is true (I guess I am an Amy fan). That is one can make boring content using the Moodle lesson module, as well as using SCORM authoring programs! Those of us that need SCORM most likely need it because that is the accepted compliance standard right now (and yes, it allows for portability. I can create a SCORM compliant content package and distribute it to many different clients). These packages create consistency. No one talks about this too much. Social constructionism changes the message over time. Certain content needs to be static which ensures a consistent message. You know every employee that went through the orientation got the same message! I am over-simplifying a bit here to save time/space! So in a nutshell, my corporate clients have to meet a regulatory requirement for training on certain job tasks (content), ensure a consistent message and verify successful completion of stated objectives (SCORM). And as I stated in my earlier posts, my job is to consult with them on how to best include the other approaches into their corporate LMS and allow employees to return and continue with education (Employee Development). So SCORM compliance is a must, even if Moodle contains a Flash activity module. We must be able to serve the industries that are seeking certain compliance standards. My business depends on this! For what it’s worth, thanks for reading, Blaine H.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is SCORM worth it?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Marshal & everyone, The critical phrase in your post is "... so they will work in any VLE..." It really does depend on what you mean by "work". I can create a content package that be displayed by any VLE in which I can add a hyperlink, and without using SCORM at all, just by creating a simple HTML website. SCORM offers: - tracking of page views (note: this doesn't mean the learner has learnt anything, just that they've clicked on the link for that page); - bookmarking of pages for coming back to (note: I have not yet met a learner that makes use of this. Anyone that wants to come back to pages ought to be able to use their browser bookmarks or a tool like Diigo, a right often denied by content package designers/procurers) - passing of final results to the VLE (note: is this really granular enough) A few years ago, I was in an open meeting with Dan Rehak (one of SCORM's) architects, where he stated categorically that SCORM is pedagogically not neutral and inappropriate for some situations (eg. Primary and Higher education). According to Rehak, "SCORM is essentially about a single-learner, self-paced and self-directed. It has a limited pedagogical model unsuited for some environments." This is mainly a consequence of the needs of the main initiators of SCORM: the US federal government in general, and the Department of Defence in particular. Their needs are mainly in the area of training for specific systems and situations by people who are not generally in full time education. This need is addressed very well by the spec, but "SCORM has nothing in it about collaboration. This makes it inappropriate for use in HE and K-12". (from Google's cache of the CETIS website: http://www.cetis.ac.uk/content/20021002000737 ) "The risk is that SCORM is being adopted in areas beyond its intended area of application and without such careful consideration of the changes needed to support pedagogical goals as well as the technological ones." Marshall: http://www.ascilite.org.au/conferences/perth04/procs/marshall.html I would argue that SCORM is based on a behaviourist model of learning that works well in a military training context (or any situation where you are expecting learners to come out with specific, simple behaviours), but does not work at all well in the far more complex formal education contexts. SCORM assumes that everything the learner needs is inside the content package. Whereas, certainly in a Moodle case, much of what the learner needs is definitely outside of that package (and can't be brought inside), eg. forums, glossaries, wikis, assignments etc - basically anything that involves the learner interacting with anyone other than the computer. To my mind (and this is personal opinion only), SCORM is over-rated and over-complex, and its use should be limited to those situations where it best fits, as described above. It is an irrelevance for most formal education contexts, and also for most corporate learning contexts. I see it being specified a lot for compliance training, but all it does is allows managers to report that learning has been delivered, not necessarily that learning has taken place. (I'm with Donald Clark on this one). Please excuse the rant. Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is SCORM worth it?
ResponsesInList.Text: Mark, interesting. I would add that there are 3 words I use with clients: training, education,and learning. I will leave it up to readers to decide on their own definitions. But those of us in the regulatory/compliance arena know that much of the required "training" starts with basic knowledge of particular standards, regulations, guidelines or "rules". Building on these we can show/communicate examples of how to comply with said stds., regs., etc. SCORM and even non-SCORM (HTML) content can certainly perform this basic function. However, training should go beyond just simple compliance with a need to train on a particular reg. or rule via one-way communication. This is why I think Moodle is a great tool. One can bridge training and education, thus facilitating/enhancing the learning process. By using SCORM to satisfy the need to force workers into viewing each page and listen to each presentation before advancing (navigation controls) and verifying they viewed each page and correctly answered each quiz question before the system "passes" them we satisfy the basic compliance requirement. Then with Moodle we can build other activities, resources, assessments, etc. around this simple SCORM thus taking simple corporate training one step further. In the corporate setting there is high demand for compliance training. Clients first want to ensure they can prove the training was delivered/viewed by the employee. They usually worry about follow-up evaluations to ensure the training was effective later. SCORM does this job for us. Our jobs as consultants is to educate the client that while we have these employees engaged we should take advantage of the learning opportunity and not just verify they sat there for a specified period of time looking/listening to something! This is why I value LMS (Moodle). At the end of the day, for this sort of scenario - forget it. However I also do some consultancy/training work for training organisations who have engaged Content Development Company XYZ to make up some specific training and who are using Moodle primarily as a delivery and tracking mechanism for such content. This is often compliance type training (i.e. all our employees must complete training in <whatever> to meet legislative requirements) and so many of the social constructivist elements of Moodle are not required. In fact most of Moodle's functionality isn't required in this situation. When it comes to these clients, the ability for Moodle to run seamlessly with SCORM content is paramount, and anyone who has read some of my other posts on this subject will know that I was on the verge of no longer recommending Moodle as an option to such clients because of this very issue. I have seen SCORM/Gradebook interaction work perfectly in v1.8, but it was with content developed by Content Development Company XYZ (who knew what they were doing when it came to SCORM) rather than using eXe (which was done by me who knows very little about SCORM). In summary, for many users I believe that this whole issue is a 'SCORM in a teacup', but if Moodle wants to be considered as a genuine alternative to Overpriced Proprietary LMS XYZ, particularly in the corporate sector, then being 100% SCORM compliant is essential.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: "The page cannot be found" Error when starting a SCORM course
ResponsesInList.Text: If you haven't already, try using one of the SCORM packages in the SCORM Repository . Make sure you are using the SCORM activity and not the IMS Content Package resource when adding the SCORM package. Also, if you are not using the latest version of Moodle, you may want to consider upgrading. If you still get the same error message then the problem is with Moodle. If not, then you need to look at your SCORM package. Depending on the tool you use to create the SCORM package, some of these may not apply, but each of these can cause a problem. The SCORM course must be packaged in a "zip" format and contain all course files as well as the "imsmanifest. xml " file in the root folder of the course. Note: For very large SCORM courses you may need to cheat on the packaging as noted below. The "imsmanifest.xml" file must point to at least one file for launching the first SCO. If the file to be launched is not in the root folder, then a realtive path must be included as part of the launch filename. After uploading the SCORM pacage as a SCORM activity, don't unzip the file, just select "Choose". Moodle will take care of unzipping the files, reading the imsmanifest and launching the file indicated. If the SCORM package is very large in size, the server may not extract all the files from the package. This is a limitation of the PHP zip/unzip function not Moodle. This can lead to blank pages and missing files. Exactly what size? It depends on a number of things. Configuration of server and PHP time limits, number of files in the package, size of files in the package, etc. Verify that the SCORM package is SCORM compliant with the ADL SCORM Conformance Test Suite aapropriate to the version of SCORM being used. You can download the test suites at: http://www.adlnet.gov/downloads/index.aspx

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm2004 Support
ResponsesInList.Text: To make the delivery of multiple SCO SCORM courses more flexible and automated, SCORM 1.3 (aka SCORM 2004) introduced new navigation functionality called sequencing. This is the area that most LMS applications do not fully support yet. The reason, it is not as simple as adding some fields in a database to store information and report on it. It involves reading the imsmanifest and analyzing how all the pieces fit together and how they should flow. Prior versions of SCORM were fairly straight forward in comparison. The advantage to this type of navigation is being able to make a course that contains multiple paths through it, and package each path as a separate SCO. Then the LMS determines which SCO to present next based on criteria in the imsmanifest and the learners performance in the previous SCO. Of course, there are other changes that were made in SCORM 2004, and not all LMS applications have been fully updated with all the changes. Most tools do not even fully support SCORM 2004, but as SCORM 2004 sequencing becomes more popular and demanded, both tools and LMS applications will have to be updated or lose market share.
