As you go from page to page, no state information is retained. For example, if page1.html called LMSInitialize, when you went to page2.html nothing persisted to remember that LMSInitialize has already been called. Since the SCO must remember at least the state of the communication session with the API, a method must be devised to remember this information. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: AICC course errors
ResponsesInList.Text: Carol, It’s been a while since I did anything AICC, but my guess is that the LMS is communicating with the Splash Screen window (window launched by the LMS) and does not recognize the second (content window launched from first window) window. Typically, the LMS can only communicate with the window it calls.  This window then needs to stay open for the duration of the lesson (even if it is in the background).  Other windows can be opened from the main window, but are not usually trackable by the LMS.  Upon lesson completion, the lesson would be closed from the primary (first) window. So, can you reconfigure your lesson to test if tracking works when the LMS launches the content window versus the Splash Screen? V/R Les Amidon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm other tracks
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Petr, the element reported (cmi.suspend_data) is a not mandatory, but an expected field in SCORM standard. The SCORM module for Moodle can't understand what this data are about, so print it only in the form Element and Value. This field are generally used by tools (such as Articulate) that produce Learning Objects to store data used to remember some things, such as the last page visited or the visited page. Which software are you using to produce the LOs? Bye, Luca.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm other tracks
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Luca! Just minor correction: cmi.suspend_data element is mandatory field for LMS (both SCORM 1.2 and 2004), but is not mandatory for use by SCO (or Learning Object). That is the only correction. cmi.suspend_data is "custom data" storage for Learning Object - data format depends on authoring tool, objects used in LO etc. LMS must store this data element "as is" and return it to LO on request also "as is". Vyacheslav Shchinov CourseLab Development Team

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm other tracks

ResponsesInList.Title: SCORM, Moodle, Suspend data and quotes (a fix)
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi There, For those aware, there is an issue with Moodle up to and including 1.8 where when attempting to send a suspend data, you will receive a JavaScript error that manifests itself usually in the form of a timeout or a message stating that it expected a semicolon. I was able to find that the reason for this is because of the way in which the SCORM api handles the suspend data string (or any string which contains double quotes). Looking at the source, it evaluates the string as code... To try and clarify what I'm describing, below is the element and corresponding value that produces the error: Command to be executed: LMSSetValue('cmi.suspend_data','

') Actual element and value evaluated by SCORM API: cmi.suspend_data="

";

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM, Moodle, Suspend data and quotes (a fix)
ResponsesInList.Text: This is a general gotcha for any string value passed in the SCORM API. If that string is going to be included in a evaluate statement, it must first be escaped and "neutralized" to avoid unexpected attempts at parsing or execution of part of the string. Think for example of what could happen with a fill-in-the blank interaction in a programming course. If the API element is reciprocal (i.e. if get must be able to get back the same value as was set), then the escape encoding for "neutralization" must be supported by a corresponding unescape decoding prior to returning the value. The same decoding must take place if the value is provided in a report. This has implications for data storage in the LMS, since an escaped string typically requires more space than a unescaped string. If you do the escaping/unescaping in the SCO, you have to absorb the extra storage, meaning that the actual string values you can set and get may be smaller than the lengths allowed by the API. However this gives you the greatest portability in case you use a LMS that is not as careful as it should be with this issue.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM, Moodle, Suspend data and quotes (a fix)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Claude, Escaping the strings should be the responsibility of the LMS as the SCO will never know what language they will ultimately be used in (different escape methods). As per the SCORM 1.2 standards as well, cmi.suspend_data is of data type CMIString4096 which allows for the double quotation marks. The player sends a string that does contain quotation marks, which are escaped in such a way that the " is recognized as a character. That is all that's required. This won't cause any problems with a "reciprocal API element", as once the string which I made include the literal \" characters is sent to the evaluate function, it will be stored in the same way the player sent it. I don't forsee any issues with data storage in the LMS, as I said previously it will be storing the same information the player original intended to send anyway. I do see that there is an outstanding bug report for Moodle in regards to the way it handles quotation marks in cmi.suspend_data, it exists in 1.8 and doesn't mention an ETA on resolution. In any case, I thought I'd pass this information along to see if it would expidite the process for our client

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Teacher seeing Student SCO in Review mode
ResponsesInList.Text: IMHO such a feature should use a combination of the Review mode and suspend/resume. It is definitely beyond the scope of standard SCORM behavior, but there is no reason why an instructor cannot be given access to a student course's "latest state", at any time. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: AICC cross-domain issues.
ResponsesInList.Text: Cross-servers issues were not a problem years ago when the HACP protocol was designed. Unfortunately that was a long time ago. Since then, browser vendors have been forced to tighten security because of the many cross-scripting exploits that were not envisioned when the Internet was a gentler place. Some of the specifications, such as the AICC HACP specification, that depended on a relaxed attitude regarding cross-scripting and single origin started running into trouble with this a while ago. In some cases, people have discovered this only relatively recently because they had been using older browsers or insecure settings. The way things stand now, browsers make it much harder to continue with unsafe web practices. This has never been a problem with SCORM, since SCORM was designed from the start to work within the normal security constraints imposed by browsers and to take advantage of the ECMAScript standard. This means that the housekeeping content provided by the LMS and the course payload must come from the same server. The SCORM API (IEEE Standard 1484.11.2) was intended keep the communication between the content and the LMS as simple as possible so that the content implementer does not have to worry about internet protocols. In the IEEE/SCORM API, it is is the responsibility of the LMS to provide a client side script object that the content can call directly, with simple function calls, to get and set data values. SCORM does of course allow launching and tracking of content that comes from different servers, or from a different server than the LMS. When that is implemented, however, it is is entirely invisible to the content: It is handled at the network infrastructure level, where it can be managed, controlled, audited and monitored, using specialized network techniques. This is much safer than creating or perpetuating vulnerabilities on the client side. It is very hard to manage, control, audit or monitor connections from individual browsers to different servers, even when that is possible at all.  Also, this does not necessarily require a lot of complexity, since the necessary components are often already in place in most enterprises. The bottom line, though, is that cross-server security is something to take very seriously, because the bad guys are constantly looking for opportunities there. As application developers, we are focused on making our applications work, but sometimes this may cause us to forget about the vulnerabilities. Unless you have an expert on board to set up, manage and monitor security at the proper level (network infrastructure), I recommend that you stay with the simple, proven solution of running LMS and content from the safe server.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cannot find LMS API ...
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Alan, First of all, i didn't ask you wich version of SCORM are you using. 2004 or 1.2. version? If you are using 2004, the API instance object has this name as I told you "win.API_1484_11". You must be using a wrapper file to look up for the API an communicate with the LMS. I attach you the code for the functions to look up for the API. function _GetAPI(win) { var ScanForAPI = function(win) { var nFindAPITries = 500; // paranoid to prevent runaway var objAPI = null; var bOK = true; var wndParent = null; while ((!objAPI)&&(bOK)&&(nFindAPITries>0)) var wndParent = null; var wndOpener = null; try { wndParent = win.parent; } catch(e) { } try { wndOpener = win.opener; } catch(e) { } if ((wndParent != null) && (wndParent != win)) { _gAPI = ScanForAPI(wndParent); } if ((_gAPI == null) && (wndOpener != null)) { _gAPI = ScanForAPI(wndOpener); } } And when you try to initialize communication you use this code on your function: _GetAPI(window); if (_gAPI == null) alert("NO API FOUND"); I hope it helps, luck! Agustina.

Discussion thread here talks about having a script of some sort check automatically for completion, but nobody goes into detail.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How do you get Moodle to act like a compliance-oriented LMS?
ResponsesInList.Text: We are drafting some plans (aimed towards 1.9) that will address this kind of usage. Some aspects are - a re-worked gradebook (from a pull API to a push API internally) - some facilities to "chain" activities within a course - a per-user transcript - course metadata of the type "provides: skills Z and Y", and "pre-requisites: skills M and P" - enrolment plugins that enforce pre-requisites ("before joining this course you need M and P - click here for some courses that help you learn that or email the teacher to ask for an exception") There might be an opportunity to sponsor some of those developments to make them happen earlier

ResponsesInList.Title: We're getting further into gradebook territory but...
ResponsesInList.Text: I assume you mean by a user someone who has already enrolled in the course, but hasn't completed it. In Course Settings you can set an enrollment expiry notification date, but that doesn't help you take preventative action. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What is the right SCORM folder?
ResponsesInList.Text: The SCORM package that you upload is unzipped by Moodle in the moodledata directory that you specified when you installed Moodle. Within the moodledata directory, there is a directory with a numeric id for each course (this is the "course files" area of the course). Within that directory there is a moddata directory containing directories for the various Moodle activities . If the course has one or more SCORM activities, you will see a directory named scorm. Within that directory, you will see more numbered directories. These correspond to the numeric id's assigned by Moodle in the database . Within each of those directories, you'll see the unzipped package. Of course you (as teacher) can navigate to the package using Moodle's files interface (Administration -> Files). Naturally your students cannot do this unless you give them the capability, which is possible (but probably not wise) in Moodle 1.7. If you or your students have shell access to the machine, you can also navigate to the SCORM directory using the OS command line. On my linux system, for example, 'cd /var/moodledata/10/moddata/scorm/9' gets me to one of my SCORM packages. Modifying a SCORM package in place within Moodle is dangerous. It is infinitely more dangerous if you allow students to do it! That consideration alone should dissuade you from doing it. Furthermore, I don't see the didactic value of this exercise. I would make this exercise an upload Assignment which instructs students to create a SCORM package using the RELOAD editor. They create the package, preview it, make some more changes, preview it again, etc., until it meets the requirements you set out in the Assignment. Students submit the finished zipped SCORM package to the Assignment. Then YOU load their packages into Moodle. That way students can see what other students have done. For real didactic value, make it a Workshop.

ResponsesInList.Text: Just found the following in the Install FAQ. It's the very first item. I probably won't get a chance to look at whether my linux hosted demo version has AcceptPathInfo on or not till the weekend. Also wondering whether there is some equivalent setting for windows servers? Just thought I'd post now, in case this helps anyone. Whenever I try to access or view a file that I uploaded, I get an error "File not Found" For example: Not Found: The requested URL /moodle/file.php/2/myfile.jpg was not found on this server. Your web server needs to be configured to allow the part of the URL after a script name to be passed directly to the script. This is usually enabled in Apache 1, but is usually disabled by default in Apache 2. To turn it on, add this line to your httpd.conf, or to a .htaccess file in your local directory (see the Install documentation for more details): AcceptPathInfo on Note, this will ONLY work for Apache versions 2.x. If you are not using Apache 2 and you still have this problem (unlikely) then you can switch Moodle to use an alternative method. The disadvantages are a slight loss of performance for your users and you won't be able to use relative links within HTML resources. To use this alternative method: login as Admin, go into the "Configure Variables" page and change the setting for " slasharguments ". You should now be able to access your uploaded files.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: scorm applications
ResponsesInList.Text: I assume they are zipped SCORM packages? The normal way to do it is to create a new SCORM activity (see screenshot). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM in 1.7 not working
ResponsesInList.Text: " How do we tell the LMS that sco has been changed when we jump from the current topic to another topic by the second menu? How do we send to LMS  the infomation about the new topic?" You don't. Only the LMS can change the status of its table of content/activity menu, or the SCO the LMS believes that it is running. What you are trying to do is not supported by SCORM. You cannot replace the LMS provided table of content or activity menu with your own. If you have navigation inside a SCO that uses "sub-SCOs" (what I call a "super-SCO"), the LMS will still only see and track one SCO. In SCORM 2004 there is a way to ask the LMS to navigate to another activity which then causes another SCO to be launched. But the LMS still owns the navigation structure.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: newbie SCORM question
ResponsesInList.Text: Analyzing a launchable resource for all the components it might need is outside the scope of what Reload is designed to do. Similarly, a SCORM player doesn't know what is inside the SCO or what a SCO uses -- all it does is launch the SCO. A resource element is a "digital descriptor of a resource". It has two purposes. If it describes a SCO, it provides the URL required to launch the SCO. This is typically a URL relative to the "root" of the package, which is the directory where the imsmanifest. xml file itself is found in the package. The other purpose is to provide a full inventory of the files that are required to play the SCO and that are included in the package, along with their relative path so that they can be imported and placed properly in a web server 's directory structure for delivery. When you add a resource element in Reload, it is your responsibility to include all the files the resource will need. If those files will be included in the package, the href attribute for each file element must be a relative URL, with the proper relative path relationship to the launchable URL for the resource (the launch URL is the value of the href attribute for that resource). If the files will remain on some other remote server, then the URL for a file must be a fully qualified URL (fully qualified domain name + path). Note that external files don't necessarily have to be included in the file collection, since neither the packager nor the LMS will know anything about them. Note also that modern security features may make execution problematic for the learner when files used in client side scripting or active behavior come from a different server; you may want to give this some consideration. BTW , each resource element describes either a launchable resource or a collection of files referenced by a dependency declared in one or more other resource elements. By "launchable" I mean launchable by the LMS as the resource used by an item in the organization element of the manifest. If a SCO launches other stuff that is not represented in the manifest. In SCORM 1.2, a launchable resource is always a SCO. Unless you are sharing files between resources (e.g. shared class files, etc.), or you have a preset collection that is easier to keep track of that way, it makes more sense to declare all the files in the resource element that describes the SCO.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 1.7 SCORM Issues
ResponsesInList.Text: I found out solutions for the issues I mentioned: 1. This is because in the file mod/scorm/locallib.php, the "Enter course" button has a form target property set to "newwin". I haven't seent this attribute before but I think this is what causing it to open 2 new windows instead of 1. I changed it to "_self" and only 1 new window opens to launch the course. 2. ResponsesInList.Title: cmi.comments overrun handling
ResponsesInList.Text: A quick question for the devs: how are overruns handled for the long strings, such as cmi.comments and cmi.suspend_data? Does Moodle just post a general error code and not do anything? Does it loop back around and overwrite itself? Does the server just die? I'm asking because I'm using both of these fields for storing relatively large amounts of text data that can easily exceed the 4K character limit in the SCORM specs. Said SCORM specs don't seem to provide for what happens if the SCO tries to write to a full field; they only specify that the field's maximum size is 4096 characters. I guess my question is then: how gracefully does Moodle fail at this? What feedback does the SCO get?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: cmi.comments overrun handling
ResponsesInList.Text: According to the SCORM specification, if a SCO tries to set a string value that is longer than the allowed size, the SCORM runtime returns "false" and sets an error state. So, all a SCO has to do is check the return value and, if it is not "true", get the error value for more detail. No error needs to be shown to the user if the SCO can recover gracefully.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: cmi.comments overrun handling
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you once more, Mr. Ostyn. I should've read the specs more carefully, I guess.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM packages from eXe in Internet Explorer
ResponsesInList.Text: Paul: We've looked at it today and think that we have cracked it. Earlier in our SCORM days we had a lot of problems with IE not calling the onunload functions before actually unloading. To resolve this we included an IE specific function called onbeforeunload. It appears that this is causing problems with the SCORM quiz functions. We have removed this from some of our eXe packages that have SCORM Quizzes in them and it seems to be working fine now in IE7. I need to test a bit more, but am hoping that this is the fix. If you want to try it out yourself you can unzip a SCORM package created with eXe and modify any .html files that include the eXe SCORM quiz. Try removing the onbeforeunload() within the body tag, rezip the package and import into Moodle again. If this is truly the fix (and i'll test some more today) then the next eXe release 0.19 will include this fix. brent.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM doesn't find API
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi, every resource in a scorm package could be an asset (a resource without tracking interaction) or a sco (a resouce that get and set element from the LMS). In the imsmanifest. xml file in you scorm package every resource must defined as asset or sco. If you don't define your resources types, the SCORM Module set them as assets. Here you find two examples. 
```text
 



    <resource identifier='delta1' type="webcontent" adlcp:scormtype="sco" href="delta01.html">



    </resource>







    <resource identifier='gamma2' type="webcontent" adlcp:scormtype="asset" href="gamma02.html">



    </resource>
```
 Probably in your package some resources types are not defined or they are defined as assets. Please check the manifest file. Bobo.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM doesn't find API
ResponsesInList.Text: If you use 1.5.x and you get error about API you must edit the imsmanifest.xml file in your package in the way I said in http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=49530#234691 post. If you use 1.6.x you still need to change your manifest file but you need to use 1.6.2+ or better 1.6.3 because in prior release there was a bug in scoring reporting. If you intend "completed", "incomplete", "passed" or "failed" for "course made", or "partially made" or "finished" this depends on what the SCO passes to Moodle SCORM Module. If no lesson status is passed you can't see it anywhere. If you can run a scorm package as administrator and with the Moodle debug mode enabled the SCORM Module will show you all the successful communication between SCO and SCORM Module. NOTE that administrator activities will tracked but not saved so you can see communication (in debug mode) but you can't see changes in SCORM module pages. Bobo.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM doesn't find API
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I'm pretty new to Moodle, but I have been using Blackboard and some other LMS's with Flash and Captivate for awhile. If you are using Captivate, I've found that you need to change how SCORM looks for the API.  By default, it looks from the "Bottom Up".  You need to change the value.  After publishing a SCORM package using Captivate, open the HTML file that is created and look for the following line of code.  It should be somewhere in the first 30 lines: var g_intAPIOrder = 0; Change this value to a 1 and then try uploading it again.  This will cause SCORM to look for the API starting at the top.  This has almost always fixed the problem for me. Steve

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM doesn't find API
ResponsesInList.Text: Looking for the API from the top down is definitely not SCORM conformant. In addition, it guarantees that your SCO will not be compatible with any wrapper that might be necessary in the future to adapt it without recoding to work with SCORM 2004, for example. That setting in Captivate should be looked at as a desperate measure to deal with a particular nonconformant LMS. Moodle should not need it--look at the other hints earlier in the thread.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM doesn't find API
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I know that top down is not SCORM conformant.  I am using Moodle without making any changes.  It was just a recommendation as something to try. I have used other LMS systems like Blackboard and WebCT that in "some" cases, the SCO package wasn't working properly and this change was a short-term work around until we could get the LMS to look at the package correctly. In an active semester, you don't always have time to work out LMS issues when you have upset professors and students that can't access their content, so you do something that gets the ball rolling until you can work out the details in your LMS. My post was not intended to be misleading, but just something to try.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Articulate Presenter SCORM packages appear as "animation not loaded"
ResponsesInList.Text: Here's my take on this problem. I've been known to be wrong, but having run into a similar issue recently I think it may be helpful. A URL that contains a query string that is as a parameter in the query string in a URL must be URL escaped, so that the "?" character in that parameter is escaped. BTW , other reserved characters within parameters must be escaped also. It seems that Apache is be a little more forgiving than IIS when encountering the syntax error, but Apache you would also see problems if there were additional parameters (e.g. foo=1&bar=2) in the URL used as parameter, and the reserved characters were not properly encoded, because the parsing would not work a expected. Whatever is responsible for correctly encoding this (here it looks like it might Articulate rather than moodle) would have to be fixed.

I checked my SCORM course with ADL Test Suite without getting errors or warnings. Next, I debuged where the error comes from, it is cmi.interactions.n.id with the following data type: CMIIdentifier The format CMIIdentifier specifies a alpha-numeric string without internal spaces. Some of my id's have an hypher in it, that is not allowed in moodle. In another documentations it is declared as alpha-numeric string inclusive . and hypher without spaces. I think, that the regular expression for CMIIdentifier should be the following: CMIIdentifier = '^\\w[\\w|\\-]{1,255}$'; Could there anyone confirm that I am right?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Regular Expressions
ResponsesInList.Text: The ultimate reference are the SCORM 1.2 Runtime Environment book and the SCORM Conformance Requirements document. Anything else is guesswork.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Regular Expressions
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm absolutely with you. The SCORM Conformance Requirements document says the following: CMIIdentifier: • Value shall contain an alphanumeric group of characters • Value shall contain no white space • Value shall contain no unprintable characters

Cheers, Bobo.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: The number of clicks needed to start a course is too many?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mads, The reason for the long route to get to the SCORM course is because your SCORM package is seen as just part of a larger "course" which contains other resources & activities . If the SCORM package is the only component of your course then there's no easy way of shortening the route, apart from providing a link somewhere directly to the SCORM package. You could put direct links on the home page of the site, or, if you have a lot of packages you could use an instance of the Database module, or just a "web page resource" which contains direct links to them. ResponsesInList.Title: SCORMS not working with macs? But with any pc
ResponsesInList.Text: I have an online course, been going great, but mac users claim that my modules will not load and they get stuck on "loading template please wait" Users say they have Java and flash... Is there something missing? What Java is needed to run these scorm modules that the mac users dont have? Is there some alternative? I feel like I am missing something, as it is something specific to apple computers and I have always solved the modules NOT loading by telling users to install JRE. That is all. Any help? Please? Modules were created in Trivantis Lectora and are...version 1.0, 1.1, or 1.2 I cannot recall but can't imagine this would make any difference since they are all scorm compliant.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORMS not working with macs? But with any pc
ResponsesInList.Text: Maybe the content depends on a different Jave JRE version than the one that is installed on the macs. Some Java code that works perfectly one one version may break with another version. You need to identify the Java version required and the users must have the same or a compatible version installed. But that could of course open a can of worms, since the older versions of Java may be less secure. Note that this is not a SCORM issue per se. There is absolutely nothing in SCORM that requires Java or Flash. Those are content implementers' choices. It should be possible to use Travantis to regenerate content created in Travantis, to make it more compatible with the recent versions of Java.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORMS not working with macs? But with any pc
ResponsesInList.Text: Also check whether the users' Macs have multiple JREs. A PC user with multiple JREs can get into trouble when Explorer defaults to launching one particular JRE, and that default happens to conflict with your course. Check if the same possibility exists on Mac. (The solution in Windows Internet Explorer is to go to Internet Options>Advanced and uncheck the default JRE setting.) Also, the example above relates to Explorer, whereas Firefox launches JREs differently, and can produce different conflicts.

ResponsesInList.Title: A good model for improvements in the SCORM module
ResponsesInList.Text: I posted a message a while ago asking whether improvements in the usability of the SCORM module were planned. I haven't got any answer but in the meantime I've found some examples of how SCORM is implemented in other LMSs which I think can be a good model for future improvements. Have a look at what SCORM looks like in DOKEOS. Notice the (always visible) navigation bar on the left column. If you have build SCORMs with a long table of contents, you know what a big pain it is to navigate through them in Moodle and what a big improvement it would be to have something like that. Now, would it be possible to have something like this in Moodle as well? http://campus.dokeos.com/courses/1234bcc0/ When you get there, just click on the graphic (where it says "Solid Waste Management") Josep M.

I am sure the example you have suggested is a great one being implementation here.. Regards Uday

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A good model for improvements in the SCORM module
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Uday, The point of my message was not to say that Dokeos implementation of SCORM is perfect and Moodle's implementation is horrible. I'm just trying to point out ways in which the Moodle SCORM's implementation could be improved. From the navigation/usability perspective (which is the only one that I was considering), I think that Moodle's implementation has something to learn from Dokeo's implementation. It's hard to care about scoring and tracking if your users find the experience so unpleasant that they hate to use the SCORM objects you create. It's not my personal complain (I hardly use SCORM), but all the teachers I've convinced to use Moodle (because I told them it had good support for SCORM) are very unhappy about the navigation issues and they are asking me for solutions which I cannot provide.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A good model for improvements in the SCORM module

In my mind I was connecting this message with a previous message I had posted before ( http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=47475 ) but of course I shouldn't have expected other people to make the connection between the two postings. These are two of the problems we are having (I reproduce the other message): >I see in this forum that different people are working on the SCORM module for >Moodle 1.6. I'm wondering whether some of these improvements will be in the >area of usability . Two of the constant complaints from my colleagues who >create SCORM contents to use in Moodle are a) that they cannot adjust the >window size properly and they get a lot of SCORM packages with horizontal >scrolling and b) navigation buttons appear only at the bottom of the window >[at the end of the table of contents] making it really uncomfortable for the user >(who has to scroll the window all the way down) to move back and forth. They >would like to be able to add buttons to the top iframe but that cannot be done >with eXe or any other application to create scorm content. I don't know wheter problem a) is a problem with Moodle's implementation of SCORM or a problem with eXe (the application we are using to generate the SCORM packages). I haven't had this problem with CourseGenie (but then again, I haven't created that many SCORM objects). Problem (b) seems to be clearly a problem with Moodle's specific implementation of SCORM. This is what they seem to have solved in DOKEOS by adding another indpenedent scrollable frame exclussively for the table of contents and making the 'previous' and 'next' buttons always visible placing them below the scrollable frame for the table of contents. Perhaps it is not the best solution but it is infinitely better than the situation in Moodle where if you have a very long Table of Contents (which is something that happens often) you always have to scroll all the way down until the end of the table of contents, no matter how short the contents of the main window are, to go to the next or previous page. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What can be the problem?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to export a SCORM content packages?
ResponsesInList.Text: Here is a method I am using to publish Moodle courses as SCORM packages.  We have a Moodle site used for professional insurance industry training, with dozens of courses. We prefer to have students log into our system, pay for and take the course in Moodle. BUT, we have some large insurance companies that have their own SCORM based in-house LMS systems that would like to license some of our individual course products. So, I had to come up with a way to give them access to the same course we have inside Moodle as a SCORM package.  Here is how I do it. Most of the objects used inside a Moodle course are stored in a server directory typically /moodledata/ and then inside a folder that has a number equivalent to the course number.  So course number 80 has all the files inside /moodledata/80/ and then by the names of folders the instructor created when he/she setup the course. So now lets us say Big Insurance Company (BIC) needs a SCORM package of course 80 for their system.  I make a directory area on our Linux server for BIC, and then using symbolic links, link /moodledata/80/ to their directory so all files, documents, movies in course 80 are also in BIC's directory.  Then I setup a subdomain for BIC (BIC.mycompany.com) and give them access to this directory using this URL .  So they can get at the objects in course 80 using this special URL. Next I take the EXE editor and duplicate the Moodle Course 80 organization using EXE.  I do not like to give out our content, so I simply point the EXE menu items to the URL I created (BIG.mycompany.com/80/video/video.html) for example, and when the user clicks this menu item in the SCORM player they see the same movie as students inside Moodle.  It takes me about an hour to setup a parallel course in EXE to the one we have in Moodle, and some of the Moodle content items that are text or web saved inside Moodle MYSQL are cut and pasted as HTML pages in EXE and those items ship with my SCORM package, but the movies, and other big documents stay on our server. Customer BIC gets a very small SCORM package that is exported from EXE editor. It runs on their LMS and reasonably duplicates the look, feel and content of our Moodle course. The objects that stay on our server if updated by the instructor are updated versions seen by the SCORM user, but pages I cut and paste into EXE do not update. So, we charge an "upgrade" fee if the customer wants upgraded versions of the SCORM package as we update our online Course.  I upgrade by hand the same way I created the course in the first place, and the fee pays for my time. In this way we meet the demand for the SCORM world.  What is missing is user authentication and provisioning. Any employee of BIG can take our course, so we have to get a "site" license fee. When a customer comes along that wants a per user fee, I will have to work out how to restrict access to registered BIC employees, and I am thinking of just manually setting them up in the .htaccess file, so they are prompted to login when they first access an object off the server. I cannot find any open source repository software that can do this or I would use it as an overlay to the BIG directory with the symbolic link to /moodledata/. When the customer no longer pays the site license fee, I simply turn off their URL, remove their directory and the symbolic link to /moodldata/ and this renders their SCORM package I sent them 95% useless. This is a crude but nonetheless fast and efficient way to publish our Moodle Courses to the SCORM world.  I searched this forum today looking for a better way, and did not find one. So, I will leave you all with my solution.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle and Netg
ResponsesInList.Text: NetG courses are not the easiest to load into an LMS.  First, they don't come SCORMed.  NetG provides a tool to SCORM the courses with.  It generally works, but does have some minor flaws.  NetG provides an update (if you're working with them to get the course loaded) that resolves most of these issues. Then there's an issue with the overall size of the course itself.  We worked with NetG to create a course that aggregated various modules from their 3 Outlook courses.  Works well, but each of the 12 modules was 45-50 MB in size.  This is mainly because of the fact that they include a wide variety of language support.  Great in an LMS that can share the player (although, in theory, this isn't recommended for SCORM), but when each of the 12 courses needs to be loaded with the player, you're suddenly faced with 500-600 MB of disk consumption. We asked NetG about this and their response was that removing language files is not "officially supported" but the customer is free to do whatever they want once they have the courses in hand.  We stripped out the extra language files and reduced the course size to 12-15 MB. We had issues with NetG's java player causing our LMS servers (SAP) to crash.  This was resolved by tweaking some settings on the servers. The courses have been in production since mid-November and have been relatively stable since going into production. That's just my 2 cents worth. Joel

ResponsesInList.Text: Hello all, I may be posting to the wrong forum here.  I have the unglamorous task of moving online courses from WebCT to moodle.  I was wondering if anyone knew of an easy way to package WebCT content modules, or even WebCT web pages (frames) and drop them into Moodle. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Webct content module
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I have done it several times, there are several ways to go. 1) Depending on your version of WebCT, export content as an IMS Package. Open that package with RELOAD Editor, do a "Preview" of that package. This will create a frame-based page with the tree structure, for you to browse through your pages, and  by using File ... -> Save preview.. you can then upload your original WebCT content module as a set of HTML pages but with a navigation system included. Probably this can be done with other applications. 2) You can also modify your IMS content to produce a SCORM package, but to be honest, I don't like the current interface of SCORM modules in Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Webct content module
ResponsesInList.Text: Marilyn, Yes, there is an option from the WebCT admin side to export content, probably that's the way to go. admins must type a command (cp_api.pl -export) to export your course, however if you only need to export the content module of a course you must add a non-documented flag to the command above. I don't recall it now but we have done it when we must move several content modules from one server to another. It has helped me also when migrating from WebCT to another CMS. This way you could export all courses from the server. If you need more info on this, please feel free to email at eduardo@go2learn.cl Now, let me tell you why the admin interface is a much much better option than what a teacher can do (and problably is a lesson to be considered in Moodle). When it comes to export a content module, the server (i.e. WebCT but it could be any other CMS) must analyze all your HTML tags to detect all files related to your content, it looks for tags such as style , img , or object this way your exported content also contains all the css , swf and jpg files you are using, but if your html uses a Flash file that loads several other swf files or if you are using portions of JavaScript to launch a pop-up window, the server is not able to detect that and your exported content looks broken. When you export content from WebCT by using the admin interface, you can also add another flag to the command above -all_files (or something like that) where your package includes all files being part of your course. This way your package includes all files from your course ensuring that every files used is contained in the package. This workaround can also add "trash" to a content package, as it includes all the course files, but what you get is a working content, and if you need to clean your package, you can open the ZIP file and delete all the files you want to remove. My 2 cents! Eduardo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Birchfield interactive - Passed variable is not an array or
ResponsesInList.Text: If you wish to upload a Version 3 Resource Pack into Moodle, the easiest way to do so is to create a '.zip' file of the \RESCD???\Res\{product_name} folder, so that the 'imsmanifest.xml' file is contained in the root of the zip. In order to upload this file, you will need to change the 'upload_max_filesize' and 'post_max_size' so that you can upload a zip file in excess of 100Mb. The SCORM content supplied in the Version 3 Professional Edition software is supplied as a Resource Package, not a Content Aggregation Package, and, as you rightly point out, we do not supply any information about the structure of the content; there is no indication of learning outcome or how one part of the content is related to another. However, this content was developed a considerable time ago, to comply with SCORM 1.2, before the standard itself had been fully developed (i.e. prior to 1.3 and 1.3.1), and before the future of VLEs was assured. We do understand the importance of VLEs, with a view to the future, and of high quality SCORM-compliant resources, and, to this end, we have undertaken a two-stage approach to improving our SCORM content. The first stage (which is currently under development and will be available soon) is to improve the structure, naming and navigation of the content. The second stage will be to fully develop the content, so that fully interactive 'Instant Lessons' (i.e. equivalent to the interactive program CD in the Version 3 Professional Edition) can be directly imported into VLEs, maintaining full functionality. With regard to an upgrade path, the Version 3 Professional Editions have been replaced by the new Lesson Kits, which are available at an upgrade cost of £20.00 per product. These do not yet, however, contain any of the changes to the SCORM content mentioned above.

Breeze 3.x automatically sets the type to choice for single or multiple-choice quiz questions and true-false items. cmi.interactions.n.correct_responses.n.pattern  The correct answer(s). cmi.interactions.n.student_response  The answer(s) given by the student. cmi.interactions.n.result  The result of the answer given by the student. The format is correct or wrong. cmi.interactions.n.weighting  The weight applied to the question. For more information about SCORM implementation, consult your Breeze LMS Adapter documentation or Working TogetherBreeze and LMS Applications, which can be found on Macromedias E-Learning White Papers web site.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Use of a scorm package several times on a site
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a solution to some extent for this problem. I have a business related site with courses developed in the usual way inside of Moodle.  These are not SCORM courses.  Some large corporate customers do not want to enrol their employees in Moodle, and approached me to let them license the same course as a SCORM package to play in their corporate LMS. In order to facilitate this request here is what I did. 1) All course material for all courses inside Moodle are maintained in a directory on the server. On Linux the default folder is /moodledata/ 2) I setup the web server software ( Apache ) to allow access to this /moodledata/ folder by a URL . I used the URL syntax of http://corporate_name.my_domain.com.  I setup Apache to not allow directory browsing, and I put an index.html page in the root of /moodledata/ that redirected people out of this site if they tried to enter and browse around. I know that this is not really secure, it is "security by obscurity" but it got the job done.  Thus, using this URL, all the content, flash movies, PDF files, and so on is available outside of Moodle if you know the URL to get to it. 3) I did not want to distribute our content with the SCORM package, instead I wanted to keep the content on our server.  So, I use the EXE editor ( www.exelearning.org ) and make a menu system that is similar to the topical menu inside the Moodle course.  I use the web page tool and point the menu to the URL where the object is in /moodledata/.  Each course has a number, and the objects are in a folder with the course number.  So if you are preparing a SCORM class for class #68, the URL will be http://corporate_name.my_domain.com/66/xxxxx  and so on.  I found it quite easy to make an EXE SCORM package that behaved just like the Moodle course.  Some of the Moodle course content was not in the /moodldata/ folder and instead was in the MYSQL database , so for those pages, I just cut and pasted the text into EXE.  When I was done, I created the SCORM Zip file and sent it to the corporate customer, and they were happy that it played perfectly in their corporate LMS. 4) In the event the corporate customer stops paying the license fee, or their subscription runs out, I just delete the Domain Name I set up, and their SCORM package then becomes mostly worthless as none of the objects it played work any longer.  Thus I continue this strategy with many corporations, each one gets a unique URL domain name using the domain name syntax above, and I can revoke any one corporate user and the rest continue to work. 5) Now to answer the post in this forum, the SCORM package I distribute to corporate users also will play in Moodle.  Thus, I can use my own SCORM package setup as above to create other courses inside Moodle and "use a SCORM package several times on a site" as the question was posed above. 6) I intend to change the above a bit when I get a chance.  Instead of pointing the URL at /moodledata/ I am going to create another folder for each corporate customer. Inside that folder I will use symbolic links to the /moodledata/ folder but just to the course number they license.  This way, each corporate user will not have access to the whole site, a bit more secure. 7) I searched all over the Internet to find a way to provide for authentication and provisioning of the content I distribute this way, and could not find any way to make this more secure. I assume this is what LOR (Learning Object Repository) software is supposed to do. In effect I turned Moodle into a LOR without authentication or provisioning, and without any way to browse or publish the contents of my SCORM packages. I note in the Moodle forums that there is a lot of discussion about setting Moodle up to act as a LOR at some point, so I will just have to wait. BUT while I wait, I was able to meet the needs of corporate users who wanted to license our content as a SCORM package.  It takes me less than two hours to setup a SCORM package using the EXE editor, so it is an expeditious solution.  I can only give a full site license to the content this way, there is no way yet to provide user level access.  I heard somewhere that SCORM can access and pass along user names and other authentication information, and perhaps some day I can use the .htaccess file and that information to provide some type of user level authentication at some level. I hope this tip is of use to someone. Rene Thomas Folse

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Articulate SCORM and new IE flash issue
ResponsesInList.Text: We did this and solved our problem: 1 - Create a subdirectory js and copy the attached file AC_RunActiveContent.js to it 2 - Edit every HTML file of the SCORM package which uses flash to include this script in the HEAD section: <script src="js/AC_RunActiveContent.js" type="text/javascript"></script> 3 - Continue editing the HTML file to replace the code that calls the flash by this one (replace xxx by the name of the swf file and xdirx by the subdirectory where the swf file is): <script type="text/javascript"> AC_FL_RunContent( 'codebase',' http://download.macromedia.com/pub/shockwave/cabs/flash/swflash.cab#version=7,0,0,0' , 'width','504', 'height','188', 'id','xxx', 'name','xxx', 'src','xdirx/xxx', 'quality','high', 4 - Repack your scorm, or copy the changed and added files to the SCORM zip file, and upload the SCORM package to Moodle

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: uploading scorm package
ResponsesInList.Text: In a scorm package you can't use asp, php or any other server side scripting languages. If you want use dynamical pages you need to define them as external resources in the manifest files. This resources can be stored on the same server with moodle but in a public webserver directory in order to permits webserver to elaborate scripts. Moodle store all the uploaded files in a particular directory "moodledata" that normally is not a public webserver directory. You must also know that, for security, the files in that directory will never elaborate so moodle pass to the browser the source of the script. This is the reason of why when you access to your scorm package your browser open dreamweaver or some other application that manage asp files. I hope this can help you. Cheers, Bobo. PS: to set external link to resources in the manifest you must set href attribute of tag resource to something like http://yourserver.com/scorm/resource/directory/yourfile.asp

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: AICC Courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle has supported AICC since version 1.5. You simply select SCORM from Add an activity within your course, and then locate your Course package. Note that AICC is a fairly ancient standard being designed during the client server computing heyday when the paradigm was dumb browser and intelligent server. ResponsesInList.Title: Articulate SCORM Output.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I have been seeing a lot of you having problems with Articulate SCORM output and  the Moodle SCORM module. I've had a look at the Articulate Quizmaker an it produces SOCRM output as advertised. The Flash not visible is indeed due to your server setup. The SCO writes cmi.core.lesson_status is set correctly to passed/incomplete as you set it up in prefs but cmi.core.exit is always set to suspend. It would appear that although commit is sent (and all the collected data is sent) Moodle never receives a LMSFinish(). This is why you can always return to the SCO and overwrite your previous status, though all results are stored correctly as can be seen if you view the extended SCO information. I can't see an easy fix in the Articulate software but will look further when I have more time.

ResponsesInList.Title: eXe & Reload
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Maria, eXe is an Open Source authoring tool for creating web content for e-learning. With eXe you  have the option of exporting your work as an IMS content package or SCORM package. Reload is a content packaging editor.  You can use Reload to combine and package a collection of existing digital resources into a Scorm package. The Reload project has also developed a SCORM player. Deciding which tool to use will depend on what you want to do. If you want to author your own web pages and export them as SCORM packages -  you  can use eXe (or one of the other commercially available tools).  If you want to  combine web-pages and other digital resources  that were created with other software (eg Frontpage or Dreamweaver) and create a SCORM package - you should use Reload. Hope this helps. Wayne

ResponsesInList.Title: Articulate reporting completions accurately
ResponsesInList.Text: New to Moodle, but have loaded several courses created in Articulate. Moodle seems to be erratic in reporting 'completion'. Some individuals appear to have viewed all the slides and answered any imbedded quizes, yet still report as incomplete. How does Moodle define 'Complete'? Has anyone else using Articulate found a similar inconsistency?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Articulate reporting completions accurately
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes. Here's a couple of things that seemed to make the reporting more consistent and reliable. Do not deviate far from the template layouts provided by Articulate. I disabled some of the controls and had bad results. Colors should not make a difference. Use AICC communications. ***Make sure that when you produce the ZIP file that you make the file path in the AICC settings box the FILE NAME ONLY. (ie. lms_index.html) DO NOT include the URL . This way Moodle will be able to find the file. I suggest when using the slides viewed method for completion that you subtract at least one from the total number of slides. For example, you might include a generic "completion" slide at the end of each show. This way, the student must view all of the actual content to receive credit while you are guaranteed a better chance of success in registering a completion result. If you try all of these and still have trouble, let me know. Jamie

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Articulate reporting completions accurately
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for the suggestions. I did some experimenting with the specific module and discovered that if I clicked the 'Exit from SCORM course' button the completion posted correctly, but if I clicked on the bread-crumb-trail, it not only posted as incomplete, but no further efforts to 'complete' the course would work. I've updated the instructions on that page, but I think some users will fail to follow them and have problems. I'll try using the AICC format and see if that works better.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Not displaying scores - Please Help
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Graham, Just in case check your SCORM setup to make sure it is set to record scores. Diagnostics would be that although you have communication established with Moodle DB through SCORM module evidenced by the reports you are collecting. Score is specifically set by the SCO using Setvalue(cmi.core.score) so: Step 1 is to trap the error message received when you send set score value. Expect to see either no communication error or value out of range (not numerical 1-100 or the range set in the SCO setup). Step 2 A common error with score is previous versions of SCORM have just used cmi.core.score. The SCORM data model accepts cmi.core.score.raw/cmi.core.score.min/cmi.core.score.max. If you choose SCORM 1.2 datamodel it is expecting cmi.core.score.raw not cmi.core.score Step 3 Create a bare bones SCO with set values to send to Moodle, trap the errors.

ResponsesInList.Title: Generating / inserting SCORM objects created by other Moodle components
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I've written a little Flash-based applet to do on-screen jigsaw puzzles. This hooks up with a bit of PHP / Moodle server -based code that gets the original image off the (teacher) user, chops it up into several pieces, each in a new sperate image file, and shoves the whole lot in a Zip file. I'd like to add SCORM tracking facilities to the client-side part of this utility, then I could use SCORM to store state information about the jigsaw, i.e. use an XML string to store the position of each jigsaw piece so that the (pupil) user can leave off doing a jigsaw part-way through and come back to it later without having to completly restart. So, I've done SCORM-based stuff before, that's no problem, and it should be easy enough to add a few JavaScript files to the Zip file my utility generates and tada, I've got a SCORM-complient jigsaw utility. However, for a (teacher) user in Moodle to use this Zip file as a SCORM object in their course they'll have to download the generated Zip file, then create a new SCORM object in their course and upload that Zip file again. This is rather fiddly and introduces more steps than the average teacher has the patience for. What I would like is for my utility to be able to generate a SCORM-complient Zip archive, then have it insert this archive into a course as a SCORM object. Then, the (teacher) user just sees a nice two-or-three-step wizard type of interface where they add a picture, enter a few details, and their jigsaw appears as an object in their Moodle course. They don't even have to know it uses SCORM, there'll just a be a "Download a SCORM archive of this jigsaw" link on the setup page. One way for me to implement this would be to clone the existing SCORM module, adding a few bits to the setup form relevant to my jigsaw utility. This, however, seems rather a duff way of going about it - is there a more sensible way? --

ResponsesInList.Title: Flash loadVariables and Moodle 1.5
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, On both Apache and IIS I've had problems in the past with scormed pages that contain flash movies which require external text files containing data to be  imported using the loadVariables function. In each case the problem has been solved by applying the "&" at the start of the text file. It doesn't work for 1.5 however! Does anyone have any ideas please?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Flash loadVariables and Moodle 1.5
ResponsesInList.Text:
Just in case anyone ends up with the same problem... my colleague discovered that the problem is that Moodle 1.5 appears to preformat text from .txt files. There are two solutions to this problem, one is to rename your .txt file with a different file extension. This is simpler easier and allows .txt files that are actually part of courses to be preformatted as before. However since this was not an option for us, we had to get rid of the preformatting. This can be done by an alteration to "lib/filelib.php"  Line: 191 Change it from : $output = '
'. format_text($text, FORMAT_MOODLE, $options, $courseid) .'
'; To: $output = $text;

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Flash loadVariables and Moodle 1.5

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Any RoboDemo-based SCORM experience/examples out there?
ResponsesInList.Text: hai, Here is what you have to do to put your SCORM content prepared using RoboDemo: Based on the assumption that you have already installed  moodle and packed your content as a SCORM Zip file in your RoboDemo For tutorials on how to install moodle and create course please refer documentation. In short moodle provides courses that consist of topics that include activities which can be your SCORM package or the moodle modules.And only a teacher or admin can edit a course in moodle. Course { Topics { Activities{SCORM,chat,forum,etc.,}}} 1 Create a user or the default admin user will do 2 Create a new course with any format (social,weekly,topics) 3 finish configuring your course 4 if editing is not possible ( ie., there are no ways to add or remove topics in your course) switch " Turn editing on " button in the front page of the course 5 after editing is turned on, you could add content to the course now . 6 try by clicking the Activities... drop down menu in one of the topics 7 click scorm and enter description and the name you like to appear in the moodle course page 8 For the Course package option , click " choose or upgrade a SCORM package ". From the new page that pops up  , click " Upload a file " 9 from the next page, browse to the folder that has your RoboDemo SCORM Zip package you have 10 select it and click " upload this file " 11 your Zip pack will be listed in the next page.Click " choose " from same line where you find your  package name 12 a new page with screen setting options will be available.Modify if you need any change 13 press " Save Changes " 14 the course will be listed in the topics list.click on the topic 15 click on the " Enter SCORM course " button to see your package running Happy moodling! Sundar

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle not adding cumulative scores with SCORM package
ResponsesInList.Text: If the students score is recorded in the LMS using cmi.core.score it is entered as a single element in the scoes_tracking table so essentially gets overwritten every time. If you want highest lowest scores you need to have your courseware write the score to cmi.score.min, cmi.score.max. Alternatively if the courseware is writing each question out as an interaction cmi.interactions.n.id the index of the interaction is restarted from zero every instantiation. So Question 1 might have been stored as cmi.interactions.0."Q_1" and all the Q1 students results as cmi.interactions.0.learner_response, cmi.interactions.0.type etc. On reentry the student results for the scorm will start at index 0 and overwrite them. What we do is store the attempts in cmi.suspend_data and increment the index on each entry and only write out index values in the current session.

ResponsesInList.Title: Version handling
ResponsesInList.Text: Has the topic of automatic versioning for the SCORM module come up? Having used a different LMS in the past. It seems that this would be a very helpful feature for courses that have rolling enrollments with overlapping classes. The benefit would be the ability to upload an updated version of a SCORM while maintaining the previous version and its tracking. Once a user has accessed the SCORM, they would remain in that version until completion. However, if a newer version exists, a subsequent user would be presented with that newer version. This would involve the SCORM module automatically creating a new version number upon upload and therefore creating new mod data instead of overwriting the existing data and erasing the tracking records. (eg. - SCORM_v1, SCORM_v2) The user records would include which version they viewed, or are viewing. Would this be a complicated code change? It sure would be a great addition to the SCORM module.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: problem with values of data model elements
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ronnie, I haven't looked at your SCO in detail but from your description it sounds like the values you're saving might not be immediately available when the material is loading (I'm assuming you're calling getValue() immediately). Maybe try calling it after a short time. Are you using suspend_data to store your values? - I think that's probably the correct place for them. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: problem with values of data model elements
ResponsesInList.Text: I took a quick look at your fla, and I think Alex is right. First let me say that I think your project is very cool. In Flash, fscommand is tricky.  You don't want to use it until your entire movie is loaded.  There are a couple of ways to do this.  The simplest is to put this in your first frame: ____________________________________________________ rootLoader = function(intervalID:String):Void{ trace("the interval is being called"); var loadedBytes:Number = _root.getBytesLoaded(); var totalBytes:Number =_root.getBytesTotal(); var precentLoaded:Number = Math.round(loadedBytes/totalBytes*100); if(totalBytes>loadedBytes ) //everything is loaded clearInterval(eval(intervalID)); fscommand(lmsInitialize); }else{ //set the scale of a loading bar or something to percentLoaded } } var rootLoaderInterval:Number = setInterval(rootLoader,500,"rootLoaderInterval"); ____________________________________________________ SetInterval can also be tricky.  I've had experiences with it not being able to clear the interval, even if I pass "_root.rootLoaderInterval" as the intervalID.  You'll have to play around with it.  The trace in rootLoader will help you see if the interval is being cleared or not. If you have a lot of extra cash lying around, techniques.org has a great .mxp for handling all of the fscommand headaches for you called "escorte for actionscript."  It's more expensive than Flash, though! good luck! Mike -new to Moodle, been doing SCORM for years

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCO status (incomplete and complete) tracking is not working poperly
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes you are correct CMILMSFinish() correctly under SCORM 1.2 sets the LMS to mark the SCO as complete. Macromedia have much of their elearning content (Authorware, Dreamweaver) calling a finish at the end of a SCO when in fact they should be calling a Commit. The SCO should make the decision of how complete or incomplete it is. If you need to store data between sessions use suspend data (cmi.core.suspend I think) which is read/write.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: cmi.interactions
ResponsesInList.Text: When using LMSSetValue, you need to ensure that both parameters are strings - so LMSSetValue("cmi.score.raw",95) would be incorrect and might return an exception of incorrect data type, whereas LMSSetValue("cmi.score.raw","95") should be okay. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problems Validating
ResponsesInList.Text: I have attached some snap shots in the zip file to show the difference. Sorry about the image sizes if you are running at a high resolution.  Had to get the file size of the zip down below 100Kb. The problem before was that the package looked like pic1.jpg and the new package looks like pic2s.jpg.  It may not seem that different however to the importing process and the packaging rules of SCORM it is. The imsmanifest.xml and supporting .xsd files must be int the root level of the package.  In pic1.jpg they are in the directory 'appr_comp_rev3_07_22_04\'. If you look at pic2s.jpg you will see that the files have no data in the Path column of winzip.  This signifies they are at the 'root' level of the package. When an LMS imports and then expands the course it will expect to find the imsmanifest.xml file in the root location where the files were extracted.  Based on pic1s.jpg those files would have been one level deeper in 'appr_comp_rev3_07_22_04\'. pic3s.jpg shows a properly extracted course (specificly this one) in moodle. pic4s.jpg show what it looked like when you used the original zip file from SumTotal. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm - NLN materials - we want to use them with a guest log in
ResponsesInList.Text: well the 'refactoring' thing is not exactly so (as it is my job to carry out the work i feel i can be honest here) we will certainly be looking to bring some of the older content to the same level of content packaging as we used recently. As i think Helen pointed out, the use of scorm and the NLN is a muddly picture. SCORM is a reference model drawing together a java implementation of the CMI data model and IMS content packaging to support a particular view of what constitutes a "Content Object". NLN does not currently share the same view of what is a content object so does not use the same reference model. Therefore NLN could be said to use NORM or the NLN Object Reference model. Basically SCORM requires that each of the organisational elements within a content package be a self contained learning object, that basically is a course based approach with each organisational node being a lesson of piece of course material. NLN has a different view in that each organisational element is a section within course material. It stems from a different understanding of the purpose of content packaging. So, in a pretty abstract way, NLN Uses exactly the same tools contained within SCORM to describe a different conceptual model of sharable content, effectively establishing its own reference model of those standards. I believe this is a perfectly legitimate theory, but one that is under constant review. It does, however, become more a matter of policy rather than best practice at some point. Any spec or standard is an agreement between a group of people, and a reference model or profile a grouping within it. SCORM conformance offers a high degree of interoperability within a well-defined group, but merely a fair degree of flexibility. Our own model of IMS CP + IMS MDR + IEEE Javascript CMI offers a reasonable, but not guaranteed, degree of interoperability with a wider group with more flexibility. Picking what's best between them is a policy decision that's quite specific to any community. Given that that is the history, my current task is to work out where to take the materials in the future Andy

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: LMS to Course Communication Log
ResponsesInList.Text: Umesh: I'm not sure if this is what you're after, but ... if you login as 'admin' and go to your SCORM package, you should notice on the top right of the page a link that says 'View reports for X attempts'. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Not able to use SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: As I understand it: SCORM is a standard for creating e-Learning courses/modules. It defines how javascript can be used to communicate between the web pages which make up a SCORM package and the LMS(e.g. Moodle) which hosts the SCORM package. To create SCORM content you need the appropriate tools: 1. LMS - to host the package (e.g. Moodle) 2. Authoring Tool - to create the web pages/SCOs (e.g. Toolbook, eXe, Dreamweaver) 3. SCORM packager - to create a SCORM-compliant Zip file of your content (e.g. eXe, Reload)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: eXe and upgrading FireFox?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Anders, You will be fine to upgrade to the latest version of Firefox separately.  It won't effect eXe or the functioning of the browser of your choice. (At the moment, running a normal Firefox browser and eXe at the same time is still a bug that we are working to resolve. It doesn't cause any problems or conflicts with the version of Firefox you are using). Just remember to shut down eXe before launching the latest version of your browser. If you don't shut eXe down - when you launch your browser - it will want to use the "eXe" version of firefox- without your bookmarks.  Don't panic just shut eXe down & launch your browser. I realise this is irritating at the moment - but we will get it fixed over the next 2/3 releases. eXe will run & look like a desktop application. Users won't know that we're using the Mozilla framwork as our Run time environment. Chat to you soon. Wayne

ResponsesInList.Title: Alternative to SCORM tracking for Flash MX Quiz template tests.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, Thought I'd post an announcement here about the new ability of my Flash Activity module to track quizzes which are based on the Flash MX Quiz templates. A quote from my previous post to the Flash Activity forum : Extended 'moodleDebugger' I've added some new features to the debug view which is included in the 'preloader' (I ought to rename the preloader to something else probably as it does much more than preloading the fonts and movie now). When anything is output by your php service functions using for example echo, print or print_r then the output will be automatically displayed in the debug view. You can now switch to the debug view by pressing CTRL D or by this action script moodleDebug.showDebug(); and then you can switch back to the movie which is running in the background by clicking on the 'go back to movie' link. If there is a comms error the error is now handled by displaying an error message in the debug view, when there is an error there is no option to go back to the movie. New 'preloader' allows you to track Flash MX Learning Interactions without using SCORM or AICC. Just for fun I wrote some code to track Flash MX 2004 Learning Interaction movies, risking severe caffeine poisoning in the process . We can now track user activity and capture grades and answers from Flash MX 2004 Learning Interaction movies based on the Flash MX 2004 quiz template. No modifications to the Flash MX Learning Interaction movie are required. Instead of having Flash talk to javascript and pass the tracking info through a SCORM api which then passes the info to Moodle I have written a Flash movie that loads in the Flash MX Learning Interaction movie and then tracks it and sends tracking info to Moodle. This may be? a more robust and simpler alternative to using the SCORM module (for Flash MX Learning Interaction movies only). Not sure how the tracking capabilities compare (haven't used the SCORM module ) but here are the features of this tracking method : Live logs show answers submitted as the student submits them Take the test as many times as you like selectable grading methods -best grade for each question, average grade, grade for last test only, etc. No weights for grades unfortunately. Configurable feedback. No need for frames or popup windows. No scorm packaging required. Works on possibly a wider range of browsers ?? - no need for javascript , no need for Flash - js communications - two things which are not universally supported. We have access to the all of the internals of the quiz so we can easily extend tracking, to do whatever we want, almost.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Alternative to SCORM tracking for Flash MX Quiz template tests.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jamie- Yes there are non-SCORM ways to send the tracking info to Moodle and more generally to some arbitary LMS. However, the goal of SCORM is to have a universal mechanism, not tied to any particular application (or LMS), which in turn enables content producers to create content that can be tracked in multiple LMSes (like BB, WebCT, D2L, Angel, SAKAI, Learn eXact, and others). What Flash MX Learning Interactions has done is to provide the appropriate JavaScript wrappers. As you have no doubt noted, the JS can be fragile across multiple browsers. There's also what's behind the JS that communicates with the LMS, which is typically a Java applet sans UI. The communications from JS to Java will fail on some web browsers, has to do with the Web browser "plugin API". I believe what you have done is to have an embedded Flash SWF, the one that comes out of the Flash MX Learning Interactions, communicate with a 2nd Flash SWF on the same HTML page, and this 2nd one "talks to Moodle". However you are doing it, I do see that it can be done. I also think that one could create an SWF that is behind the JS that SCORM and the Flash MX Learning Interactions uses. Similar idea to yours or perhaps it's the same idea. Something like this Flash MX LI => SCORM JS => Flash SWF => Moodle

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Alternative to SCORM tracking for Flash MX Quiz template tests.
ResponsesInList.Text: I believe what you have done is to have an embedded Flash SWF, the one that comes out of the Flash MX Learning Interactions, communicate with a 2nd Flash SWF on the same HTML page, and this 2nd one "talks to Moodle". However you are doing it, I do see that it can be done. What I'm doing is loading the Flash learning interactions movie into another movie. The first Flash movie tracks the second movie all within FLash and sends the data direct to Moodle. No modification is needed of the learning interaction movie. The advantage of doing this is javascript is avoid entirely. This is not useing SCORM though. SCORM requires the content to talk to javascript. Now if someone authors a Flash MX learning interaction movie they can track it with SCORM or they can track it with my Flash module. With other LMSs they can use exactly the same movie and have it tracked using SCORM (or AICC). I also think that one could create an SWF that is behind the JS that SCORM and the Flash MX Learning Interactions uses. Similar idea to yours or perhaps it's the same idea. Something like this Flash MX LI => SCORM JS => Flash SWF => Moodle My JS is not very hot but can't you have JS talk direct to Moodle or another LMS. Isn't that what the Moodle SCORM module does? I don't know I've not looked into it. It seems to me you will have to have good support for both JS and Flash on a browser this way, you are multiplying your cross browser issues it seems. Your project seems interesting, hope you will post updats on its development to appropriate Moodle forums. Looks like it might be of interest to people here. Jamie

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Very Simple SCORM Questions
ResponsesInList.Text: 1. If I use Moodle as our target LMS, it appears that the API adapter that Moodle uses is a direct implementation of the ADL labs sample LMS Runtime. Is that correct? Incorrect, Moodle implement a RunTime Environment conformant to ADL Lab spec. 2. Am I correct in making the assumption that if I use Moodle, I can use the ADL sample javascript API scripts to interface my SCORM content with the Moodle LMS? Correct. 3. What features a different or missing from the ADL reference? Moodle 1.5 is fully conformant with ADL SCORM 1.2 spec. 4. I have a moodle test site up, but I'm using 1.4. I assume it would be in my best interests to load the current development snapshot (1.5+) in order to SCORM modules? You can download the current stable release 1.5 5. The SCORM documentation and RTE is unclear about who or what level provides the API adapter interface. It appears that the LMS provider/player will provide the API to your SCORM content so as long as I corretly package the XML manifest, my content and the API adapter javascript from ADL. Can I assume my content will work with other systems such as WebCT, Blackboard, etc? Or does each LMS require some tuning to the content? The LMS provide the API Adapter, the SCO must search the API Adapter in its DOM. If the content is SCORM conformant it must works with all conformant LMS. Bobo.

ResponsesInList.Title: Firefox http-equiv="refresh" bug?
ResponsesInList.Text: I've encountered this problem on and off since the new 1.5 SCORM module and have been trying to track it down a little, but wanted to check whether others have had similar experience. It seems to be a Firefox problem with http-equiv="refresh" which is used by the inline frame  to presumably allow a brief delay for the parent frames Javascript to load before loading in the SCO content. Firefox sometimes ignores this refresh, the result of which is that you get nothing returned and are left with just a blank frame. There is some speculation that this has something to do with the Rich Text editor; that after a Rich Text editor has been loaded in Firefox then http-equiv="refresh" does not work any more. I can confirm that if you load moodle without loading up Rich Text editing then SCOs in Firefox will load. I've reported this as a bug in Firefox, but wonder if perhaps there might be a way to fix this in the SCORM 1.5 by using javascript to do the refresh, rather than http-equiv="refresh". brent.
