When the user complete the first one, clicking on the button "continue" will let him complete the second one; When it complete the second one, clicking on "terminate" redirects him to the list of scorms.That's OK, but : the status of the scorm are : completed for the first quizz, and not attempted for the second one ! However, everything works fine if instead of clicking on the "continue" button, the user will click on the title of the second quizz in the tree view. (the package was made with reload editor). Thanks for any help or improved version... Stéphan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: wrong scorm status
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Stephan, maybe, perhaps.....it is a bug.. but but but one reason I'm think for this to happen is that the first quiz is not Finishing (correctly) its communication with the sever when you click the Continue button, a needed step, before launching a second resource for tracking. If the first SCO doesn't finish its communication, the server doesn't know that the first SCO was unloaded. Since the server ignores this, the call made by the second SCO to establish a connection, for the server looks like a second call made by the first SCO (the server doesn't know the SCO changed in the user's Browser!). If the tree view works OK, it means the event that triggers the Finish command in the SCO it's called when clicking on the tree, and by using the Continue button, it is not. So, one way around would be to change the place where Finish calls are being executed. Do you have control on how the quiz is being created?. Do you have access to see where and when the Finish command is being called?. Are they Flash-based or HTML-based.. or whatever-based?--- 2 cents..

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: wrong scorm status
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you for your answer, now it works. It was as you said  (the first SCO didn't called the finish command). Regards, Stéphan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: QTI Conformance in eXe 0.4
ResponsesInList.Text: QTI or Question and Test Interoperability is a specification that we've been in touch with for several years. Both in terms of products like WebCT, D2L, and QuestionMark (all of which we run on campus) and in tools my team has created where we have "embeded assessments" within rich content. Strictly speaking, QTI works at 3 distinct levels: entire assessment questions results The entire assessment would be a quiz or exam, typically, made up of a selection of questions from a question pool. Questions are composed of questions, answers, and feedback to the student. Results are what gets sent to a "permanent store". QTI itself is an XML format, suitable to exchange between system. Some examples of where this could be used are: * questions from a text book. Publishers only need deal with a single format. * standalone question generation tool. Respondus is a classic example. * assessment servers for high stakes examinations like the US SAT. QuestionMark is the prototypical example in this space. My team has used QTI in a couple of tools we have developed. See http://engage.doit.wisc.edu/tools (all open sourced by UW): * ConceptTutor, has an embedded assessment in the "Check" tab. * DynaLesson, coming soon, this is a much richer set of "question types". See http://engage.doit.wisc.edu/projects/MmLessonBuilder/ for an earlier incarnation. You can download ConceptTutor and look at our documentation and source code, though it's tad dense I'll confess. This is our most advanced effort to date.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Object Repositories in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: It's quite possible to have unzipped SCOs. The zipping is for exchanging between systems. Technically, what's going on is that the format used is IMS Content Packaging. That's a .zip which contents a file directory tree + imsmanifest. xml . The "manifest" is like a big table of contents, conceptually. Technically, it's an XML DOM that gives you a place to store the structure (what fits within what), the IDs, and metadata. All you need to do this is a file store. Do the zipping when you need to exchange between systems. I have seen this work in practice, and have specified yet-to-be-built systems that use this approach. One might also note that this CP format could be used for most anything, not really specific to SCORM. I would like to suggest that Moodle uses it as an "exchange format" for moving Moodle courses between servers. This is similar to what WebCT does. This would work on multiple levels of organization: * course * activity within a course: quiz, discussion * tools with data: gradebook * resources: question bank, images * all courses The trick here is to define an appropriate "exchange format" for each of these. One example is both quiz and question bank, which would use the IMS QTI (or Question and Test Interchange). I think this hasn't been done, in a standards kinda way, in other areas, because there hasn't been the will/need to do so. The Moodle community seems like a good place to do this (and yes I'm going to help )

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm Errors
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ralf, here are some problems with the imsmanifest.xml Your <organizations> tag needs to tell the LMS which table of contents to use as the default organization. You would need <organizations default="default"> Your <item> tags need a closing tag. For example: <item identifier="ID6"> <title>Framework</title> </item> You may want to use a tool to generate the manifest. We provide Manifest Maker , a free extension to Dreamweaver. You could also use Reload.

You mention that the generated SCORM is missing some files, the only time I have come across something similar was when generating a course when I had multiple Word documents (or emails) open, I had noticed that on occasion when courseGenie checked the export settings the wrong word window was selected so it could not retrieve the correct settings, this may explain why you have a manifest file but no supporting files. If this seems to be the case then please try closing the other Word windows and check the courseGenie setting then generate the course again and see if the expected files are included in the ZIP. This problem has been fixed in a development version of courseGenie and will be included in the next main release (in about a couple of months). The link that Jim Depow gave to a discussion on moodle describes a Capitalization problem with the word False in the cgstage.htm whereby the F should be lowercase which causes the JavaScript to stop executing and thus the LMSInitialize is not then called. There is one more courseGenie issue I am aware of and that involves the Page Root setting, the SCORM JavaScript which bookmarks and loads the previously view page doesnt take into account if the value has changed so looks for a non-existent file, for instance when Page Root is set to Page the files will be Page_xx.htm if it is changed to say Slide then the files will be called Slide_xx.htm but the JavaScript isnt aware of this so still looks for Page_xx.htm. The last two problems will likely be fixed in a service release, most likely in the next week. Now, to get to the moodle side of things, you say you tried the Demo_Scorm.zip and that failed. To be sure I just downloaded this file from the link I gave previously in the moodle forums, and uploaded this to the Moodle Playground (for sake of upload speed I removed the Media files from the zip but other than that it is unmodified), http://moodle.org/mod/scorm/playscorm.php?id=3917 will take you to the course. What problem did you have with demo and on which version of Moodle. I also posted previously in another thread regarding the v1.5dev version and how it handled the suspend data from a SCO using Regex incorrectly reported that our suspend data wasnt valid as it contained Commas which is incorrect, this now appears to have been corrected in the lasted moodle 1.5dev version running the moodle.org site. I hope that helps, please let me know how you get on and I will post these details for the others on the moodle forum. Josep, the licensing the situation is such that if you reinstall a computer you can use the exact same registration code again and again, if for instance you change the Hard Drive then you will need a new code. If anyone want to contact me direct to send the files they are having trouble with please feel free, paul@connectedlearning.co.uk . Best Regards, Paul Lewis courseGenie Support

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Does SCORM file size affect performance?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, My name is Claudio Erba and i'm the webmaster of the Docebolms.org project. DoceboLMS is another Open Source e-learning platform but i don't consider it a competitor of Moodle because we support different didactical approaches, so please don't consider SPAM my thread. Regarding the scorm and my manual i'd like to say that, YES, tools like Captivate and Flash create scorm packages, but are too limited because they include 1 SCO inside one SCORM package, for example <package> <organization> <SCO> </organization> </package> You understand that this is not the right scorm approach because a scorm Organization can manage MORE thatn one sco in a single organization. For example: <package> <organization1> <SCO1> <SCO2> <SCO3> </organization1> <package> And this can't be made trough captivate but trough Reload Editor. Just another thing, please consider this two proprerties of SCORM 1) The package: Support the IMS part of the standard, you can package SCO'S that CAN be tracked or also ASSET that CAN'T be tracked 2) The Tracking part is delegated to the SCO's and not to the Package and is called RTE. If you don't support RTE you have enabled only Half of the scorm functions. P.S I have included in the manual some sources for examples Regards Claudio DoceboLMS.org Staff

Each lesson has several images, applets, etc. The goal is that all applets, and several of the more important images are to be search-able Assets for use by teachers in creating future content (whether it be in Moodle or some object repository). A lot of my applets share common files, or images may be shared between lessons.  Is there a way to maintain that sharing, or will I need to create multiple copies of these common files to enforce the modularity of each lesson? 3. To implement the assets as their own search-able objects in an object repository (am i correct in thinking that moodle will implement a search-able OR for a not-so-distant release?), do I have to individually create each asset as it's own SCORM package, or can I simply tag assets with proper meta-data and will an O.R. be smart enough to do a subset search and return the proper files from the bigger package? 4. Not withstanding #3, if I was to tag an applet /image as a asset, is it customary to include a stub HTML page that is the main point of the asset so that the image (or more importantly) applet can be utilized properly?

ResponsesInList.Title: Why use Moodle if you only want to do SCORM?
ResponsesInList.Text: If you create SCORM- activities , then you end-up with a set of exercises for individual students. Nothing wrong with that. Then ask yourself: "Am I creating courses for individual students or wish I to integrate group-activities?" If you choose the second option, then take Moodle and start - what we call - a bricoleur design: A course for how many weeks? seven ? OK we give you seven cards plus one extra card. (Extra card is called Card Zero: always on the screen and the place for resources and activities that are needed all these seven weeks.) Give every card a title. (= theme for students for orientation that week) Paste your resources (docs, weblinks, multimedia, simulations) under each theme. Choose from the more then 30 types of group- and individual activities those one that fits your needs and paste these activities in the neigbourhood of these reources. (Your individual SCORM activities could be part of these activities.) Do a little screen shuffling with the clever indent option of Moodle, suggesting a hierachy of importance. (We call this design by Gestalt: two things, visulal grouped together must belong together, will the user think etc.. ) Choose and add blocks around this course to help students and teachers during the runtime of the course. Populate it with students, hire some tutors to help you, create groups if you like, and run...

ResponsesInList.Title: eXe plans to provide offline authoring capabilities for Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Joyce, I'm the project lead for the eXe project and appreciate your feedback. The current release (albeit very early) was intended for folk to play in order to get an idea of what we're trying to do. Thanks for the green tick on "usability"  - this is a high priority for us and we appreciate your feedback. Nonetheless, we still have a lot of work in frint of us to make the usability even better. So keep the feedback coming! With reference to your little "ask"  we are planning to deliver much more . In our roadmap we are planning for a Moodle specific export. Therefore, over and above the SCORM import capabilities of Moodle - users of eXe will be able to incorporate a selected number of Moodle specific tools in while authoring content in eXe and export this content into a Moodle course.  The added advantage is that you will be able to author Moodle course content offline using eXe, and import this into the Moodle LMS when done. This creates a number of interesting opportunities. For example embedding a discussion forum iDevice in the web content authored in eXe. When imported into Moodle - the link will automatically launch a Moodle discussion forum. OSS makes deep-linking so much easier! At the moment we have someone from the Moodle clan assisting us with specifying the Moodle file structure to enable eXe to achieve this rich offline authoring capability in eXe. Can't wait to see this working. Cheers Wayne Associate Professor Wayne Mackintosh Director Centre for Flexible and Distance Learning University of Auckland New Zealand http://exe.cfdl.auckland.ac.nz w.mackintosh@auckland.ac.nz

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Chardelle, Thanks for the feedback. We're looking forward to building an intelligent eXe export for Moodle - and shouldn't be too difficult using Moodle's SCORM module. Glad that you find eXe easier than Reload - we are trying hard to lower the entry barrier for non-technical users. Good point about tracking time & Score. We'll need to think carefully about this for the Moodle specific export. Are there any QTI-Light guru's out there? We're a little thin on QTI experience - so any help in this area will be welcome. Stylesheets in eXe will become more sophisticated, for example: a stylesheet for sight impaired learners; or a stylesheets for cultural diversity where culturally inspired icon sets are used; and we're exploring the implications of a stylesheet editor. Good idea for the link to a default stylesheet which more technical folk could adapt. Yes - there are plans for more question types and embedding media (In eXe we use the concept of "instructional devices" or iDevices for these elements). We are relying on educators, learning designers, practitioners etc. to submit requests for things they would like us to incorporate into eXe. So if you have any special requests or ideas for question types or embedded media, you can submit requests for iDevices at: http://cfdl.auckland.ac.nz/idevice_interest/introduction.html You will find most of the project info, downloads etc at: http://exe.cfdl.auckland.ac.nz Chat to you soon. ResponsesInList.Title: eXe and IMS LD
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Tony,  appreciate the positive feedback on the UI -- Its going to get a lot better . Wait till you see the XUL toolbar - the prototype is looking rather nice. We will be able to get rid of the somewhat "brittle" javascript which we think will become cumbersome when displaying complex content outlines. Given our pedagogical slant and commitment to specifications , we are keen explore ways to meaningfully support the LD spec. We've been watching your IMS-LD discussions with great interest. Having had an early look at eXe - Do you have any ideas how we might use LD in a smart way? Drop us an issues note at http://exe.cfdl.auckland.ac.nz At this time eXe development is focused on coding an iDevice editor and some XUL magic on the UI. The iDevice editor will enable users to create their own iDevices, or modify existing ones. (We don't want eXe to become a template driven straightjacket.) Then we will shift our focus to developing  a Moodle specific export for eXe.  (We're working  with the NZOSVLE project on this dimension.)  The idea is to provide value-add functionality over & above the SCORM export for Moodle. Lets say a user selects a Topic outline for authoring in eXe. eXe will export a SCO for each Topic - but at the same time intelligently set up the Moodle Topic titles and corresponding Moodle resource links under each topic to the web content authored in eXe. It should also be possible for eXe users to setup discussion forums for intelligent import into Moodle. In this way there will be embedded discussion forum links in the web content as well as the usual discussion forum link in Moodle. I think that eXe will provide Moodle users with two significant advantages: 1.  An alternative to author Moodle content offline 2.  Added web-authoring features than is currently possible with a rich text editor. Chat to you soon Wayne

I enjoyed seeing this from your more objective point of view. Glad to hear that moving items up & down is now working. Wait till you see the XUL functionality we're working on at the moment. It's going to make things like this so much better. I can't think what the problem might be with the Moodle SCORM navigation on moodle.org. We must investigate. Likewise, when we tested the SCORM import on Moodle, BlackBoard and WebCT - things appeared to be working (see eXe SCORM import Screenshots ) with the local LMS navigation. We've had many discussions about the font control issues. I'd like to hear your views and advice. Is the selection of typeface a presentation element that should rather be controlled through stylesheets? or Should users control the typeface at point of entry, irrespective of what the stylesheet template reccommends? An interesting philisophical question. Its relatively easy to provide users control over font type in the rich text editor - but we potentially loose control over look & feel of the output with post-authoring manipulation - unless we strip the input of typeface elements before export. This is why we have limited presentation control in the editing environment to italics, bold, lists etc. Should we provide a user-friendly CSS editor where folk can change fonts for different elements of the stylesheet? Help! We're working on a simple online evaluation form for this release of eXe - and it would be great if you could test it for us. Will let you know when its up and running. Hopefully within the next day or two. Chat to you soon. Wayne

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: AICC-certified
ResponsesInList.Text: SCORM is a container for a raft of "specifications". It includes the IMS specifications for content packaging,  which are basically an XML schema for describing a menu structure and the resources it refers to. It also includes a specification to allow the content to communicate with the containing learning environment(LE). This permits bookmarking and score information to be sent from the content to LE, and for the LE to ask for information (e.g. Student Name and previous bookmark) from the LE. The spec for doing this is a series of well defined Javascript function calls. The were lifted from the AICC spec and although they aren't identical, they are very similar.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MOODLE´s conformance to SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: On the moment you can see Moodle as a clever hybrid system as answer to the current state of the art of the standards. In a handy loose design you set the ouline of a course, like  a marketplace. On this market place you can fill tables with local activities, which can be one of the more then 30  Moodle activities or the new blocks. It can also be "plugins" like the Scorm modul: in that modul you can run a scorm-play and at the end our scorm-plugin gives the final score back to the gradebook in Moodle: a very clever way of integration. Another standard is QTI: if you create quizzes in Moodle, you can choose to do this in a special part of the editor, so you can EXPORT these quizzes in QTI 2.0 format. There is also a project (Gustav's) that is connecting Moodle to a real QTI engine, so that any quizz, created according to the QTI format can run in a Moodle system. Scorm has it's roots in good old CBT and AICC: it can design the most complex scripts for individuals, but has no idea how to organise even the simplest group-activity. Moodle people believe that the best form of education is a mix of individual and group learning activites, as open as possible, but not complete free, we are not naive. When we as community grow in design skills, we need a common language to express and exchange our more complex designs. We are looking for tools like IMS/LD, but that is another discussion I see you have a long succesful career in the design of teacher replacing software. The driving idea behind this approach is that if you are able to construct good instruction moduls with valide tests, students can learn any subject. I came also from this tradition, but am now convinced that it is not enough: we should also organise groupactivities. So don't throw away all your experience, but try to combine it with the flavors of Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Suggestions or advice greatly needed!
ResponsesInList.Text: Well - a pointer - apologise if I am stating something you already know, and personally I have not looked at this in detail. the SCORM package contains a page with some code like if (!cmi.core) {   alert("cmi.core not found"); } cmi.core should be a function that is present in Moodle's SCORM wrapper - that is, the frame that the SCORM package is running in, or the window that "popped it up". Likely causes: a) A coding error (e.g.  a case error:  e.g. cmi.core and CMI.core are not the same thing.) b) disassociation. The SCORM package is running in a window that is not a 'child' window of the SCORM wrapper. For example, you'd likely get this error if you tried to run the SCORM package outside of a VLE or in a VLE that didn't understand SCORM at all.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Upgrading to new version
ResponsesInList.Text: The trick here is to match the mods to the appropriate moodle "build."  If you have picked up the 1.5 scorm package and unzipped it into a 1.4.3 moodle build, it won't work. The message you have received seems to indicate this particular issue.  If you do upgrade, realize that 1.5 isn't ready for prime time at all yet.  It hasn't even reached "beta testing" status yet. Many moodle.org folks are "early testers" who experiment with development stuff, but we would never risk using the stuff on servers with actual students until the code has matured more. I hope this helps. -Tom

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm file size
ResponsesInList.Text: You just need to move the file into your course folder for access then. 1) find out the id number of your course by visiting it (look at the URL when you are on the course page) 2) move the file into the corresponding moodledata folder (e.g. the folder called 1 in the moodledata directory is for the site.  The folder called 2 is for the course that has an id that equals 2. Once you have placed the zip file in the appropriate folder, go back into your the FILES menu from within your course (via the browser).  Unzip the file by clicking the "unzip" link next to its name.  Voila. -Tom

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cummunication between RTE & LMS Database
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Anand, if you asked for the technics behind: Of course these are not defined by ADL, because these are in the responsibility of the LMS. ADL only defines an interface (the object API, which supports the functions for initialising, setting, reading and committing data and the specified dataelements). How this API is implemented and where the data is stored is not part of the interface. The SCORM-API of Moodle uses Javascript to implement the API. The cmi-dataelements are stored in variables and when LMSCommit is called, these variables are sent to Moodle, where the data is processed and stored into the database. If you look into the database, table mdl_scorm_sco_users, you can see a column for each supported cmi-dataelement. Regards, Sven

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cummunication between RTE & LMS Database
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Anand, now my question is: Are you a developer? How deep can I go into the material? The data is stored in a HTML-form, like other forms you can see around the web. If you call LMSCommit(), it is like pressing the "submit"-button on other pages (if you order something in an e-shop, for example). This form in the SCORM-module contains the cmi-dataelements and the sco-id of the current SCO. Using the session-data of the current session (a cookie is used in Moodle), where the user-id is stored, the data can be refered to the student... So, the SCORM-module knows, which SCO has transferred the data and which user has used the SCO. Now the cmi-data is stored into the corresponding row in mdl_scorm_sco_users. The next time, the SCO is called by this student, this row is read and filled into the form again by the server and the SCO can read the data using LMSGetValue. Does this answer you question? Regards, Sven

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ooops! Was: Problems with SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi to all, first of all don't worry for different menu option. The script in Admin >> Configuration >> Modules >> Scorm check for your installation setup and display only usable option. If you find only "none", your PHP is 4.x.x and it's not compiled with DOMXML library (no validation will performed on packages, only manifest check). If you find also "DOMXML external library", your PHP is compiled with this external library (validation is done but there are some problems with some packages - this is the reason because Martin said to set this option to "None") If you find "PHP5 (DOMXML native library)", your PHP version is 5.x.x (at this time no validation is performed with this option, I'm working on new validation procedure using PHP5 intenal functions, the manifest check still performed). The commented code was executed only if no settings are done in Admin >> Configuration >> Modules >> Scorm (the general case) With the current version (if you don't set nothing) Moodle check only for the manifest presence (the less impact solution). Sorry for this big missunderstanding, Bobo.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: problems with SCORM and Moodle 1.4.x
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi to all, today I've patched some small errors in the SCORM module that came with Moodle 1.4.x. One of this was rmdir error that Joyce posted . For the "unable to find api adapter" error I can't give to you a solution because the problem is the SCORM package; probably some or all the learning objects are define as asset in the imsmanifest. xml file, the SCORM standard said that the LMS can't provide the api adapter for assets; so in the Moodle 1.4.x the SCORM module does not provide it (the previous version - 1.3.x -, wrongly, provided that). But what is the solution? Unfortunately the only solution, in order to mantain standard compliance, it's to modify your SCORM packages. You must edit the imsmanifest.xml file and replace: adlcp:scormtype="asset" with: adlcp:scormtype="sco" This work only if your learning resource interact with LMS (it's a real SCO), otherwise you don't get error messages but the LMS (Moodle) provide an api adapter for nothing. I hope this mine solves some problems, thanks, Bobo.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Tracking of results with SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Eduardo, the Reload Player and SCORM Visualizer have some similar functions. They both launch SCO's and show the values of the SCORM data items. We created SCORM Visualizer to provide immediate and detailed analysis of the communication between a SCO and a LMS. We also wanted to create a tool to help course developers create and debug their SCORM session management code. Here are some direct comparisons of the tools. SCORM Visualizer versus Reload Player SCORM Visualizer shows you the specific details of the communications between your SCO and the LMS. Whenever your SCO makes a SCORM API call you immediately see an update to the log of API calls. If your SCO calls LMSSetValue(), you immediately see the result in the table of SCO data items. This immediate feedback shows you how specific interactions with your SCO result in SCORM Runtime communications. SCORM Visualizer can save the state of your SCORM data and let you reload that state at any time. This helps you debug your session management code and it helps you test your code. SCORM Visualizer can install between a real LMS and a SCO to show you the specific communication between the two. It helps you find the source of a SCORM communication problem. SCORM Visualizer is much smaller (K bytes versus M bytes) and it runs very quickly. SCORM Visualizer is implemented in client-side JavaScript . All of the source code is provided and it is well documented. You do need to worry about the version of Java you have and you can use a JavaScript debugger to trace right into the function calls. Leo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: (will there be) Tracking of ind. question results with SCORM?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Josep, Just a small clarification.  While the SCORM module of Moodle doesn't support all the data elements of the CMI data model ( http://ltsc.ieee.org/wg11/files/1484_11_1_D6.doc ), it is 100 % SCORM compliant, since compliance in SCORM 1.2 only requires support of the mandatory elements. There are 12 mandatory elements and the cmi.interactions are not included in this group in SCORM 1.2.  Ultimately, it would be nice to see Moodle evolve to SCORM 2004, where all elements of the CMI data model are mandatory. Joel

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: (will there be) Tracking of ind. question results with SCORM?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Josep, This is what I think..my two cents. Probably, we could say that everything is technically possible, and what we have today in Moodle can be used as a base to build the complete set of features offered by SCORM. I really wish I could help but my PHP skills are not that good As Joel was sharing with us, there are several certification levels for an LMS, where those levels depend on what an LMS can do (or in other words how far an LMS can go supporting SCORM). So, probably the first step we should define is what level we want or need to support; obviously offering support for all SCORM features will be great, but do we need all of them right now?; if "yes" then we should work on that, if "no" we could go step by step. Problably level 1, then .. 2 (defining which optional elements to support).. and then 3 (all of them). Probably, we at the Moodle community should work/discuss on the elements needed. SCORM defines some information on a per-SCO basis, and some other information per-student basis, and some info per-content package basis. If we want support for all the elements in the data-model (or part of them), this could lead to an impact in the actual DB structure being used in Moodle for SCORM (tables and fields, relationships). So, for example, trying to support the tracking for individual questions within a SCO, needs a review in the actual DB structure being used. As an example, not directly related to the individual questions issues, but in the version of Moodle I run (1.3), I don't see a field for storing the cmi.core.credit which is a mandatory element (page 3-24, SCORM 1.2 Run-Time Environment ). However, the same page in the SCORM documentation reads "Initialization: LMS is responsible for determining whether or not the student is taking the course for credit or no-credit." This leads to offer course teachers a checkbox or something to establish a content as "credit" or "non-credit", as seen in other LMS. I remember now the interface of WebCT Vista where a teacher can check/uncheck this option. So, the support for this element, not only leads to a review of the DB, but also could mean a change in the SCORM User Interface. So, hiring someone is not a bad idea ... but that someone should have a good (solid) knowledge on SCORM. Eduardo

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: (will there be) Tracking of ind. question results with SCORM?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM, courseGenie and Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Josep The current version of courseGenie, v1.5, produces a SCORM 1.2 package that can be launched, but it does not pass any tracking or scoring data. The upcoming courseGenie version 1.6, due out early October, passes full tracking, bookmarking and test score data to the host LMS. This has already been tested with other VLE/LMS systems, and we will be testing with Moodle over the next couple of weeks. CourseGenie does allow you to build selftest questions within Word, and with the new version the scoring data from these questions will be passed to the host VLE/LMS. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Example SCORM packages
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Richard, I've been corresponding with a colleague of yours, Paul Lewis, about the upcoming release of the 1.6 version. In his last message he told me something that dampened my enthusiasm a little bit. This has to do with the way question scores are tracked by the host system with SCORM packages created with CourseGenie. I was hoping that we would be able to generate grade reports that were detailed enough to be able to track how each student did in a particular question (assuming a question is a subpart of an exercise which is composed of 1 or more questions). This in turn would allow the teacher to analyze how students have done in relation to specific questions: e.g. question 1 was answered correctly only by 10% of the students, question 2 was answered correctly by 80% of the students, etc. This kind of report can be obtained presently with the Moodle quiz module. However, it appears that with a quiz generated by CourseGenie only a running total of the question scores is stored and thus the final report only tells us whether the module has been 'passed' based on the mastery score set. The only info available to Moodle is thus the time taken, total score, and 'passed' or 'failed'. I don't know about other potential users but this limitation is for me rather unfortunate because knowing in which particular questions students have done well and in which ones they have done poorly is an essential piece of information for teachers. This information is essential, for instance, to determine weaknesses of students in specific areas, to reevaluate the way certain areas are being taught or to help teachers detect problems with the wording of specific questions. Do you have any plans to add this functionality to CourseGenie? I really like what I have seen so far in CourseGenie and I can see myself and many of our teachers using it to create materials and quizzes to add to their Moodle courses. Most teachers that are starting to work with Moodle in my university find the quiz module in Moodle a bit limited (not a criticism to Moodle on my part, for me it is clear that Moodle is a platform based on a social constructivist approach to learning and quizz building capabilities are just an added functionality that was not part of its core objectives). Not being able to obtain the kinds of reports I've mentioned, though, is a major drawback. I would appreciate it if you told me if indeed this is something you intend to work on in the near future. Perhaps I am wrong, but I think there would be a lot of people that would appreciate such functionality. Josep M.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Example SCORM packages

ResponsesInList.Title: Tracking user's score in a SCO
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm curious to know whether one would be able to obtain reports from scores of individual questions in quizzes packaged as SCORM.  I mean, I know we might be able to retrieve the total score a user gets in a particular quiz or exercise via a Javascript variable called totalScore.  My question is whether whether, besides the total score at the end of an activity, it is also possible to retrieve the scores for the individual questions that make up a quiz or an exercise as we can do in the quiz module in Moodle. Thanks. Josep M.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Tracking user's score in a SCO
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Josep, The answer is "Yes". What we can store/retrieve in an LMS is defined by a "data model" which is part of the SCORM's "Run-Time Environment" (aka RTE) specification. In SCORM 1.2 there's an element to do what you were asking. However, the SCORM 1.2 Data Model contains "mandatory" and "optional" elements that an LMS must (mandatory) or can (optional) support. This is the reason why ADL has different Levels of Certifications for LMS; All of them depending on how many optional elements your LMS is supporting. One optional element is cmi.interactions , which is defined at page 3-49 in the RTE: " In this context , an interaction is a recognized and recordable input or group of inputs from the student to the computer. All of the items in this group are related to a recognized and recordable input from the student. The category collects detailed information on each interaction measured as the student takes a SCO ". So, now before sending data to an LMS, we must put some extra code to know which elements the current LMS is supporting. We must send a command to the LMS, and the LMS returns a list of the supported elements.

Bobo.

The array $values is initialized in line 235 (in the "foreach ($grades as $grade)" -block): foreach ($grades as $grade) { if (!isset($valutations[$grade->userid])) { if ($scorm->grademethod == VALUEAVERAGE) { $values = array(); $values[$grade->userid]->grade = 0; $values[$grade->userid]->values = 0; } $valutations[$grade->userid] = 0; but by doing this the whole "history" (all previous calculated values) could be deleted and only the last userids remain in the array. $values should be initialized before the foreach-block: $values = array(); foreach ($grades as $grade) { if (!isset($valutations[$grade->userid])) { if ($scorm->grademethod == VALUEAVERAGE) { $values[$grade->userid]->grade = 0; $values[$grade->userid]->values = 0; } $valutations[$grade->userid] = 0; } ... or remove it... 3. ResponsesInList.Title: Tips for solving SCORM problems...
ResponsesInList.Text: So far, I've found 3 things that can easily go wrong when preparing/uploading SCORM modules: 1. Improper "Zipping": When you zip up your files, ensure that imsmanifest. xml is in the "root" directory/folder. If not, you will see a "Manifest file not found" error.  To check this, in winzip, open the zip file and find imsmanifest.xml (it is probably 2nd from the bottom).  Look at the right column - if you see a directory/folder in the "path" column for imsmanifest.xml, this zip file will not work with Moodle's SCORM.  You need to re-zip the files so you do not include the parent directory.  I do this by selecting all the files & sub-directories in Explorer (make sure you are in the directory where imsmanifest.xml resides - not in its parent directory), right-clicking on any one of the selected files, then selecting "Winzip"..."Add to zip file".  When done, check out the .zip file and ensure imsmanifest.xml does not have a directory/folder in the path column. When you set up a SCORM module in MOODLE, MOODLE automatically unzips the .zip file under /moddata/SCORM/ in the Moodle files directory on the server (e..g. /moodledata/). Moodle then looks for imsmanifest.xml only at the top of the new directory it created - not in any sub-directories. 2. Case-sensitive directory/folder names: If you get a "Can't find file" error after adding a SCORM module, check to ensure that the folder/file names in your imsmanifest.xml file are correct - including the user of upper/lower case. We have tool that creates the imsmanifest.xml file for us, but it changes directory names to be all lower case.  This seems to work OK on some servers (e.g. MS IIS ?), but not on Linux/ Apache .  After Moodle unzipped the SCORM zip file, we went to the "files" area for the course, drilled down under moddata/SCORM/, found the unzipped directory, and renamed the sub-directories to match those in the imsmanifest.xml file (all lower-case names) - then everything worked. 3. Internet Explorer version incompatibility: If nothing appears in the window when you run a SCORM module, it might be because you need an update to your version of Internet Explorer. If you see an error icon in the lower-left corner of IE 's bottom status bar, click on it. If this is the problem, you will probably see and error like this: Line: 58 Char: 4 Error: Object doesn't support this property or method Code: 0 URL : http://www.../moddata/scorm/SCORMxxxxxxx/xx/<your SCO/File> In Internet Explorer, click on "Help" menu, then "About Internet Explorer". If you have Version 6.0.2800.1106, look at line 4 "Update Vertsions".  If you do not see "Q831167", you need to install it by going to http://www.microsoft.com/downloads/details.aspx?amp;amp;displaylang=en&familyid=254EB128-5053-48A7-8526-BD38215C74B2&displaylang=en . This solved the problem for me. - Jack Jensen www.isdcenter.org (coming 1 Oct 04 - a site where we can all share e-learning and SCORM templates, lessons-learned, expertise, tools, advice, opinions, etc.)

ResponsesInList.Text: ***  I'll take the heat for this as everyone reads this but it's worth the effort.  *** I continue to see several posts in this forum about --> 'Created a SCORM course with <<fill in tool name>> and it doesn't work' That's great and thats what forums like this are for.  However, I have gotten to the point that I look for the following things before I even load the supplied course package for testing - 1.  Is the imsmanifest. xml even referencing the ADL SCORM schema and properly referencing the appropriate XSD files in the <manifest> tag 2.  If Yes, do the XSD files exist as part of the zip file 3.  If Yes, is there an external JavaScript file or code embedded in the files and do they look for the API Adapter and attempt to call the LMSInitialize() function. 4.  If Yes, does the package past the ADL's Conformance Test (v1.2.7) 5.  If Yes, now I load it into the LMS (moodle) as a SCORM activitiy and test for other issues. If No is answered to any of the above questions then I can guarntee your course will not work in moodle or any other LMS if loaded properly as a SCORM course. As I posted in another thread ( http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=11046 ) --------------------------------------------------------------------------- 1. SCORM is a 'Read the Manual' first specification. 2. Look at implementation examples and understand what is happening.  There are alot of things that happen in implementing SCORM and one needs to understand them. 3. Try to implement into your own solution - start small then work big. Unfortunately alot of people are trying to work from the bottom of the list.  I feel comfortable in stating this because that is where I started and then quickly realized my frustrations were because I didn't start at the beginning - Read the Manual. If you are just starting out go to the ADLnet.org ( www.adlnet.org ) website download the documentation, the Conformance TestSuite, sample Runtime Environment, visit the Reload site ( http://www.reload.ac.uk/ ) and get the SCORMplayer, find a good development tool for building the manifest and dive in with both feet first with the manual. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- Remember - start small then work big - But, most importantly - know what you are doing. I hope no one takes personal offense to this but as I see more and more activity on this forum I thought it needed to be said.  Also, for those that still have outstanding problems and I have made replies to your posts, I am still looking at your posts in between my everyday job taskings. Gotta make that $$$ somehow. Also, I think everyone should register onto ADL's Forum for insight into SCORM specific discussions - http://www.adlnet.org/forums/implement/index.cfm Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Help on Scorm module creation
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello all, i need to create a Scorm module for a Banc than have an LMS on my country Chile, I dont know much about SCORM ( i know its a standard but not more than what i have learn in adlnet.org) i would like to know what can be done as a SCORM module (my boss have the idea to create a colaborative module where people can interact, is that posible? ) what are you free to do and what aspects you need to keep close to SCORM, any hints for this newby will be welcome thanks

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Help on Scorm module creation
ResponsesInList.Text: Paolo, SCORM does not put restrictions on how the content is built - regular HTML, Flash for interactivity, QuickTime movies.  Where the restrictions / specification interjects is in the delivery and tracking of activity mechanisms.  If your client has LMS 'A' today will they have that same LMS in the future? Does the client use the same LMS in every location of delivering training? If they purchase a new LMS should they recontract to have all of their courses redeveloped?  Or if they want to restructure the course and add new content later should they redesign?  If the answer to these questions is 'No' then that's where SCORM implementation benefits. The SCORM specification allows for the developer of the course to provide an organizational structure of the content and it's dependencies to the LMS along with a set of rules that the LMS can use to track and manage a learner's progress through the course.  Without SCORM a developer is limited to the chosen LMS's proprietary implementations of tracking and structuring of the course. Organization and dependency identification is handled through the manifest file (imsmanifest. xml ).  Tracking of a learner's progress is handled by using various data elements that the LMS must provide access to for storing data about the learners experience ( lesson status, lesson score, etc).  The organization of the course outlines how the learner would navigate between each learning object/activity. With all specifications there are mandatory musts and optionals - SCORM specification has this same collection of mandatories vs. optionals.  As an example the all SCORM LMSs must (mandatory) provide a way to store the learners status in an identified SCO (learning object/activity) - completed, sus.  An optional item the LMS may provide capability for is storing the minimum and maximum score achievable for the SCO. Also, one key aspect in SCORM in the level of dependency throughout the content.  SCORM states that all SCOs (Learning Activities ) should stand alone as a single learning experience.  This allows the SCOs to be organized in any fashion with other SCOs to build a complete learning experience across a general theme.  As an example using your client's line of work (being a Banc), a learning activity (SCO) on how to do a simple balance of debits and credits.  This could be used for training tellers, loan officers, even banc customers wanting to know how to balance their accounts.  The key is in keeping the content free of any specific references to specific types of accounts when you deliver that SCO.  The minute you add direct references to specific type of account then the content is only good for that focus.  So the 'trick' to building a SCORM conformant course is not how the content is delivered - static or interactive, but what content is presented and how well does it stand alone for reuse. As I mentioned in a previous thread ( http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=11046 ) - there are alot of things that the specification covers and one should really study the various documents and look through the ADL's forum for addiitonal insight.  This spec is not a jump in with two feet and few weeks later you have a SCORM course.  You really need to read through it and know how it fits your development practices. Hope this helps.  Take a look at examples from this forum and others to see how things work and most important - read and have the SCORM documents handy.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Help on Scorm module creation
ResponsesInList.Text: My boss have the idea to create a collaborative module where people can interact, is that possible? Not really.  The idea with SCORM is to remove learning content from any dependency on a particular LMS and that means any particular server -side technology.  In fact, SCOs should really be functional in stand-alone players that don't even use a server.  SCORM is really intended as a tool for delivering and sharing independent study materials.  Instructor grading of SCORM-based materials is not even a part of the specification.  I like to think of it as a way of creating textbook-type materials with automated interactivity, grading, and user tracking.  The textbook can be used as a part of a course where there are collaborative activities, but the textbook is not where the collaborative activities take place.  Now, technically, I don't think the specification forbids you from, say, creating a SCO that connects to some proprietary data store or communication server that would allow different users access to communicate, but this would tend to work against the idea of portability of the SCOs produced.  This resource would have to referenced by an absolute URL to work when transferred to another server, which is the main point of SCORM.  I think such a use case would be considered a brittle hack and bad form.  Now, it may be that SCORM-based materials could include materials that conformed to some other specification that allowed for some sort of portable collaboration and communication system, but I am not aware of any such and that would certainly be pushing the envelope. Rob

ResponsesInList.Text: Hey all, I finally have fixed the hierarchical side menu modifications that I posted prematurely before. It was a lot harder than I thought, but I've tested it on several SCORM aggregations and I think it should work now. With the modifications, the SCORM table of contents listing generates more standard list markup. This allowed me to use an expandable/collapsible nested lists script that I wrote. That way, you aren't limited to the Prev/Continue buttons for naviagtion while you are viewing SCORM content. I've also added a breadcrumb trail navigation structure in the top frame and modified the previous/next navs. I've tested it out in the latest IE , Firefox , Mozilla, and Opera on a PC. The new nav system uses mostly JavaScript and the W3C DOM, so I think eventually it could be engineered so that the whole frameset doesn't have to be reloaded to load a new SCO and update the navigation elements. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: New Hierarchical/Collaps ible Side  Menu for SCORMs
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Bobo, Thanks for taking the time to look at what I'd written and incorporating some of the ideas into your module.  I agree that the side menu does take up a lot of space.  The popup is a good solution.  However, without the hierarchical side menu, I think it becomes even more important to add a breadcrumb trail to help users know where they are in the aggregation. A lot of the convoluted nature of the code I wrote to generate those nested lists was so that it would produce valid markup.  The main issue being that a <ul> cannot have a <ul> as a parent (as is currently the case with your revised script).  Rather, it must be nested in an <li>.  I believe this also makes the deprecated "compact" attribute unnecessary.   Valid markup is important for reliability in the javascript code as well as for accessibility for vision-impaired users.  Screen readers can easily navigate nested lists if well-formed.  You're taking your chances on these points if you use non-standard markup. It would also be good to make the box surrounding the collapsible menu of a fixed with.  It is disconcerting to have the box resize when you collapse a menu. I also thought I would let you know about a great little tutorial I found called "Remote Scripting with Javascript, IFrames and PHP."  It is at: http://www.phpbuilder.com/columns/vance20040507.php3 Mostly it uses the same techniques you are using but it has some neat tricks in it that you might find valuable. Have you heard that PHP 5 is going to include a lot of XML improvements?  It should make parsing the imsmanifest file a lot easier. Anyway, thanks again for your efforts.  You're module is awesome, and I
can't wait to see what you are doing with SCORM 2004.  Do you have any
plans for supporting metadata or content repository functionality?  Let
me know if you need or want any help. Rob

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM not ready for prime time?
ResponsesInList.Text: No Mark, your assumptions are quite accurate on where ADL and most current supporters of SCORM have focused their efforts with respect to tools and even conformant LMSs.  Also, if you were to ask an ADL person on where are the tools for other platforms - like I have - you will get the answer that 'We are not in the business of building tools, but in the business of developing, implementing and managing a specification.' When you look at the specification itself, it is not platform specific.  The specification does not state a specific DB platform or even specific method for storing persistent data.  The spec only outlines the type of data that an LMS must or optionally store for use.  The spec does not state the development language that must be used to create the LMS.  The only definitive must is that the communication from the client (browser) to the server (LMS engine) will be through a ECMA script language ( JavaScript ).  The LMS provided API will have specific function names that are accessible and perform specific tasks when called by the ECMA script.  Now for the most part JavaScripting is fairly stable across several platforms and if the platform does not support JavaScripting then SCORM will not work. But to answer one other point - Yes the implementation of the specification is in it's infancy.  But it's the implementation of the spec that is still young.  Alot of LMS environment's are still adjusting and developing their environments to support the spec.  Just like Bobo's efforts here and moodle's LMS environment they are growing and still in earlier stages of developing to support the SCORM specs. But you are stating the facts correctly.  It is early in the game and for people like us this is a great time to learn something new and be on the ground floor.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Page status in SCORM package
ResponsesInList.Text: By saying 'Page status', I am going to assume that your course/package is using single page SCOs. And based on that assumption, I will do my best to explain your question. When the package is loaded into an LMS (Moodle/SCORM mod) by default all SCOs are set to 'not attempted'. This is the guidance given by ADL on what an LMS is responsible for - see ADL SCORM 1.2 The SCORM Run-time Environment book page 3-25. Now here is where all the crazy stuff occurs: Depending on the cmi.core.credit value (pg 3-23) the cmi.core.lesson_status can utilize different vocabularies to represent the SCO's status. For courses that are for 'credit' the status options are passed, failed, and incomplete. For courses that are for 'no-credit' the status options are incomplete and completed. With that said the only lesson status left is 'browsed'. This status can be set only when the lesson mode is set to 'browse'. Again this is an LMS set value and is read-only to us, the developers. So unless the LMS provides a method to set the mode to 'browse' vs. 'normal' or 'review', the lesson_status for a SCO will not be able to be set to 'browsed'. Now I have looked through the SCORM mod's code for the API, and I know that you can select 'browse' vs. 'normal' when entering the course; unfortunately though I have not found the code that allows for the differentiation between the two modes if selected. I have also skimmed through other pieces of code to see if the any of the rules I mentioned above are being enforced. Unfortunately, I have not found any restrictions in the code - then again I have only skimmed the code. Could you send me your course, an I can take a look at what you have done and see if I can come up with a better explanation. I hope I haven't confused things more. Chris

ResponsesInList.Title: Scorm module: new release
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi to all, I have just finish to watch the MoodleMoot UK, wow great job Sean and all guys. Today I have updated the CVS with a new version of  scorm module. First of all thanks to Matt for your update. I've included that in this release. I have also patched the time problem with Firefox and Mozilla (there still remain this problem with Safari/Konqueror but, as for Firefox, I think that this is a browsers bug). The main new features is a new validation procedure. Until now, the module only check if the imsmanifest. xml exists, now the manifest is also validated (this may report some manifest errors in packages that works fine) . This procedure needs domxml extension in order to work, so the module check for it. If your server doesn't support this extension the module works in the old mode. Soon I will convert this procedure to the new PHP 5.0 XML DOM support library. You can find the validation type selection in the scorm module settings page.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scorm score
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Stéphane, It's not easy to answer to you, but I will try. When you create a SCO you must implement all the actions such as save the score, calculate and save the time. The SCORM module, as every SCORM players is a stupid black box that launch your SCO, implement some APIs, and wait for your requests. This means that your SCOes must call for a LMSSetValue for score and for time and then call for  a LMSCommit to store your changes. This is just a little view on what you must do to work with SCORM, I think that if you want to know much on SCORM the ADL site is your reference.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Module
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, my name is Bernhard Zech, I'm new in the Moodle discussions and in this forum. We are a german based small company named cogito and are highly interested that Moodle gets SCORM 1.2 functionality. I have read some discussions here about SCORM in different threads. I understand the fears. It would be calamitous if SCORM compatibility or compliance would impact Moodles specific philosophy and appoach. But I believe it's possible to do this without to attack the current didactical philosophy and advantages of Moodle. I see SCORM just as an standard mechanism to define and exchange Learning Objects (SCOs), to import them in a defined hierarchical structure (packages and "organisations" in the imsmanifest) und how to communicate with them (status data, language settings ...)  It should be up to the learning designer to use just single SCOs, to reorganize them to any structure or to embed single or aggregated SCOs in any social environments and conditions and learning flows. A SCORM enabled course in Moodle would be just a small subset of  the hole Moodle functionality. And nothing in the SCORM specification talks about or regulates the things and learning flows around a SCORM enviroment. @Roberto: It's great that you started this work and I would like to support this development as much as I can. Regarding to the implementation of the client side API object (API adapter): You wrote, that you are working on a Javascript solution to communicate with the server (perhaps via XML RPC or things like this). I suggest also to look at a Flash based solution and to compare the pros and cons. There is an technology called " Flash remoting ". This way you can realize very fast communication with the server in both directions. You deal with binary data and you have not the data and parsing overhead as when you communicate via strings and XML tags. There are at least two Open Source solutions to communicate using Flash Remoting with PHP: - AMFPHP http://sourceforge.net/projects/amfphp/ - PHPOBJECT http://ghostwire.com/resources/phpobject/ Additional advantages of this approach are: - You can exchange high level entities like objects with properties: both solutions serialize the data for you. - it's easier to encrypt the data. I think encryption is a must in many scenarios because we deal with private data. In addition, we still need some Javascript wrapper code around the flash control, which gets the API function calls from the SCO and transmits them into Flash. But the most funktionality of the API adapter I would implement in Flash. What do you mean?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Module
ResponsesInList.Text: @ Ger: I spoke about SCORM 1.2 only. SCORM 1.3 alias SCORM 2004 alias SCORM with IMS SS (Simple Sequencing) has been released in January, but even co-creators of SCORM 2004  like Claude Ostyn warned at the ADL International Plugfest in Zurich to start with implementations because it contains to much  open points. In addition I don't like the SS approach because it's still limited to single learner scenarios. In many ways SS is a poor competitor to IMS Learning Design, with is also a IMS specification. IMS LD is much better because with this language you can express also social environments, synchronisation of learner and teacher activities or blended learning scenarios. So when we come to the point that we want to model learning scenarios and "learnflows" in a interoperable and LMS independent way IMS LD  is a much better choice. Please note: IMS LD is really paedagogical neutral because it's up to the learning designer to decide what parts of a learning flow control are "automated" and shall follow hard coded sequencing rules ("conditions", defined by the learning designer)  and what parts are just containers for more or less free negotiated social interactions. IMS LD is very complex and hard to implement so let us start with SCORM 1.2 and interoperable Learning Objects ... quote: "Question: must this javascript for the API still be the subset called ECMAscript?" Pragmatic answer: must be a kind of ECMAscript / Javascript which can be correctly interpreted from your target browers(s). @ Martin: ok, it's nice to have congruence. We have to discuss how to collaborate and combine the activities.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SCORM Module
ResponsesInList.Text: Ger, note that I suggested to use Flash resp.the Flash control in this context mainly as a better way to communicate with the server (via Flash Remoting). So far this flash "content" would have no user interface and could be invisible. SVG  resp. the embeddable Adobe SVG viewer in contrast has no comparable communication feature (as I know). Another question is what we should use when we deliver and show scalable vector graphics and GUIs inside browsers. The clear answer of the market is: Flash. Some reasons are: - diffusion rate. Flash was faster on the market, SVG viewers came to late - Amount of data to download the player / viewer - Available high level tools to create content - The Flash file format is also open (like SVG), so you can write your own tools (like many vendors do) - as you know SVG is open and has a W3C recommendation, but the needed Adobe viewer is proprietary and "closed source" like the Flash Player. May be SVG gets a second chance and genuin support with Windows Longhorn. The GUI of this new version will be completely vector based and will be encoded in a SVG "similar" XML file format.

ResponsesInList.Title: How to cope with SCORM
ResponsesInList.Text: I think that the way BoBO is implementing SCORM (or the way I perceive it ) is very clever and can be a inspiring for other standards-projects: create a "plug&play-shell" where the modul can run look which information can go to the gradebook: connect it create a "local gradebook" for the dirty details of the modul, unitl Gradebook can cope with it This way we can say that we are SCORM compatible (specify which level/ which part), BUT ALSO we can say that we do more and other things, like group activities , giving grades for that AND INTEGRATING IT... Looking at the discussion about SCORM, I see a lot of activity where people who have better knowledge of SCORM, test and refine the SCORM shell more and more. (like the trick that will be needed to intercept and handle the call to LMS and the API-connector) For all the others it would be handy to have a list of public available SCORM-moduls and the status of "Moodle, handling that SCORM-modul". (Would be great if you do a lecture and that S-question comes again from the audiance, that you can demonstrate several of these public files and then ask the other one: "Ok I showed you mine, How about yours.." The killing remark will be: "So you can only do SCORM.."
